source.title: Potential automorphy over CM fields
source.authors: Patrick B. Allen, Frank Calegari, Ana Caraiani, Toby Gee, David Helm, Bao V. Le Hung, James Newton, Peter Scholze, Richard Taylor, Jack A. Thorne
readSections: The published version, read in full: the Annals PDF posted on Frank Calegari's page (https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~fcale/papers/Ramanujan.pdf; 217 pages with the header 'Annals of Mathematics 197 (2023), 897–1113', created 15 March 2023, SHA-256 c5429e4f384384045dbb48502d71547bb21699783c0f77cce27b24e742467f02, fetched 23 September 2026). Received 24 December 2018, revised and accepted 14 June 2022, published online 23 March 2023. Item locators, statement numbers and pages are the published ones.

arXiv 1812.09999v2 (16 June 2022, 'the accepted version'; PDF SHA-256 7c882c4dc7208e08a0b1f4b3ce6e5c5234c9815f139a4c3a372898378a24d08c, TeX source SHA-256 94711e862ccdc2998f06f4b384d42aad587de2d7246ec5cc0f18c7be1932886b), whose TeX was read alongside for the exact formulas. Its content agrees with print up to copy-editing, but the numbering does not: from §2.2 on, print numbers displays and statements in one counter (v2 Lemma 2.2.3 is published Lemma 2.2.4, v2 Lemma 6.2.25 is published 6.2.26), so citations of v2 numbers elsewhere in the atlas are off by one in places. Every slip recorded as introduced in print was compared with v2. v1 (December 2018) was not compared.

Read: §1 (Theorems 1.0.1–1.0.2, the overview with Theorem 1.1.1, the notation of §1.2), §2 (2.1 locally symmetric spaces and Hecke algebras of monoids, 2.2 the quasi-split unitary group, its Hecke operators at split places including the pro-ℓ-Iwahori and parahoric levels of §2.2.5, duality and twisting, 2.3 automorphic Galois representations, 2.4 boundary cohomology), §3 (local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p), §4 (the Fontaine–Laffaille case at ℓ = p), §5 (the ordinary case: Hida theory, ordinary parts of parabolic inductions, degree shifting), §6 (automorphy lifting: deformation theory, avoiding Ihara's lemma, ultrapatching, the proofs of Theorems 6.1.1 and 6.1.2), §7 (compatible systems, Theorem 7.1.11 and Corollaries 7.1.12–7.1.16, the proof of the main potential automorphy theorem) and the references. The reading was split into seven section blocks, each with a coverage table mapping every numbered statement and numbered paragraph to an item; every recorded mistake was checked on the published page images.

Cited inputs were not read; items resting on Scholze [Sch15], Caraiani–Scholze [CS19], Calegari–Geraghty [CG18], Newton–Thorne [NT16], Khare–Thorne [KT17], Clozel–Harris–Taylor [CHT08], Taylor [Tay08], Thorne [Tho12], [Tho15], Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor [BLGGT14], Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne [HLTT16], Varma [Var14], Geraghty [Ger19], Emerton [Eme10a], [Eme10b], Hauseux [Hau16], Chenevier [Che14], Bellaïche–Chenevier [BC09], Gee–Newton [GN22], Franke [Fra98], Franke–Schwermer [FS98], Borel–Serre [BS73], Bushnell–Kutzko [BK98], Kostant [Kos61], Fontaine–Laffaille [FL82], Jacquet–Shalika [JS81a], [JS81b], Harris [Har09], Moret-Bailly, Breuil [Bre00], Kisin [Kis06], Raynaud [Ray74], Serre [Ser72] and the other references state them as the paper uses them.

summary: Allen, Calegari, Caraiani, Gee, Helm, Le Hung, Newton, Scholze, Taylor and Thorne prove the first unconditional automorphy lifting theorems for n-dimensional Galois representations of CM fields with no self-duality: Theorem 6.1.1 (Fontaine–Laffaille, p unramified, p > n², weights in a Fontaine–Laffaille range) and Theorem 6.1.2 (ordinary, p > n), for ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, decomposed generic and of enormous image over F(ζ_p). The inputs are local–global compatibility for the Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations of Scholze's torsion theorem, at ℓ ≠ p (§3, through ramified Hecke operators at split places of the quasi-split unitary group U(n, n) and its boundary) and at ℓ = p (§4 Fontaine–Laffaille and §5 ordinary, by degree shifting with Caraiani–Scholze's vanishing theorem for the generic part of the cohomology of non-compact unitary Shimura varieties), and a derived Ihara avoidance inside ultrapatching of complexes (§6) that replaces the unproved vanishing of mod-p cohomology outside a range. Applications (§7): potential automorphy of rank-2 compatible systems with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, 1} and their symmetric powers (Theorem 7.1.11), hence potential modularity and the Sato–Tate conjecture for elliptic curves over CM fields (Theorem 1.0.1) and the Ramanujan conjecture for weight-0 cuspidal representations of GL_2 over CM fields (Theorem 1.0.2). The atlas's PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure (PA.0–PA.5) is built from this paper, and with its suppliers it plans about three quarters of the items. The rest are routed as sources of the existing layers of twelve roadmaps: the lifting theorems themselves and the endgames are sources of PA, and the ℓ ≠ p local–global compatibility with its ramified Hecke operators is a proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. The recorded mistakes include two introduced in print, a lemma that is false for l = 2, and a missing prime bound in the choice of auxiliary primes of §7.2.

items.name: Theorem 1.0.1: potential modularity of symmetric powers of elliptic curves over CM fields, and Sato–Tate
items.statement: Let F be a CM number field (in the sense of §1.2: F has an automorphism c with c∘i = i∘c for every embedding i : F ↪ ℂ, so F is totally real or a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field), and let E/F be an elliptic curve. Then E and all the symmetric powers of E are potentially modular: for every m ≥ 0 there is a finite extension F′/F over which Symm^m of the compatible system H¹(E) becomes automorphic. Consequently the Sato–Tate conjecture holds for E. (Stated as a special case of Corollaries 7.1.13 and 7.1.14; Corollary 7.1.14 assumes E non-CM, and the automorphy of Symm^m over a finite Galois CM extension is Corollary 7.1.12 / Theorem 7.1.11.)
items.note: PA README: 'The final potential-automorphy assembly has downstream owner ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2; symmetric powers and Sato–Tate have downstream owner ML.3.' ML.2: 'Apply PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure with full regularity, polarization, residual-image, local and field-extension hypotheses'; ML.3: 'Integrate ... symmetric-power automorphy, CM/non-CM branches and resulting analytic/equidistribution arguments'. Same routing as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (ML.2, ML.3) and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/sato-tate (ML.3). The Sato–Tate half needs E non-CM (Corollary 7.1.14; The analytic input (Brauer induction, non-vanishing [HSBT10, Thm 4.2]) is ML.3's with AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4.

items.name: Theorem 1.0.2: Ramanujan conjecture for weight-0 regular algebraic cuspidal GL₂ over CM fields
items.statement: Let F be a CM field and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_F) of weight 0 (i.e. of weight (0)_{τ,i} in the sense of §1.2: π_∞ has the infinitesimal character of the trivial representation). Then for every prime v of F the local component π_v is tempered.
items.note: Proved as Corollary 7.1.15: purity of the compatible system (Corollary 7.1.13(1)) from potential automorphy of all Symm^m together with the Jacquet–Shalika bound [JS81b, Cor. 2.5]. ML.3: 'Integrate ... symmetric-power automorphy ... and resulting analytic/equidistribution arguments'; AL.3 plans the GL_n×GL_m Rankin–Selberg theory behind the Jacquet–Shalika bound ('Construct the GL_n×GL_m local zeta integrals'). Consistent with PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 (Theorem A, parallel-weight Ramanujan) routed to ML.3.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.1 (Caraiani–Scholze): torsion vanishing outside the middle degree for the quasi-split unitary group
items.statement: (Caraiani–Scholze [CS19, Th. 1.1].) Let F/F⁺ be an imaginary CM field, G̃ the quasi-split unitary group of §2.2.1 with locally symmetric spaces X̃_{K̃}, 𝒱_λ̃ an integral coefficient system, d = n²[F⁺:ℚ] the complex (middle) dimension of X̃_{K̃}, 𝔪 ⊂ T^S a maximal ideal with associated 𝔪̃ ⊂ T̃^S. Assume F⁺ ≠ ℚ, 𝔪 is non-Eisenstein, ρ̄_𝔪̃ is decomposed generic (Definition 4.3.1), and for every prime l that is the residue characteristic of a prime dividing S or Δ_F there is an imaginary quadratic field F₀ ⊂ F in which l splits. Then H^i(X̃_{K̃}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ)_𝔪̃ = 0 for i < d and H^i_c(X̃_{K̃}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ)_𝔪̃ = 0 for i > d. Consequently there is a diagram H^d(X̃_{K̃}, 𝒱_λ̃[1/p])_𝔪̃ ↩ H^d(X̃_{K̃}, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ ↠ H^d(∂X̃_{K̃}, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃.
items.note: IG.7: 'Prove the reusable source inequalities on the unitary arithmetic quotient: H^i(X_K,F_ell)_m=0 for i<d and H_c^i(X_K,F_ell)_m=0 for i>d ... Export ACC+ Theorem 4.3.3's middle-degree injection into rational cohomology and surjection onto the boundary, with the source's level/ramification and [F^+:Q]>1 hypotheses.' This is the introduction's form of Theorem 4.3.3 (which uses 'ρ̄_𝔪̃ of length at most 2' in place of '𝔪 non-Eisenstein'); PA matrix routes §4.3 to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration. Consistent with PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-24 (Remarks 1.5–1.6 at IG.7).

items.name: Euler-characteristic criterion for characteristic-zero support (the introduction's 'simple avatar')
items.statement: If M is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module, then M[1/p] ≠ 0 if and only if M ⊗^𝐋_{ℤ_p} 𝔽_p has non-zero Euler characteristic over 𝔽_p (indeed χ(M ⊗^𝐋 𝔽_p) = dim M/pM − dim M[p] = rank_{ℤ_p} M).
items.note: Illustration of the derived Ihara-avoidance principle, formulated in general as Lemma 6.3.4. P9: 'Make the derived length identity of ACC+ §6.3.4 a reusable intermediate theorem ... prove the dimension-zero vanishing and dimension-one generic-length formula for the Euler characteristic after derived reduction modulo f.' The avatar is the case S = T = ℤ_p, f = p.

items.name: Basic conventions and the residual representation ρ̄
items.statement: ᵗA is the transpose of A; char_A its characteristic polynomial; GL_n is the reductive group scheme over ℤ, with T_n ⊂ B_n ⊂ GL_n the diagonal and upper-triangular subgroups; O(n) = {g ∈ GL_n(ℝ) : ᵗg^c g = 1_n} and U(n) = {g ∈ GL_n(ℂ) : ᵗg^c g = 1_n}; 𝔪_R is the maximal ideal of a local ring R. For an abelian group Δ, Δ^tor is its maximal torsion subgroup and Δ^tf its maximal torsion-free quotient; for Δ profinite abelian, Δ(l) is its Sylow pro-l subgroup (≅ its maximal pro-l continuous quotient). For a profinite group Γ, Γ^ab is its maximal abelian quotient by a closed subgroup, and H^i(Γ, M) is continuous cohomology of a topological abelian group M with continuous Γ-action. For a continuous ρ : Γ → GL_n(Q̄_l), ρ̄ : Γ → GL_n(F̄_l) is the semisimplification of its reduction (of any invariant lattice), well defined up to conjugacy by the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem.
items.note: R01.1: 'Define reduction followed by semisimplification and prove independence of lattice by characteristic polynomials and the characteristic-p Brauer–Nesbitt theorem.' The remaining items are pure notation; Library pointers (for parts only): Matrix.charpoly, Matrix.unitaryGroup / Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/UnitaryGroup.lean), IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal.

items.name: Derived categories, perfect complexes and localization of a perfect complex at the maximal ideals of a Hecke image
items.statement: For a (possibly non-commutative) ring R, 𝐃(R) is the derived category of R-modules (objects: cochain complexes); an object is perfect if it is isomorphic in 𝐃(R) to a bounded complex of projective R-modules. If R is a complete Noetherian local ring, C ∈ 𝐃(R) is perfect and T → End_{𝐃(R)}(C) is a homomorphism of R-algebras, then the image T̄ of T is a finite R-algebra, hence T̄ = ∏_𝔪 T̄_𝔪 over its maximal ideals with 1 = Σ_𝔪 e_𝔪; since 𝐃(R) is idempotent complete this gives C = ⊕_𝔪 C_𝔪 in 𝐃(R), the summands C_𝔪 being well defined up to unique isomorphism. (C^• denotes an actual cochain complex; 'C^• = 0 in 𝐃(R)' means acyclic.)
items.note: IHG.2: 'For a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex define its finite image algebras ... Prove localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings'; P7: 'Define perfectness through local finite-projective resolutions'. Mathlib has DerivedCategory (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory); perfectness and the idempotent splitting are not in it.

items.name: The Hecke algebra ℋ(U, G) of a locally profinite group
items.statement: For G locally profinite and U ⊂ G open compact, ℋ(U, G) is the algebra of compactly supported U-biinvariant functions f : G → ℤ under convolution for the Haar measure giving U volume 1; for a compact U-biinvariant X ⊂ G, [X] ∈ ℋ(U, G) is its characteristic function. (Everywhere after §1.2 the paper writes this algebra as ℋ(G, U).)
items.note: SR.1: 'Construct compactly supported locally constant functions and convolution ... identify e_U corners with U-biinvariant Hecke algebras ... construct integral double-coset operators by finite correspondences where averaging is unavailable.

items.name: Weyl groups W(G,T), W_P(G,T), dominant cones and the Kostant representatives W^P(G,T)
items.statement: For G reductive over a field k and T ⊂ G a split maximal torus, W(G,T) is the set of k-points of N_G(T)/T; e.g. W((Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n)_ℂ, (Res_{F/ℚ}T_n)_ℂ) ≅ S_n^{Hom(F,ℂ)}. For a parabolic P ⊃ T with unique Levi L ⊃ T, W_P(G,T) = W(L,T) ⊂ W(G,T). If B ⊂ P is a Borel containing T, X*(T)⁺ ⊂ X*(T) is the set of B-dominant characters and X*(T)^{+,P} the set of (B ∩ L)-dominant ones. Claim: W^P(G,T) = {w ∈ W(G,T) : w(X*(T)⁺) ⊂ X*(T)^{+,P}} is a set of representatives for W_P(G,T)\W(G,T).
items.note: Weyl groups, parabolics and Levis are planned in the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap, Layer 7 ('Root datum ... with its Weyl group'; 'parabolic subgroups and Levi decomposition'), but no stage plans the Kostant representatives W^P or the coset-representative claim; the Kostant-formula search found only LieHighestWeight Layer 6 (character formulas, not W^P). W^P indexes the degree shifts of §4.4 and §5.4 (Theorem 2.4.x, Theorem 5.4.3). Library pointers (for parts only): Mathlib RootPairing/RootSystem weylGroup. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Galois-theoretic notation: G_F, ε_l, ω_l, δ_{E/F}, Br_F
items.statement: For a perfect field F: F̄ is an algebraic closure and G_F = Gal(F̄/F); ζ_n is a primitive n-th root of 1; ε_l is the l-adic cyclotomic character and ε̄_l its reduction mod l; ω_l : G_F → μ_{l−1} ⊂ ℤ_l^× is the Teichmüller lift of ε̄_l; for a separable quadratic E/F, δ_{E/F} is the non-trivial character of Gal(E/F); Br_F is the Brauer group of F.
items.note: R01.2: 'Construct tame characters and fundamental characters of levels one and two' (ω_l is the level-one fundamental character); Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 owns 'the Brauer group'. Library pointers (for parts only): Mathlib modularCyclotomicCharacter (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean) for ε_l.

items.name: Local-field notation and normalizations: Q_{l^r}, K^nr, I_K, geometric Frobenius, W_K, Art_K, fundamental characters ω_{l,r}
items.statement: ℚ_{l^r} is the unramified extension of ℚ_l of degree r, ℤ_{l^r} its ring of integers; ℚ_l^nr, ℤ_l^nr the maximal unramified extension and its integers; ℤ̂_l^nr the l-adic completion of ℤ_l^nr and ℚ̂_l^nr its fraction field. For K/ℚ_p finite: K^nr its maximal unramified extension, I_K ⊂ G_K inertia, Frob_K ∈ G_K/I_K the geometric Frobenius, W_K the Weil group; for K′/K Galois, I_{K′/K} ⊂ Gal(K′/K) the inertia subgroup. Art_K : K^× ⥲ W_K^ab is normalized to send uniformizers to geometric Frobenius elements. ω_{l,r} : G_{ℚ_{l^r}} → ℤ_{l^r}^× is the character with ω_{l,r}∘Art_{ℚ_{l^r}}(l) = 1 and ω_{l,r}∘Art_{ℚ_{l^r}}(a) = Teichmüller lift of (a mod l) for a ∈ ℤ_{l^r}^× ('fundamental character of niveau r'); ω_{l,1} = ω_l.
items.note: LocalFieldsRamification Layer 2 (unramified extensions and Frobenius); ClassFieldTheory Layer 7: 'the absolute local Artin map, its normalizations' — 'geometricArtinMap is defined only as the precomposition of the arithmetic map with inversion', which is ACC+'s Art_K; Layer 9 'the local Weil group'. R01.2 plans fundamental characters only 'of levels one and two'; ω_{l,r} for general r is not planned (flag).

items.name: Local Langlands correspondences rec_K (Harris–Taylor) and rec^T_K (arithmetic normalization)
items.statement: rec_K is the local Langlands correspondence of [HT01]: for π an irreducible complex admissible representation of GL_n(K), rec_K(π) is a Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation of W_K (written rec when K is clear). rec^T_K is the arithmetic normalization of the local Langlands correspondence, as in [CT14, §2.1]; it is defined on irreducible admissible representations of GL_n(K) over any field abstractly isomorphic to ℂ (e.g. Q̄_l).
items.note: ET.6: 'Construct the characteristic-zero local correspondence for GL_m(E) ... with full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters and monodromy'; AG2.0: 'After ET.6, prove its agreement with rec(π_v ⊗ |det|^((1−n)/2))' (this is rec^T; in [CT14, §2.1] rec^T_K(π) = rec_K(π ⊗ |det|^{(1−n)/2}), which the paper only cites); ML.0: 'normalization conversions'.

items.name: Weil–Deligne representations for l ≠ p, Frobenius semisimplification, Steinberg representations, local isobaric sums and local base change
items.statement: For a Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) of W_K, (r, N)^{F-ss} is its Frobenius semisimplification. For a continuous representation ρ of G_K over Q̄_l, l ≠ p (K/ℚ_p finite), WD(ρ) is the associated Weil–Deligne representation of W_K [TY07, §1]. A Steinberg representation of GL_n(K) is Sp_n(ψ) ([HT01, §1.3]) with ψ an unramified character of K^×. For irreducible smooth π_i of GL_{n_i}(K) (i = 1, 2), π₁ ⊞ π₂ is the irreducible smooth representation of GL_{n₁+n₂}(K) with rec(π₁ ⊞ π₂) = rec(π₁) ⊕ rec(π₂). For K′/K finite and π irreducible smooth of GL_n(K), BC_{K′/K}(π) is characterized by rec_{K′}(BC_{K′/K}(π)) = rec_K(π)|_{W_{K′}}.
items.note: R01.2: 'For ℓ different from the residue characteristic, prove quasi-unipotence and construct the monodromy operator and Weil–Deligne representation ... Distinguish the full object, its semisimplification, and its Frobenius semisimplification'; ET.6: 'Verify compatibility with the Weil semisimplification ..., Steinberg twists, direct sums'; ML.5 registers 'cyclic base change ... with exact hypotheses' (local base change is its local shadow).

items.name: Weil–Deligne representation at p and the Hodge–Tate convention HT_τ(ε_p) = {−1}
items.statement: If ρ is a de Rham representation of G_K over Q̄_p (K/ℚ_p finite), WD(ρ) is the associated Weil–Deligne representation of W_K. For a continuous embedding τ : K ↪ Q̄_p, HT_τ(ρ) is the multiset of dim ρ integers in which i occurs with multiplicity dim_{Q̄_p}(ρ ⊗_{τ,K} K̂̄(i))^{G_K} (printed dim_{Q̄_l}); thus HT_τ(ε_p) = {−1}.
items.note: R06.3: 'attach a potentially semistable Weil–Deligne parameter to a de Rham representation ... Compare the determinant, twists and Frobenius conventions with R01'; R06.2 'Define D_HT, D_dR ...'; AG2.6: 'Calculate the labelled Hodge–Tate multiset from the algebraic highest weight, respecting the dual convention'. The convention (cyclotomic character has weight −1) is used in Theorem 2.3.3(b) and §4.

items.name: Un-normalized and normalized parabolic induction; δ_P; ⊞ as a subquotient
items.statement: For G reductive over K, P a parabolic with unipotent radical N and Levi L, and π a smooth representation of L(K): Ind_{P(K)}^{G(K)} π is the space of locally constant f : G(K) → π with f(hg) = π(hN(K)) f(g) for h ∈ P(K), g ∈ G(K), with (g₁f)(g₂) = f(g₂g₁) ('natural'/'un-normalized'); δ_P is the determinant of the action of L on Lie N, and n-Ind_{P(K)}^{G(K)} π = Ind_{P(K)}^{G(K)}(π ⊗ |δ_P|_K^{1/2}). If P ⊂ GL_{n₁+n₂} has Levi GL_{n₁} × GL_{n₂}, then π₁ ⊞ π₂ is a subquotient of n-Ind_{P(K)}^{GL_{n₁+n₂}(K)} π₁ ⊗ π₂.
items.note: SR.2: 'For P=MN define unnormalized induction and N-coinvariants, then normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character'; ET.6: 'use the multisegment/Langlands classification to assemble the full Frobenius-semisimple parameter' (gives the subquotient claim).

items.name: Archimedean conventions: Art_ℝ, Art_ℂ, rec_ℝ, rec_ℂ, archimedean ⊞ and BC_{ℂ/ℝ}
items.statement: c is complex conjugation on ℂ; Art_ℝ : ℝ^× ↠ Gal(ℂ/ℝ) and Art_ℂ : ℂ^× ↠ Gal(ℂ/ℂ) are the unique continuous surjections. rec_ℝ (resp. rec_ℂ) — the paper prints the two labels interchanged — is Langlands' correspondence [Lan89] from irreducible admissible (Lie GL_n(ℝ) ⊗_ℝ ℂ, O(n))-modules (resp. (Lie GL_n(ℂ) ⊗_ℝ ℂ, U(n))-modules) to continuous semisimple n-dimensional representations of W_ℝ (resp. W_ℂ). For such modules π_i of rank n_i (i = 1, …, r; n = Σ n_i), π₁ ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ π_r is defined by rec(π₁ ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ π_r) = rec(π₁) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ rec(π_r). For π an irreducible admissible (Lie GL_n(ℝ) ⊗ ℂ, O(n))-module, BC_{ℂ/ℝ}(π) is the (Lie GL_n(ℂ) ⊗ ℂ, U(n))-module with rec_ℂ(BC_{ℂ/ℝ}(π)) = rec_ℝ(π)|_{W_ℂ}.
items.note: Art_ℝ and Art_ℂ are planned at ClassFieldTheory Layer 11 ('The archimedean Artin package belongs here: Art_ℂ is trivial, and Art_ℝ has kernel ℝ_{>0}'). No stage plans the archimedean local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(ℝ), GL_n(ℂ), archimedean isobaric sums or BC_{ℂ/ℝ} (searched 'W_R', 'Langlands classification', 'archimedean Langlands'). Used for weights at infinity in §2.3 and §7. Route: a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.0 normalization registry, ML.2 potential-automorphy assembly, ML.3 symmetric powers).

items.name: Regular algebraic automorphic representations of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight ξ
items.statement: An irreducible admissible representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) is regular algebraic of weight ξ ∈ (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,ℂ)} if the infinitesimal character of π_∞ equals that of V_ξ^∨, where V_ξ is the algebraic representation of Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n of highest weight ξ (§2.2.1); π is regular algebraic if it is regular algebraic of some weight.
items.note: AG2.0: 'Define regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual, essentially conjugate self-dual and polarized cases separately'; AF.4: 'Define algebraic highest weights, infinitesimal characters and cohomological representations'.

items.name: Idelic norm, global Artin map and global place notation
items.statement: ‖ ‖ = ∏_v | |_v : 𝔸^×/ℚ^× → ℝ^×_{>0} with the usual normalizations (|p|_p = 1/p); for K/ℚ finite, ‖ ‖_K = ‖ ‖ ∘ N_{K/ℚ}; Art_K = ∏_v Art_{K_v} : 𝔸_K^×/\overline{K^×(K_∞^×)^0} ⥲ G_K^ab. For a finite place v: k(v) is the residue field, q_v = #k(v), Frob_v = Frob_{K_v}; for a real place v, [c_v] is the conjugacy class of complex conjugations at v. For K′/K quadratic, δ_{K′/K} also denotes the non-trivial character of 𝔸_K^×/K^×N_{K′/K}𝔸_{K′}^× (the Galois character composed with Art_K).
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 11: 'The resulting globalArtinMap must satisfy: compatibility with every local Artin map ... arithmetic Frobenius normalization'; the geometric normalization is the Layer 7 conversion. Library pointers (for parts only): Mathlib NumberField.AdeleRing and IdeleGroup (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/AdeleRing.lean) for 𝔸_K^×; check for an idelic norm.

items.name: Global base change for soluble extensions and global isobaric sums
items.statement: If K′/K is a soluble finite Galois extension of number fields and π is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_K), BC_{K′/K}(π) is its base change, an isobaric automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_{K′}) with BC_{K′/K}(π)_v = BC_{K′_v/K_{v|K}}(π_{v|K}) for all places v of K′. For automorphic π_i of GL_{n_i}(𝔸_K) (i = 1, 2), π₁ ⊞ π₂ is the automorphic representation of GL_{n₁+n₂}(𝔸_K) with (π₁ ⊞ π₂)_v = π_{1,v} ⊞ π_{2,v} for all v.
items.note: ML.5: 'Register cyclic base change, automorphic induction and selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers with exact hypotheses' (soluble base change is iterated cyclic base change, Arthur–Clozel); AG2.2: 'keep cuspidal parameters distinct from discrete isobaric parameters'.

items.name: CM fields (including totally real fields) and K⁺
items.statement: A number field K is a CM field if it has an automorphism c such that c∘i = i∘c for all embeddings i : K ↪ ℂ. Then K is either totally real or a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field; in either case K⁺ is the maximal totally real subfield of K.
items.note: Mathlib NumberField.IsCMField (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean) is the totally imaginary case, a totally complex quadratic extension of maximalRealSubfield K, and NumberField.IsTotallyReal the other; the paper's notion is their disjunction. Mathlib proves the characterization by an automorphism commuting with all complex embeddings only for Galois K (IsCMField.of_forall_isConj).

items.name: Algebraic Hecke characters, their l-adic avatars r_{l,ı}(χ) and weight wt(χ)
items.statement: A continuous χ : 𝔸_K^×/K^× → ℂ^× is algebraic if there is a ∈ ℤ^{Hom(K,ℂ)} with χ|_{(K_∞^×)^0}(x) = ∏_{τ∈Hom(K,ℂ)} (τx)^{a_τ}. Then for each prime l and isomorphism ı : Q̄_l ⥲ ℂ there is a unique continuous character r_{l,ı}(χ) : G_K → Q̄_l^× with ı ∘ r_{l,ı}(χ)|_{W_{K_v}} ∘ Art_{K_v} = χ_v for all v ∤ l, and an integer wt(χ) with |χ| = ‖ ‖_K^{−wt(χ)/2} ([BLGGT14, §A.2]).
items.note: AF.5: 'Prove the GL_1 dictionary with Hecke characters including infinity type, conductor and unitary twist'; AG2.0 acceptance: 'n=1 algebraic Hecke characters'; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0: 'Develop locally algebraic Hecke characters, their algebraic and p-adic avatars through chosen embeddings, conductors, infinity types'.

items.name: Totally odd characters
items.statement: For K totally real, a continuous character χ : 𝔸_K^×/K^× → ℂ^× is totally odd if χ_v(−1) = −1 for all v | ∞; a continuous character μ : G_K → Q̄_l^× is totally odd if μ(c_v) = −1 for all v | ∞.
items.note: No stage defines totally odd characters (search 'totally odd'); G7 plans oddness only for polarized representations ('Oddness for polarized dimension n is specified by the sign at each real place'), R01.4 the rank-two case. Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: The symmetric space X^G of a connected group over a number field
items.statement: Let F be a number field, G a connected linear algebraic group over F and 𝔾 = Res_{F/ℚ}G. Fix a space of type S−ℚ for 𝔾 in the sense of [BS73, §2]: a homogeneous space X^G for 𝔾(ℝ) with a family of Levi subgroups of 𝔾_ℝ satisfying Borel–Serre's conditions; by [BS73, Lem. 2.1] X^G is determined up to isomorphism ('the symmetric space' for G). For G = GL_{n,F} one can take X^G = GL_n(F_∞)/K_∞ℝ^× with K_∞ ⊂ GL_n(F_∞) maximal compact. X^G is diffeomorphic to Euclidean space.
items.note: ALS.0: 'Construct Cartan involutions, maximal compact subgroups and the contractible symmetric space with G(F∞)-action ... The reductive center correction is part of the definition, not silently absorbed into K∞.'

items.name: Neat and good subgroups; the locally symmetric spaces X^G_{K_G} and 𝔛_G
items.statement: An element g = (g_v)_v ∈ G(𝔸_F^∞) is neat if ∩_v Γ_v is trivial, Γ_v ⊂ Q̄^× being the torsion subgroup of the subgroup of F̄_v^× generated by the eigenvalues of g_v in some faithful representation of G; an open compact K_G ⊂ G(𝔸_F^∞) is neat if all its elements are. A good subgroup is a neat open compact K_G = ∏_v K_{G,v} (product over finite places). For good K_G: X^G_{K_G} = G(F)\(X^G × G(𝔸_F^∞)/K_G) and 𝔛_G = G(F)\(X^G × G(𝔸_F^∞)) (discrete topology on G(𝔸_F^∞)). These are smooth manifolds, G(𝔸_F^∞) acts on 𝔛_G by right translation, X^G_{K_G} = 𝔛_G/K_G, and by neatness X^G_{K_G} is a finite disjoint union of quotients of X^G by torsion-free arithmetic subgroups of G(F).
items.note: ALS.0: 'Prove the finite decomposition of X_K into arithmetic Γ-components ... Prove proper discontinuity and, at neat level, freeness'; ShimuraData D5: 'Define neatness with representation independence'; AA.3: 'Supply the finiteness of G(F)\G(A_f)/K ... needed for locally symmetric components'.

items.name: Partial Borel–Serre compactification and boundary
items.statement: X̄^G is the partial Borel–Serre compactification of X^G [BS73, §7.1]; X̄^G_{K_G} = G(F)\(X̄^G × G(𝔸_F^∞)/K_G) and 𝔛̄_G = G(F)\(X̄^G × G(𝔸_F^∞)). For every good K_G, X̄^G_{K_G} = 𝔛̄_G/K_G is compact [BS73, Th. 9.3]; more precisely it is a compact smooth manifold with corners with interior X^G_{K_G}, and X^G_{K_G} ↪ X̄^G_{K_G} is a homotopy equivalence. ∂X^G = X̄^G − X^G, ∂X^G_{K_G} = G(F)\(∂X^G × G(𝔸_F^∞)/K_G), ∂𝔛_G = G(F)\(∂X^G × G(𝔸_F^∞)).
items.note: ALS.2: 'prove the manifold-with-corners structure at neat level, compactness of the quotient and the homotopy equivalence from the interior'.

items.name: Local systems from coefficient modules and the Hecke action on RΓ(X^G_{K_G}, 𝒱) and RΓ_c
items.statement: For S a finite set of finite places: G^S = G(𝔸_F^{∞,S}), G_S = G(𝔸_{F,S}), K_G^S = ∏_{v∉S}K_{G,v}, K_{G,S} = ∏_{v∈S}K_{G,v}, G^∞ = G(𝔸_F^∞). For a ring R and an R[G(F) × K_{G,S}]-module 𝒱, finite free over R: pulling back from a point gives a G(F) × G^S × K_{G,S}-equivariant sheaf on X^G × G(𝔸_F^∞), which descends (free action, [NT16, Lem. 2.17]) to a G^S × K_{G,S}-equivariant sheaf on 𝔛_G; RΓ(K_G, RΓ(𝔛_G, 𝒱)) is an object of 𝐃(ℋ(G^S,K_G^S) ⊗_ℤ R) whose image under the forgetful functor is RΓ(X^G_{K_G}, 𝒱) [NT16, Prop. 2.18]. This gives the canonical homomorphism (2.1.3) ℋ(G^S, K_G^S) ⊗_ℤ R → End_{𝐃(R)}(RΓ(X^G_{K_G}, 𝒱)). The same holds on the Borel–Serre compactification; for any right G^S × K_{G,S}-space Y and bounded-below complex C of equivariant sheaves of R-modules there is ℋ(G^S,K_G^S) ⊗ R → End_{𝐃(R)}(RΓ(K_G, RΓ(Y, C))); with j : X^G × G(𝔸_F^∞) ↪ X̄^G × G(𝔸_F^∞) and j_!𝒱 this gives ℋ(G^S,K_G^S) ⊗ R → End_{𝐃(R)}(RΓ_c(X^G_{K_G}, 𝒱)).
items.note: ALS.1: 'Construct local systems from discrete integral coefficient modules ... compact-support cochains'; ALS.3: 'For g and K construct the two finite-level maps ... composition via the double-coset algebra and compatibility with ... compact support and boundary restriction. Lift relations to the derived category with their coherence data'.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.4: finite generation of cohomology
items.statement: Let K_G be a good subgroup, R a Noetherian ring and 𝒱 an R[G(F) × K_G]-module, finite free as an R-module. Then H*(X^G_{K_G}, 𝒱) is a finitely generated R-module.
items.note: Consequence of the Borel–Serre compactification [BS73, §11]. ALS.1: 'Under finite-CW/neat hypotheses and finite-projective coefficient stalks, build bounded finite projective models over the coefficient ring'.

items.name: The equivariant complex RΓ_{K_G/K′_G}(X^G_{K′_G}, 𝒱) and its Hecke action (2.1.5), (2.1.6)
items.statement: For a normal good subgroup K′_G ⊂ K_G with K_G^S = (K′_G)^S, RΓ_{K_G/K′_G}(X^G_{K′_G}, 𝒱) ∈ 𝐃(R[K_G/K′_G]) computes H*(X^G_{K′_G}, 𝒱) with its natural K_G/K′_G = K_{G,S}/K′_{G,S}-action; its image under the forgetful functor 𝐃(R[K_G/K′_G]) → 𝐃(R) is RΓ(X^G_{K′_G}, 𝒱), and there is a homomorphism (2.1.5) ℋ(G^S,K_G^S) ⊗_ℤ R → End_{𝐃(R[K_G/K′_G])}(RΓ_{K_G/K′_G}(X^G_{K′_G}, 𝒱)) recovering (2.1.3) after composing with the map (2.1.6) End_{𝐃(R[K_G/K′_G])}(RΓ_{K_G/K′_G}(X^G_{K′_G},𝒱)) → End_{𝐃(R)}(RΓ(X^G_{K_G},𝒱)) induced by RΓ(K_G/K′_G, ?).
items.note: ALS.6: 'Prove finite-level descent and the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application'; ALS.3: 'Prove change-of-level and groupoid versions'.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.7: perfectness of RΓ_{K_G/K′_G} over R[K_G/K′_G]
items.statement: Let K_G be a good subgroup and K′_G ⊂ K_G a normal subgroup which is also good; let R be Noetherian and 𝒱 an R[G(F) × K_G]-module, finite free over R. Then RΓ_{K_G/K′_G}(X^G_{K′_G}, 𝒱) is a perfect object of 𝐃(R[K_G/K′_G]), i.e. isomorphic to a bounded complex of projective R[K_G/K′_G]-modules. (Proof: X̄^G_{K_G} has a finite triangulation; with C_• the bounded complex of finite free ℤ[G(F) × K_G]-modules of simplicial chains of the pulled-back triangulation of X̄^G × G(𝔸_F^∞), the complex is Hom_{ℤ[G(F)×K′_G]}(C_•, 𝒱).)
items.note: ALS.1: 'build bounded finite projective models over the coefficient ring'; CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.4: 'Build cellular complexes on finite CW or Borel–Serre models and equivariant lifted cell complexes on a cofinal torsion-free tower'.

items.name: Decomposed levels and the constant-term maps r_P, r_M, 𝒮 = r_M ∘ r_P (2.1.8)
items.statement: Let G be reductive, P = MN a parabolic with Levi M, K_G ⊂ G(𝔸_F^∞) good; K_P = K_G ∩ P(𝔸_F^∞), K_N = K_G ∩ N(𝔸_F^∞), K_M the image of K_P in M(𝔸_F^∞). K_G is decomposed w.r.t. P = MN if K_P = K_M ⋉ K_N (equivalently K_M = K_G ∩ M(𝔸_F^∞)). If K_G is decomposed and K_{G,v} is hyperspecial for v ∉ S, restriction to P and integration along N give algebra homomorphisms r_P : ℋ(G^S,K_G^S) → ℋ(P^S,K_P^S) and r_M : ℋ(P^S,K_P^S) → ℋ(M^S,K_M^S), integration along N preserving integrality ([NT16, §§2.2.3–2.2.4]); (2.1.8) 𝒮 = 𝒮^G_M = r_M ∘ r_P, and the same notation is used for the local Hecke algebras at v ∉ S.
items.note: ALS.4: 'Develop the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for each unipotent/Levi stratum and compare its Hecke action with parabolic induction and Satake transforms, including modulus and Tate shifts'; TC.3: 'calculate the Hecke action through the Levi Satake map'.

items.name: Hecke algebras of positive monoids (§2.1.9) and Lemma 2.1.10
items.statement: Local setting: F non-archimedean with residue field of cardinality q, G reductive over F. For U ⊂ G(F) open compact and Δ ⊂ G(F) an open submonoid with UΔU = Δ, ℋ(Δ, U) ⊂ ℋ(G(F), U) (functions supported in Δ) is a subalgebra, and for an R[Δ]-module (or complex) M there is ℋ(Δ,U) → End_{𝐃(R)}(RΓ(U, M)). Let P = MN be a parabolic with opposite P̄ = MN̄ and U admit an Iwahori decomposition w.r.t. P: with U_N = U ∩ N(F), U_M = U ∩ M(F), U_N̄ = U ∩ N̄(F), both product maps U_N × U_M × U_N̄ → U and U_N̄ × U_M × U_N → U are bijective. Δ_M = {t ∈ M(F) : tU_Nt^{-1} ⊂ U_N and U_N̄ ⊂ tU_N̄t^{-1}} (U-positive elements), Δ = U_NΔ_MU_N̄. Lemma 2.1.10: Δ_M and Δ are monoids, Δ_M is open in M(F), Δ is open in G(F), UΔU = Δ and Δ ∩ M(F) = Δ_M. Hence ℋ(Δ,U), ℋ(Δ_M,U_M) are defined, Δ_P = Δ ∩ P(F) is a monoid and ℋ(Δ_P,U_P) is defined.
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators ... Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters'. PA.2 names the positive monoids for the §5 tower; the general Iwahori-decomposition lemma is not stated separately (flag).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.11: restriction and integration are algebra homomorphisms on monoid Hecke algebras; basis formulas
items.statement: The maps r_P : ℋ(Δ,U) → ℋ(Δ_P,U_P) (restriction to P(F)) and r_M : ℋ(Δ_P,U_P) → ℋ(Δ_M,U_M) (integration along U_N) are algebra homomorphisms. On basis elements, for m ∈ Δ_M, r_P([UmU]) = [U_PmU_P] and 𝒮([UmU]) := r_M∘r_P([UmU]) = #(U_N/mU_Nm^{-1})[U_MmU_M] = |δ_P(m)|_F^{-1}[U_MmU_M].
items.note: PA.2 (positive-monoid operators, 'Track positive monoids, normalization'); the unramified analogue is ALS.4's Satake comparison. Proof uses [NT16, Lem. 2.4, 2.7].

items.name: Lemma 2.1.12: the map t : ℋ(Δ_M,U_M) → ℋ(Δ,U) is an algebra homomorphism; t∘𝒮, 𝒮∘t; strongly positive elements
items.statement: The ℤ-linear map t : ℋ(Δ_M, U_M) → ℋ(Δ, U), t([U_MmU_M]) = [UmU], is an algebra homomorphism [BK98, Cor. 6.12]. Thus t and 𝒮 are injective algebra homomorphisms with t∘𝒮([UmU]) = |δ_P(m)|_F^{-1}[UmU] and 𝒮∘t([U_MmU_M]) = |δ_P(m)|_F^{-1}[U_MmU_M] for m ∈ Δ_M. Definition (after [BK98]): z ∈ Δ_M central in M is strongly positive if for all open compact H₁, H₂ ⊂ U_N (resp. H̄₁, H̄₂ ⊂ U_N̄) there is n ≥ 0 with z^nH₁z^{−n} ⊂ H₂ (resp. z^{−n}H̄₁z^n ⊂ H̄₂).
items.note: The Bushnell–Kutzko cover map t and strongly positive elements appear in no stage (searched 'strongly positive', 'Bushnell', 'Iwahori decomposition'); PA.2 mentions positive monoids only. Used for the ramified Hecke operators of §2.2.5 and for §3 (l ≠ p). Route: a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1 (Hecke algebras over rings).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.13: localization at a strongly positive element
items.statement: Let z ∈ Δ_M be strongly positive. (1) [U_MzU_M] lies in the centre of ℋ(Δ_M,U_M), is invertible in ℋ(M(F),U_M) (inverse [U_Mz^{-1}U_M]), and ℋ(Δ_M,U_M)[[U_MzU_M]^{-1}] = ℋ(M(F),U_M). (2) Let R be a ring in which q is a unit and suppose [UzU] is invertible in ℋ(G(F),U) ⊗_ℤ R. Then t ⊗ R and 𝒮 ⊗ R extend uniquely to algebra isomorphisms t : ℋ(M(F),U_M) ⊗_ℤ R → (ℋ(Δ,U) ⊗_ℤ R)[[UzU]^{-1}] and 𝒮 : (ℋ(Δ,U) ⊗_ℤ R)[[UzU]^{-1}] → ℋ(M(F),U_M) ⊗_ℤ R.
items.note: Not in any stage (see Lemma 2.1.12). Used in §2.2.5 (t for pro-l Iwahori levels), Proposition 2.2.18 and Theorem 2.4.8's compatibility with localization. Route: a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1 (Hecke algebras over rings).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.14: Hecke-equivariant evaluation map on invariants of an induced module, with functorial R-splitting
items.statement: Let R be a ring, W an R[P(F)]-module and V = Ind_{P(F)}^{G(F)} W. There is a natural morphism φ : V^U → r_P^*W^{U_P} of ℋ(Δ,U) ⊗_ℤ R-modules (f ↦ f(1)), and, writing (?)^∼ for the forgetful functor to R-modules, (V^U)^∼ → (r_P^*W^{U_P})^∼ has a functorial splitting: for representatives g₁ = 1, g₂, …, g_n of P(F)\G(F)/U, V^U ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n W^{g_iUg_i^{-1}∩P(F)} via f ↦ (f(g_i))_i.
items.note: PA.0: 'Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument and identify their twists and degree shifts'; ALS.4: 'compare its Hecke action with parabolic induction'.

items.name: Global split morphisms relating G-, P- and M-cohomology with monoid Hecke actions
items.statement: Let F be a number field, G reductive over F, P = MN a parabolic, and K_G = K_{G,S}K_{G,T}K_G^{T∪S} good where T, S are disjoint finite sets of finite places, G_{F_v} is unramified and K_v hyperspecial for v ∉ S ∪ T, and K_{G,v} has an Iwahori decomposition w.r.t. P for v ∈ T (monoids Δ_{G,v}, Δ_{G,T} = ∏_{v∈T}Δ_{G,v}, and Δ_{P,T}, Δ_{M,T}). Then 𝒮 : ℋ(G^{S∪T} × Δ_{G,T}, K_G^S) → ℋ(M^{S∪T} × Δ_{M,T}, K_M^S), and for a ring R: (i) there is a split morphism RΓ([Ind_{P^∞}^{G^∞}𝔛_P]/K_G, R) → RΓ(X^P_{K_P}, R) in 𝐃(R), equivariant for ℋ(G^{S∪T} × Δ_{G,T}, K_G^S) ⊗ R (acting on the target via r_P; [NT16, Cor. 2.6], Lemma 2.1.14), whence a surjection H*([Ind 𝔛_P]/K_G, R) → r_P^*H*(X^P_{K_P}, R) of Hecke modules (the splitting need not be equivariant); (ii) there is a split morphism RΓ(X^M_{K_M}, R) → RΓ(X^P_{K_P}, R) in 𝐃(R), equivariant for ℋ(P^{S∪T} × Δ_{P,T}, K_P^S) ⊗ R acting on the source via r_M [NT16, Prop. 3.4].
items.note: ALS.4: 'Develop the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for each unipotent/Levi stratum and compare its Hecke action with parabolic induction and Satake transforms'; PA.0: 'Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument'. Used in the proof of Theorem 2.4.8.

items.name: The quasi-split unitary group G̃, its Siegel parabolic P = U ⋊ G, the isomorphisms ι_v and the dimensions of X̃, X
items.statement: Fix n ≥ 1 and an imaginary CM field F with maximal totally real subfield F⁺. Ψ_n is the n×n antidiagonal matrix of 1's and J_n = (0 Ψ_n; −Ψ_n 0). G̃ = G̃_n is the group scheme over 𝒪_{F⁺} with G̃(R) = {g ∈ GL_{2n}(R ⊗_{𝒪_{F⁺}} 𝒪_F) : ᵗg J_n g^c = J_n}; G̃_{F⁺} is a quasi-split reductive group, a form of GL_{2n} split by F/F⁺. For v̄ split in F and v | v̄, ι_v : G̃(F⁺_v̄) ≅ GL_{2n}(F_v) is G̃(F⁺_v̄) ⊂ GL_{2n}(F_v) × GL_{2n}(F_{v^c}) followed by the first projection. T ⊂ B ⊂ G̃ are the diagonal and upper-triangular subgroups, G ⊂ P ⊂ G̃ the block-diagonal and block upper-triangular subgroups with n × n blocks; P = U ⋊ G with U the unipotent radical, and diag(A, D) ↦ D identifies G ≅ Res_{𝒪_F/𝒪_{F⁺}}GL_n. Over F⁺, T is a maximal torus, B a Borel, and G the unique Levi of P containing T. X̃ = X^{G̃}, X = X^G; K̃, K denote good subgroups of G̃(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) and G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) = GL_n(𝔸_F^∞). dim_ℝ X̃ = 2n²[F⁺:ℚ] and dim_ℝ X = n²[F⁺:ℚ] − 1.
items.note: TC.3: 'For the symplectic/unitary parabolics whose Levi contains a restriction of scalars of GL_n, identify the boundary fibration'; IG.0: 'Construct the additional unitary/similitude comparison on components, levels and spherical Hecke operators (CSnc §2.1)' (CSnc §2.1 uses the same quasi-split U(n,n)). No stage writes out J_n or ι_v; the dimension count is an ALS.0 computation.

items.name: Dominant weights, algebraic representations and integral dual-Weyl lattices 𝒱_λ for G = Res GL_n
items.statement: Fix a prime p and a finite E/ℚ_p in Q̄_p containing the images of all embeddings F ↪ Q̄_p, with ring of integers 𝒪 and uniformizer ϖ. For Ω of characteristic 0 with #Hom(F,Ω) = [F:ℚ], identify X*((Res_{F⁺/ℚ}T)_Ω) = (ℤⁿ)^{Hom(F,Ω)} via (Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n)_Ω = ∏_{τ∈Hom(F,Ω)}GL_n and (λ₁,…,λ_n) ↦ (diag(t₁,…,t_n) ↦ t₁^{λ₁}⋯t_n^{λ_n}); the Res_{F⁺/ℚ}(B ∩ G)_Ω-dominant weights form (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,Ω)} = {(λ_{τ,i}) : λ_{τ,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_{τ,n} for all τ}. V_λ = ⊗_τ V_{λ_τ} is the algebraic representation of (Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n)_Ω of highest weight λ; λ^∨_{τ,i} = −λ_{τ,n+1−i}, and V_λ^∨ ≅ V_{λ^∨} (not for the lattices below without further hypotheses). For Ω = E, 𝒱_{λ_τ} ⊂ V_{λ_τ} is the GL_n(𝒪)-stable lattice of [Ger19, §2.2] (M_{λ_τ} there), the integral dual Weyl module of highest weight λ_τ (global sections of a line bundle on the full flag variety), and 𝒱_λ = ⊗_τ 𝒱_{λ_τ}, an 𝒪[∏_{v|p}GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]-module, finite free over 𝒪.
items.note: PA.1: 'Construct integral algebraic coefficient modules over O, reduction modulo p, Weyl/dual Weyl modules, their highest-weight filtrations'; AF.4: 'Construct coefficient systems from algebraic representations with lattices'.

items.name: Weights for G̃, the weight dictionary λ ↦ λ̃ (2.2.2), and the integral lattices 𝒱_λ̃
items.statement: Choose Ĩ ⊂ Hom(F,Ω) with Hom(F,Ω) = Ĩ ⊔ Ĩ^c, and for τ ∈ Hom(F⁺,Ω) let τ̃ ∈ Ĩ be its extension. This gives (Res_{F⁺/ℚ}G̃)_Ω ≅ ∏_{τ∈Hom(F⁺,Ω)}GL_{2n,Ω} (Res T to the diagonal tori), X*((Res_{F⁺/ℚ}T)_Ω) = (ℤ^{2n})^{Hom(F⁺,Ω)}, dominant weights (ℤ^{2n}₊)^{Hom(F⁺,Ω)}, and the identification (ℤⁿ)^{Hom(F,Ω)} ≅ (ℤ^{2n})^{Hom(F⁺,Ω)}, λ ↦ λ̃, with (2.2.2) λ̃_τ = (−λ_{τ̃c,n}, …, −λ_{τ̃c,1}, λ_{τ̃,1}, λ_{τ̃,2}, …, λ_{τ̃,n}) (the paper prints λ_{τ,2}). Integral structures (Ω = E), assuming every p-adic place v̄ of F⁺ splits in F: S_p (resp. S̄_p) are the p-adic places of F (resp. F⁺), S̃_p ⊂ S_p with S_p = S̃_p ⊔ S̃_p^c, Ĩ = Ĩ_p the embeddings F ↪ E inducing places of S̃_p, and ṽ ∈ S̃_p the place over v̄. The choice of S̃_p gives G̃ ⊗_{𝒪_{F⁺}} 𝒪_{F⁺,p} ≅ ∏_{v̄∈S̄_p}GL_{2n,𝒪_{F⁺_v̄}}, and for dominant λ̃ the lattice 𝒱_λ̃ ⊂ V_λ̃ (defined as for G) is an 𝒪[∏_{v̄|p}G̃(𝒪_{F⁺_v̄})]-module, finite free over 𝒪.
items.note: PA.1: 'Construct integral algebraic coefficient modules over O ... Prove the linkage and weight bounds actually used for degree shifting'; the dictionary (2.2.2) is the bookkeeping behind those weights (Proposition 4.4.1 uses it) but is not named in any stage (flag).

items.name: The Hecke algebras T^S, T^S(K,𝒱), T^S(K,λ), T̃^S, T̃^S(K̃,λ̃) and the map 𝒮 : T̃^S → T^S (2.2.3)
items.statement: For S ⊃ S_p a finite set of finite places of F and K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_F^∞) good with K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) for v ∉ S and K_v ⊂ GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) for v | p: T_v = ℋ(GL_n(F_v), GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪, T^S = ℋ(GL_n^S, K^S) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪, and for an 𝒪[K_S]-module 𝒱 finite free over 𝒪, T^S(K,𝒱) is the image of T^S → End_{𝐃(𝒪)}(RΓ(X_K,𝒱)) (from (2.1.3)); T^S(K,λ) = T^S(K,𝒱_λ). For S ⊃ S_p with S = S^c, S̄ the places of F⁺ below S, and K̃ good with K̃_v̄ = G̃(𝒪_{F⁺_v̄}) for v̄ ∉ S̄ and K̃_v̄ ⊂ G̃(𝒪_{F⁺_v̄}) for v̄ | p (writing G̃^S = G̃^{S̄}, G̃_S = G̃_{S̄}, K̃^S = K̃^{S̄}, K̃_S = K̃_{S̄}): T̃^S = ℋ(G̃^S, K̃^S) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪, T̃^S(K̃,𝒱̃) the image of T̃^S in End_{𝐃(𝒪)}(RΓ(X̃_K̃,𝒱̃)), T̃^S(K̃,λ̃) = T̃^S(K̃,𝒱_λ̃), and (2.2.3) 𝒮 : T̃^S → T^S is induced by (2.1.8). By Lemma 2.1.7 T^S(K,λ) and T̃^S(K̃,λ̃) are finite 𝒪-algebras. Use of the notation T^S(K,λ) (resp. T̃^S(K̃,λ̃)) implies these hypotheses (for T̃^S in particular S = S^c).
items.note: IHG.2: 'For a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex define its finite image algebras'; ALS.3 (Hecke correspondences on complexes); TC.3: 'calculate the Hecke action through the Levi Satake map'. Consistent with PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 ('T^S(K) ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K) is IHG.2's finite image algebra').

items.name: Hecke algebras of equivariant complexes: T^S(K/K′,𝒱), _{K/K′}T^S, T^S(C^•)
items.statement: For K′ ⊂ K normal good with (K′)^S = K^S, R an 𝒪-algebra and 𝒱 an R[K_S]-module finite free over R, T^S(K/K′,𝒱) = T^S(RΓ_{K/K′}(X_{K′},𝒱)) is the image of T^S → End_{𝐃(R[K/K′])}(RΓ_{K/K′}(X_{K′},𝒱)); there are canonical surjections T^S(K/K′,𝒱) → T^S(K′,𝒱) and T^S(K/K′,𝒱) → T^S(K,𝒱), induced by the forgetful functor and by RΓ(K/K′, ?). If K/K′ is abelian, _{K/K′}T^S = T^S ⊗_𝒪 𝒪[K/K′] and _{K/K′}T^S(RΓ_{K/K′}(X_{K′},𝒱)) is its image. For any C^• ∈ 𝐃(R) (resp. 𝐃(R[K/K′])) with an 𝒪-algebra map T^S → End(C^•) (e.g. RΓ(∂X̃_K̃,𝒱_λ̃) for T̃^S), T^S(C^•) (resp. _{K/K′}T^S(C^•)) denotes the image.
items.note: IHG.2 (finite image algebras, 'compare chain, homotopy/derived and cohomology actions'); ALS.6 (finite-level descent, change of level).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.4: nilpotence of the kernel of the derived Hecke action on cohomology
items.statement: Let R be a (possibly non-commutative) ℤ-algebra, C^• ∈ 𝐃(R), T ⊂ End_{𝐃(R)}(C^•) a commutative subring and I = ker(T → End_R(H*(C^•))). If there is d ≥ 0 with H^i(C^•) = 0 for i ∉ [0, d], then I^{d+1} = 0. In particular, if C^• has bounded cohomology then T^S(C^•) → T^S(H*(C^•)) has nilpotent kernel.
items.note: IHG.2: 'Establish the nilpotence bound for the ideal of degree-zero derived endomorphisms acting trivially on all cohomology of a bounded-amplitude object, using the t-structure filtration and composition; transport to Hecke images. Preserve the dependence on amplitude.'

items.name: Change-of-level Hecke maps modulo a nilpotent ideal
items.statement: If K′ ⊂ K is a normal good subgroup with (K′)^S = K^S, then in the diagram T^S(K′,𝒱_λ) ← T^S(K/K′,𝒱_λ) → T^S(K,𝒱_λ) the kernel I of the left arrow satisfies I^{dim_ℝ X + 1} = 0 by Lemma 2.2.4 with R = 𝒪[K/K′] (printed I^{dim_ℝ X} = 0, which holds for n ≥ 2 but can fail for n = 1). Hence, with J ⊂ T^S(K,𝒱_λ) the image of I, there is a canonical T^S-algebra map T^S(K′,𝒱_λ) → T^S(K,𝒱_λ)/J. The integer dim_ℝ X depends only on n and [F:ℚ].
items.note: IHG.2: 'transport to Hecke images. Preserve the dependence on amplitude. A quotient by this nilpotent ideal is not identified with the full algebra.' Used repeatedly (e.g. Theorem 2.3.8, Proposition 2.3.9, §6).

items.name: Unramified Hecke operators T_{v,i} and the Hecke polynomial P_v(X) (2.2.6); P_{v,σ}(X)
items.statement: Fix a uniformizer ϖ_v at each finite place v of F. For 1 ≤ i ≤ n, T_{v,i} = [GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) diag(ϖ_v,…,ϖ_v,1,…,1) GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})] ∈ ℋ(GL_n(F_v), GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})) (ϖ_v appearing i times; = T_{M,v,i} of [NT16, Prop.-Def. 5.3]), and (2.2.6) P_v(X) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} T_{v,i} X^{n−i} ∈ ℋ(GL_n(F_v), GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}))[X] (T_{v,0} = 1; the printed last term lacks the sign (−1)^n), which corresponds to the characteristic polynomial of a Frobenius element on rec^T_{F_v}(π_v) for π_v unramified. For σ ∈ W_{F_v}, P_{v,σ}(X) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i e_{v,i}(σ) X^{n−i} ∈ T_v[X] is the polynomial equal to the characteristic polynomial of σ on rec^T_{F_v}(π_v).
items.note: IHG.3 plans exactly this: 'let T_{v,i} be the characteristic function of K diag(uniformizer repeated i times,1 repeated n−i times) K, with vol(K)=1 ... use the Hecke polynomial P_v(X)=Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} T_{v,i} X^{n−i}' — with the sign (−1)^n that the printed (2.2.6) omits.

items.name: Unramified Hecke operators T̃_{v,i} for G̃ and the Hecke polynomial P̃_v(X) (2.2.7); P̃_{v,σ}(X)
items.statement: For v̄ a place of F⁺ unramified in F, v | v̄ and 1 ≤ i ≤ 2n, T̃_{v,i} ∈ ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄), G̃(𝒪_{F⁺_v̄})) ⊗_ℤ ℤ[q_v̄^{-1}] is the operator T_{G,v,i} of [NT16, Prop.-Def. 5.2], and (2.2.7) P̃_v(X) = Σ_{j=0}^{2n} (−1)^j q_v^{j(j−1)/2} T̃_{v,j} X^{2n−j} (the printed general term omits X^{2n−j}), with last term q_v^{n(2n−1)}T̃_{v,2n}; it corresponds to the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on rec^T_{F_v}(π_v) for π_v the base change of an unramified σ_v̄ of G̃(F⁺_v̄). For σ ∈ W_{F_v}, P̃_{v,σ}(X) = Σ_{i=0}^{2n} (−1)^i ẽ_{v,i}(σ) X^{2n−i} ∈ T̃_v[X] = (ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄), G̃(𝒪_{F⁺_v̄})) ⊗ 𝒪)[X] (printed X^{n−i}) corresponds to the characteristic polynomial of σ.
items.note: AG2.2: 'identify the direct sum attached to a cohomological unitary automorphic representation with the required degree-2n Hecke polynomial'; TC.3: 'Prove polynomial identities relating Levi factors, contragredients and character twists to the ambient Hecke polynomial'; IG.0: 'spherical Hecke operators (CSnc §2.1)'.

items.name: Iwahori-level operators U_{v,i}, U_v, ⟨u⟩ for GL_n, the monoid Δ_p, the character α_λ and the twisted action ·_p on 𝒱_λ
items.statement: For c ≥ b ≥ 0, Iw_v(b,c) ⊂ GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) consists of matrices upper-triangular mod ϖ_v^c and unipotent upper-triangular mod ϖ_v^b; Iw_v = Iw_v(0,1) (standard Iwahori), Iw_{v,1} = Iw_v(1,1); these have Iwahori decompositions w.r.t. B_n. For c ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ i ≤ n: U_{v,i} = [Iw_v(b,c) diag(ϖ_v,…,ϖ_v,1,…,1) Iw_v(b,c)] (i entries ϖ_v), U_v = [Iw_v(b,c) diag(ϖ_v^{n−1},…,ϖ_v,1) Iw_v(b,c)], ⟨u⟩ = [Iw_v(b,c) u Iw_v(b,c)] for u ∈ T_n(𝒪_{F_v}) (depending on ϖ_v and the level). Δ_v = ⊔_{μ∈ℤⁿ₊} Iw_v diag(ϖ_v^{μ₁},…,ϖ_v^{μ_n}) Iw_v. Assume every p-adic place of F⁺ splits in F; Δ_p = ∏_{v∈S_p}Δ_v and for λ ∈ (ℤⁿ)^{Hom(F,E)} the monoid homomorphism α_λ : Δ_p → E^× is α_λ((k_{v,1} diag(ϖ_v^{a_{v,1}},…,ϖ_v^{a_{v,n}}) k_{v,2})_{v∈S_p}) = ∏_{v∈S_p}∏_{τ∈Hom_{ℚ_p}(F_v,E)}∏_{i=1}^n τ(ϖ_v)^{a_{v,i}(w_0^Gλ)_{τ,i}}, w_0^G the longest element of W((Res_{F⁺/ℚ}G)_E, (Res_{F⁺/ℚ}T)_E). For λ dominant, g ·_p x = α_λ(g)^{-1} g·x makes 𝒱_λ an 𝒪[Δ_p]-module (the lattice is preserved because w_0^Gλ is the lowest weight, [Ger19, Def. 2.8, Lem. 2.2]); if K_v = Iw_v(b,c) for all v | p there is a canonical ℋ(G^S,K^S) ⊗_ℤ ℋ(Δ_p,K_p) → End_{𝐃(𝒪)}(RΓ(X_K,𝒱_λ)), so U_{v,i} and U_v act (depending on ϖ_v through ·_p).
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes ... Track positive monoids, normalization'. The α_λ-twisted integral action (Geraghty) is the 'normalization' there; flag that the twist is not named.

items.name: Iwahori-level operators Ũ_{v,i}, Ũ_v, ⟨u⟩ for G̃, the monoid Δ̃_p and the twisted action on 𝒱_λ̃
items.statement: For v̄ split in F and v | v̄: ι_v^{-1}(Iw_v(b,c)) = ι_{v^c}^{-1}(Iw_{v^c}(b,c)) =: Iw̃_v̄(b,c) ⊂ G̃(F⁺_v̄) (Iw inside GL_{2n}); for 1 ≤ i ≤ 2n, Ũ_{v,i} = ι_v^{-1}[Iw_v(b,c) diag(ϖ_v,…,ϖ_v,1,…,1) Iw_v(b,c)] (i entries ϖ_v), Ũ_v = ι_v^{-1}[Iw_v(b,c) diag(ϖ_v^{2n−1},…,ϖ_v,1) Iw_v(b,c)], ⟨u⟩ = [Iw̃_v̄(b,c) u Iw̃_v̄(b,c)] for u ∈ T(𝒪_{F⁺,v̄}). If ϖ_{v^c} = ϖ_v^c then Ũ_{v^c,i} = Ũ_{v,2n−i}Ũ_{v,2n}^{-1} and Ũ_{v^c} = Ũ_vŨ_{v,2n}^{1−2n}. Δ̃_v̄ = ι_v^{-1}(⊔_{μ∈ℤ^{2n}₊} Iw_v diag(ϖ_v^{μ₁},…,ϖ_v^{μ_{2n}}) Iw_v) (independent of v). If every p-adic place of F⁺ splits: Δ̃_p = ∏_{v̄∈S̄_p}Δ̃_v̄ and for λ̃ ∈ (ℤ^{2n})^{Hom(F⁺,E)}, α̃_λ̃((k_{v̄,1}ι_ṽ^{-1}(diag(ϖ_ṽ^{a_{v̄,1}},…,ϖ_ṽ^{a_{v̄,2n}}))k_{v̄,2})_{v̄}) = ∏_{v̄∈S̄_p}∏_{τ∈Hom_{ℚ_p}(F_ṽ,E)}∏_{i=1}^{2n} τ(ϖ_ṽ)^{a_{v̄,i}(w_0^{G̃}λ̃)_{τ,i}} (ṽ ∈ S̃_p as in the definition of 𝒱_λ̃). For λ̃ dominant, g ·_p x = α̃_λ̃(g)^{-1} g·x makes 𝒱_λ̃ an 𝒪[Δ̃_p]-module, and if K̃_v̄ = Iw̃_v̄(b,c) for all v̄ | p there is a canonical ℋ(G̃^S,K̃^S) ⊗_ℤ ℋ(Δ̃_p,K̃_p) → End_{𝐃(𝒪)}(RΓ(X̃_K̃,𝒱_λ̃)); in particular Ũ_{v,i}, Ũ_v act.
items.note: PA.2: 'This layer owns its additional general-rank CM/unitary arithmetic application: construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators'. I checked the relation Ũ_{v^c,i} = Ũ_{v,2n−i}Ũ_{v,2n}^{-1} from ᵗgJ_ng^c = J_n: it holds.

items.name: Pro-ℓ-Iwahori Hecke operators at v ∤ p: Ξ_v, t, t_{v,i}(α), e_{v,i}(α) and P_{v,σ}(X) (2.2.8)
items.statement: Let v ∤ p and I_v ⊂ GL_n(F_v) open compact with Iw_v(1,1) ⊂ I_v ⊂ Iw_v(0,1), so Iw_v(0,1)/I_v is a quotient of (k(v)^×)ⁿ; Ξ_v = (F_v^×)ⁿ/ker((𝒪_{F_v}^×)ⁿ → (k(v)^×)ⁿ → Iw_v(0,1)/I_v). I_v has an Iwahori decomposition w.r.t. B_n = T_nN_n, and for g ∈ Ξ_v, [I_vgI_v] is invertible in ℋ(GL_n(F_v),I_v) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪 ([Fli11, Cor. 3.4]; q_v ∈ 𝒪^×), so Lemma 2.1.13 gives an injective 𝒪-algebra homomorphism t : 𝒪[Ξ_v] → ℋ(GL_n(F_v),I_v) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪 sending positive g to [I_vgI_v] (printed with domain Ξ_v). For α ∈ F_v^×, t_{v,i}(α) is the image under t of q_v^{−⟨λ, ρ + (1−n)/2·det⟩}(1,…,1,α,1,…,1) (α in position i; λ ∈ X_*(T_n) the image of α under Ξ_v → (F_v^×/𝒪_{F_v}^×)ⁿ = X_*(T_n); ρ the half-sum of positive roots); e_{v,i}(α) is the coefficient of (−1)^iX^{n−i} in ∏_{i=1}^n(X − t_{v,i}(α)). For σ ∈ W_{F_v}, t_{v,i}(σ) = t_{v,i}(α) and e_{v,i}(σ) = e_{v,i}(α) where Art_{F_v}(α) = σ|_{F_v^ab}, and (2.2.8) P_{v,σ}(X) = ∏_{i=1}^n(X − t_{v,i}(σ)) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i e_{v,i}(σ) X^{n−i} ∈ ℋ(GL_n(F_v),I_v) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪[X].
items.note: No stage plans Hecke algebras at pro-ℓ-Iwahori level or Flicker's description of their centre (searched 'Iwahori', 'pro-p Iwahori', 'Flicker', 'Bernstein cent'); IHG.3 is spherical only, SR.3's Bernstein centre is for complex representations without these integral operators. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.9: pro-ℓ-Iwahori invariants and the characteristic polynomial of rec^T
items.statement: Let v ∤ p, I_v with Iw_v(1,1) ⊂ I_v ⊂ Iw_v(0,1), and π_v an irreducible admissible Q̄_p[GL_n(F_v)]-module. (1) π_v^{I_v} ≠ 0 iff π_v is isomorphic to an irreducible subquotient of Ind_{B_n(F_v)}^{GL_n(F_v)}χ for a smooth character χ = χ₁ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ χ_n : (F_v^×)ⁿ → Q̄_p^× factoring through (F_v^×)ⁿ → Ξ_v. (2) If π_v^{I_v} ≠ 0, then for every α ∈ F_v^×, e_{v,i}(α) acts on π_v^{I_v} by a scalar e_{v,i}(α, π_v) ∈ Q̄_p (printed Q̄_p^×). (3) If π_v^{I_v} ≠ 0 and (r_v, N_v) = rec^T_{F_v}(π_v), then for every σ ∈ W_{F_v} the characteristic polynomial of r_v(σ) is Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i e_{v,i}(α, π_v) X^{n−i}, where α = Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ|_{F_v^ab}).
items.note: Proof: [Fli11, Thm 2.1, Prop. 4.11, §4]. Not in any stage (see the previous item). AG2.5 plans ramified local–global comparison for characteristic-zero Galois representations, not this Hecke-algebra statement. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Parahoric subgroups 𝔭_v ⊃ 𝔭_{v,1} and 𝔮̃_v at a split place v ∤ p
items.statement: For v ∤ p split over F⁺: 𝔭_v ⊂ GL_{2n}(𝒪_{F_v}) is the parahoric of matrices whose reduction mod ϖ_v is block upper-triangular with blocks of sizes n, 1, …, 1; projection to the lower-right block gives 𝔭_v → B_n(k(v)), and 𝔭_{v,1} = ker(𝔭_v → B_n(k(v)) → T_n(k(v))). For an open compact 𝔮_v with 𝔭_{v,1} ⊂ 𝔮_v ⊂ 𝔭_v, set 𝔭̃_v = ι_v^{-1}(𝔭_v), 𝔭̃_{v,1} = ι_v^{-1}(𝔭_{v,1}), 𝔮̃_v = ι_v^{-1}(𝔮_v) ⊂ G̃(F⁺_v̄). Then 𝔭̃_v ∩ G(F⁺_v̄) = GL_n(𝒪_{F_{v^c}}) × Iw_v, 𝔭̃_{v,1} ∩ G(F⁺_v̄) = GL_n(𝒪_{F_{v^c}}) × Iw_{v,1}, 𝔭̃_v/𝔭̃_{v,1} ≅ (k(v)^×)ⁿ, and 𝔮̃_v has an Iwahori decomposition w.r.t. P = GU.
items.note: No stage names these levels (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 constructs parahoric group schemes in general, not these subgroups or their intersections with the Siegel Levi). They are the Taylor–Wiles/ramified levels of Theorem 2.4.8 and §3. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.10: a strongly positive central element of the Siegel Levi with invertible Hecke operator at level 𝔮̃_v
items.statement: The element g = (ϖ_v^{−c}·1_n, 1_n) ∈ GL_n(F_{v^c}) × GL_n(F_v) = G(F⁺_v̄) is strongly positive, and [𝔮̃_v g 𝔮̃_v] is invertible in ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄), 𝔮̃_v) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪.
items.note: Proof via ι_v: [𝔮_v diag(ϖ_v 1_n, 1_n) 𝔮_v] = [𝔮_v]·[Iw_v(1) diag(ϖ_v 1_n,1_n) Iw_v(1)] with the second factor invertible [Fli11, Cor. 3.4] and commuting with [𝔮_v] [Fli11, Thm 4.5]. Not planned (Bushnell–Kutzko/Flicker material, see Lemma 2.1.13). Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Transferred operators at level 𝔮̃_v: t_{v,i}(σ), e_{v,i}(σ), e_{v^c,i}(σ), P_{v,σ} (2.2.11), P_{v^c,σ} (2.2.12), P̃_{v,σ} and ẽ_{v,i}(σ)
items.statement: Writing 𝔮̃_v ∩ G(F⁺_v̄) = GL_n(𝒪_{F_{v^c}}) × I_v and Ξ_v for the quotient of (F_v^×)ⁿ attached to I_v, Lemma 2.1.13 (with Lemma 2.2.10) gives an injective 𝒪-algebra homomorphism t : ℋ(GL_n(F_{v^c}) × GL_n(F_v), GL_n(𝒪_{F_{v^c}}) × I_v) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪 → ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄), 𝔮̃_v) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪. For σ ∈ W_{F_v}, t_{v,i}(σ) ∈ ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄),𝔮̃_v) ⊗ 𝒪 is the image under t of ‖σ‖_v^{−n} t_{v,i}(σ), e_{v,i}(σ) is the coefficient of (−1)^iX^{n−i} in (2.2.11) P_{v,σ}(X) = ∏_{i=1}^n (X − t_{v,i}(σ)). For σ ∈ W_{F_{v^c}}, e_{v^c,i}(σ) is the image under t of ‖σ‖_v^{i(n−1)} e_{v^c,i}(σ) ∈ ℋ(GL_n(F_{v^c}), GL_n(𝒪_{F_{v^c}})) ⊗ 𝒪, and (2.2.12) P_{v^c,σ}(X) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i e_{v^c,i}(σ) X^{n−i} (printed e_{v,i}(σ)). For σ ∈ W_{F_v}, P̃_{v,σ}(X) = P_{v^c,σ^{−c}}(X)·P_{v,σ}(X) = Σ_{i=0}^{2n} (−1)^i ẽ_{v,i}(σ) X^{2n−i} (printed X^{n−i}) defines ẽ_{v,i}(σ) ∈ ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄),𝔮̃_v) ⊗ 𝒪.
items.note: Not planned (same layer as (2.2.8)). Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.13: the operators ẽ_{v,i}(σ) act by the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of rec^T
items.statement: Let π̃_v̄ be an irreducible admissible Q̄_p[G̃(F⁺_v̄)]-module with π̃_v̄^{𝔮̃_v} ≠ 0, and σ ∈ W_{F_v}. (1) Each ẽ_{v,i}(σ) acts on π̃_v̄^{𝔮̃_v} by a scalar ẽ_{v,i}(σ, π̃_v̄) ∈ Q̄_p. (2) If (r_v, N_v) = rec^T_{F_v}(π̃_v̄ ∘ ι_v^{-1}), the characteristic polynomial of r_v(σ) equals Σ_{i=0}^{2n} (−1)^i ẽ_{v,i}(σ, π̃_v̄) X^{2n−i} (printed X^{n−i}).
items.note: Proof: π̃_v̄ is a subquotient of a tamely ramified principal series; universal unramified twist, Zariski density, [BK98, Thm 7.9] (Jacquet module and t), and the geometrical lemma [Zel80]. SR.2 plans 'the geometric lemma with double-coset indexing' but not this Hecke-operator statement. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.14: when the resultant is a unit, P_{v,φ_v}(r_v(φ_v)) kills monodromy and inertia
items.statement: Fix a Frobenius lift φ_v ∈ W_{F_v} and let Res_v ∈ ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄),𝔮̃_v) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪 be the resultant of P_{v^c,φ_v^{−c}}(X) and P_{v,φ_v}(X). Let π̃_v̄ be an irreducible admissible Q̄_p[G̃(F⁺_v̄)]-module with π̃_v̄^{𝔮̃_v} ≠ 0, (r_v, N_v) = rec^T_{F_v}(π̃_v̄ ∘ ι_v^{-1}), and T_v̄ ⊂ End_{Q̄_p}(π̃_v̄^{𝔮̃_v}) the Q̄_p-subalgebra generated by the images of the e_{v^c,i}(φ_v^{−c}) and e_{v,i}(φ_v). Then for each maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ T_v̄, either Res_v ∈ 𝔪, or Res_v ∉ 𝔪, T_{v̄,𝔪} = T_v̄/𝔪 = Q̄_p, and for all τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}: N_v P_{v,φ_v}(r_v(φ_v)) = 0 and (r_v(τ_v) − 1) P_{v,φ_v}(r_v(φ_v)) = 0 in M_{2n}(T_v̄/𝔪) = M_{2n}(Q̄_p).
items.note: Proof uses rec^T(St_m) = Sp_m, the geometrical lemma, [Tho21, Prop. 2.2] and Lemma 2.2.13; This is the local engine of Theorem 3.1.1 at Taylor–Wiles/ramified places; AG2.5 ('a bound on monodromy') plans only characteristic-zero global comparisons. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Corollary 2.2.15: Res_v^{(2n)!}(ρ(τ_v) − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(ρ(φ_v)) = 0
items.statement: Let π̃_v̄ be an irreducible admissible Q̄_p[G̃(F⁺_v̄)]-module with π̃_v̄^{𝔮̃_v} ≠ 0, and ρ : G_{F_v} → GL_{2n}(Q̄_p) continuous with WD(ρ)^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{F_v}(π̃_v̄ ∘ ι_v^{-1}); let T_v̄ be as in Proposition 2.2.14. Then for all τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}, Res_v^{(2n)!}(ρ(τ_v) − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(ρ(φ_v)) = 0 in M_{2n}(Q̄_p) ⊗_{Q̄_p} T_v̄ = M_{2n}(T_v̄).
items.note: Not planned; see Proposition 2.2.14. The justification of the exponent (2n)! is loose but the statement holds. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.16: unramified Satake transform of P̃_v(X) to the Siegel Levi
items.statement: Convention: for f(X) of degree d with unit constant term a₀, f^∨(X) = a₀^{-1}X^d f(X^{-1}). Let v be a place of F unramified over the place v̄ of F⁺ and 𝒮 : ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄), G̃(𝒪_{F⁺_v̄})) → ℋ(G(F⁺_v̄), G(𝒪_{F⁺_v̄})) the homomorphism of (2.1.8). Then 𝒮(P̃_v(X)) = P_v(X) · q_v^{n(2n−1)} P_{v^c}^∨(q_v^{1−2n}X).
items.note: Proof: [NT16, Prop.-Def. 5.3]. TC.3: 'calculate the Hecke action through the Levi Satake map. Prove polynomial identities relating Levi factors, contragredients and character twists to the ambient Hecke polynomial'; ALS.4: 'compare its Hecke action with parabolic induction and Satake transforms, including modulus and Tate shifts'.

items.name: Ramified split case: levels Ĩ_v̄ with Iw̃_v̄(1,1) ⊂ Ĩ_v̄ ⊂ Iw̃_v̄(0,1), the polynomial P̃_{v,σ}(X) (2.2.17) and the invertible strongly positive element
items.statement: For v split over v̄ and Ĩ_v̄ ⊂ G̃(F⁺_v̄) with Iw̃_v̄(1,1) ⊂ Ĩ_v̄ ⊂ Iw̃_v̄(0,1), Ĩ_v̄ ∩ G(F⁺_v̄) = I_{v^c} × I_v with I_{v^c} ⊂ GL_n(F_{v^c}), I_v ⊂ GL_n(F_v) open compact. For σ ∈ W_{F_v}, (2.2.17) P̃_{v,σ}(X) = ∏_{i=1}^{2n}(X − ι_v^{-1}(t_{v,i}(σ))) = Σ_{i=0}^{2n}(−1)^i ι_v^{-1}(e_{v,i}(σ)) X^{2n−i} ∈ ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄), Ĩ_v̄) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪[X] (the GL_{2n} operators of (2.2.8) at level ι_v(Ĩ_v̄)). Ĩ_v̄ has an Iwahori decomposition w.r.t. P, and (ϖ_{v^c}^{-1}·1_n, 1_n) ∈ G(F⁺_v̄) = GL_n(F_{v^c}) × GL_n(F_v) is strongly positive with [Ĩ_v̄(ϖ_{v^c}^{-1}·1_n, 1_n)Ĩ_v̄] invertible in ℋ(G̃(F⁺_v̄), Ĩ_v̄) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪, so Lemma 2.1.13 applies.
items.note: Not planned (same ramified layer). Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.18: Satake transform of P̃_{v,σ}(X) at Iwahori-type level
items.statement: For v split over v̄, Ĩ_v̄ as above and any σ ∈ W_{F_v}: 𝒮(P̃_{v,σ}(X)) = P_{v,σ}(X) · ‖σ‖_v^{n(1−2n)} P_{v^c,σ^{−c}}(‖σ‖_v^{2n−1}X).
items.note: Calculation with 𝒮∘t = |δ_P|^{-1} (§2.1.9); I checked the monic normalization and the v^c-twist ‖σ‖^{−i(2n−1)} against the definitions. TC.3 plans only the unramified Levi-Satake identity; no stage covers the ramified one. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.19: Satake transform at level 𝔮̃_v
items.statement: For v split over v̄ and 𝔮̃_v ⊂ G̃(F⁺_v̄) open compact with 𝔭̃_{v,1} ⊂ 𝔮̃_v ⊂ 𝔭̃_v and 𝔮̃_v ∩ G(F⁺_v̄) = GL_n(𝒪_{F_{v^c}}) × I_v, and for any σ ∈ W_{F_v}: 𝒮(P_{v,σ}(X)) = P_{v,σ}(X) and 𝒮(P_{v^c,σ^{−c}}(X)) = ‖σ‖_v^{n(1−2n)} P_{v^c,σ^{−c}}(‖σ‖_v^{2n−1}X).
items.note: Proved as Proposition 2.2.18. Not planned. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Duality anti-involutions ι, ι̃, their effect on Hecke polynomials, and dual maximal ideals 𝔪^∨
items.statement: Let S = S^c. ι : ℋ(G^S,K^S) → ℋ(G^S,K^S) and ι̃ : ℋ(G̃^S,K̃^S) → ℋ(G̃^S,K̃^S) are the anti-involutions [K^SgK^S] ↦ [K^Sg^{-1}K^S], [K̃^SgK̃^S] ↦ [K̃^Sg^{-1}K̃^S]; on the commutative T^S, T̃^S they are involutions. For v ∉ S: ι̃(P̃_v(X)) = q_v^{2n(2n−1)} P̃_v^∨(q_v^{1−2n}X) = P̃_{v^c}(X) and ι(P_v(X)) = q_v^{n(n−1)} P_v^∨(q_v^{1−n}X). For a maximal ideal 𝔪̃ ⊂ T̃^S (resp. 𝔪 ⊂ T^S) with residue field finite over k: 𝔪̃^∨ = ι̃(𝔪̃) (printed ι̃(𝔪)), 𝔪^∨ = ι(𝔪). D̃ = dim_ℝ X̃, D = dim_ℝ X.
items.note: ALS.5:finite-level-duality: 'Construct evaluation, relative/compact-support pairings, and restriction/corestriction and Hecke adjoint formulas on the complexes'; IHG.3: 'Every other convention is connected by an explicit conversion theorem, including geometric Frobenius/inverse roots'. I checked ι(P_v) = q_v^{n(n−1)}P_v^∨(q_v^{1−n}X) with ι(T_{v,i}) = T_{v,n}^{-1}T_{v,n−i}; it needs the constant term (−1)^n q_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{v,n} (cf. the (2.2.6) misprint).

items.name: Proposition 2.2.21: Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality
items.statement: Let R = 𝒪 or 𝒪/ϖ^m (m ≥ 1), K̃ ⊂ G̃(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) (resp. K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_F^∞)) a good subgroup, and 𝒱 an R[K̃_S]-module (resp. R[K_S]-module), finite free over R, with 𝒱^∨ = Hom(𝒱, R). Then there is an isomorphism R Hom_R(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, 𝒱), R) ≅ RΓ(X̃_K̃, 𝒱^∨)[D̃] (resp. R Hom_R(RΓ_c(X_K, 𝒱), R) ≅ RΓ(X_K, 𝒱^∨)[D]) in 𝐃(R), equivariant for ℋ(G̃^S, K̃^S) (resp. ℋ(G^S, K^S)) acting through ι̃^t (resp. ι^t) on the left and in the usual way on the right.
items.note: Proof: [NT16, Prop. 3.7]. ALS.5:finite-level-duality: 'construct Poincaré–Lefschetz/Verdier duality for perfect coefficient complexes, keeping derived Hom and orientation twists ... Hecke adjoint formulas on the complexes'. Same routing as PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 Prop. 13.6.

items.name: Corollary 2.2.22: duality of Hecke algebras and of supports
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 2.2.21, ι̃ (resp. ι) descends to an isomorphism of R-algebras T̃^S(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, 𝒱)) ≅ T̃^S(RΓ(X̃_K̃, 𝒱^∨)) (resp. T^S(RΓ_c(X_K, 𝒱)) ≅ T^S(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱^∨))). In particular if 𝔪̃ (resp. 𝔪) is a maximal ideal of T̃^S (resp. T^S) in the support of H*_c(X̃_K̃, 𝒱) (resp. H*_c(X_K, 𝒱)), then 𝔪̃^∨ (resp. 𝔪^∨) is in the support of H*(X̃_K̃, 𝒱^∨) (resp. H*(X_K, 𝒱^∨)).
items.note: ALS.5:finite-level-duality (Hecke adjoint formulas) with IHG.2's image algebras ('support and annihilator lemmas').

items.name: Twisting of Hecke algebras by a character: f_ψ and 𝔪(ψ)
items.statement: Let K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_F^∞) be good and ψ : G_F → 𝒪^× continuous with ψ∘Art_{F_v} trivial on det(K_v) for all v ∉ S. f_ψ : ℋ(G^S,K^S) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪 → ℋ(G^S,K^S) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪, f_ψ(f)(g) = ψ(Art_F(det g))^{-1} f(g), is an 𝒪-algebra isomorphism (inverse f_{ψ^{-1}}). If K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) for all v ∉ S (so ψ is unramified outside S and ℋ(G^S,K^S) ⊗ 𝒪 = T^S), then f_ψ(T_{v,i}) = ψ(Frob_v)^{−i}T_{v,i} for all v ∉ S. For 𝔪 ⊂ T^S maximal with residue field finite over k, 𝔪(ψ) = f_ψ(𝔪).
items.note: No stage plans twisting of arithmetic cohomology or Hecke algebras by characters of det (searched 'twist' in ALS/IHG/TC/PA; only Galois-side twists in R01.1, AG2.2). Route: a source of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.0 levels, ALS.3 Hecke correspondences, ALS.5 comparison).

items.name: Proposition 2.2.23: twisting RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ) by a character
items.statement: Let K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_F^∞) be good and S ⊃ S_p. Let ψ : G_F → 𝒪^× be continuous with (1) ψ∘Art_{F_v} trivial on det(K_v) for each finite v ∤ p, and (2) some m = (m_τ) ∈ ℤ^{Hom(F,E)} with ψ(Art_{F_v}(k)) = ∏_{τ∈Hom_{ℚ_p}(F_v,E)} τ(k)^{−m_τ} for all v | p and k ∈ det(K_v). Let μ ∈ (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,E)}, μ_τ = (m_τ,…,m_τ). Then for any λ ∈ (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,E)} there is an isomorphism RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ) ≅ RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_{λ+μ}) in 𝐃(𝒪), equivariant for ℋ(G^S,K^S) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪 acting in the usual way on the left and through f_ψ on the right.
items.note: Proof: ψ gives a class in H⁰(X_K,𝒱_μ); cup product 𝒱_λ → 𝒱_λ ⊗ 𝒱_μ ≅ 𝒱_{λ+μ}, and equivariance is computed in 𝐃(ℋ(G^S,K^S) ⊗ 𝒪) via 𝒜 = Ind_{GL_n(F)}^{GL_n(𝔸_F^∞)}𝒪 and the twist 𝒱_μ(ψ^{-1,S}). Not planned (see f_ψ). Route: a source of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.0 levels, ALS.3 Hecke correspondences, ALS.5 comparison).

items.name: Corollary 2.2.24: twisting isomorphism of Hecke algebras T^S(K,λ) ≅ T^S(K,λ+μ)
items.statement: Suppose S ⊃ S_p and K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_F^∞) is good with K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) for all v ∉ S; let ψ, m and μ be as in Proposition 2.2.23 (conditions (1) and (2)). Then for any λ ∈ (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,E)}, f_ψ descends to an isomorphism T^S(K,λ) ≅ T^S(K,λ+μ). In particular, if 𝔪 ⊂ T^S is in the support of H*(X_K, 𝒱_λ), then 𝔪(ψ) is in the support of H*(X_K, 𝒱_{λ+μ}).
items.note: Immediate from Proposition 2.2.23. Not planned. Route: a source of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.0 levels, ALS.3 Hecke correspondences, ALS.5 comparison).

items.name: Weight of an automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F)
items.statement: For π an irreducible admissible representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) and λ ∈ (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,ℂ)}, π is of weight λ if the infinitesimal character of π_∞ equals that of V_λ^∨.
items.note: Repeats the §1.2 definition of 'regular algebraic of weight ξ'. AG2.0 / AF.4 as there.

items.name: Theorem 2.3.2 (Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne): Galois representations for regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n over CM fields
items.statement: Let λ ∈ (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,ℂ)} and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ (F imaginary CM). Then for any isomorphism ι : Q̄_p → ℂ there is a continuous semisimple r_ι(π) : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) such that for each prime l ≠ p above which both F and π are unramified and each place v | l of F, r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified and the characteristic polynomial of r_ι(π)(Frob_v) equals the image of P_v(X) in Q̄_p[X] under the homomorphism T_v → Q̄_p attached to ι^{-1}π_v.
items.note: Proof: the main theorem of [HLTT16]. AG2.4: 'Deliver the characteristic-zero semisimple system of HLTT Theorem 7.13/Corollary 7.14; do not promote its good-prime conclusion to full local–global compatibility'; AG2.5: 'Prove good-prime unramifiedness and the full characteristic-polynomial identity'. Same routing as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (HLTT at AG2.4/AG2.5/AG2.6).

items.name: Theorem 2.3.3 (1)–(3): base change of cohomological cuspidal representations of G̃ to GL_{2n}(𝔸_F)
items.statement: Suppose F contains an imaginary quadratic field. Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of G̃(𝔸_{F⁺}) and ξ an irreducible algebraic representation of G̃_ℂ such that π is ξ-cohomological. Then there are a partition 2n = n₁ + ⋯ + n_r and discrete conjugate self-dual automorphic representations Π₁, …, Π_r of GL_{n₁}(𝔸_F), …, GL_{n_r}(𝔸_F) such that, with Π = Π₁ ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Π_r: (1) if l is unramified in F and π is unramified above l, then Π is unramified above l and for each v | l of F over v̄ of F⁺, Π_v and π_v̄ are related by unramified base change; (2) if F₀ ⊂ F is imaginary quadratic and l′ splits in F₀, then for each v | l′ over v̄, Π_v and π_v̄ correspond under ι_v : G̃(F⁺_v̄) ≅ GL_{2n}(F_v); (3) the infinitesimal character of Π equals that of the representation (ξ ⊗ ξ)^∨ of GL_{2n}(F ⊗_ℚ ℂ).
items.note: Proof: Shin's base change [Shi14] for the similitude group G̃′ (1 → Res_{F⁺/ℚ}G̃ → G̃′ → 𝔾_m → 1), after extending π to π′ via a type-A₀ Hecke character ψ of F₀ matching ω_π on (𝔸_{F₀}^×)^{c=1} and unramified at l^aux ([HT01, Thm VI.2.9]); strong multiplicity one to vary l^aux. AG2.2: 'This stage supplies the characteristic-zero unitary system interface used in ACC+ §2.3.3' and 'Apply stable unitary base change and endoscopic character identities from ET.4/ET.7a'; ET.7a: 'construct the unitary-to-GL_m cohomological base-change character identities at the stated split/unramified places and infinity'.

items.name: Theorem 2.3.3 (a)–(c): the Galois representation r_ι(π) of a cohomological cuspidal π of G̃
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 2.3.3, for any isomorphism ι : Q̄_p → ℂ there is a continuous semisimple r_ι(π) : G_F → GL_{2n}(Q̄_p) with: (a) for each prime l ≠ p unramified in F above which π is unramified and each v | l of F, r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified and the characteristic polynomial of r_ι(π)(Frob_v) equals the image of P̃_v(X) in Q̄_p[X]; (b) for each v | p, r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is de Rham and for each τ : F ↪ Q̄_p, HT_τ(r_ι(π)) = {λ̃_{τ,1} + 2n − 1, λ̃_{τ,2} + 2n − 2, …, λ̃_{τ,2n}}, where λ̃ ∈ (ℤ^{2n}₊)^{Hom(F,Q̄_p)} is the highest weight of the representation ι^{-1}(ξ ⊗ ξ) of GL_{2n} over Q̄_p (printed ι^{-1}(ξ ⊗ ξ)^∨; with (3) as printed, one of the two carries a stray dual); (c) if F₀ ⊂ F is imaginary quadratic and l splits in F₀, then for each v | l over v̄, WD(r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{F_v}(ι^{-1}π_v̄ ∘ ι_v^{-1}) (printed rec^T_{F_v}(π_v̄ ∘ ι_v)).
items.note: Deduced from Π (e.g. [Car14]). AG2.2 (unitary discrete-parameter sums with 'the required degree-2n Hecke polynomial'); AG2.5: 'Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne equality retaining N' for the polarized branch; AG2.6: 'Calculate the labelled Hodge–Tate multiset from the algebraic highest weight, respecting the dual convention. Prove de Rham'. Parts (b) and (c) have convention slips.

items.name: Theorem 2.3.5: residual Galois representations for maximal ideals of T^S(K, λ) (Scholze)
items.statement: Let S be a finite set of finite places of F containing the p-adic places, and 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) a maximal ideal. Suppose S = S^c and, for every finite place v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or there is an imaginary quadratic F₀ ⊂ F in which l splits (achievable by enlarging S). Then there is a continuous semisimple ρ̄_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K,λ)/𝔪) such that for each finite v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of ρ̄_𝔪(Frob_v) equals the image of P_v(X) in (T^S(K,λ)/𝔪)[X].
items.note: Proof: [Sch15, Cor. 5.4.3] over F̄_p (unconditional under the S-condition via Theorem 2.3.3 and [Sch15, Rem. 5.4.6]), then Chebotarev, Brauer–Nesbitt and Br(finite field) = 0 [DS74, Lem. 6.13] to descend to T^S(K,λ)/𝔪. TC.3: 'Build the abstract factor-separation lemma ... At the arithmetic point of use, ... only the matching CM/unitary instance consumes AG2's constructed characteristic-zero package'; TC.4: 'all four routes from a finite-level class to Hecke characteristic polynomials commute after the quantified quotient'; IHG.5 (determinant from a quantified geometric comparison); IHG.1 ('reconstruction over algebraically closed fields up to semisimplification'); R01.5 (coefficient descent). Caveat: TC's summary says it is 'not an additional requirement to formalize [Scholze's] final Galois-representation theorem'; PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 routed the same statement as planned (TC.4, IHG.5), PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 treated analogous statements as missing.

items.name: Definition 2.3.6: maximal ideals of Galois type and non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: A maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ T^S is of Galois type if its residue field is a finite extension of k and there is a continuous semisimple ρ̄_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S/𝔪) such that for each finite v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of ρ̄_𝔪(Frob_v) equals the image of P_v(X) in (T^S/𝔪)[X]. 𝔪 is non-Eisenstein if it is of Galois type and ρ̄_𝔪 is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: No stage defines Galois type or non-Eisenstein for GL_n Hecke algebras (ALS.4: 'the phrase non-Eisenstein alone is not a proof of vanishing'; IG.6 warns about it); consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/non-eisenstein (GL(n)) and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 Def. 6.11, both missing. R14.3/R19.6 plan only the GL₂ notion. Route: a source of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.5 (specialization of Hecke-valued determinants to residual semisimple representations).

items.name: Galois type is preserved by duality and twisting: ρ̄_{𝔪^∨} ≅ ρ̄_𝔪^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−n}, ρ̄_{𝔪(ψ)} ≅ ρ̄_𝔪 ⊗ ψ̄
items.statement: Theorem 2.3.5 says that, under its condition on S, every maximal ideal of T^S in the support of H*(X_K, 𝒱_λ) is of Galois type. If 𝔪 ⊂ T^S is of Galois type, so is 𝔪^∨, with ρ̄_{𝔪^∨} ≅ ρ̄_𝔪^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−n}; hence 𝔪 non-Eisenstein ⇒ 𝔪^∨ non-Eisenstein. If ψ : G_{F,S} → 𝒪^× is continuous and 𝔪 is of Galois type, so is 𝔪(ψ), with ρ̄_{𝔪(ψ)} ≅ ρ̄_𝔪 ⊗ ψ̄; hence 𝔪 non-Eisenstein ⇒ 𝔪(ψ) non-Eisenstein.
items.note: Follows from ι(P_v) = q_v^{n(n−1)}P_v^∨(q_v^{1−n}X) (roots q_v^{n−1}α_i^{-1} = ε^{1−n}(Frob_v)α_i^{-1}) and f_ψ(T_{v,i}) = ψ(Frob_v)^{−i}T_{v,i}; I checked both. Not planned because Definition 2.3.6, ι on T^S and f_ψ are not (IHG.3's conversion theorems would cover the polynomial identity). Route: a source of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.5 (specialization of Hecke-valued determinants to residual semisimple representations).

items.name: Theorem 2.3.7: Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations modulo a nilpotent ideal (Scholze)
items.statement: Let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be a maximal ideal, and suppose S = S^c and that for every finite place v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic F₀ ⊂ F. Suppose ρ̄_𝔪 is absolutely irreducible. Then there are an integer N ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F:ℚ], an ideal I ⊂ T^S(K,λ) with I^N = 0, and a continuous homomorphism ρ_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K,λ)_𝔪/I) such that for each finite v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of ρ_𝔪(Frob_v) equals the image of P_v(X) in (T^S(K,λ)_𝔪/I)[X].
items.note: Proof: [Sch15, Cor. 5.4.4]. TC.2: 'Export a quantified nilpotent ideal and compatible quotient maps'; TC.3: 'Include the case of nilpotent coefficient quotients'; IHG.5: 'theorem schemas which take an actual geometric Hecke comparison with a quantified nilpotent error ideal and produce the determinant in the appropriate quotient'. Same caveat as Theorem 2.3.5 about TC's disclaimer of Scholze's final theorem; BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 routed it to TC.4/IHG.5.

items.name: Theorem 2.3.8: residual representations for maximal ideals of T̃^S(K̃, λ̃)
items.statement: Let 𝔪̃ ⊂ T̃^S(K̃, λ̃) be a maximal ideal (so S = S^c), and suppose that for every finite place v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic F₀ ⊂ F. Then there is a continuous semisimple ρ̄_𝔪̃ : G_{F,S} → GL_{2n}(T̃^S(K̃,λ̃)/𝔪̃) such that for each finite v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of ρ̄_𝔪̃(Frob_v) equals the image of P̃_v(X) in (T̃^S(K̃,λ̃)/𝔪̃)[X].
items.note: Proof: [NT16, Thm 5.7] gives a 2n-dimensional determinant valued in T̃^S(RΓ(X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ)) when K̃ is small (K̃_q inside the principal congruence subgroup of level q, or 2q if q = 2, for some q ≠ p); in general two auxiliary odd primes q₁ ≠ q₂ prime to S, the diagram T̃^{S₁}(K̃₁) ← T̃^{S₁}(K̃/K̃₁) ↠ T̃^{S₁}(K̃) ↪ T̃^S(K̃), Chebotarev and [Che14, Lem. 1.12, Thm A], then descent as in Theorem 2.3.5.
