TC.2/TC.4 (Scholze's torsion comparison for the Shimura tower, 'quantified nilpotent ideal'); IHG.4: 'Construct compatible determinants over finite coefficient quotients from a dense family of classical Hecke systems ... Prove uniqueness from Frobenius density'; IHG.1 (reconstruction).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.9: 2n-dimensional determinant valued in T̃^S(K̃, λ̃)/I with I^{2 dim_ℝ X̃} = 0
items.statement: Suppose S = S^c and that for every finite place v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic F₀ ⊂ F. Then there are an ideal I ⊂ T̃^S(K̃, λ̃) with I^{2 dim_ℝ X̃} = 0 and a 2n-dimensional group determinant D̃ of G_{F,S} valued in T̃^S(K̃, λ̃)/I such that for each finite v ∉ S, D̃(X − Frob_v) equals the image of P̃_v(X) in (T̃^S(K̃, λ̃)/I)[X]. (If K̃ is small one can take I = 0.)
items.note: Proof: [NT16, Thm 5.7] and T̃^S(K̃,λ̃) ≅ lim_m T̃^S(RΓ(X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m)) when K̃ is small; in general auxiliary primes q₁, q₂ with kernels J_i, J_i^{dim_ℝ X̃} = 0 by Lemma 2.2.4 (cohomology of X̃_{K̃_i} vanishes outside [0, dim_ℝ X̃ − 1]), I = (I₁, I₂). IHG.2 (nilpotence bound), IHG.4/IHG.5 (determinants modulo a quantified nilpotent ideal), TC.2/TC.4 (geometric comparison).

items.name: Decomposed level, strata of the Borel–Serre boundary of X̃_K̃ and their localized cohomology (set-up of §2.4.1)
items.statement: Let K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}) be a good subgroup decomposed with respect to the Siegel Levi decomposition P = GU (K̃_P = K̃_U ⋊ K̃_G), and put K = K̃ ∩ G(A^∞_{F⁺}) (a good subgroup of GL_n(A_F^∞)) and K_U = K̃ ∩ U(A^∞_{F⁺}). Let S = S^c, let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal and let 𝔪̃ = 𝒮*(𝔪) ⊂ T̃^S be its pullback under the unnormalized Satake map 𝒮 = r_G ∘ r_P : T̃^S → T^S of (2.2.3). The boundary ∂X̃_K̃ = X̄̃_K̃ − X̃_K̃ of the Borel–Serre compactification carries a G̃(A^∞_{F⁺})-equivariant stratification indexed by the standard parabolic subgroups Q ⊇ B of G̃ [NT16 §3.1.2, Lem. 3.10]; the stratum labelled by Q is X̃^Q_K̃ = Q(F⁺)\(X^Q × G̃(A^∞_{F⁺})/K̃). For every λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F⁺,E)} the formalism of §2.1.2 gives a homomorphism T̃^S → End_{D(O)}(RΓ(X̃^Q_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)), hence the localization RΓ(X̃^Q_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃, which is non-zero in D(O) iff 𝔪̃ is in the support of H*(X̃^Q_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃).
items.note: ALS.2: 'Construct rational parabolic boundary components …', 'Prove boundary strata are fibrations with nilmanifold fibers over Levi arithmetic quotients', 'Build a finite stratification filtration'; ALS.3: Hecke correspondences with 'compatibility with cup products, compact support and boundary restriction'; ALS.4: 'compatibility with localization at a Hecke ideal'. PA's matrix routes §2.4 to ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ('boundary filtration'). The decomposed-level notion and r_P, r_M, 𝒮 are §2.1.2.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.2 (non-Eisenstein localization of the boundary sees only the Siegel stratum)
items.statement: Let K̃, K be as in §2.4.1 (K̃ good, decomposed with respect to P = GU; S = S^c), let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, 𝔪̃ = 𝒮*(𝔪) ⊂ T̃^S, and λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F⁺,E)}. Then there is a natural T̃^S-equivariant isomorphism RΓ(X̃^P_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ ≅ RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ in D(O). More precisely RΓ_c(X̃^Q_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ = 0 for every standard proper parabolic Q ≠ P, so RΓ(∂X̃_K̃ ∖ X̃^P_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ = 0, and the natural maps RΓ_c(X̃^P_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ → RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ and RΓ_c(X̃^P_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ → RΓ(X̃^P_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃ are isomorphisms.
items.note: ALS.4: 'Describe conditions under which boundary localization vanishes or admits a useful summand by an actual eigenvalue argument'; PA.0: 'Prove … boundary localization compatibilities. Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument'. Proof: enlarge S to satisfy Theorem 2.3.5's condition; excision triangles for X̃^P_K̃ ⊂ ∂X̃_K̃ (P maximal, so the embedding is open) and for X̃^P_K̃ in its closure; derived Nakayama for perfect complexes (C = 0 iff C ⊗^L_O k = 0); Poincaré duality on strata [NT16 Prop. 3.7]; then items 77–78 (boundary Galois representations; Levi reduction). The isomorphism is induced by G̃(A^∞_{F⁺})-equivariant maps, so it is equivariant for all of H(G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}), K̃) ⊗ O, which Theorem 2.4.8's proof uses although only T̃^S-equivariance is stated (see issues). Cited later by PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-24/4 (routed there to IG.7, a different statement).

items.name: Residual Galois representations attached to boundary strata of G̃ (formula (2.4.3)); non-Siegel strata are Eisenstein
items.statement: Assume S satisfies the condition of Theorem 2.3.5. The standard F⁺-rational Levi subgroups of G̃ are the block-diagonal subgroups M ≅ Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{n_1} × ⋯ × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{n_r} × G̃_{n−s} attached to 2n = n_1 + ⋯ + n_r + 2(n−s) + n_r + ⋯ + n_1 (for proper Q: r ≥ 1, n_i ≥ 1, s = Σ n_i ∈ {1, …, n}). Let K_M = K_1 × ⋯ × K_r × K̃_s be good (K_i ⊂ GL_{n_i}(A_F^∞), K̃_s ⊂ G̃_{n−s}(A^∞_{F⁺})) with K_M^S = K̃_M^S, and let 𝔪′ ⊂ T^S_M be a maximal ideal in the support of H*(X^M_{K_M}, k), identified (after enlarging k; Künneth) with (𝔪_1, …, 𝔪_r, 𝔪̃_s) under T^S_M ≅ T^S_{GL_{n_1}} ⊗_O ⋯ ⊗_O T^S_{GL_{n_r}} ⊗_O T^S_{G̃_{n−s}}, all of residue field k. With ρ̄_{𝔪_i} : G_{F,S} → GL_{n_i}(k) (Theorem 2.3.5, char. poly of Frob_v = P^i_v mod 𝔪_i) and ρ̄_{𝔪̃_s} : G_{F,S} → GL_{2(n−s)}(k) (Theorem 2.3.8, char. poly P̃^s_v mod 𝔪̃_s), the semisimple representation ρ̄_{𝒮*(𝔪′)} = ⊕_{i=1}^r (ρ̄_{𝔪_i} ⊗ ε^{n_1+⋯+n_i−2n} ⊕ ρ̄_{𝔪_i}^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−(n_1+⋯+n_i)}) ⊕ ρ̄_{𝔪̃_s} ⊗ ε^{−s} : G_{F,S} → GL_{2n}(T̃^S/𝒮*(𝔪′)) has characteristic polynomial of Frob_v equal to P̃_v(X) mod 𝒮^{G̃,*}_M(𝔪′) for all v ∉ S (computation of 𝒮^{G̃}_M(P̃_v), cf. [NT16 Prop.-Def. 5.3]). Hence every maximal ideal 𝔪̃′ ⊂ T̃^S in the support of RΓ(X̃^Q_K̃, k) has such a ρ̄_{𝔪̃′}, of the form (2.4.3) ρ̄_{𝔪̃′} = ⊕_i ρ̄′_i ⊕ ρ̄′(n−s) ⊕ ⊕_i (ρ̄′_i)^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n} with dim ρ̄′_i = n_i, dim ρ̄′(n−s) = 2n − 2s (printed without the twist ε^{1−2n}). Since non-Eisensteinness gives ρ̄_𝔪̃ = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_1, ρ̄_2 absolutely irreducible of dimension n (= ρ̄_𝔪 ⊕ ρ̄_𝔪^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n} by Proposition 2.2.16), RΓ(X̃^Q_K̃, k)_𝔪̃ = 0 unless (r, s) = (1, n), i.e. Q = P.
items.locator: §2.4.1, proof of Theorem 2.4.2 and equation (2.4.3), pp. 942–945
items.note: TC.3: 'For the symplectic/unitary parabolics whose Levi contains a restriction of scalars of GL_n, identify the boundary fibration and calculate the Hecke action through the Levi Satake map. Prove polynomial identities relating Levi factors, contragredients and character twists to the ambient Hecke polynomial'; ALS.4: 'compare its Hecke action with parabolic induction and Satake transforms, including modulus and Tate shifts'. The paper omits the Satake computation. The printed twist formula is correct if GL_{n_i} is the i-th upper-left block; §2.2.1 identifies the Siegel Levi via the lower-right block (see issues). Only the count of Jordan–Hölder factors is used.

items.name: Cohomology of a boundary stratum via the Levi: pullback along r_Q and r_M, and eigensystems of boundary strata as Satake pullbacks
items.statement: Let Q = M ⋉ N be a standard proper parabolic of G̃, T^S_Q = H(Q^S, K̃^S_Q) ⊗_Z O, T^S_M = H(M^S, K̃^S_M) ⊗_Z O, r_Q : T̃^S → T^S_Q (restriction to Q), r_M : T^S_Q → T^S_M (integration along N), 𝒮^{G̃}_M = r_M ∘ r_Q. (i) Writing G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}) = ⊔_{i} Q(A^∞_{F⁺}) g_i K̃ (Iwasawa decomposition away from S) and K_{Q,i} = Q(A^∞_{F⁺}) ∩ g_i K̃ g_i^{−1}, there is an isomorphism RΓ(X̃^Q_K̃, k) ≅ ⊕_i r_Q^* RΓ(X^Q_{K_{Q,i}}, k) in D(T̃^S) [NT16 (4.2)–(4.3)]. (ii) For a neat compact open K_Q ⊂ Q(A^∞_{F⁺}) with image K_M ⊂ M(A^∞_{F⁺}) and K_N = K_Q ∩ N(A^∞_{F⁺}), let 𝒲 be the object of the derived category of sheaves on X^M_{K_M} attached to RΓ(K_{N,S}, k) ∈ D(k[K_{M,S}]); then RΓ(X^Q_{K_Q}, k) ≅ r_M^* RΓ(X^M_{K_M}, 𝒲) in D(T^S_Q) [NT16 pp. 56–58]. (iii) Consequently (Hochschild–Serre, shrinking K_{M,S} to trivialize the local systems 𝒲^i attached to H^i(K_{N,S}, k), as in [NT16 Lem. 4.3]), for every maximal ideal 𝔪̃′ ⊂ T̃^S in the support of H*(X̃^Q_K̃, k) there are a good K̃′_M ⊂ K̃_M with (K̃′_M)^S = K̃^S_M and a maximal ideal 𝔪′ ⊂ T^S_M in the support of H*(X^M_{K̃′_M}, k) with 𝔪̃′ = 𝒮^{G̃,*}_M(𝔪′).
items.note: ALS.2: 'boundary strata are fibrations with nilmanifold fibers over Levi arithmetic quotients; retain nontrivial monodromy of their cohomology'; ALS.4: 'Develop the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for each unipotent/Levi stratum and compare its Hecke action with parabolic induction and Satake transforms'. The paper only outlines this, deferring to [NT16 Thm. 4.2, Lem. 4.3]. The printed proof uses r both for the number of double cosets in (i) and for the number of GL-blocks of M.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.4 (𝒮 descends to boundary and GL_n Hecke algebras with coefficients)
items.statement: Let K̃ be as in §2.4.1 (good, decomposed with respect to P = GU; K = K̃ ∩ G(A^∞_{F⁺})), let λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} be dominant with image λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n})^{Hom(F⁺,E)} (under (2.2.2)) G̃-dominant, let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be non-Eisenstein and 𝔪̃ = 𝒮*(𝔪) ⊂ T̃^S. Then 𝒮 : T̃^S → T^S descends to a homomorphism T̃^S(RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃) → T^S(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ)_𝔪).
items.note: PA.0: 'Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument and identify their twists … A splitting must be proved under the source's genericity condition'; ALS.4: 'admits a useful summand by an actual eigenvalue argument'. Proof: Theorem 2.4.2 reduces to the Siegel stratum; (2.4.5) T̃^S(RΓ(X̃^P_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)) → T̃^S(RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, 𝒱_λ̃)) (T̃^S acting via r_P) from the split morphism at the end of §2.1.9; (2.4.6), reduced by [NT16 Lem. 3.12] to (2.4.7) modulo ϖ^m, follows from item 80. Printed '∂X̃^P' in the first reduction and in (2.4.5) should be the stratum X̃^P (see issues).

items.name: GL_n cohomology as a direct summand of Siegel-stratum cohomology (splitting 𝒱_λ ↪ R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}}𝒱_λ̃)
items.statement: With K̃ decomposed (so K̃_P = K̃_U ⋊ K) and λ, λ̃ as in Theorem 2.4.4, for each m ≥ 1: (i) arguing as in [NT16 p. 58], RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m) ≅ RΓ(K̃^S_P × K_S, RΓ(Inf^{P^S×K_S}_{G^S×K_S} 𝔛_G, R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}} 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m)), where R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}} sends P^S × K̃_{P,S}-equivariant complexes of sheaves on 𝔛_G to P^S × K_S-equivariant ones; (ii) the K̃_P-equivariant embedding 𝒱_λ → 𝒱_λ̃^{K̃_{U,S}} ⊂ 𝒱_λ̃, which splits K-equivariantly [NT16 Cor. 2.11], makes 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m a direct summand of R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}}(𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m): the inclusion is 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m → (𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m)^{K̃_{U,S}} → R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}}𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m and the retraction is R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}}𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m → 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m (restriction to the trivial subgroup) followed by the splitting 𝒱_λ̃ → 𝒱_λ mod ϖ^m; (iii) hence r_G^* RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m) is a direct summand of RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m) in D(H(P^S × K̃_{P,S}, K̃_P) ⊗_Z O/ϖ^m), and 𝒮 = r_G ∘ r_P descends to (2.4.7) T̃^S(RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m)) → T̃^S(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m)).
items.note: PA.0: 'Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument and identify their twists and degree shifts. A splitting must be proved … replace none by a formal direct-summand assumption'. The coefficient-module input ([NT16 Cor. 2.11], branching of dual Weyl modules to the Levi) fits PA.1's 'Weyl/dual Weyl modules, their highest-weight filtrations'.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.8 (𝒮 descends to boundary Hecke algebras with ramified operators at R, trivial coefficients)
items.statement: Let K̃ be as in §2.4.1, let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, 0) be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal and 𝔪̃ = 𝒮*(𝔪) ⊂ T̃^S. Suppose R ⊂ S satisfies: each v ∈ R is prime to p and split over F⁺; for each v ∈ R − R^c above v̄, K̃_v̄ = q̃_v with p̃_{v,1} ⊂ q̃_v ⊂ p̃_v; for each v ∈ R ∩ R^c above v̄, K̃_v̄ = Ĩ_v̄ with Iw̃_{v̄,1} ⊂ Ĩ_v̄ ⊂ Iw̃_v̄. Let T = S − (R^c − R); let T̃^T_R ⊂ H(G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}), K̃) ⊗_Z O be the (commutative) O-subalgebra generated by T̃^S, all t_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}) and all e_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R^c − R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}), and T^T_R ⊂ H(GL_n(A_F^∞), K) ⊗_Z O the (commutative) O-subalgebra generated by T^T and all t_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}) (item 82). Then there is a map 𝒮 : T̃^T_R → T^T_R, which descends to an O-algebra homomorphism T̃^T_R(RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, O)_𝔪̃) → T^T_R(RΓ(X_K, O)_𝔪).
items.note: PA.0: 'Prove derived coefficient change, level change and boundary localization compatibilities. Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument'; ALS.4: 'compatibility with localization at a Hecke ideal … admits a useful summand'. Proof: by Theorem 2.4.2 pass to X̃^P_K̃; morphisms RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, O) →α RΓ(X̃^P_K̃, O) →β RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, O) and RΓ(X_K, O) →γ RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, O) →δ RΓ(X_K, O) with βα = δγ = id, β r_P-equivariant and γ r_G-equivariant for the positive-monoid Hecke algebras, so 𝒮_+ = 𝒮|_{T̃^T_{R,+}} descends; then invert z = product over R̄_0 of strongly positive operators (Lemma 2.1.13), a unit on both sides with T = T_+[z^{−1}]. Needs Theorem 2.4.2's isomorphism to be T̃^T_R-equivariant (true, not stated).

items.name: Hecke algebras T̃^T_R, T^T_R with ramified operators at R, and the extended Satake map 𝒮 : T̃^T_R → T^T_R
items.statement: Let S = S^c and R ⊂ S with every v ∈ R prime to p and split over F⁺, K̃_v̄ = q̃_v (p̃_{v,1} ⊂ q̃_v ⊂ p̃_v) for v ∈ R − R^c above v̄, and K̃_v̄ = Ĩ_v̄ (Iw̃_{v̄,1} ⊂ Ĩ_v̄ ⊂ Iw̃_v̄) for v ∈ R ∩ R^c above v̄. Put T = S − (R^c − R), R_0 = R ∪ R^c, S_0 = S − R_0. T̃^T_R ⊂ H(G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}), K̃) ⊗_Z O is the (commutative) O-subalgebra generated by T̃^S, all t_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}) and all e_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R^c − R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}); T^T_R ⊂ H(GL_n(A_F^∞), K) ⊗_Z O is the (commutative) O-subalgebra generated by T^T and all t_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}). The map 𝒮 : T̃^T_R → T^T_R is the unramified Satake map of §2.1.2 away from S and, at R_0, arises by localization (inverting strongly positive elements, Lemma 2.1.13) from the composite r_P : H(G̃^S × Δ_{G̃,R_0}, K̃^{S_0}) → H(P^S × Δ_{P,R_0}, K̃_P^{S_0}) and r_G : H(P^S × Δ_{P,R_0}, K̃_P^{S_0}) → H(G^S × Δ_{G,R_0}, K^{S_0}); its values on P̃_v, P̃_{v,σ}, P_{v,σ}, P_{v^c,σ^{−c}} are given by Propositions 2.2.16, 2.2.18, 2.2.19.
items.locator: §2.4.1, statement and proof of Theorem 2.4.8, pp. 946–947; recalled in §3.2, pp. 957–958
items.note: PA.0: 'Compare algebraic coefficient local systems, finite-level cellular complexes and the integral Hecke actions used by each source'. The local operators t_{v,i}(σ), e_{v,i}(σ), the monoids Δ and Lemma 2.1.13 are §§2.1.9, 2.2.5. Image algebras T(C^•) are IHG.2's 'finite image algebras'.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.10(1) (cuspidal regular algebraic π of weight ιλ contribute to T^S(K, λ))
items.statement: Fix ι : Q̄_p ≅ C. Let π be a cuspidal, regular algebraic automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) of weight ιλ (the infinitesimal character of π_∞ is that of V_{ιλ}^∨), and suppose (π^∞)^K ≠ 0 for a good subgroup K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) (printed 'GL_n(A_F)'). Then the homomorphism T^S → Q̄_p given by the Hecke eigenvalues on (ι^{−1}π^∞)^K factors through the quotient T^S → T^S(K, λ).
items.note: AS.5: 'compare relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of all smooth functions … with algebraic coefficient systems and Hecke equivariance'; ALS.5 (later full part): 'compares Betti, de Rham and relative Lie algebra cohomology in characteristic zero'. The proof needs H*(𝔪_G, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ V_{ιλ}) ≠ 0 ([Clo90, Lem. 3.14] + Künneth), which no stage names explicitly (AF.1 only defines relative Lie algebra cochains). PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/40 routed Theorem 2.4.10 to AS.5 and AG2.0.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.10(2), first part (degree range of rational cohomology localized at a non-Eisenstein ideal)
items.statement: Fix ι : Q̄_p ≅ C. Let q_0 = [F⁺:Q]·n(n−1)/2 and l_0 = [F⁺:Q]·n − 1. Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup and 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, 𝒱_λ) a maximal ideal with ρ̄_𝔪 absolutely irreducible. Then for j ∈ Z, H^j(X_K, 𝒱_λ)_𝔪[1/p] ≠ 0 only if j ∈ [q_0, q_0 + l_0]; and if one of the groups H^j(X_K, 𝒱_λ)_𝔪[1/p], j ∈ [q_0, q_0 + l_0], is non-zero then all of them are.
items.note: Proof: Franke decomposition (item 86 below); (E^K_{{Q}})_𝔪 = 0 for proper Q because r_ι(𝔐) is reducible while ρ̄_𝔪 is absolutely irreducible; for cuspidal π with central character ξ_{ιλ}^{−1} on R_{>0}, H*(𝔪_G, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ V_{ιλ}) = 0 unless π is regular algebraic of weight ιλ ([BW00, II Prop. 3.1]) and is non-zero exactly in degrees [q_0, q_0 + l_0] ([Clo90, Lem. 3.14], Künneth: 𝔪_G = ⊕_{v|∞} g̃_v ⊕ an abelian algebra of dimension [F⁺:Q] − 1, range (n−1)[F⁺:Q] + [F⁺:Q] − 1 = l_0). Check: 2q_0 + l_0 = n²[F⁺:Q] − 1 = dim_R X. PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/40 marked Theorem 2.4.10 planned under AS.5/AG2.0; AS.5 plans only the comparison and warns 'ordinary cohomology must not be replaced by cusp or L² cohomology', so I mark the localized statement missing. Route: a source of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.0 levels, ALS.3 Hecke correspondences, ALS.5 comparison).

items.name: Theorem 2.4.10(2), second part (every Q̄_p-point of T^S(K, 𝒱_λ)_𝔪 is cuspidal automorphic)
items.statement: In the situation of the previous item (ι fixed, K good, 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, 𝒱_λ) with ρ̄_𝔪 absolutely irreducible), for every homomorphism f : T^S(K, 𝒱_λ)_𝔪 → Q̄_p there is a cuspidal, regular algebraic automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_F) of weight ιλ such that f is the system of Hecke eigenvalues on (ι^{−1}π^∞)^K; in particular \overline{r_ι(π)} ≅ ρ̄_𝔪.
items.note: Same proof as the previous item: after localization only the cuspidal summand E^K_{{G}} = H*_cusp(X_K, V_{ιλ}) survives. Theorem 2.4.10 is cited on pp. 985, 1031, 1062, 1064, 1076, 1080–1081 and by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/40. Route: a source of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.0 levels, ALS.3 Hecke correspondences, ALS.5 comparison).

items.name: Eisenstein summands of H*(X_K, V_{ιλ}) are parabolically induced from regular algebraic cuspidal data; their Galois representations (Franke–Schwermer)
items.statement: By [Fra98, Th. 18] as in [FS98, §2.2]: H*(X_K, V_{ιλ}) = (⊕_{{Q}∈𝒞} E_{{Q}})^K with E_{{Q}} = H*(𝔪_G, K_∞; A_{V_{ιλ},{Q}} ⊗_C V_{ιλ})(χ_λ), where 𝒞 is the set of associate classes of parabolic Q-subgroups of Res_{F/Q}GL_n, 𝔪_G = Lie of ker(N_{F/Q} ∘ det)(R), A_{V,{Q}} a space of automorphic forms and (χ_λ) the twist by the central character of V_{ιλ}; E^K_{{G}} = H*_cusp(X_K, V_{ιλ}) = ⊕_π (π^∞)^K ⊗_C H*(𝔪_G, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗_C V_{ιλ}) over cuspidal π with central character ξ, ξ|_{R>0} = ξ_{ιλ}^{−1}|_{R>0}. If Q is the standard block upper-triangular parabolic for n = n_1 + ⋯ + n_r, with Levi L_Q, then every maximal ideal 𝔐 of H(GL_n(A_F^{∞,S}), K^S) ⊗_Z C in the support of E^K_{{Q}} is the Hecke eigensystem of the unnormalized induction Ind^{GL_n(A_F^∞)}_{Q(A^∞)} σ^∞, where σ = ⊗_{i=1}^r π_i is cuspidal on L_Q(A_Q) = ∏_i GL_{n_i}(A_F) with the infinitesimal character of the dual of the (L_Q)_C-representation of highest weight w(ιλ + ρ) − ρ for some w ∈ W^Q (so each π_i is regular algebraic); and r_ι(𝔐) := ⊕_{i=1}^r r_ι(π_i) ⊗ ε^{−(n_{i+1}+⋯+n_r)} : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) has det(X − r_ι(𝔐)(Frob_v)) = P_v(X) mod 𝔐 for all but finitely many v ∉ S.
items.note: AS.5: 'finite-infinitesimal-character functors. Prove the filtration and acyclicity statements that compare relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of all smooth functions' (Franke's theorem and filtration); AG2.4: 'Deliver the characteristic-zero semisimple system of HLTT Theorem 7.13/Corollary 7.14' (Theorem 2.3.2). Proof details: [FS98, Prop. 3.3] gives a filtration of A_{V,{Q},φ} with graded pieces normalized inductions Ind(δ_Q ⊗ π^∞), δ_Q(l) = e^{⟨H_Q(l), ρ_Q⟩}; σ = δ_Q ⊗ π has χ_σ = v(ιλ^∨ + ρ) + ρ_Q = λ^∨_{w_{0,Q} v w_0} + ρ_{L_Q} with w_{0,Q} v w_0 ∈ W^Q (checked). The GL_2 case of the Galois formula (roots qa_1, a_2 for Ind(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2), geometric Frobenius) confirms the sign of the twist. Reused for G̃ in Theorem 2.4.11.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.11 (middle-degree rational cohomology of G̃ at 𝔪̃ is semisimple and cuspidal automorphic)
items.statement: Let ρ be half the sum of the positive roots of Res_{F⁺/Q}G̃ (printed as an element of X*(Res_{F⁺/Q}T_n); read X*(Res_{F⁺/Q}T)), fix ι : Q̄_p ≅ C, and let λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F⁺,E)} be such that for every w ∈ W^P((Res_{F⁺/Q}G̃)_C, (Res_{F⁺/Q}T)_C) there is no cuspidal automorphic representation of G (i.e. of GL_n(A_F)) of weight ιλ_w, λ_w = w(λ̃ + ρ) − ρ. Let 𝔪̃ ⊂ T̃^S be a maximal ideal in the support of H*(X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃) such that ρ̄_𝔪̃ is a direct sum of n-dimensional absolutely irreducible representations of G_F, and let d = ½ dim_R X̃ = n²[F⁺:Q]. Then H^d(X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃[1/p] is a semisimple T̃^S[1/p]-module, and for every homomorphism f : T̃^S(H^d(X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃)_𝔪̃) → Q̄_p there is a cuspidal, regular algebraic automorphic representation π̃ of G̃(A_{F⁺}) of weight ιλ̃ such that f is the system of Hecke eigenvalues on (ι^{−1}π̃^∞)^{K̃}. Hypotheses needed by the proof and not printed: F contains an imaginary quadratic field (Theorem 2.3.3 is used), and S satisfies the conditions of Theorem 2.3.8.
items.note: Proof: Franke decomposition for Res_{F⁺/Q}G̃ (no central twist, as the group has no rational characters); for the Siegel class the hypothesis on λ_w kills E_{{P}}; for other proper P̃, L_P̃ ≅ ∏ Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{n_i} × U(n−s, n−s) and r(𝔐̃) (Theorems 2.3.2, 2.3.3) has ≥ 3 Jordan–Hölder factors unless (r, s) ∈ {(1, n), (0, 0)}, contradicting ρ̄_𝔪̃ = two n-dimensional irreducibles. Printed decomposition '2n = n_1 + ⋯ + n_r + 2(n − s)' is wrong (issues). Strict reading gives 'missing'; by analogy with PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/40's routing of Theorem 2.4.10 one could instead record AS.5 + AG2.2 as planned. Route: a source of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.0 levels, ALS.3 Hecke correspondences, ALS.5 comparison).

items.name: Setting of §3: the ramification set R, T = S − (R^c − R), and the Hecke algebras T^T_R(K, λ) and their localizations
items.statement: F is a CM field containing an imaginary quadratic field, n ≥ 1, p a prime, E/Q_p inside Q̄_p containing all embeddings of F, and every p-adic place of F⁺ splits in F. K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) is good, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, and S is a finite set of finite places of F containing the p-adic ones with S = S^c and such that for every finite v ∉ S of residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic F_0 ⊂ F. R ⊂ S satisfies: every v ∈ R is prime to p; the residue characteristic of each v ∈ R splits in some imaginary quadratic F_0 ⊂ F (so v is split over F⁺); Iw_{v,1} ⊂ K_v ⊂ Iw_v for v ∈ R; K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v ∈ R^c − R (R^c ⊂ S). T = S − (R^c − R); T^T_R ⊂ H(GL_n(A_F^∞), K) ⊗_Z O is the commutative O-subalgebra generated by T^T and all t_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}); T^T_R(K, λ) ⊂ End_{D(O)}(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ)) is its image, so T^S(K, λ) ⊂ T^T(K, λ) ⊂ T^T_R(K, λ). For a maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ), T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪 is the localization as a T^S(K, λ)-algebra; it is an O-subalgebra of End_{D(O)}(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ)_𝔪) containing T^S(K, λ)_𝔪 (not necessarily local). If 𝔪 is non-Eisenstein, Theorem 2.3.7 gives ρ_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K, λ)_𝔪/I) with I nilpotent of exponent depending only on n and [F:Q].
items.note: PA.0: 'Compare … the integral Hecke actions used by each source'; IHG.2: 'For a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex define its finite image algebras … Prove localization decompositions'. The ramified operators t_{v,i}(σ) are §2.2.5.

items.name: Theorem 3.1.1 (local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p for Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations, up to a nilpotent ideal)
items.statement: In the setting of §3.1, let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be non-Eisenstein. There exist an integer N ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F:Q], an ideal I_R ⊂ T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪 with I_R^N = 0, and a continuous homomorphism ρ_{𝔪,R} : G_{F,T} → GL_n(T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪/I_R) such that: (1) for every place v ∉ T of F, det(X − ρ_{𝔪,R}(Frob_v)) is the image of P_v(X) in (T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪/I_R)[X]; (2) for every v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v}, det(X − ρ_{𝔪,R}(σ)) is the image of P_{v,σ}(X) in (T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪/I_R)[X].
items.note: Deduced from Proposition 3.1.2 by [Che14, Th. 2.22] (determinant residually absolutely irreducible ⇒ representation over each local factor; IHG.1 plans 'reconstruction … over complete local rings when residual absolute irreducibility supplies an actual representation'). Also stated in the introduction (p. 900) and used on pp. 1063, 1067. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 records 'the §3 inputs routed to AG2/IHG'; neither AG2.5 (characteristic 0) nor IHG.4–5 (generic) states this torsion statement. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.2 (determinant form of ℓ ≠ p local–global compatibility)
items.statement: In the setting of §3.1, let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be non-Eisenstein. There exist N ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F:Q], an ideal I_R ⊂ T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪 with I_R^N = 0, and a T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪/I_R-valued determinant D_{𝔪,R} of G_{F,T} of dimension n such that: (1) for every v ∉ T, the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v under D_{𝔪,R} is the image of P_v(X); (2) for every v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v}, the characteristic polynomial of σ under D_{𝔪,R} is the image of P_{v,σ}(X) in (T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪/I_R)[X].
items.note: Proof (pp. 962–964), after Lemma 3.2.1: Theorem 2.4.8 and Corollary 3.2.3 give the 2n-dimensional determinant D′ = D·(D^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n}), D = det ρ_𝔪 (item below). For v ∈ R let E_v be the unique n-dimensional determinant of W_{F_v} over T^T_R(K,0)_𝔪 with char. poly of σ equal to P_{v,σ} (for v ∈ R^c − R: unramified, char. poly of Frob_v equal to P_v); then D|_{W_{F_v}}(D^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n})|_{W_{F_v}} = E_v(E^{c,∨}_{v^c} ⊗ ε^{1−2n}). Twisting by ψ (Lemma 3.2.1(3), Proposition 2.2.23) and comparing φ_v-eigenvalues with [Che14, Th. 2.12] gives det ρ̄_𝔪|_{W_{F_v}} = E_v mod 𝔫 for all maximal 𝔫, and Lemma 3.2.4 gives D|_{W_{F_v}} = E_v. For v ∈ R − R^c, 𝒮(Res_v) is a unit (Lemma 3.2.1(2) and Proposition 2.2.19), so tr((ρ_𝔪^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n})(σ(τ_v − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(φ_v))) = 0 for all σ, τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}; absolute irreducibility of ρ̄_𝔪 then forces ρ_𝔪|_{W_{F_{v^c}}} unramified. I checked the eigenvalue-separation step: with A, B the φ_v-roots of ρ̄_𝔪 and ρ̄_𝔪^{c,∨}ε^{1−2n}, Lemma 3.2.1(3) says ψ(Frob_v)A ∩ ψ(Frob_{v^c})^{−1}(A ∪ B) = ∅, which forces A′ = A. TC.3's 'abstract factor-separation lemma using actual auxiliary characters' is the unramified analogue of this step. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.1 (reduction of Proposition 3.1.2 to small, weight-0, decomposable level with separated Frobenius eigenvalues)
items.statement: Fix for each v ∈ R a Frobenius lift φ_v ∈ W_{F_v}; let R_1 = R ∩ R^c and R̄ ⊃ R̄_1 the places of F⁺ below R, R_1. To prove Proposition 3.1.2 it suffices to prove it under the additional assumptions: (1) K_v = Iw_{v,1} for all v ∈ R, and there is an odd prime q, prime to R and p, with K_q = ker(GL_n(O_{F,q}) → GL_n(O_F/(q))); (2) for each v ∈ R, the characteristic polynomials of ρ̄_𝔪(φ_v) and (ρ̄_𝔪^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n})(φ_v) are coprime; (3) there is a character ψ : G_F → O^× of finite prime-to-p order, unramified above R ∪ R^c ∪ S_p, with ψ ∘ Art_F ∘ det trivial on K, such that for each v ∈ R the characteristic polynomials of ψ̄(Frob_v)ρ̄_𝔪(φ_v) and ψ̄(Frob_{v^c})^{−1}(ρ̄_𝔪 ⊕ ρ̄_𝔪^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n})(φ_v) are coprime; (4) λ = 0; (5) there is a good K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}) with (a) K̃ decomposed with respect to P and K = K̃ ∩ G(A^∞_{F⁺}); (b) K̃_q = ker(G̃(O_{F⁺,q}) → G̃(O_{F⁺}/(q))); (c) K̃_v̄ = G̃(O_{F⁺_v̄}) for v̄ prime to S, K̃_v̄ = Iw̃_v̄(1,1) for v̄ ∈ R̄_1, and K̃_v̄ = p̃_{v,1} for v̄ ∈ R̄ − R̄_1 with v the unique place of R above v̄.
items.note: Proof chain: (1) via two auxiliary primes q_1, q_2, normal K_i ⊂ K, Lemma 2.2.4 (exponent d), ideal I with I^{2Nd} = 0, Chebotarev and [Che14, Lem. 1.12]; (2) and (3) via auxiliary finite-order characters ψ_1, ψ_2 (unramified at S, never both ramified at the same rational prime) and Proposition 2.2.23 (twisting, extended tacitly to the operators at R); (4) via K(p^m) = ker(K → GL_n(O_{F,p}/(p^m))), constancy of 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m on X_{K(p^m)}, T^T_R(K, λ) ≅ lim_m T^T_R(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m)) and [Che14, Ex. 2.32] (exponent Nd); (5) by the construction in the next item. Generic inputs are planned (IHG.2 nilpotence bound, IHG.4 'change-of-level … passage to inverse limits'); the reduction itself is not. The printed sub-labels of (5) are '(a) (a) (a)'. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: A decomposed level K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}) with K̃ ∩ G = K (proof of Lemma 3.2.1(5))
items.statement: Given K satisfying (1)–(4) of Lemma 3.2.1, define K̃ = ∏_v̄ K̃_v̄ by: K̃_v̄ = G̃(O_{F⁺_v̄}) if v̄ ∉ S̄; K̃_v̄ = Iw̃_v̄(1,1) if v̄ ∈ R̄_1; K̃_v̄ = p̃_{v,1} if v̄ ∈ R̄ − R̄_1 (v the place of R above v̄); K̃_q = ker(G̃(O_{F⁺,q}) → G̃(O_{F⁺}/(q))); for every other finite v̄, fix m ≥ 1 with ker(G̃(O_{F⁺_v̄}) → G̃(O_{F⁺}/(ϖ_v̄^m))) ∩ G(O_{F⁺_v̄}) ⊂ K ∩ G(O_{F⁺_v̄}) and set K̃_v̄ = ker(G̃(O_{F⁺_v̄}) → G̃(O_{F⁺}/(ϖ_v̄^m))) · (K ∩ G(O_{F⁺_v̄})). Then K̃ is a good open subgroup of G̃(A^∞_{F⁺}), decomposed with respect to P, with K̃ ∩ G(A^∞_{F⁺}) = K.
items.note: Checks: p̃_{v,1} ∩ G = GL_n(O_{F_{v^c}}) × Iw_{v,1} and Iw̃_v̄(1,1) ∩ G = Iw_{v^c,1} × Iw_{v,1} match Lemma 3.2.1(1); places ramified in F/F⁺ lie in S by the S-condition. 'It is easy to check' tacitly needs K_v̄ ⊂ G(O_{F⁺_v̄}) at the remaining places, which a good subgroup need not satisfy (see issues). Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.2 (ℓ ≠ p local–global compatibility at R for the compactly supported cohomology of G̃, with the resultant condition)
items.statement: Assume K, 𝔪 satisfy (1)–(5) of Lemma 3.2.1, with φ_v fixed for v ∈ R and K̃, T̃^T_R as there; for v ∈ R − R^c let Res_v ∈ H(G̃(F⁺_v̄), K̃_v̄) ⊗ O be the resultant of P_{v^c,φ_v^{−c}}(X) and P_{v,φ_v}(X) (defined before Proposition 2.2.14). There exist N ≥ 1 depending only on [F:Q] and n, an ideal Ĩ_{c,R} ⊂ T̃^T_R(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O)) with Ĩ_{c,R}^N = 0, and a T̃^T_R(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O))/Ĩ_{c,R}-valued determinant D̃_{c,R} of G_{F,S} of dimension 2n such that: (1) for every v ∉ S, the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v is the image of P̃_v(X); (2) for every v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v}, the characteristic polynomial of σ is the image of P̃_{v,σ}(X) (printed modulo 'Ĩ_R'; read Ĩ_{c,R}); (3) if t̃r_{c,R} : T̃^T_R(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O))[G_{F,S}] → T̃^T_R(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O))/Ĩ_{c,R} is the trace of D̃_{c,R} [Che14, §1.10], then Res_v^{(2n)!} · t̃r_{c,R}(σ(τ_v − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(φ_v)) = 0 for every v ∈ R − R^c, σ ∈ G_{F,S} and τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}.
items.note: Proved by redoing [Sch15, Cor. 5.2.6] keeping track of the operators at R, via the two key steps below. The remark 'in the case where R is empty, [this] is Proposition 2.3.9' is imprecise: 2.3.9 concerns RΓ(X̃_K̃, 𝒱_λ̃), not RΓ_c (see issues). Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Determinants over continuous quotients of the classical Hecke algebra T_cl with local conditions at R (essential statement in the proof of Proposition 3.2.2)
items.statement: Let C = Q̂̄_p, m ≥ 1, and let T_cl be T̃^T_R with the weakest topology making all maps T̃^T_R → End_C(H^0(𝒳_{K̃^pK̃_p}, ω^{mk}_{K̃^pK̃_p} ⊗ ℐ)) continuous (as in [Sch15, Th. 4.3.1]; k ≥ 1 and open compact K̃_p ⊂ G̃(F⁺_p) with K̃^pK̃_p good, varying). For every continuous quotient T_cl → A with A discrete there is a unique A-valued determinant D_A of G_{F,S} of dimension 2n such that: for v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v is the image of P̃_v(X); for v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v} that of σ is the image of P̃_{v,σ}(X); and Res_v^{(2n)!} tr_A(σ(τ_v − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(φ_v)) = 0 for v ∈ R − R^c, σ ∈ G_{F,S}, τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}.
items.note: IHG.4: 'Construct compatible determinants over finite coefficient quotients from a dense family of classical Hecke systems … Prove uniqueness from Frobenius density using Chebotarev and continuity, then existence by polynomial-law identities'; TC.1: 'compare finite-level sections with infinite-level sections … produce finite-level classical sections'. Proved as [Sch15, Cor. 5.1.11] by [Che14, Ex. 2.32] from the single-π̃ statement (next item), which supplies the conditions at R. The role of the fixed integer m is not explained in the text.

items.name: Hecke-algebra form of local–global compatibility at R for one cuspidal cohomological π̃ of G̃
items.statement: Let π̃ be a cuspidal cohomological automorphic representation of G̃(A_{F⁺}) with π̃^{∞,K̃} ≠ 0, ι : Q̄_p ≅ C, T̃^T_R(π̃) = im(T̃^T_R ⊗_O Q̄_p → End_{Q̄_p}(ι^{−1}π̃^{∞,K̃})), and ρ : G_{F,S} → GL_{2n}(T̃^T_R(π̃)) the composite of r_ι(π̃) (Theorem 2.3.3) with GL_{2n}(Q̄_p) ⊂ GL_{2n}(T̃^T_R(π̃)). Then: for v ∉ S, det(X − ρ(Frob_v)) is the image of P̃_v(X); for v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v}, det(X − ρ(σ)) is the image of P̃_{v,σ}(X) in T̃^T_R(π̃)[X]; and for each v ∈ R − R^c (printed 'R^c − R') and τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}, Res_v^{(2n)!} ρ((τ_v − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(φ_v)) = 0 in M_{2n}(T̃^T_R(π̃)).
items.note: AG2.5: 'Good-prime and ramified local–global comparison … Compare restrictions to Weil groups through the actual arbitrary-rank local Langlands construction'; AG2.2: 'identify the direct sum attached to a cohomological unitary automorphic representation with the required degree-2n Hecke polynomial' (Theorem 2.3.3(a),(c)). The local translations are §2.2's Proposition 2.2.9 (v ∈ R ∩ R^c), Lemma 2.2.13 (v ∈ R − R^c; not cited, see issues) and Corollary 2.2.15 (resultant condition). The splitting of residue characteristics of R in an imaginary quadratic subfield is needed exactly for Theorem 2.3.3(c).

items.name: Corollary 3.2.3 (the same local–global compatibility for the boundary cohomology RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, O))
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 3.2.2, there exist N ≥ 1 depending only on [F:Q] and n, an ideal Ĩ_{∂,R} ⊂ T̃^T_R(RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, O)) with Ĩ_{∂,R}^N = 0, and a T̃^T_R(RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, O))/Ĩ_{∂,R}-valued determinant D̃_{∂,R} of G_{F,S} of dimension 2n with: (1) characteristic polynomial of Frob_v equal to the image of P̃_v(X) for v ∉ S; (2) characteristic polynomial of σ ∈ W_{F_v} equal to the image of P̃_{v,σ}(X) for v ∈ R; (3) Res_v^{(2n)!} t̃r_{∂,R}(σ(τ_v − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(φ_v)) = 0 for v ∈ R − R^c, σ ∈ G_{F,S}, τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}.
items.note: Proof: the T̃^T_R-equivariant triangle RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O) → RΓ(X̃_K̃, O) → RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, O) → gives T̃^T_R(RΓ_c ⊕ RΓ) → T̃^T_R(RΓ(∂X̃_K̃, O))/J̃ with J̃² = 0 (ALS.4 plans the triangle, IHG.2 the image algebras); Proposition 3.2.2 handles RΓ_c and the duality step (next item) handles RΓ. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Poincaré duality for the Hecke algebras T̃^T_R and the dual Galois representation (proof of Corollary 3.2.3)
items.statement: From the Verdier-duality square of Proposition 2.2.21 (H(G̃^∞, K̃) acting on RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O) and, through the anti-involution ι̃([K̃gK̃]) = [K̃g^{−1}K̃], on RΓ(X̃_K̃, O)), ι̃ descends to an isomorphism ι̃(T̃^T_R)(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O)) ≅ T̃^T_R(RΓ(X̃_K̃, O)), where ι̃(T̃^T_R)(RΓ_c) is the image of T̃^T_R → H(G̃^∞, K̃) ⊗ O →ι̃ H(G̃^∞, K̃) ⊗ O → End_{D(O)}(RΓ_c(X̃_K̃, O)). For π̃ cuspidal cohomological with π̃^{∞,K̃} ≠ 0, ι̃ induces an isomorphism T̃^T_R(π̃^∨) ≅ ι̃(T̃^T_R)(π̃) (transpose for the pairing of ι^{−1}π̃^{∞,K̃} with ι^{−1}π̃^{∨,∞,K̃}), and r_ι(π̃^∨) ≅ r_ι(π̃)^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−2n}; hence ρ = r_ι(π̃)^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−2n} over ι̃(T̃^T_R)(π̃) satisfies the three properties of the single-π̃ item, and the analogue of Proposition 3.2.2 holds for T̃^T_R(RΓ(X̃_K̃, O)) with a nilpotent ideal Ĩ of exponent bounded in terms of [F:Q] and n.
items.note: ALS.5:finite-level-duality: 'construct Poincaré–Lefschetz/Verdier duality for perfect coefficient complexes … and restriction/corestriction and Hecke adjoint formulas on the complexes'; AG2.2: 'Prove compatibility of dual, conjugate, tensor-by-character and solvable restriction operations'. Proposition 2.2.21 is stated for H(G̃^S, K̃^S); the square is used here for the full H(G̃^∞, K̃) including the operators at R.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.4(1) (Hensel's lemma for group determinants: uniqueness of a residually coprime factorization)
items.statement: Let A be a complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue field k, Γ a group, n_1, n_2 ≥ 0, n = n_1 + n_2, and D_1, D_2 A-valued group determinants of Γ of dimensions n_1, n_2 with D = D_1D_2. Suppose the semisimple representations ρ̄_i : Γ → GL_{n_i}(k) with det ρ̄_i = D̄_i := D_i mod 𝔪_A have no common Jordan–Hölder factor. If E_1, E_2 are group determinants of Γ of dimensions n_1, n_2 with E_i mod 𝔪_A = D̄_i and E_1E_2 = D, then E_1 = D_1 and E_2 = D_2. Explicitly, with S = A[Γ]/CH(D) and idempotents e_1 + e_2 = 1, e_1e_2 = 0 in S lifting the central idempotents of M_{n_1}(k) × M_{n_2}(k), D_1(x) = D(e_1x + e_2) for all A-algebras B and x ∈ S ⊗_A B.
items.note: IHG.1: 'Construct the characteristic-polynomial ideal and Cayley–Hamilton quotient, faithful determinant descent and generalized matrix algebra decompositions'; TC.3: 'Build the abstract factor-separation lemma … Prove uniqueness, change-of-ring … Include the case of nilpotent coefficient quotients'. Proof uses [Che14, Lem. 1.21, Lem. 2.4] and idempotent lifting [BC09, p. 32 footnote]; it tacitly uses CH(D) ⊂ ker D_1 ∩ ker D_2 (true since χ^D(x) = χ^{D_1}(x)χ^{D_2}(x)) so that D_1 is defined on S. In §3 it is applied at each maximal ideal of the semilocal T^T_R(K,0)_𝔪/I_R, whose residue fields may be larger than k.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.4(2) (kernel of a product of residually disjoint determinants)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 3.2.4(1) (A complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue field k, D = D_1D_2 with ρ̄_1, ρ̄_2 having no common Jordan–Hölder factor), ker D = ker D_1 ∩ ker D_2 (ker D = {x : D(1 + xy) = 1 for all A-algebras B and y ∈ A[Γ] ⊗_A B}, as in [Che14]).
items.note: IHG.0: 'Prove characteristic-polynomial identities, direct sum/product'; IHG.1: 'characteristic-polynomial ideal and Cayley–Hamilton quotient'. Proof: D_1(1 + xy) = D(1 + e_1xy) = 1 for x ∈ ker D.

items.name: The boundary 2n-dimensional determinant D′ = D·(D^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n}) over T^T_R(K, 0)_𝔪 (proof of Proposition 3.1.2)
items.statement: Assume (1)–(5) of Lemma 3.2.1 and let 𝔪̃ = 𝒮*(𝔪). There are N ≥ 1 depending only on [F:Q] and n, an ideal I_R ⊂ T^T_R(RΓ(X_K, O)_𝔪) = T^T_R(K, 0)_𝔪 with I_R^N = 0, and a T^T_R(K, 0)_𝔪/I_R-valued determinant D′ of G_{F,S} of dimension 2n (the pushforward of D̃_{∂,R} along Theorem 2.4.8's map) such that: (1) for v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v is the image of P_v(X) q_v^{n(2n−1)} P_{v^c}^∨(q_v^{1−2n}X); (2) for v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v}, that of σ is the image of P_{v,σ}(X) ‖σ‖_v^{n(1−2n)} P^∨_{v^c,σ^c}(‖σ‖_v^{2n−1}X); (3) 𝒮(Res_v)^{(2n)!} tr′(σ(τ_v − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(φ_v)) = 0 for v ∈ R − R^c, σ ∈ G_{F,S}, τ_v ∈ I_{F_v}. Enlarging I_R (N still depending only on [F:Q] and n) there is ρ_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^T_R(K, 0)_𝔪/I_R) with det(X − ρ_𝔪(Frob_v)) = P_v(X) for v ∉ S (Theorem 2.3.7), and D′ = det(ρ_𝔪 ⊕ ρ_𝔪^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n}) = D·(D^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n}), D = det ρ_𝔪 (twisted determinant notation matching the representation, so the law underlying D^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n} is twisted by ε^{n(1−2n)}). Moreover 𝒮(Res_v) is the resultant of P_{v,φ_v}(X) and q_v^{n(2n−1)}P^∨_{v^c}(q_v^{1−2n}X) and is a unit in T^T_R(K, 0)_𝔪.
items.note: Uses Theorem 2.4.8, Corollary 3.2.3 and Propositions 2.2.16, 2.2.18, 2.2.19. Consistency checks: (1)–(2) match ρ ⊕ ρ^{c,∨}ε^{1−2n} with geometric Frobenius (ε(Frob_v) = q_v^{−1}, ‖φ_v‖_v = q_v^{−1}) and P^∨_{v^c,σ^c} = P_{v^c,σ^{−c}}. TC.3 plans the unramified analogue ('polynomial identities relating Levi factors, contragredients and character twists to the ambient Hecke polynomial'), not the conditions at R. Route: the proposed Part II of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p); IHG.3 plans only the unramified normalization, and no stage plans local–global compatibility at ramified places for Hecke-algebra-valued determinants.

items.name: Fontaine–Laffaille categories MF_O, MF^a_O, MF^0_O, MF_k, MF^a_k
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of §4: F is a CM field, p is unramified in F and F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits; E/Q_p contains the images of all embeddings of F; S is a finite set of finite places of F containing the p-adic places, with S = S^c, and for every finite place w ∉ S of F with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic field F_0 ⊂ F. Let v | p be a place of F, so F_v/Q_p is unramified. MF_O is the category of finite O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O-modules M with (i) a decreasing filtration Fil^i M by O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O-submodules that are O_{F_v}-direct summands, such that for each τ: F_v ↪ E, writing M_τ = M ⊗_{O_{F_v}⊗O, τ⊗1} O, there is an integer a_τ with Fil^{a_τ} M_τ = M_τ and Fil^{a_τ+p−1} M_τ = 0; and (ii) Frob_p^{−1}⊗1-semilinear maps Φ^i: Fil^i M → M with Φ^i|_{Fil^{i+1} M} = pΦ^{i+1} and M = Σ_i Φ^i(Fil^i M). Then Fil^i M = ∏_τ Fil^i M_τ and Φ^i = ∏_τ Φ^i_τ with Φ^i_τ: Fil^i M_τ → M_{τ∘Frob_p} (printed M_{τ∘Frob_p^{−1}}). For a = (a_τ) ∈ Z^{Hom(F_v,E)}, MF^a_O is the full subcategory of M with Fil^{a_τ} M_τ = M_τ and Fil^{a_τ+p−1} M_τ = 0 for every τ; MF^0_O = MF^{(0,…,0)}_O; MF_k and MF^a_k are the full subcategories of MF_O and MF^a_O of objects killed by ϖ.
items.note: R07.3: 'Construct the integral filtered modules and the Galois functor … Use an absolutely unramified base K=K₀ (e=1) … keep filtration indices in [0,p−2]' — ACC+'s filtration jumps lie in [a_τ, a_τ+p−2]. PA.1: 'FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.3 supplies the integral Fontaine–Laffaille classification and lattice comparison'. Normalizations are those of [CHT08, §2.4.1]. Same routing as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (FL condition → L7/R07.3/PA.1).

items.name: The Fontaine–Laffaille functor G^0 on MF^0_O and its tensor compatibility (4.1.1)
items.statement: For p > 2 there is an exact, fully faithful, covariant functor G^0 from MF^0_O to the category of finite O-modules with continuous O-linear G_{F_v}-action ([CHT08, §2.4.1], where it is called G). Its essential image is closed under subquotients, and on MF^0_k it takes values in continuous G_{F_v}-representations on finite-dimensional k-vector spaces. If M_1, M_2 ∈ MF^0_O and M_1 ⊗_{O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O} M_2 ∈ MF^0_O, then (4.1.1) G^0(M_1 ⊗_{O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O} M_2) = G^0(M_1) ⊗_O G^0(M_2).
items.note: R07.3: 'prove exactness and full faithfulness in the valid range' (range [0,p−2] matches MF^0_O). The tensor compatibility (4.1.1), used to show G is independent of a, is not named in R07.3 and should be recorded there. Recollection of [FL82] as normalized in [CHT08]; nothing proved here. v2 numbers the display (4.1.0); print has (4.1.1).

items.name: The twisted functor G = G^0(M(a)) ⊗ ψ_a on MF_O and its restrictions G^a
items.statement: Let M ∈ MF_O and a = (a_τ) ∈ Z^{Hom(F_v,E)} with M ∈ MF^a_O. Let ψ_a: G_{F_v} → O^× be the crystalline character with ψ_a∘Art_{F_v}(x) = ∏_τ τ(x)^{−a_τ} for x ∈ O^×_{F_v} and ψ_a∘Art_{F_v}(p) = 1, and let M(a) ∈ MF^0_O be given by Fil^i M(a)_τ = Fil^{i+a_τ} M_τ, Φ^i_{M(a),τ} = Φ^{i+a_τ}_{M,τ}. Put G(M) = G^0(M(a)) ⊗_O ψ_a; by (4.1.1) this does not depend on the choice of a with M ∈ MF^a_O. G^a := G|_{MF^a_O} is fully faithful with essential image stable under subquotients; G is not full on all of MF_O; the essential image of G is stable under twists by crystalline characters.
items.note: R07.3 ('with the covariance and HT-sign translation explicitly proved'; 'after a common Tate shift keep filtration indices in [0,p−2]') and R06.4 ('Translate the filtration indices to HT(χ_p)=+1 instead of changing covariance silently') plan the shifted functor. The embedding-dependent shift (a_τ varying with τ) via ψ_a and the stability of the essential image under crystalline twists are not stated in either stage and should be recorded at R07.3 or PA.1.

items.name: Fontaine–Laffaille weights FL_τ(M̄)
items.statement: For M̄ ∈ MF_k and an embedding τ: F_v ↪ E, FL_τ(M̄) is the multiset of integers i with gr^i M̄ ⊗_{O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}k, τ⊗1} k ≠ 0, each counted with multiplicity equal to the k-dimension of that space.
items.note: PA.1 is 'Fontaine–Laffaille weights and degree shifting'; R07.3: 'Prove how torsion subquotients and reductions change the filtration.'

items.name: Hodge–Tate weights of Fontaine–Laffaille lattices; lattice criterion for the essential image of G^a
items.statement: Let p > 2. (i) If M ∈ MF_O is p-torsion free, then G(M) ⊗_O E is crystalline and HT_τ(G(M) ⊗_O E) = FL_τ(M ⊗_O k) for every τ: F_v ↪ E. (ii) If W is an O-lattice in a crystalline representation of G_{F_v} such that, for some integers a_τ, every τ-Hodge–Tate weight lies in [a_τ, a_τ + p − 2], then W is in the essential image of G^a, a = (a_τ).
items.note: R07.3: 'identify the finite-flat and crystalline examples used in the programme'; R06.4: 'rational admissibility at filtration length <p'; PA.1: 'R07.3 supplies the integral Fontaine–Laffaille classification and lattice comparison'. Convention check for the consumer: in this paper the cyclotomic character has HT weight −1 (det ρ_x = r_ι(ω_π)ε^{n(1−n)/2} in the proof of Thm 4.5.1), opposite to R06.4's HT(χ_p)=+1.

items.name: Theorem 4.5.1: local–global compatibility at l = p in the Fontaine–Laffaille case
items.statement: Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, S a finite set of finite places of F containing the p-adic places with S = S^c, and m ⊂ T^S(K,λ) a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal with T^S(K,λ)/m = k of characteristic p. Let v̄ be a p-adic place of F^+ and assume: (1) p is unramified in F and F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits; (2) for every finite place w ∉ S of F with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic field F_0 ⊂ F; (3) K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for every v | v̄; (4) λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} ≤ p − 2n − 1 for every τ: F ↪ E inducing v̄; (5) p > n²; (6) there is a p-adic place v̄' ≠ v̄ of F^+ with Σ_{v̄'' ∈ S̄_p, v̄'' ≠ v̄, v̄'} [F^+_{v̄''}:Q_p] > ½[F^+:Q]; (7) ρ̄_m is decomposed generic; (8) either (a) H^*(X_K, V_λ)_m[1/p] ≠ 0, or (b) for every τ inducing v̄, −λ_{τc,n} − λ_{τ,n} ≤ p − 2n − 2 and −λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,1} ≥ 0. Then there are an integer N ≥ 1 depending only on [F^+:Q] and n, an ideal J (of T^S(K,λ)_m; printed 'J ⊂ T^S(K,λ)') with J^N = 0, and a continuous ρ_m: G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K,λ)_m/J) such that: (a) for each finite v ∉ S, the characteristic polynomial of ρ_m(Frob_v) is the image of P_v(X); (b) for each v | v̄, ρ_m|_{G_{F_v}} lies in the essential image of G^a with a = (λ_{τ,n})_{τ ∈ Hom(F_v,E)}; (c) for each v | v̄ there is M̄ ∈ MF_k with ρ̄_m|_{G_{F_v}} ≅ G(M̄) and FL_τ(M̄) = {λ_{τ,1}+n−1, λ_{τ,2}+n−2, …, λ_{τ,n}} for every τ: F_v ↪ E.
items.note: PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§4.4–4.5 | PA.1 | Degree shifting and Fontaine–Laffaille comparison'; PA.1: 'Combine with IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration's geometric concentration theorem to transfer the local p-adic Hodge condition.' ML.2 consumes it through PA. Proof, case (8a): Thm 2.4.10 gives π with r̄_ι(π) ≅ ρ̄_m; purity [Clo90, Lem. 4.9] gives λ_{τ,i}+λ_{τc,n+1−i} = w; choose τ_0 at ṽ maximizing λ_{τ_0,1}+λ_{τ_0c,1} and a crystalline ψ (item 131) so that λ' = λ+μ (μ = HT weights of ψ) satisfies Cor. 4.4.8(3); reduce to T^S(K,λ') by item 132 and Prop. 2.2.23; then HT_τ(ρ_x⊗ψ) is the n-element subset of FL_τ(N̄) whose sum Σ(λ'_{τ,i}+n−i) is forced by det ρ_x = r_ι(ω_π)ε^{n(1−n)/2} (ω_π of type A_0, HT_τ(r_ι(ω_π)) = {Σ_i λ_{τ,i}}), hence the bottom n. Case (8b): Cor. 4.4.8 for m and for m(ψ) with ψ|_{O^×_{F_ṽc}} = ∏τc, then Lemma 4.5.2.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1: R Γ(X_K, V_λ/ϖ^m)_m[−l(w)] is a T̃^S-equivariant direct summand of the boundary cohomology of X̃_K̃
items.statement: Notation (§4.2): for τ: F^+ ↪ E, W_τ = W(G̃⊗_{F^+,τ}E, T⊗_{F^+,τ}E) ≅ W(GL_{2n}), W_{P,τ} = W(G⊗E, T⊗E) ≅ W(GL_n×GL_n), W^P_τ ⊂ W_τ the representatives of W_{P,τ}\W_τ of §1.2, ρ_τ the half-sum of B⊗E-positive roots; W_v̄, W_{P,v̄}, W^P_v̄ the products over τ ∈ I_v̄ (embeddings inducing v̄), ρ_v̄ = Σ_{τ ∈ Hom(F^+_v̄,E)} ρ_τ; W_T̄, W^P_T̄ for T̄ ⊂ S̄_p, W = W_{S̄_p} with length l and ρ = Σ_v̄ ρ_v̄; λ̃_v̄ = (λ̃_τ)_{τ ∈ Hom(F^+_v̄,E)} and λ_v̄ = (λ_τ)_{τ inducing ṽ or ṽ^c}. Statement: let K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F^+}) be a good subgroup decomposed with respect to P with K̃_{U,v̄} = U(O_{F^+_v̄}) for every v̄ ∈ S̄_p, and K = K̃ ∩ G(A^∞_{F^+}); let m ⊂ T^S be non-Eisenstein and m̃ = S^*(m) ⊂ T̃^S. Let S̄_p = S̄_1 ⊔ S̄_2 and let λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)}, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} be dominant with (1) λ̃_v̄ = λ_v̄ (via (2.2.2)) for v̄ ∈ S̄_1; (2) λ̃_v̄ = 0 for v̄ ∈ S̄_2; (3) for each v̄ ∈ S̄_2 some w_v̄ ∈ W^P_v̄ with λ_v̄ = w_v̄(ρ_v̄) − ρ_v̄; (4) p > n² (p unramified in F throughout §4). Put w_v̄ = 1 for v̄ ∈ S̄_1 and w = (w_v̄). Then for every m ≥ 1, R Γ(X_K, V_λ/ϖ^m)_m[−l(w)] is a T̃^S-equivariant direct summand (T̃^S acting through S) of R Γ(∂X̃_K̃, V_λ̃/ϖ^m)_m̃.
items.note: Matrix: '§4.2 | ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces; TC.3 | Boundary summands and Hecke-normalized Levi maps'. PA.0: 'Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument and identify their twists and degree shifts.' ALS.4: 'admits a useful summand by an actual eigenvalue argument'. TC.3: 'For the symplectic/unitary parabolics whose Levi contains a restriction of scalars of GL_n, identify the boundary fibration and calculate the Hecke action through the Levi Satake map.' Proof: Thm 2.4.2 (reduction to the Siegel stratum X̃^P), the pushforward formula from the proof of Thm 2.4.4, Künneth over v̄ ∈ S̄ (prime-to-p factors K̃_{U,v̄} contribute only H^0 — left implicit), claim (1) for S̄_1 as at the end of Thm 2.4.4, claim (2) for S̄_2 from Lemmas 4.2.2 and 4.2.3.

items.name: R-equivariant direct summand in D(S)
items.statement: Let S be a ring, R an S-algebra (R is not introduced in the text), and A, B ∈ D(S) complexes with S-algebra maps f_A: R → End_{D(S)}(A), f_B: R → End_{D(S)}(B). A is an R-equivariant direct summand of B if there are C ∈ D(S) with an S-algebra map f_C: R → End_{D(S)}(C) and an isomorphism φ: B ≅ A ⊕ C in D(S) with f_B(r) = φ^{−1}∘(f_A(r) ⊕ f_C(r))∘φ for every r ∈ R.
items.note: PA.0: 'Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument … A splitting must be proved under the source's genericity condition; replace none by a formal direct-summand assumption.' This is the notion of summand those maps must realize (Hecke equivariance only in the derived category).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.2(1): cohomology of U(O_K) is the exterior algebra on Hom(U(O_K), O/ϖ^m)
items.statement: Let v̄ ∈ S̄_p, K = F^+_v̄ (a local field here), m ≥ 1. For each i ≥ 0 there is a G(O_K)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(U(O_K), O/ϖ^m) ≅ Hom_{Z_p}(∧^i_{Z_p} U(O_K), O/ϖ^m) = Hom_O(∧^i_O(U(O_K) ⊗_{Z_p} O), O/ϖ^m), with G(O_K) acting on the right through its conjugation action on U(O_K) ≅ Z_p^{n²[K:Q_p]} (continuous group cohomology; the map is the cup-product extension of H^1 = Hom).
items.note: Proof: Künneth for Z_p^{n²[K:Q_p]}. No stage computes continuous cohomology of Z_p^N with its Levi action: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1–R02.2 give generic continuous cohomology and Hochschild–Serre, and ALS.4's unipotent strata are the real nilmanifold fibres. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.2(2): integral Kostant decomposition of Hom_O(∧^i(U(O_K)⊗O), O) for p ≥ 2n−1
items.statement: Let v̄ ∈ S̄_p, K = F^+_v̄ and assume p ≥ 2n − 1. For w ∈ W^P_v̄ put λ_w = w(ρ_v̄) − ρ_v̄ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom_{Q_p}(F⊗_{F^+}F^+_v̄, E)} (via (2.2.2)). For each i ≥ 0 there is a G(O_K)-equivariant isomorphism Hom_O(∧^i_O(U(O_K) ⊗_{Z_p} O), O) ≅ ⊕_{w ∈ W^P_v̄, l(w) = i} V_{λ_w} (V_{λ_w} the integral dual Weyl module lattice).
items.note: PA.1: 'Construct integral algebraic coefficient modules over O, reduction modulo p, Weyl/dual Weyl modules … Prove the linkage and weight bounds actually used for degree shifting'; PA.0: 'identify their twists and degree shifts'. Proof: reduce to one τ; Kostant [Kos61] rationally (U is abelian, so Hom(∧^i n, E) = H^i(n, E)); V_{λ_w}⊗k simple for p ≥ 2n−1 [Jan03, Cor. II.5.6] (⟨λ_w+ρ_L, α^∨⟩ ≤ 2n−1); no extensions between the distinct bottom-alcove simples (remark after Cor. II.5.6) and [Jan03, Prop. I.4.18a]. Kostant's theorem on n-cohomology is not named by any stage (RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight has only Kostant's multiplicity formula); PA.0/PA.1 must supply it.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3: R Γ(U(O_K), O/ϖ^m) splits as the sum of its shifted cohomology when p > n²
items.statement: Let v̄ ∈ S̄_p, K = F^+_v̄, m ≥ 1 and p > n². There is a natural isomorphism, inducing the identity on cohomology, R Γ(U(O_K), O/ϖ^m) ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n²[K:Q_p]} H^i(U(O_K), O/ϖ^m)[−i] in D(O/ϖ^m[G(O_K)]).
items.note: PA.0: 'A splitting must be proved'; ALS.4: 'admits a useful summand by an actual eigenvalue argument'. The proof is such an argument: with f = [K:Q_p] and v̄ split in F, a central z ∈ (O_F⊗_{O_{F^+}}O_K)^× of order p^f−1 acts on U(O_K) by a primitive (p^f−1)-th root ζ, hence on the summand M_{(i_σ)} of H^i by ∏_σ σ(ζ)^{−i_σ}; for p > n², Σ_j i_j p^j mod (p^f−1) determines (i_j) except 0 ≡ p^f−1 (only when p = n²+1, degrees 0 and n²f), so idempotents e_i ∈ O[z] split τ_{≥1}R Γ by degree (idempotent completeness); H^0 is split off using claim (1) of the proof of Thm 4.2.1.

items.name: Definition 4.3.1(1): generic unramified local representation
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p, l ≠ p a prime and L/Q_l finite. A continuous r̄: G_L → GL_n(k) is generic if it is unramified and the eigenvalues α_1, …, α_n ∈ k̄ (with multiplicity) of r̄(Frob_L) satisfy α_i/α_j ≠ |O_L/m_L| for all i ≠ j.
items.note: AG2.7: 'At a completely split auxiliary prime p different from the coefficient prime ell, preserve precisely the residual condition α_i,v ≠ p α_j,v … Compare a stronger decomposed-generic API only as a separate specialization.' IG.7: 'Require a completely split p≠ell at which ρ_m is unramified and α_i≠p α_j for every i≠j.' Same routing as PAPER-QIAN-23 and PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. After [CS17, Def. 1.9] with the roles of p and l swapped.

items.name: Definition 4.3.1(2)–(3): decomposed generic primes and decomposed generic representations
items.statement: Let L be a number field and r̄: G_L → GL_n(k) continuous. A prime l ≠ p is decomposed generic for r̄ if l splits completely in L and r̄|_{G_{L_v}} is generic for every place v | l of L; r̄ is decomposed generic if some prime l ≠ p is decomposed generic for r̄. If r̄ and r̄' have the same associated projective representation, one is (decomposed) generic if and only if the other is.
items.note: As item 112 (AG2.7 'decomposed-generic API'; IG.7 hypothesis). The projective-invariance remark is folded in; it is used for twists ρ̄⊗ψ̄ in Cor. 4.4.8 and Thm 4.5.1.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.2: infinitely many decomposed generic primes
items.statement: Let L be a number field and r̄: G_L → GL_n(k) continuous and decomposed generic. Then there are infinitely many primes l ≠ p which are decomposed generic for r̄.
items.note: Proof: with K'/Q the Galois closure of the extension of L(ζ_p) cut out by r̄ and l_0 decomposed generic, every l unramified in K' with Frob_l, Frob_{l_0} conjugate in Gal(K'/Q) is decomposed generic (then l ≡ l_0 mod p); Chebotarev. Needed (tacitly) to choose the decomposed generic prime outside S, where Caraiani–Scholze need hyperspecial level. Library pointers (for parts only): Chebotarev density theorem (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4; FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration LI.4 imports 'Chebotarev'). Route: a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (AG2.0 algebraic weights and characters, AG2.7 decomposed genericity).

items.name: Theorem 4.3.3: middle-degree cohomology of X̃_K̃ is torsion free and surjects onto the boundary
items.statement: Let d = n²[F^+:Q] = ½ dim_R X̃ = dim_R X + 1. Assume [F^+:Q] > 1; let m̃ ⊂ T̃^S(K̃, λ̃) be a maximal ideal with ρ̄_m̃ of length at most 2; assume S satisfies: for every finite place w ∉ S of F with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic field F_0 ⊂ F; and assume ρ̄_m̃ decomposed generic. Then H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃)_m̃ → H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃[1/p])_m̃ is injective (H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃)_m̃ is O-torsion free) and H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃)_m̃ → H^d(∂X̃_K̃, V_λ̃)_m̃ is surjective.
items.note: IG.7: 'Export ACC+ Theorem 4.3.3's middle-degree injection into rational cohomology and surjection onto the boundary, with the source's level/ramification and [F^+:Q]>1 hypotheses.' Matrix: '§4.3 | IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration'. Proof: item 116, the sequence 0→V_λ̃→V_λ̃→V_λ̃/ϖ→0 (H^{d−1}(…/ϖ)_m̃ = 0 gives no ϖ-torsion) and excision for X̃_K̃ ⊂ X̃̄_K̃ (cokernel ⊂ H^{d+1}_c(…)_m̃ = 0). Caraiani–Scholze also need hyperspecial level at a decomposed generic prime; Lemma 4.3.2 lets one take it outside S (not said).

items.name: Caraiani–Scholze vanishing for X̃_K̃ (input to Theorem 4.3.3)
items.statement: ([CS19, Thm. 1.1], as used.) Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.3.3 ([F^+:Q] > 1, the condition on S, ρ̄_m̃ of length ≤ 2 and decomposed generic): H^i(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃/ϖ)_m̃ = 0 for i < d and H^i_c(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃/ϖ)_m̃ = 0 for i > d, where d = n²[F^+:Q].
items.locator: §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.3.3, p. 973 (also the introduction's statement of [CS19, Thm. 1.1])
items.note: IG.7: 'Prove the reusable source inequalities on the unitary arithmetic quotient: H^i(X_K,F_ell)_m=0 for i<d and H_c^i(X_K,F_ell)_m=0 for i>d.' IG.4–IG.6 supply the mechanism. [CS19] here is Caraiani–Scholze (the bibliography also uses [CS19] for Calegari–Specter;).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.4(i): S descends to T̃^S(H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃))_m̃ → T^S(H^{d−l(w)}(X_K, V_{λ_w}))_m
items.statement: Assume [F^+:Q] > 1. Let K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F^+}) be good and decomposed with respect to P (K = K̃ ∩ G), with K̃_{U,v̄} = U(O_{F^+_v̄}) for each v̄ ∈ S̄_p (a hypothesis of Theorem 4.2.1 that the proof needs and the statement omits), λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} and S̄_p = S̄_1 ⊔ S̄_2 with (1) λ̃_v̄ = 0 for v̄ ∈ S̄_2; (2) for every finite place w ∉ S of F with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic field F_0 ⊂ F; (3) p > n² (p unramified in F). Let w ∈ W^P_{S̄_2}, λ_w = w(λ̃+ρ) − ρ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, m ⊂ T^S non-Eisenstein in the support of H^*(X_K, V_{λ_w}), m̃ = S^*(m), and assume ρ̄_m̃ decomposed generic. Then S: T̃^S → T^S descends to a homomorphism T̃^S(H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃))_m̃ → T^S(H^{d−l(w)}(X_K, V_{λ_w}))_m.
items.note: PA.1: 'Combine with IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration's geometric concentration theorem'; IG.7: 'PA.1/PA.2 then own the degree-shifting applications.' Proof: Thm 4.3.3 + Thm 4.2.1; the latter is stated mod ϖ^m and the O-coefficient form needed here (limit over m, or Lemmas 4.2.2–4.2.3 over O) is left implicit.: Thm 4.2.1 also needs K̃_{U,v̄} = U(O_{F^+_v̄}) for v̄ ∈ S̄_2, which is not assumed.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.4(ii): the middle-degree Hecke algebra of X̃_K̃ is O-torsion free
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of item 117, T̃^S(H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃))_m̃ → T̃^S(H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃))_m̃[1/p] is injective.
items.note: IG.7: 'prove middle-degree torsion-freeness and the boundary exact sequence'. Immediate from Thm 4.3.3: the Hecke algebra acts faithfully on the O-torsion-free H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃)_m̃.

items.name: Definition 4.3.5: CTG weights ('cohomologically trivial for G')
items.statement: A weight λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} (printed Hom(F,E)) is CTG if for every w ∈ W^P, with λ_w = w(λ̃+ρ) − ρ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, and every i_0 ∈ Z, there is τ ∈ Hom(F,E) with λ_{w,τ} − λ^∨_{w,τc} ≠ (i_0, …, i_0) (λ^∨_{τ,i} = −λ_{τ,n+1−i}). Purpose (paragraph after the definition): by the purity lemma [Clo90, Lem. 4.9] no cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) has weight ιλ_w, so Theorem 2.4.11 computes H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃)_m̃[1/p] through cuspidal automorphic representations of G̃.
items.note: No stage names this condition. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.6: CTG weights exist after changing one embedding
items.statement: Assume [F^+:Q] > 1. Let λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} and τ_0: F^+ ↪ E. There is λ̃' ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} with λ̃'_τ = λ̃_τ for all τ ≠ τ_0 and λ̃' CTG; one may take λ̃'_{τ_0} = λ̃_{τ_0} + (a, 0, …, 0) with a ∈ Z_{≥0} sufficiently large (depending on λ̃).
items.note: The proof's sufficient criterion (4.3.7) has the wrong sign as printed: with '+' it reads Σ_i(μ_{w,τ̃,i} + μ_{w,τ̃c,i}) ≠ Σ_i(μ_{w,τ̃_0,i} + μ_{w,τ̃_0c,i}) for all w ∈ W^P (some τ ≠ τ_0), and raising λ̃_{τ_0,1} by a moves the τ_0 side by ±a for each of the finitely many w. (τ for τ_0). Used in Prop. 4.4.6 with τ_0 inducing v̄'. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Hecke algebras A(K,λ,q), A(K,λ,q,m) and Ã(K̃,λ̃)
items.statement: For m ⊂ T^S non-Eisenstein, m̃ := S^*(m) ⊂ T̃^S, and A(K,λ,q) = T^S(H^q(X_K, V_λ)_m), A(K,λ,q,m) = T^S(H^q(X_K, V_λ/ϖ^m)_m), Ã(K̃,λ̃) = T̃^S(H^d(X̃_K̃, V_λ̃)_m̃) (images of the abstract Hecke algebras in the endomorphisms of these cohomology groups). There is no natural map A(K,λ,q) → A(K,λ,q,m).
items.note: IHG.2: 'For a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex define its finite image algebras and compare chain, homotopy/derived and cohomology actions.'

items.name: Proposition 4.4.1: degree shifting to the middle degree of X̃ (degrees ⌊d/2⌋ ≤ q ≤ d−1)
items.statement: Let λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} and let v̄ ≠ v̄' be p-adic places of F^+ (so F^+ ≠ Q). Fix m ≥ 1 and a good K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F^+}) (K = K̃ ∩ G). Assume: (1) −λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,1} ≥ 0 for every τ: F ↪ E inducing v̄; (2) Σ_{v̄'' ∈ S̄_p, v̄'' ≠ v̄, v̄'} [F^+_{v̄''}:Q_p] > ½[F^+:Q]; (3) U(O_{F^+_{v̄''}}) ⊂ K̃_{v̄''} ⊂ {g ≡ (1_n *; 0 1_n) mod ϖ^m_{v̄''}} for every p-adic v̄'' ≠ v̄, and K̃_v̄ = G̃(O_{F^+_v̄}); (4) p > n²; (5) for every finite place w ∉ S of F with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic field F_0 ⊂ F; (6) m ⊂ T^S is non-Eisenstein and ρ̄_m̃ is decomposed generic. Define λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} by λ̃_τ = 0 if τ induces neither v̄ nor v̄', λ̃_τ = (−λ_{τ̃c,n}, …, −λ_{τ̃c,1}, λ_{τ̃,1}, …, λ_{τ̃,n}) if τ induces v̄ (dominant by (1)), and λ̃_τ ∈ Z^{2n}_+ arbitrary if τ induces v̄'. For m' ≥ m let K̃(m')_{v̄''} = K̃_{v̄''} ∩ {g ≡ (1_n *; 0 1_n) mod ϖ^{m'}_{v̄''}} for p-adic v̄'' ≠ v̄ and K̃(m')_{v̄''} = K̃_{v̄''} otherwise (K̃ = K̃(m)). Let q ∈ [⌊d/2⌋, d−1]. Then there are m' ≥ m, N ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F^+:Q], a nilpotent ideal J ⊂ A(K,λ,q,m) with J^N = 0, and a commutative square T̃^S → Ã(K̃(m'), λ̃) → A(K,λ,q,m)/J, T̃^S →^S T^S → A(K,λ,q,m)/J.
items.locator: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.1 (with Hypothesis 4.4.2 and (4.4.3)–(4.4.5) in its proof), pp. 975–978
items.note: Matrix: '§§4.4–4.5 | PA.1 | Degree shifting'. PA.1: 'Build the cohomological connecting morphisms and spectral-sequence comparison, with their Hecke equivariance and precise shifted degrees.' Proof by descending induction (Hypothesis 4.4.2): S̄_1 = {v̄,v̄'}, w ∈ W^P_{S̄_2} with l(w) = d−q (possible by (2)), λ'(q) = w(λ̃+ρ)−ρ (A(K,λ'(q),q,m) = A(K,λ,q,m) because K acts on V/ϖ^m through K_v̄); (4.4.3) 0→H^q(V)/ϖ^m→H^q(V/ϖ^m)→H^{q+1}(V)[ϖ^m]→0 and m' killing torsion give (4.4.4); duality (item 123) and HS (item 124) give (4.4.5); Prop. 4.3.4 and torsion-freeness (Thm 4.3.3) give J = image of S(Ann_{T̃^S} H^d(X̃_{K̃(m'')}, V_λ̃)_m̃) with J^{1+(d−q−1)N} = 0.

items.name: Poincaré duality for annihilators of localized mod ϖ^m cohomology of X_K
items.statement: Let m ⊂ T^S be non-Eisenstein and m^∨ = ι(m), where ι([K^S g K^S]) = [K^S g^{−1} K^S]; then m^∨ is non-Eisenstein and, for V = V_λ, Ann_{T^S} H^i(X_K, V/ϖ^m)_m = ι(Ann_{T^S} H^{d−1−i}(X_K, V^∨/ϖ^m)_{m^∨}) as ideals of T^S (d − 1 = dim_R X).
items.note: ALS.5:finite-level-duality: 'construct Poincaré–Lefschetz/Verdier duality for perfect coefficient complexes … Hecke adjoint formulas on the complexes'; the passage from H_c to H after localizing at a non-Eisenstein ideal is [NT16, Thm. 4.2], planned in ALS.4 ('Describe conditions under which boundary localization vanishes … by an actual eigenvalue argument'). In the text: Cor. 2.2.22 + [NT16, Thm. 4.2] + injectivity of O/ϖ^m over itself.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre inclusion of annihilators for a normal subgroup of finite index
items.statement: If K' ⊂ K is a normal good subgroup with (K')^S = K^S, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H^i(K/K', H^j(X_{K'}, V)_m) ⇒ H^{i+j}(X_K, V)_m gives ∏_{j=0}^{q} Ann_{T^S} H^j(X_{K'}, V)_m ⊂ Ann_{T^S} H^q(X_K, V)_m (V a finite O/ϖ^m[K_S]-module, e.g. V_λ/ϖ^m or V^∨_λ/ϖ^m).
items.locator: §4.4, proofs of Proposition 4.4.1 (p. 978) and Corollary 4.4.8 (p. 983); used again in Theorem 4.5.1 (p. 986)
items.note: ALS.6: 'Prove finite-level descent and the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application'; IHG.2: 'support and annihilator lemmas'.

items.name: Proposition 4.4.6: Fontaine–Laffaille property of ρ_m on A(K,λ,q,m) for ⌊d/2⌋ ≤ q ≤ d−1
items.statement: Let λ, v̄ ≠ v̄', m ≥ 1 and a good K̃ satisfy (1) −λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,1} ≥ 0 and −λ_{τc,n} − λ_{τ,n} ≤ p − 2n − 1 for every τ inducing v̄, and (2)–(6) of Proposition 4.4.1. Let q ∈ [⌊d/2⌋, d−1], and (for (c), which the statement gives without it) assume A(K,λ,q,m) ≠ 0. Then there are N ≥ 1 depending only on [F:Q] and n, an ideal J ⊂ A(K,λ,q,m) with J^N = 0 and a continuous ρ_m: G_{F,S} → GL_n(A(K,λ,q,m)/J) with (a) char(ρ_m(Frob_v)) = image of P_v(X) for v ∉ S; (b) for each v | v̄, ρ_m|_{G_{F_v}} is in the essential image of G^a, a = (λ_{τ,n})_{τ ∈ Hom_{Q_p}(F_v,E)}; (c) for each v | v̄ there is N̄ ∈ MF_k with ρ̄_m̃|_{G_{F_v}} ≅ G(N̄) and FL_τ(N̄) = {−λ_{τc,n}+2n−1, …, −λ_{τc,1}+n, λ_{τ,1}+n−1, …, λ_{τ,n}} for every τ ∈ Hom_{Q_p}(F_v,E), where ρ̄_m̃ = ρ̄_m ⊕ ρ̄_m^{c,∨}ε^{1−2n}.
items.note: PA.1: 'Combine with IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration's geometric concentration theorem to transfer the local p-adic Hodge condition.' Proof: take λ̃ CTG (Lemma 4.3.6 at v̄'); Prop. 4.4.1; Ã O-flat (Thm 4.3.3); Thm 2.4.11; Thm 2.3.3 gives ρ̃ over Ã⊗Q̄_p, crystalline at v | v̄ (its part (c) at l = p with K̃_v̄ hyperspecial) with HT_τ as in (c); lattice criterion (item 105) since the width is ≤ p−2; distinct weights ⇒ ρ̄_m|_{G_{F_v}} ≇ (ρ̄_m^{c,∨}ε^{1−2n})|_{G_{F_v}}; determinant transfer (item 126); Thm 2.3.7 for ρ_m; N = N_0+N_1.: (c) needs A(K,λ,q,m) ≠ 0.

items.name: Transfer of the Fontaine–Laffaille property from a flat determinant to a nilpotent quotient (step in Prop. 4.4.6)
items.statement: Let Ã be a finite flat O-algebra, D̃ a continuous 2n-dimensional determinant of G_{F,S} valued in Ã ([Che14, Ex. 2.32]) such that for each v | v̄ the G_{F_v}-module Ã[G_{F,S}]/ker D̃ lies in the essential image of G^a. Let Ã → A/J be a homomorphism with D̃ ⊗_Ã A/J = det(ρ ⊕ ρ'), where ρ, ρ': G_{F,S} → GL_n(A/J) have absolutely irreducible, non-isomorphic residual representations. Then (A/J)[G_{F,S}]/ker(D̃_{A/J}) = M_n(A/J) × M_n(A/J), this algebra is a quotient of Ã[G_{F,S}]/ker D̃, and hence ρ|_{G_{F_v}} lies in the essential image of G^a. Inputs: kernels of determinants commute with flat base change; [Che14, §1.17, Thm 2.12, Thm 2.22(i),(ii), Lem. 1.18].
items.note: IHG.1: 'Construct the characteristic-polynomial ideal and Cayley–Hamilton quotient, faithful determinant descent and generalized matrix algebra decompositions under residually multiplicity-free hypotheses'; IHG.0: 'Define a determinant … direct sum/product … scalar extension'; the Fontaine–Laffaille transfer itself is PA.1's. Remark 4.4.7 points to more general ideas of Wake–Wang-Erickson [WWE19], which no stage plans.

items.name: Corollary 4.4.8: Fontaine–Laffaille property of ρ_m on A(K,λ,q,m) in all degrees 0 ≤ q ≤ d−1
items.statement: Let v̄ ∈ S̄_p (printed S_p), K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) good, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, m ⊂ T^S(K,λ) non-Eisenstein. Assume: (1) K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v | v̄; (2) there is v̄' ∈ S̄_p, v̄' ≠ v̄, with Σ_{v̄'' ∈ S̄_p, v̄'' ≠ v̄, v̄'} [F^+_{v̄''}:Q_p] > ½[F^+:Q]; (3) −λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,1} ≥ 0 and −λ_{τc,n} − λ_{τ,n} ≤ p − 1 − 2n for every τ inducing v̄; (4) p > n²; (5) for every finite place w ∉ S of F with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic field F_0 ⊂ F; (6) ρ̄_m is decomposed generic. Then for all integers q ∈ [0, d−1] and m ≥ 1 there are N ≥ 1 depending only on [F:Q] and n, J ⊂ A(K,λ,q,m) with J^N = 0, and a continuous ρ_m: G_{F,S} → GL_n(A(K,λ,q,m)/J) satisfying (a), (b), (c) of Proposition 4.4.6.
items.note: PA.1 as for Prop. 4.4.6 ('Degree shifting and Fontaine–Laffaille comparison'). Proof: (i) assuming ρ̄_m̃ decomposed generic, choose K̃ with K̃∩G = K, pass to principal-congruence level at p-adic v̄'' ≠ v̄ via HS (item 124) and Carayol (item 128); degrees ≥ ⌊d/2⌋ by Prop. 4.4.6, degrees < ⌊d/2⌋ by duality and twist (item 129); (ii) reduce (6) to decomposed genericity of ρ̄_m̃ by a prime-to-p twist ψ (item 130) and Prop. 2.2.23.

items.name: Carayol's theorem: conjugating a product representation into the image of the Hecke algebra
items.statement: ([Car94, Théorème 2], as used.) Let ρ_i: G_{F,S} → GL_n(A_i) (i = 0, …, q) be continuous, where the A_i are finite local T^S-algebras, with a common absolutely irreducible residual representation and characteristic polynomials of Frobenius in the image R of T^S → ∏_i A_i. Then ∏_i ρ_i is conjugate to a representation valued in GL_n(R).
items.note: IHG.1: 'Prove reconstruction … over complete local rings when residual absolute irreducibility supplies an actual representation.' Used in Cor. 4.4.8 and, via 'just as in the proof of Corollary 4.4.8', in Thm 4.5.1.

items.name: Degree reflection by duality and a cyclotomic twist (step in Cor. 4.4.8)
items.statement: Assume K is principal-congruence of level ϖ^m at the p-adic places ≠ v̄, λ_{v̄''} = 0 for p-adic v̄'' ≠ v̄, and λ satisfies (3) of Cor. 4.4.8. Then V_{λ^∨} ≅ V_λ^∨ ([Jan03, Cor. II.5.6]). With n_0 = (2n+1−p)/2 and μ_{0,τ} = (n_0, …, n_0), the maximal ideal m^∨(ε^{−n_0}) lies in the support of H^*(X_K, V_{λ^∨+μ_0}), λ^∨+μ_0 again satisfies (3), and [K^S g K^S] ↦ ε(Art_F(det g))^{−n_0}[K^S g^{−1} K^S] (printed Art_K) descends to an isomorphism f: T^S(H^{d−1−q'}(X_K, V_{λ^∨+μ_0}/ϖ^m))_{m^∨(ε^{−n_0})} ≅ A(K,λ,q',m); a representation ρ' for the left side gives ρ = (f∘ρ')^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−2n+(p−1)/2} for the right side, with the same properties (a)–(c).
items.note: PA.1: 'Weyl/dual Weyl modules … the linkage and weight bounds actually used for degree shifting'; ALS.5:finite-level-duality: 'Hecke adjoint formulas'. Twisting is Prop. 2.2.23 (§2; ALS per the matrix). Check not in the text: ρ̄ for m^∨(ε^{−n_0}) doubled is ≅ ρ̄_m̃^∨ ⊗ ε̄^{1−n−n_0} because 2(n−n_0) = p−1, so hypothesis (6) of Prop. 4.4.6 holds for the dual ideal.

items.name: Existence of a twist making ρ̄_m̃ decomposed generic (step in Cor. 4.4.8)
items.statement: (Asserted without proof.) If ρ̄_m is decomposed generic then, after enlarging k, there is a character ψ̄: G_F → k^× with ψ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial for every v ∈ S such that (ρ̄_m ⊗ ψ̄) ⊕ ((ρ̄_m ⊗ ψ̄)^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n}) is decomposed generic.
items.note: No proof is given and no stage states it. It follows from class field theory (Grunwald–Wang for odd, prime-to-p order): at a decomposed generic l ∉ S prescribe ψ̄(Frob_v)ψ̄(Frob_{v^c}) for v | l to avoid the finitely many values making a cross ratio equal to l. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Existence of a crystalline character ψ with prescribed restriction to O^×_{F_{ṽ^c}} (step in Thm 4.5.1)
items.statement: ([HSBT10, Lem. 2.2], as used.) After enlarging E there is a continuous ψ: G_F → O^×, crystalline at every v | p, unramified at ṽ and at every v ∈ S − S_p, with ψ∘Art_{F_{ṽ^c}}|_{O^×_{F_{ṽ^c}}} = ∏_{τ: F_ṽ ↪ E}(τc)^{λ_{τ_0,1}+λ_{τ_0c,1}}; in case (8b), a ψ crystalline at every v' | p, unramified at ṽ, with ψ∘Art_{F_{ṽ^c}} = ∏_{τ: F_ṽ ↪ E}(τc) on O^×_{F_{ṽ^c}}.
items.note: This is the existence of an algebraic Hecke character of type A_0 of the CM field F with prescribed local behaviour, and of its p-adic Galois avatar. No stage states it. Such ψ must have non-zero HT weights above each v̄'' ≠ v̄ (h_τ + h_{τc} is constant ≠ 0), which is the point of Route: a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (AG2.0 algebraic weights and characters, AG2.7 decomposed genericity).

items.name: Hecke algebra as inverse limit of mod ϖ^m derived Hecke algebras, with nilpotent kernel to cohomology
items.statement: For K good and λ' dominant, R Γ(X_K, V_{λ'}) is perfect with cohomology in degrees [0, d−1] (Lemma 2.1.7), so T^S(K,λ') → lim_{m≥1} T^S(R Γ(X_K, V_{λ'}/ϖ^m)) is an isomorphism ([NT16, Lem. 3.11]); and for each m ≥ 1 the kernel I of T^S(R Γ(X_K, V_{λ'}/ϖ^m)) → ∏_q T^S(H^q(X_K, V_{λ'}/ϖ^m)) satisfies I^d = 0 ([KT17, Lem. 2.5]).
items.note: IHG.2: 'Establish the nilpotence bound for the ideal of degree-zero derived endomorphisms acting trivially on all cohomology of a bounded-amplitude object'; IHG.4: 'passage to inverse limits'. Assembling the degree-wise ideals over q and m into one J' ⊂ T^S(K,λ')_{m(ψ)} with bounded exponent (compatible choices in the inverse limit, and Carayol over the degrees) is left implicit in the text.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.2: recovering a partition from two shifted partitions
items.statement: Let m ≥ 1 and let A, B, C, D be sets of integers, each of size m, with c > d for all c ∈ C and d ∈ D. If A ∪ B = C ∪ D and (A+1) ∪ B = (C+1) ∪ D, and both sets have 2m elements, then A = C and B = D.
items.note: Elementary induction (max C lies in A, min D lies in B). Used only at the end of Thm 4.5.1, case (8b), with A = FL_τ(M̄'), B = FL_τ(M̄), C = {−λ_{τc,n}+2n−1, …, −λ_{τc,1}+n}, D = {λ_{τ,1}+n−1, …, λ_{τ,n}}. Not in Mathlib; trivial to formalize. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Setup of §5: the level subgroups K(b,c), the ordinary Hecke algebra T^{S,ord}, U_v and U_p
items.statement: Standing data: F a CM field, n ≥ 1, p a prime, E/Q_p finite containing the images of all embeddings F ↪ Q̄_p; standing hypothesis for all of §5: F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits (p may ramify in F). Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, S a finite set of finite places of F containing S_p and stable under c, such that (i) for every finite v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic subfield of F; (ii) K_v = Iw_v for v | p and K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for finite v ∉ S. For integers c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1, K(b,c) ⊂ K is the good subgroup with K(b,c)_v = K_v for v ∤ p and K(b,c)_v = Iw_v(b,c) for v | p; K(0,1) = K and K(0,c)/K(b,c) ≅ ∏_{v|p} T_n(O_{F_v}/ϖ_v^b). Define T^{S,ord} = T^S ⊗_O O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧[{U_{v,1},…,U_{v,n},U_{v,n}^{-1}}_{v|p}] (U_{v,i} formal variables), U_v = U_{v,1}U_{v,2}⋯U_{v,n−1}, U_p = ∏_{v|p} U_v. The canonical surjection O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧ → O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)] extends to T^{S,ord} → End_{D(O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)])}(RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)), U_{v,i} acting by the double coset operator [Iw_v(b,c) diag(ϖ_v,…,ϖ_v,1,…,1) Iw_v(b,c)] (i entries ϖ_v). Additional standing hypothesis for §§5.2–5.5: ϖ_{v^c} = ϖ_v^c for every v | p; the U_{v,i} depend on ϖ_v but RΓ^ord, T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord and the truth of Theorem 5.5.1 do not.
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses'. PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§5.4–5.5 | PA.2 | Ordinary degree shifting/local compatibility'. The operators U_{v,i}, U_v are those of §2.2.5 (p. 923). The printed definition of K(b,c) has a slip (K_v for K(b,c)_v;

items.name: Ordinary part RΓ^ord and the ordinary Hecke algebra T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord; Galois-type and non-Eisenstein ideals of T^{S,ord}
items.statement: In the setting of the previous item, there is a well-defined direct summand RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)^ord of RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ) in D(O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)]) on which U_p acts invertibly (theory of ordinary parts, [KT17 §2.4]). T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord is the image of T^{S,ord} → End_{D(O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)])}(RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)^ord), i.e. T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord = T^{S,ord}(RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)^ord). There is a canonical homomorphism T^S(K(0,c)/K(b,c), V_λ) → T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord (in general neither injective nor surjective); consequently every maximal ideal 𝔪 of T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord has an associated ρ̄_𝔪: G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord/𝔪). A maximal ideal of T^{S,ord} with residue field finite over k is of Galois type (resp. non-Eisenstein) if its pullback to T^S is so in the sense of Definition 2.3.6.
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses'. L0a: 'For an endomorphism U of a finite underlying module, prove the Fitting decomposition into its eventually invertible image and eventually killed kernel' and 'Apply the result degreewise to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U' (the finite-quotient projector supplying the summand).

items.name: The characters χ_{λ,v,i}
items.statement: The operators U_{v,i} are invertible in T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord (because U_p is). For each v | p and i = 1,…,n, χ_{λ,v,i}: G_{F_v} → (T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord)^× is the unique continuous character with χ_{λ,v,i}(Art_{F_v}(u)) = ε^{1−i}(Art_{F_v}(u)) · ∏_{τ∈Hom_{Q_p}(F_v,E)} τ(u)^{−(w_0^G λ)_{τ,i}} · ⟨diag(1,…,u,…,1)⟩ for u ∈ O_{F_v}^× (u in the i-th diagonal entry), and χ_{λ,v,i}(Art_{F_v}(ϖ_v)) = ε^{1−i}(Art_{F_v}(ϖ_v)) · U_{v,i}/U_{v,i−1} (with U_{v,0} = 1).
items.note: PA.2: 'Prove the ordinary degree-shifting comparison independently of PA.1, preserving the resulting filtration of the Galois representation and its characters'. The same characters (for λ(a) and v ∈ S_p) are the diagonal characters in Theorem 5.5.1(b),(c) and Proposition 5.4.18.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.1: local–global compatibility at l = p, ordinary case
