items.statement: Assume the §5 standing hypotheses (F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits; ϖ_{v^c} = ϖ_v^c) and [F^+:Q] > 1. Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup with K_v = Iw_v for each v ∈ S_p (and K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S), let c ≥ b ≥ 0 be integers with c ≥ 1, let λ be a weight (printed λ ∈ (Z^n)^{Hom(F,E)}; the objects require λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}), and let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal. Suppose (1) for every finite place v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or there is an imaginary quadratic F_0 ⊂ F in which l splits; (2) ρ̄_𝔪 is decomposed generic. Then there exist an integer N ≥ 1 depending only on [F^+:Q] and n, an ideal J ⊂ T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord_𝔪 with J^N = 0, and a continuous ρ_𝔪: G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord_𝔪/J) such that: (a) for every finite v ∉ S, det(X − ρ_𝔪(Frob_v)) is the image of P_v(X); (b) for every v ∈ S_p and g ∈ G_{F_v}, det(X − ρ_𝔪(g)) = ∏_{i=1}^n (X − χ_{λ,v,i}(g)); (c) for every v ∈ S_p and g_1,…,g_n ∈ G_{F_v}, (ρ_𝔪(g_1) − χ_{λ,v,1}(g_1))(ρ_𝔪(g_2) − χ_{λ,v,2}(g_2))⋯(ρ_𝔪(g_n) − χ_{λ,v,n}(g_n)) = 0.
items.locator: §5.1, Theorem 5.5.1, p. 991; restated and proved in §5.5, pp. 1026–1027
items.note: PA.2: 'Prove the ordinary degree-shifting comparison independently of PA.1, preserving the resulting filtration of the Galois representation and its characters'; 'An eigenvalue called a unit is not sufficient to assert an ordinary Galois filtration.' PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§5.4–5.5 | PA.2 | Ordinary degree shifting/local compatibility'. Proof: reduce as in Theorem 4.5.1 to A(K,λ,q,m) = T^{S,ord}(H^q(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ/ϖ^m)^ord_𝔪), 0 ≤ q ≤ d−1; Hochschild–Serre and Cor 5.2.16 give c = b ≥ m; Cor 5.2.18 replaces λ by the weight of Prop 5.4.18; Prop 5.4.18 in degrees q, q+1 and 0 → H^q/ϖ^m → H^q(V_λ/ϖ^m) → H^{q+1}[ϖ^m] → 0 finish. Condition (c) is the determinant-ordinary identity whose deformation-side counterpart LocalGaloisDeformationRings:L8 owns; Lemma 6.2.11 converts it into a flag over a field with distinct characters. Consumed in §6.5 (ordinary automorphy lifting). The n = 1 case is not covered by the written proof (Lemma 5.4.8(3)(a) fails for n = 1; see issues).

items.name: Smooth modules over a monoid (§5.2.1, (5.2.2)–(5.2.3))
items.statement: Fix m ≥ 1 and work with O/ϖ^m-coefficients. For a locally profinite group G, Mod(O/ϖ^m[G]) is the category of O/ϖ^m[G]-modules and Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[G]) ⊂ Mod(O/ϖ^m[G]) the full subcategory of smooth modules (5.2.2). For an open submonoid Δ ⊂ G containing an open compact subgroup of G, Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) ⊂ Mod(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) (5.2.3) is the full subcategory of modules in which every vector is fixed by an open subgroup of Δ; M ↦ M^sm (smooth vectors) is right adjoint to the inclusion (5.2.3). D_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) denotes the derived category of Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]).
items.note: PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds'. SR.0: 'Construct smooth vectors in an arbitrary representation and prove the relevant adjunction' (group case only; the monoid version is PA.2's). SR.0:derived-extension 'constructs the enhanced derived smooth category'.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.4: smooth modules over a monoid have enough injectives; restriction preserves injectives
items.statement: Let Δ ⊂ G be an open submonoid of a locally profinite group containing an open compact subgroup. (1) Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) is abelian and has enough injectives. (2) If Δ' ⊂ Δ is a subgroup which is either compact or open (hence locally profinite), the forgetful functor Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ']) preserves injectives.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'; PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds'. SR.0: 'construct kernels, cokernels and the abelian category'; SR.2: 'compact induction ... Frobenius reciprocity with correct adjoint direction'. Proof: (−)^sm has an exact left adjoint; c-Ind_{Δ'}^{Δ} is an exact left adjoint for open Δ'; the compact case reduces to [Eme10b, Prop. 2.1.11]. No stage names 'enough injectives' for the monoid category explicitly.

items.name: Positive monoids, T_n(O_{F,p})(b), u_p, B_n(F_p)^+ and the T^{S,ord}-action on complexes over T_n(F_p)^+_b
items.statement: T_n(F_p)^+ ⊂ T_n(F_p) is the open submonoid of t with t N_n(O_{F,p}) t^{-1} ⊂ N_n(O_{F,p}); T_n(F_v)^+ = T_n(F_v) ∩ T_n(F_p)^+; Δ_p = ∏_{v|p} Iw_v T_n(F_v)^+ Iw_v (§2.2.5). For b ≥ 0: T_n(O_{F,p})(b) = ∏_{v∈S_p} ker(T_n(O_{F_v}) → T_n(O_{F_v}/ϖ_v^b)), T_n(O_{F,p})_b = T_n(O_{F,p})/T_n(O_{F,p})(b), T_n(F_p)^+_b = T_n(F_p)^+/T_n(O_{F,p})(b), T_n(F_p)_b = T_n(F_p)/T_n(O_{F,p})(b). u_p = (p^{n−1}, p^{n−2}, …, 1) ∈ T_n(Q_p) ⊂ T_n(F_p) lies in T_n(F_p)^+. B_n(F_p)^+ = N_n(O_{F,p})·T_n(F_p)^+ ⊂ Δ_p; B_n(O_{F,p})(b) is the preimage of T_n(O_{F,p})(b) in B_n(O_{F,p}). Every C ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]) carries a functorial homomorphism O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧[{U_{v,1},…,U_{v,n},U_{v,n}^{-1}}_{v∈S_p}] → End(C), via O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧ → O/ϖ^m[T_n(O_{F,p})_b] and U_{v,i} ↦ diag(ϖ_v,…,ϖ_v,1,…,1) ∈ T_n(F_v) (i entries ϖ_v); hence a T^S-action on C extends to a T^{S,ord}-action.
items.note: PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds'; PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses' ('commuting positive-monoid operators').

items.name: The characters O(λ) and the kernel K_λ of the lowest-weight projection
items.statement: For λ ∈ X^*((Res_{F/Q}T_n)_E) = (Z^n)^{Hom(F,E)}, O(λ) is the free rank-one O-module on which u ∈ T_n(O_{F,p}) acts by ∏_{τ∈Hom(F,E)} ∏_{i=1}^n τ(u_i)^{λ_{τ,i}} and every diag(ϖ_v^{a_1},…,ϖ_v^{a_n}) (a_i ∈ Z) acts trivially. For dominant λ, projection to the lowest weight space gives an O-linear map V_λ → O(w_0^G λ) which is B_n(F_p)^+-equivariant (·_p-action of §2.2.5 on the source, action through the projection to T_n(F_p) on the target); K_λ := ker(V_λ → O(w_0^G λ)) is an O[B_n(F_p)^+]-module, finite free over O.
items.note: PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds' ('normalization'). The lattices V_λ with twisted ·_p-action come from §2.2.5 (PA.1 plans the integral coefficient modules and their highest-weight filtrations).

items.name: The ordinary-parts functors Γ(N_n(O_{F,p}),−), Γ(B_n(O_{F,p})(b),−), Γ(Iw_p(b,c),−), Γ(T_n(O_{F,p})(b),−), ord and ord_b
items.statement: Γ(N_n(O_{F,p}),−): Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]) is N_n(O_{F,p})-invariants with t ∈ T_n(F_p)^+ acting by t·v = Σ_{n∈N_n(O_{F,p})/tN_n(O_{F,p})t^{-1}} n t v (5.2.5), i.e. by the double coset operator [N_n(O_{F,p}) t N_n(O_{F,p})]. Γ(B_n(O_{F,p})(b),−): Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]) is B_n(O_{F,p})(b)-invariants with the same formula. For c ≥ b ≥ 0, c ≥ 1, Iw_p(b,c) = ∏_{v∈S_p} Iw_v(b,c) and Γ(Iw_p(b,c),−): Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]), t acting by [Iw_p(b,c) t Iw_p(b,c)]. Γ(T_n(O_{F,p})(b),−) maps Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]) and Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]). ord = − ⊗_{O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]} O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]: Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]) and ord_b = − ⊗_{O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]} O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]: Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]) (localizations; on modules finite over O/ϖ^m they agree with the maximal summand on which the torus acts invertibly, [Eme10b, Lem. 3.2.1]).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'; 'At coefficient characteristic equal to residue characteristic it is not the exact Jacquet functor of the ell-not-p theory.' PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§5.2–5.3 | PA.2; PadicFamilies (finite-module projector only) | General-rank CM/unitary ordinary towers and characteristic-p ordinary parts of parabolic induction'.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.6: ord commutes with T_n(O_{F,p})(b)-invariants
items.statement: For b ≥ 0 the square Γ(T_n(O_{F,p})(b),−) ∘ ord ≅ ord_b ∘ Γ(T_n(O_{F,p})(b),−) of functors Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]) commutes up to natural isomorphism; i.e. the natural map M^{T_n(O_{F,p})(b)} ⊗_{O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]} O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b] → (M ⊗_{O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]} O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)])^{T_n(O_{F,p})(b)} is an isomorphism for every smooth M.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.7(1): N_n(O_{F,p})-invariants send injectives to T_n(O_{F,p})(b)-acyclics
items.statement: The functors Γ(N_n(O_{F,p}),−), Γ(B_n(O_{F,p})(b),−) and Γ(Iw_p(b,c),−) on Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]) are left exact, and for every b ≥ 0 the functor Γ(N_n(O_{F,p}),−) sends injective objects of Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]) to Γ(T_n(O_{F,p})(b),−)-acyclic objects of Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. Proof restricts to B_n(O_{F,p})(b) and T_n(O_{F,p})(b) (Lemma 5.2.4(2)) and uses that N_n-invariants has the exact left adjoint 'inflation'.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.7(2): ord and ord_b are exact and preserve injectives
items.statement: The localization functors ord: Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]) and ord_b: Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]) are exact and preserve injectives.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. ord_b: localization of the Noetherian ring O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)^+_b]; ord: Zorn's-lemma extension argument via Lemma 5.2.6.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.8: ordinary parts of Iwahori and B_n(O)(b) invariants agree
items.statement: For c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1 there is a natural isomorphism ord_b ∘ Γ(Iw_p(b,c),−) ≅ ord_b ∘ Γ(B_n(O_{F,p})(b),−) of functors Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]) → Mod(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]), induced by the inclusion V^{Iw_p(b,c)} ⊂ V^{B_n(O_{F,p})(b)} (which is T_n(F_p)^+_b-equivariant because Iw_p(b,c) has an Iwahori decomposition).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements' ('control statements'). Uses [Ger19, Lem. 2.19]: Iw_p(b,c') u_p Iw_p(b,c') is left Iw_p(b,c'−1)-invariant.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.9: comparison of derived ordinary parts
items.statement: Let π ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]) be bounded below. For c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1 there is a natural isomorphism RΓ(T_n(O_{F,p})(b), ord RΓ(N_n(O_{F,p}), π)) ≅ ord_b RΓ(Iw_p(b,c), π) in D(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. Proof: Grothendieck composition [Wei94, Cor. 10.8.3] with Lemmas 5.2.6–5.2.8 (Library pointers (for parts only): composition of right derived functors).

items.name: Weight-λ completed cohomology π(K^p,λ,m), π(K^p,m) and T^S(K^p,m) (§5.2.10, (5.2.11)–(5.2.13))
items.statement: For K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) good there are functors Γ_{K^p,sm}: Mod(O/ϖ^m[G^∞]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[G(F_p^+)]) and Mod(O/ϖ^m[G^{p,∞}×Δ_p]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]), M ↦ Γ(K^p,M)^sm. For λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, π(K^p,λ,m) := RΓ_{K^p,sm} RΓ(𝔛_G, V_λ/ϖ^m) ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p]). If K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(O_{F_v}) it carries T^S → End_{D_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ_p])}(π(K^p,λ,m)) (5.2.11), and for K_p ⊂ Δ_p a canonical T^S-equivariant isomorphism RΓ(K_p, π(K^p,λ,m)) ≅ RΓ(X_K, V_λ/ϖ^m) in D(O/ϖ^m) (5.2.12). π(K^p,m) := RΓ_{K^p,sm} RΓ(𝔛_G, O/ϖ^m) ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[G(F_p^+)]) carries T^S → End_{D_sm(O/ϖ^m[G(F_p^+)])}(π(K^p,m)) (5.2.13), recovering (5.2.11) for λ = 0; T^S(K^p,m) := image of (5.2.13).
items.note: CC.1: 'Construct the filtered colimit at fixed s in modules and derived modules ... the action of the full local group by conjugating levels ... Construct commuting tame Hecke operators'. CC.6: 'Give the derived invariants formulation ... comparing tower cohomology and fixed-level cohomology' (5.2.12). PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds' ('derived limits').

items.name: Lemma 5.2.14: the completed Hecke algebra is semi-local and complete
items.statement: Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup. Then T^S(K^p,m) is a semi-local ring, complete for the J-adic topology defined by its Jacobson radical J, and for each maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K^p,m) there is a unique idempotent e_𝔪 ∈ T^S(K^p,m) with e_𝔪 H^*(π(K^p,m)) = H^*(π(K^p,m))_𝔪. Consequently the localization π(K^p,m)_𝔪 ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[G(F_p^+)]) is defined.
items.note: CC.8: 'Transport finite-level Galois and tame Hecke actions ... and construct localisation at a specified residual Hecke ideal'. Source proof is a citation: [GN22 (Gee–Newton), Lem. 2.1.14].

items.name: The ordinary part of completed cohomology π^ord(K^p,λ,m)
items.statement: π^ord(K^p,λ,m) := ord RΓ(N_n(O_{F,p}), π(K^p,λ,m)) ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]); for λ = 0 it is written π^ord(K^p,m).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'; PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§5.2–5.3 | PA.2; PadicFamilies (finite-module projector only) | General-rank CM/unitary ordinary towers and characteristic-p ordinary parts of parabolic induction'.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.15: completed versus classical ordinary cohomology
items.statement: Let K ⊂ G^∞ be a good subgroup with K_v = Iw_v for each v | p and K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(O_{F_v}), and let c ≥ b ≥ 0 be integers with c ≥ 1. For every λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} there is a T^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphism RΓ(T_n(O_{F,p})(b), π^ord(K^p,λ,m)) ≅ RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ/ϖ^m)^ord in D(O/ϖ^m[K(0,c)/K(b,c)]) (K(0,c)/K(b,c) ≅ T_n(O_{F,p})_b).
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses'. L0a: 'For an endomorphism U of a finite underlying module, prove the Fitting decomposition into its eventually invertible image and eventually killed kernel' and 'Apply the result degreewise to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U'; the proof reduces to: for M finite over O/ϖ^m with endomorphism U, M^ord → M ⊗_{O/ϖ^m[U]} O/ϖ^m[U,U^{-1}] is an isomorphism [Eme10b, Lem. 3.2.1].

items.name: Corollary 5.2.16 (Independence of level)
items.statement: Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be good with K_v = Iw_v for v | p and K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(O_{F_v}); let c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1 and λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}. The natural morphism RΓ_{K(0,max(1,b))/K(b,max(1,b))}(X_{K(b,max(1,b))}, V_λ/ϖ^m)^ord → RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ/ϖ^m)^ord in D(O/ϖ^m[T_n(O_{F,p})_b]) is an isomorphism.
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses' ('prove the stabilization hypotheses'); PA.2 also 'the required adjunction/control statements'. Used in the proof of Theorem 5.5.1 and in §6.5.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.17: independence of weight for completed ordinary cohomology
items.statement: Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be good with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(O_{F,v}) and λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}. There are T^S-equivariant isomorphisms in D(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]): π^ord(K^p,λ,m) ≅ ord RΓ(N_n(O_{F,p}), RΓ_{K^p,sm} RΓ(𝔛_G, O(w_0^G λ)/ϖ^m)) ≅ π^ord(K^p,m) ⊗_O O(w_0^G λ).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements' ('control statements'); PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds'. Key input: u_p^N K_λ/ϖ^m = 0 for N ≫ 0 (cf. [Ger19, Prop. 2.22]).

items.name: Corollary 5.2.18 (Independence of weight)
items.statement: Let K be good with K_v = Iw_v for v | p and K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(O_{F_v}); c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1. For λ, λ' ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} with O(w_0^G λ)/ϖ^m ≅ O(w_0^G λ')/ϖ^m as O/ϖ^m[T_n(O_{F,p})(b)]-modules there is a T^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphism RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ/ϖ^m)^ord ≅ RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_{λ'}/ϖ^m)^ord ⊗_O O(w_0^G λ) ⊗_O O((w_0^G λ')^{-1}) in D(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)_b]).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements' ('control statements'). Combine Props 5.2.15 and 5.2.17. Used in the proof of Theorem 5.5.1.

items.name: Hida theory for G̃ (§5.2.19): T̃^{S,ord}, Ũ_v, Ũ_p, K̃(b,c), T̃(K̃(b,c),λ̃)^ord and the monoids for G̃
items.statement: Every p-adic place of F^+ splits in F; the fixed lifts ṽ ∈ S̃_p give ∏_{v̄∈S̄_p} ι_ṽ: G̃(F_p^+) ≅ ∏_{v̄∈S̄_p} GL_{2n}(F_ṽ), with T ⊂ B ⊂ G̃ corresponding to T_{2n} ⊂ B_{2n}. T̃^{S,ord} = T̃^S ⊗_O O⟦T(O_{F^+,p})⟧[{Ũ_{v,1},…,Ũ_{v,2n},Ũ_{v,2n}^{-1}}_{v∈S_p}] / (Ũ_{v^c,i} − Ũ_{v,2n−i} Ũ_{v,2n}^{-1})_{v∈S_p, i=1,…,2n}; Ũ_v (printed Ũ_{v,1}Ũ_{v,2}⋯Ũ_{v,n−1}; §2.2.5 has Ũ_v = [Iw diag(ϖ^{2n−1},…,ϖ,1) Iw]) and Ũ_p = ∏_{v∈S_p} Ũ_v. For K̃ good with K̃_v̄ = Ĩw_v̄ (v̄ ∈ S̄_p) and c ≥ b ≥ 0, c ≥ 1: K̃(b,c)_v̄ = K̃_v̄ (v̄ ∉ S̄_p), Ĩw_v̄(b,c) (v̄ ∈ S̄_p). For λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} there is a well-defined direct summand RΓ_{K̃(0,c)/K̃(b,c)}(X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃)^ord on which Ũ_p acts invertibly, and T̃(K̃(b,c),λ̃)^ord := T̃^{S,ord}(RΓ_{K̃(0,c)/K̃(b,c)}(X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃)^ord). Monoids: T(F_p^+)^+ ⊂ T(F_p^+) = elements contracting N(O_{F^+,p}); under T(F_p^+) = T_n(F_p), T(F_p^+)^+ ⊂ T_n(F_p)^+ (strictly for n ≥ 2); Ĩw_p(b,c) = ∏_{v̄} Ĩw_v̄(b,c); Δ̃_p = Ĩw_p(b,c) T(F_p^+)^+ Ĩw_p(b,c) with its ·_p-action on V_λ̃; T(O_{F^+,p})(b) = T_n(O_{F,p})(b); B(O_{F^+,p})(b) = preimage of T(O_{F^+,p})(b) in B(O_{F^+,p}); B(F_p^+)^+ = N(O_{F^+,p})·T(F_p^+)^+.
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses' (the CM/unitary 'general-rank ... arithmetic application'). The printed Ũ_v is inconsistent with §2.2.5.

items.name: Extension of the Satake map S to the ordinary Hecke algebras
items.statement: With the Siegel Levi G ≅ Res_{O_F/O_{F^+}} GL_n (so T ≅ Res_{O_F/O_{F^+}} T_n), the unnormalized Satake homomorphism S: T̃^S → T^S of (2.1.8) extends to S: T̃^{S,ord} → T^{S,ord} using O⟦T(O_{F^+,p})⟧ ≅ O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧ and Ũ_{v,i} ↦ U_{v^c,n−i} U_{v^c,n}^{-1} (1 ≤ i ≤ n), Ũ_{v,i} ↦ U_{v^c,n}^{-1} U_{v,i−n} (n+1 ≤ i ≤ 2n); these are double coset operators of elements of T(F_p^+) and T_n(F_p) that match under T(F_p^+) = T_n(F_p). (The assignment respects the relations Ũ_{v^c,i} = Ũ_{v,2n−i}Ũ_{v,2n}^{-1}.)
items.note: PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds' ('normalization'); PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses'. S itself on T̃^S is the Levi Satake map of §2.1 (ALS.4 / TC.3 compare boundary Hecke actions with Satake).

items.name: Completed and completed boundary cohomology of G̃ and their ordinary parts ((5.2.20)–(5.2.27))
items.statement: Fix m ≥ 1; K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F^+}) good with K̃_v̄ = Ĩw_v̄ (v̄ ∈ S̄_p), λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)}. π̃(K̃^p,λ̃,m) := RΓ_{K̃^p,sm} RΓ(𝔛_G̃, V_λ̃/ϖ^m) ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ̃_p]) (5.2.20), with T̃^S → End (5.2.21) if K̃^S = G̃(Ô^S_{F^+}); π̃(K̃^p,m) := RΓ_{K̃^p,sm} RΓ(𝔛_G̃, O/ϖ^m) ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[G̃(F_p^+)]) with (5.2.22); boundary versions π̃_∂(K̃^p,λ̃,m) := RΓ_{K̃^p,sm} RΓ(∂𝔛_G̃, V_λ̃/ϖ^m) (5.2.23)–(5.2.24) and π̃_∂(K̃^p,m) (5.2.25). For c ≥ b ≥ 0, c ≥ 1, canonical T̃^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphisms RΓ(Ĩw_p(b,c), π̃(K̃^p,λ̃,m)) ≅ RΓ(X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃/ϖ^m) (5.2.26) and RΓ(Ĩw_p(b,c), π̃_∂(K̃^p,λ̃,m)) ≅ RΓ(∂X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃/ϖ^m) (5.2.27) in D(O/ϖ^m). Ordinary parts: π̃^ord(K̃^p,λ̃,m) = ord RΓ(N(O_{F^+,p}), π̃(K̃^p,λ̃,m)) and π̃^ord_∂(K̃^p,λ̃,m) = ord RΓ(N(O_{F^+,p}), π̃_∂(K̃^p,λ̃,m)) in D_sm(O/ϖ^m[T(F_p^+)]); λ̃ = 0 is omitted from the notation.
items.note: CC.1 (smooth colimit with group and tame Hecke action), CC.6 ('derived invariants formulation', for (5.2.26)–(5.2.27)), CC.7: 'Pass the finite-level support triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_boundary through the derived tower construction' (completed boundary cohomology). PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.28: Hida theory comparisons for G̃ and its boundary
items.statement: Let K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F^+}) be good with K̃_v̄ = Ĩw_v̄ for v̄ ∈ S̄_p and K̃^S = G̃(Ô^S_{F^+}); c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1. For every λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} there are T̃^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphisms RΓ(T(O_{F^+,p})(b), π̃^ord(K̃^p,λ̃,m)) ≅ RΓ(T(O_{F^+,p})(b), O(w_0^G̃ λ̃) ⊗_O π̃^ord(K̃^p,m)) ≅ RΓ_{K̃(0,c)/K̃(b,c)}(X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃/ϖ^m)^ord, and likewise RΓ(T(O_{F^+,p})(b), π̃^ord_∂(K̃^p,λ̃,m)) ≅ RΓ(T(O_{F^+,p})(b), O(w_0^G̃ λ̃) ⊗_O π̃^ord_∂(K̃^p,m)) ≅ RΓ_{K̃(0,c)/K̃(b,c)}(∂X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃/ϖ^m)^ord, in D_sm(O/ϖ^m[K̃(0,c)/K̃(b,c)]).
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses'; PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. The paper omits the proof ('entirely similar' to Props 5.2.15, 5.2.17).

items.name: Relative Weyl groups, ^rW^P, lengths and the Bruhat cells S_w, S_w°, G̃_{≥i}
items.statement: For a p-adic place v̄ of F^+: ^rW_v̄ = W(G̃_{F^+_v̄}, T_{F^+_v̄}) (≅ S_{2n}), ^rW_{P,v̄} = W(G_{F^+_v̄}, T_{F^+_v̄}) (≅ S_n × S_n), ^rW^P_v̄ ⊂ ^rW_v̄ the representatives of ^rW_{P,v̄}\^rW_v̄ attached to B_{F^+_v̄}; ^rW, ^rW_P, ^rW^P are the products over v̄ ∈ S̄_p; ^rW ⊂ W (absolute Weyl group), l_r = relative length, l = absolute length; w_0^P = w_0^G w_0^G̃, the longest element of W^P (equivalently of ^rW^P), has l(w_0^P) = [F^+:Q]n^2 (printed l_r(w_0^P) = |S_p|n^2; correct value |S̄_p|n^2); ρ = half-sum of (Res_{F^+/Q}B)_E-positive roots. ^rW is identified with permutation matrices in G̃(F_p^+) = ∏_{ṽ∈S̃_p} GL_{2n}(F_ṽ); G̃(F_p^+) = ⊔_{w∈^rW^P} P(F_p^+) w B(F_p^+) [BT65, Cor. 5.20]. For w ∈ ^rW^P: S_w = P(F_p^+) w N(F_p^+), S_w° = P(F_p^+) w N(O_{F^+,p}) ⊂ S_w; the closure of S_w is ⊔_{w'≤w} S_{w'} (Bruhat order on ^rW^P), and w' < w ⇒ l_r(w') < l_r(w). For i ≥ 0, G̃_{≥i} = ⊔_{w∈^rW^P, l_r(w)≥i} S_w is open in G̃(F_p^+), left P(F_p^+)- and right B(F_p^+)-invariant.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements' ('its maps on parabolic induction'). ReductiveGroups Layer 7 plans 'Bruhat decomposition and BN-pairs / Tits systems' (the P\G/B decomposition and closure relation are imported from there).

items.name: The functors I_{≥i}, I_w and I_w° attached to parabolic induction
items.statement: Ind_{P(F_p^+)}^{G̃(F_p^+)}: Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[G̃(F_p^+)]) is exact and preserves injectives (right adjoint of the exact restriction). For i ≥ 0, I_{≥i}: Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[B(F_p^+)]), I_{≥i}(π) = {f: G̃_{≥i} → π locally constant, compactly supported modulo P(F_p^+), f(pg) = p f(g) for p ∈ P(F_p^+), g ∈ G̃_{≥i}} with B(F_p^+) acting by right translation; for w ∈ ^rW^P, I_w(π) is defined the same way with S_w in place of G̃_{≥i}; I_w°: Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[B(F_p^+)^+]) sends π to the subspace of I_w(π) of functions supported in S_w°.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. SR.2: 'Construct smooth induction from closed subgroups and compact induction ... Frobenius reciprocity ... induction in stages and Mackey filtrations'.

items.name: Proposition 5.3.1: the Bruhat filtration of Res_B Ind_P
items.statement: (1) I_{≥0} = Res^{G̃(F_p^+)}_{B(F_p^+)} ∘ Ind^{G̃(F_p^+)}_{P(F_p^+)}. (2) Each of I_{≥i}, I_w, I_w° is exact. (3) For every i ≥ 0 and π ∈ Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) there is a functorial exact sequence 0 → I_{≥i+1}(π) → I_{≥i}(π) → ⊕_{w∈^rW^P, l_r(w)=i} I_w(π) → 0. Hence for π ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) there is a functorial distinguished triangle I_{≥i+1}(π) → I_{≥i}(π) → ⊕_{l_r(w)=i} I_w(π) → I_{≥i+1}(π)[1] (5.3.2) in D_sm(O/ϖ^m[B(F_p^+)]).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'; SR.2: 'Mackey filtrations'. Proof uses a continuous section of G̃(F_p^+) → P(F_p^+)\G̃(F_p^+) and [Hau16, §2.1, Prop. 2.1.3].

items.name: Lemma 5.3.3: exactness of the degreewise B(O)(b)-invariants of the Bruhat filtration
items.statement: Let π ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) be bounded below, b ≥ 0 and λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)}. For every i ≥ 0 and j ∈ Z the sequence 0 → R^jΓ(B(O_{F^+,p})(b), O(w_0^G̃ λ̃) ⊗_O I_{≥i+1}(π)) → R^jΓ(B(O_{F^+,p})(b), O(w_0^G̃ λ̃) ⊗_O I_{≥i}(π)) → R^jΓ(B(O_{F^+,p})(b), ⊕_{w∈^rW^P, l_r(w)=i} O(w_0^G̃ λ̃) ⊗_O I_w(π)) → 0 in Mod(O/ϖ^m[T(F_p^+)^+_b]) associated with (5.3.2) is (short) exact.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. Proof: I_{≥i+1} is a filtered colimit of direct summands I_{U_1} of I_{≥i} (cf. [Hau16, Prop. 2.2.3]). Printed with B(O_{F,p})(b) for B(O_{F^+,p})(b).

items.name: Lemma 5.3.4(1): I_w° takes injectives to N(O_{F^+,p})-acyclics
items.statement: For w ∈ ^rW^P, the functor I_w° takes injective objects of Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) to Γ(N(O_{F^+,p}),−)-acyclic objects.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. Proof: I_w°(Ind_1^{P(F_p^+)} I) ≅ C^∞(P(F_p^+) w N(O_{F^+,p}), I) is an injective smooth N(O_{F^+,p})-module; [Eme10b, Lem. 2.1.10].

items.name: Lemma 5.3.4(2): the ordinary part does not see the non-compact part of a Bruhat cell
items.statement: For w ∈ ^rW^P and π ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) bounded below there is a natural isomorphism ord RΓ(N(O_{F^+,p}), I_w°(π)) ≅ ord RΓ(N(O_{F^+,p}), I_w(π)); equivalently ord RΓ(N(O_{F^+,p}), J_w(π)) = 0 for J_w = I_w/I_w°.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'. Proof: choose t ∈ T(F_p^+)^+ with S_w = ∪_{k≥0} t^{-k} S_w° t^k ([Hau16, Lem. 3.1.3, 3.3.1]); t acts locally nilpotently on J_w(π).

items.name: N_w and the functor Γ(N_w,−) with its torus action
items.statement: For w ∈ ^rW^P, N_w := P(F_p^+) ∩ w N(O_{F^+,p}) w^{-1}, a compact subgroup of P(F_p^+) containing N_n(O_{F,p}). Γ(N_w,−): Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T(F_p^+)^+]), with t ∈ T(F_p^+)^+ acting by t·v = tr_{t^w N_w (t^w)^{-1} / N_w}(t^w v), where t^w = w t w^{-1} (this makes sense since t^w N_w (t^w)^{-1} = P(F_p^+) ∩ w t N(O_{F^+,p}) t^{-1} w^{-1} ⊂ N_w); moreover w T(F_p^+)^+ w^{-1} ⊂ T_n(F_p)^+.
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'; PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds'.

items.name: Lemma 5.3.5: N(O)-invariants of I_w° are N_w-invariants
items.statement: For w ∈ ^rW^P and π ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[P(F_p^+)]) bounded below there is a natural isomorphism RΓ(N(O_{F^+,p}), I_w°(π)) ≅ RΓ(N_w, π) (compatible with the T(F_p^+)^+-actions), induced by f ↦ f(w).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements' ('its maps on parabolic induction').

items.name: The characters χ_w, α_w and the twist functor τ_w
items.statement: For w ∈ ^rW^P, χ_w: T(F_p^+) → O^× is χ_w(t) = N_{F_p^+/Q_p} det_{F_p^+}(Ad(t^w)|_{Lie U(F_p^+) ∩ w N(F_p^+) w^{-1}})^{-1} / |N_{F_p^+/Q_p} det_{F_p^+}(Ad(t^w)|_{Lie U(F_p^+) ∩ w N(F_p^+) w^{-1}})|_p. There is an isomorphism O(χ_w) ≅ O(−ρ + w^{-1} w_0^P(ρ)) ⊗_O O(α_w) of O[T(F_p^+)]-modules, where w_0^P = w_0^G w_0^G̃ is the longest element of ^rW^P and α_w: T(F_p^+) → O^× is trivial on T(O_{F^+,p}) and agrees with χ_w on every ι_v^{-1}(diag(ϖ_v^{a_1},…,ϖ_v^{a_{2n}})) (a_i ∈ Z). τ_w: Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]) sends π to π with t acting as π(t^{w^{-1}}).
items.note: PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits and the needed duality/finite-generation bounds' ('normalization, central characters').

items.name: Lemma 5.3.7: ordinary part of N_w-invariants of an inflated representation (the shift by the unipotent radical)
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^rW^P and π ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[G(F_p^+)]) bounded below. There is a natural isomorphism in D_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]) ord RΓ(N_w, Inf_{G(F_p^+)}^{P(F_p^+)} π) ≅ O/ϖ^m(χ_w) ⊗_{O/ϖ^m} τ_w^{-1} ord RΓ(N_n(O_{F,p}), π)[−[F^+:Q]n^2 + l(w)].
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'; 'At coefficient characteristic equal to residue characteristic it is not the exact Jacquet functor of the ell-not-p theory.' Key step: N_{w,U} = N_w ∩ U(F_p^+) ≅ Z_p^{n^2[F^+:Q]−l(w)}, and z_p = diag(p,…,p,1,…,1) acts on H^i(N_{w,U}, O/ϖ^m) through p^{n^2[F^+:Q]−l(w)−i}, so only the top degree survives localization ([Hau16, Prop. 3.1.8]).

items.name: Proposition 5.3.8: the ordinary part of the w-th Bruhat piece of parabolic induction
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^rW^P and π ∈ D_sm(O/ϖ^m[G(F_p^+)]) bounded below. There is a natural isomorphism in D_sm(O/ϖ^m[T_n(F_p)]) ord RΓ(N(O_{F^+,p}), I_w(Inf_{G(F_p^+)}^{P(F_p^+)} π)) ≅ O/ϖ^m(χ_w) ⊗_{O/ϖ^m} τ_{w^{-1}} ord RΓ(N_n(O_{F,p}), π)[−[F^+:Q]n^2 + l(w)] (τ_{w^{-1}} = τ_w^{-1}).
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor in the coefficient regime of ACC+ §§5.2–5.3, its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements' ('its maps on parabolic induction'); PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§5.2–5.3 | PA.2; PadicFamilies (finite-module projector only) | General-rank CM/unitary ordinary towers and characteristic-p ordinary parts of parabolic induction'. Combines Lemmas 5.3.4, 5.3.5, 5.3.7.

items.name: Theorem 5.4.1: parabolic induction of completed cohomology is a summand of completed boundary cohomology
items.statement: Let K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F^+}) be a good subgroup decomposed with respect to P (K = K̃ ∩ G(A^∞_{F^+})); let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal and 𝔪̃ = S^*(𝔪) ⊂ T̃^S. Then Ind_{P(F_p^+)}^{G̃(F_p^+)} (Inf_{G(F_p^+)}^{P(F_p^+)} π(K^p,m)_𝔪) is a T̃^S-equivariant direct summand (T̃^S acting through S) of π̃_∂(K̃^p,m)_{𝔪̃} in D_sm(O/ϖ^m[G̃(F_p^+)]).
items.note: PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§5.4–5.5 | PA.2 | Ordinary degree shifting/local compatibility'. PA.0: 'Construct the summand/filtration maps entering the unitary boundary argument and identify their twists and degree shifts. A splitting must be proved under the source's genericity condition'. Proof: non-Siegel strata vanish after localization by the finite-level statement in the proof of Theorem 2.4.2; the Siegel stratum is computed by strong approximation for U, the U-contribution disappearing in the limit ([NT16, Lem. 2.1, Cor. 2.8]). CC.7 supplies the completed boundary triangle.

items.name: Theorem 5.4.3: ordinary degree shifting from the boundary
items.statement: Let K̃ be good, decomposed with respect to P, with K̃_v̄ = Ĩw_v̄ for v̄ ∈ S̄_p (printed Iw_v̄). Let λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)}, w ∈ ^rW^P, λ_w = w(λ̃+ρ) − ρ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}; 𝔪 ⊂ T^S non-Eisenstein, 𝔪̃ = S^*(𝔪); c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1. Then for every j ∈ Z, S descends to a homomorphism, surjective onto the image of T̃^{S,ord} acting through S (printed: 'a surjective homomorphism' onto the whole algebra, which the proof does not establish), T̃^{S,ord}(H^j(∂X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃)^ord_{𝔪̃}) → T^{S,ord}(O(α_{w_0^G w w_0^G̃}) ⊗_O τ^{-1}_{w_0^G w w_0^G̃} H^{j−l(w)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_{λ_w})^ord_𝔪).
items.note: PA.2: 'Prove the ordinary degree-shifting comparison independently of PA.1, preserving the resulting filtration of the Galois representation and its characters'; PA source-to-owner matrix: '§§5.4–5.5 | PA.2 | Ordinary degree shifting/local compatibility'. PA.0: 'identify their twists and degree shifts'. Proof chains Thm 5.4.1, Prop 5.2.28, Lemma 5.3.3, Prop 5.3.8, Props 5.2.15/5.2.17, using w ↦ w_0^G w w_0^G̃ (an involution of ^rW^P with l ↦ [F^+:Q]n^2 − l). The proof yields surjectivity only onto the image of T̃^{S,ord};

items.name: Lemma 5.4.8: choice of weights for ordinary degree shifting
items.statement: Notation: for λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} and a ∈ Z, λ(a)_{τ,i} = λ_{τ,i} + a. Assume n ≥ 2 (the statement is printed for n ≥ 1 and fails for n = 1). Fix m ≥ 1. There is λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} such that (1) O(λ)/ϖ^m ≅ O/ϖ^m as T_n(F_p)-modules; (2) Σ_{i=1}^n (λ_{τ,i} + λ_{τc,i}) is independent of τ ∈ Hom(F,E); (3) for each i = 0,…,n^2 there are w_i = (w_{i,v̄})_{v̄∈S̄_p} ∈ ^rW^P, a_i ∈ (p−1)Z and a dominant λ̃_i ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} with (a) λ̃_i CTG (Definition 4.3.5); (b) l_r(w_{i,v̄}) = n^2 − i for every v̄ ∈ S̄_p, hence l(w_i) = [F^+:Q](n^2 − i); (c) w_i(λ̃_i + ρ) − ρ = λ(a_i). Construction: M > 16n divisible by 8(p−1)·#(O/ϖ^m)^×; λ_τ = (−nM, −2nM, …, −n^2M) if τ ∈ Ĩ_p and (0, −M, …, (1−n)M) if τc ∈ Ĩ_p, so λ̃(a) = ((n−1)M − a, …, −a, −nM + a, …, −n^2M + a); w_{i,v̄} = σ_{X_i}, X_i = {x+1,…,x+r, x+r+2,…,x+n+1} with nx + n − r = n^2 − i, 1 ≤ r ≤ n; a_i = the unique integer in [(nx+2n−r−1)M/2, (nx+2n−r)M/2] congruent to M/8 mod M/2; λ̃_i = w_i^{-1}(λ̃(a_i) + ρ) − ρ.
items.note: PA.2: 'Prove the ordinary degree-shifting comparison independently of PA.1, preserving the resulting filtration of the Galois representation and its characters'. Pure weight combinatorics internal to the ordinary degree-shifting argument; no other stage names it.

items.name: Proposition 5.4.13: Hecke algebras of X_K in degrees i[F^+:Q] as quotients of middle-degree Hecke algebras of X̃
items.statement: Suppose [F^+:Q] > 1 and n ≥ 2 (printed without n ≥ 2), and fix m ≥ 1. There exist a dominant λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} on whose V_λ a finite-index subgroup of O_F^× acts trivially and, for each i = 0,…,n^2−1, a CTG dominant weight λ̃_i ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)}, an integer a_i divisible by p−1 and w_i ∈ ^rW^P, such that for every good K̃ ⊂ G̃(A^∞_{F^+}) decomposed with respect to P with K̃_v̄ = Ĩw_v̄ (v̄ ∈ S̄_p), all integers c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1, and every non-Eisenstein 𝔪 ⊂ T^S with ρ̄_{𝔪̃} decomposed generic (𝔪̃ = S^*(𝔪)): (1) O(λ)/ϖ^m ≅ O/ϖ^m as O[T(F_p^+)]-modules; (2) for each i = 0,…,n^2−1, S descends to an algebra homomorphism T̃^{S,ord}(H^d(X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_{λ̃_i})^ord_{𝔪̃}) → T^{S,ord}(O(α_{w_i}) ⊗_O τ_{w_i}^{-1} H^{i[F^+:Q]}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_{λ(a_i)})^ord_𝔪), where d = [F^+:Q]n^2.
items.note: PA.2: 'Prove the ordinary degree-shifting comparison independently of PA.1, preserving the resulting filtration of the Galois representation and its characters'; PA.2: 'The degree-shifting application also imports IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.7's concentration theorem ... as in ACC+ §5.4' (IG.7 exports Theorem 4.3.3 and says 'PA.1/PA.2 then own the degree-shifting applications'). Proof: Theorem 4.3.3 + Theorem 5.4.3 + Lemma 5.4.8; the w_i here is w_0^G (w_i of Lemma 5.4.8) w_0^G̃.

items.name: The torus A_K, its identity component and the arithmetic groups Γ_{g,K}
items.statement: For K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) good, A_K := F^×\A_F^×/det(K) det(K_∞) R_{>0}. The quotient map A_K → F^×\A_F^×/det(K) F_∞^× identifies A_K with an extension of a ray class group by a real torus of dimension [F^+:Q] − 1 with cocharacter lattice F^× ∩ det(K) (a torsion-free congruence subgroup of O_F^×). A_K° is the identity component. For g ∈ GL_n(A_F^∞), Γ_{g,K} = GL_n(F) ∩ gKg^{-1} (written Γ_g). One has dim X_K = d − 1 = [F^+:Q]n^2 − 1 and dim A_K = [F^+:Q] − 1.
items.note: Part of the 'trick based on the fact that the group G has a non-trivial center' used to reach all cohomological degrees. PA.2's 'central characters' is the nearest phrase but names neither A_K nor the determinant fibration; ALS.0 plans components of X_K only. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 5.4.14(1): component decomposition of X_K
items.statement: For K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) good, the maps x ↦ (x,g) induce a homeomorphism ⊔_{[g]∈GL_n(F)\GL_n(A_F^∞)/K} Γ_g\X ≅ X_K.
items.note: ALS.0: 'Prove the finite decomposition of X_K into arithmetic Γ-components, with explicit stabilizers and component maps.'

items.name: Lemma 5.4.14(2)–(4): the determinant map X_K → A_K and the product structure of components
items.statement: (2) det: X_K → A_K is continuous and induces a bijection on sets of connected components (equivalently det: G(F^+)\G(A^∞_{F^+})/K → F^×\(A_F^∞)^×/det(K) is bijective, by strong approximation for Res_{F/F^+} SL_n). (3) If g ∈ GL_n(A_F^∞) satisfies det(Γ_g) = det(F^× ∩ K) and Γ_g^1 = SL_n(F) ∩ Γ_g, then the product map Γ_g^1 × (F^× ∩ K) → Γ_g is a group isomorphism; writing X = X^1 × (∏_{v|∞} R_{>0})/R_{>0} with X^1 = SL_n(F_∞)/∏_{v|∞} SU(n), one gets Γ_g\X = (Γ_g^1\X^1) × (F^× ∩ K)\(∏_{v|∞} R_{>0})/R_{>0}. (4) Under the same hypothesis det: F^× ∩ K → F^× ∩ det(K) is an isomorphism, the composite Γ_g\X ↪ X_K → A_K is (x,z) ↦ det(g) z^n, and z ↦ det(g) z^n is an isomorphism from (F^× ∩ K)\(∏_{v|∞} R_{>0})/R_{>0} onto the connected component A_K^{[det(g)]} of A_K containing [det(g)]. (K is neat.)
items.note: No stage plans the determinant fibration X_K → A_K or the splitting Γ_g ≅ Γ_g^1 × (F^× ∩ K). Inputs: strong approximation for SL_n (AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4 'Develop strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple groups'), components (ALS.0). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 5.4.15: shrinking K so that det(Γ_{g,K'}) = det(F^× ∩ K')
items.statement: Let K be a good subgroup of G(A^∞_{F^+}) = GL_n(A_F^∞) and T a finite set of finite places of F. There is a good normal subgroup K' ⊂ K with K'_T = K_T such that det(Γ_{g,K'}) = det(F^× ∩ K') for all g ∈ GL_n(A_F^∞). Construction: an ideal 𝔞 of O_F prime to T with ker(O_F^× → (O_F/𝔞)^×) torsion-free and contained in F^× ∩ K (Chevalley [Che51, Th. 1]); an ideal 𝔟 prime to 𝔞 and T with ker(O_F^× → (O_F/𝔞𝔟)^×) ⊂ (ker(O_F^× → (O_F/𝔞)^×))^n; K' = ker(O_F^× → (O_F/𝔞)^×)·K(𝔞𝔟), K(𝔞𝔟) = K ∩ (principal congruence subgroup of level 𝔞𝔟).
items.note: No stage plans this level choice. Library pointers (for parts only): Chevalley's theorem that every finite-index subgroup of O_F^× contains a congruence subgroup ker(O_F^× → (O_F/𝔞)^×) (not expected in Mathlib). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 5.4.16: cohomology of X_K is the cohomology of the torus A_K° tensor the fibrewise cohomology (central degree shifting)
items.statement: Let K = K(b, c) ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be good with K_v = Iw_v(b, c) for v | p (needed for T^{S,ord} to act; the statement omits it) and λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, and suppose (1) det(Γ_g) = det(F^× ∩ K) for all g ∈ GL_n(A_F^∞) and (2) F^× ∩ K acts trivially on V_λ. Then R det_*(V_λ) is constant on each connected component of A_K and R det_*(V_λ) = ⊕_{i=0}^{dim X^1} R^i det_*(V_λ)[−i]; there is a T^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphism of graded O-modules ⊕_{i=0}^{dim X_K} H^i(X_K, V_λ) ≅ (⊕_{j=0}^{dim A_K°} H^j(A_K°, O)) ⊗_O (⊕_{k=0}^{dim X^1} H^0(A_K, R^k det_*(V_λ))) (5.4.17), with trivial Hecke action on the first factor. Consequently the image of T^{S,ord} in End_O(⊕_{i=0}^{dim X_K} H^i(X_K, V_λ)) equals its image in End_O(⊕_{i=0}^{n^2−1} H^{i[F^+:Q]}(X_K, V_λ)).
items.note: No stage plans this Künneth/torus-factor argument; PA.2's 'central characters' is not specific. The proof treats only operators [K^S g K^S], g ∈ G^S; the p-adic operators in T^{S,ord} (which need K_v = Iw_v(b,c) at v | p) are handled the same way but are not discussed. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Proposition 5.4.18: ordinary local–global compatibility for a well-chosen weight, in every degree
items.statement: Suppose [F^+:Q] > 1. Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be good with K_v = Iw_v for v ∈ S_p; c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1; m ≥ 1; 𝔪 ⊂ T^S non-Eisenstein, 𝔪̃ = S^*(𝔪). Suppose (1) ρ̄_𝔪 is decomposed generic; (2) for every finite v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic F_0 ⊂ F. Then there are λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} and N ≥ 1 depending only on [F^+:Q] and n such that (1) O(λ)/ϖ^m ≅ O/ϖ^m as O[T(F_p^+)]-modules; (2) for each i = 0,…,d−1 there are a nilpotent ideal J_i ⊂ T^{S,ord}(H^i(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)^ord_𝔪) with J_i^N = 0 and a continuous ρ_𝔪: G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^{S,ord}(H^i(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)^ord_𝔪)/J_i) with (a) det(X − ρ_𝔪(Frob_v)) = image of P_v(X) for v ∉ S; (b) for v | p and g ∈ G_{F_v}, det(X − ρ_𝔪(g)) = ∏_{j=1}^n (X − χ_{λ,v,j}(g)); (c) for v | p and g_1,…,g_n ∈ G_{F_v}, ρ_𝔪 maps (g_1 − χ_{λ,v,1}(g_1))⋯(g_n − χ_{λ,v,n}(g_n)) to 0 in M_n(…/J_i).
items.note: PA.2: 'Prove the ordinary degree-shifting comparison independently of PA.1, preserving the resulting filtration of the Galois representation and its characters'. Proof ingredients planned elsewhere: TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure:TC.3 ('abstract factor-separation lemma using actual auxiliary characters ... Include the case of nilpotent coefficient quotients'), IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1 (Cayley–Hamilton/determinants, [Che14 Ex. 2.32, Thm 2.22]) and IHG.5 (nilpotent descent), Theorem 2.3.3 (AG2.2) and [Tho15, Th. 2.4] for the ordinary form (5.4.19) of ρ̃, [Ger19, Lem. 5.4], Carayol's lemma, Lemma 5.4.16. Statement (c) prints T^S where T^{S,ord} is meant (see issues).

items.name: Corollary 5.5.2: ordinary local–global compatibility for a single ι-ordinary cuspidal representation
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field (the §5 standing hypotheses are dropped), ι: Q̄_p ≅ C, and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F), regular algebraic of weight ιλ with λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,Q̄_p)}. Suppose (1) π is ι-ordinary at every v ∈ S_p ([Ger19, Def. 5.3]); (2) r̄_ι(π) is decomposed generic and irreducible. Then for every v ∈ S_p, r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is ordinary of weight λ ([Ger19, §5.2]): r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is conjugate to an upper-triangular representation with diagonal characters ψ_{v,1},…,ψ_{v,n}, where ψ_{v,i}(Art_{F_v}(u)) = ε^{1−i}(Art_{F_v}(u)) ∏_{τ∈Hom_{Q_p}(F_v,Q̄_p)} τ(u)^{−(w_0^G λ)_{τ,i}} ⟨u⟩_{ι,i} (u ∈ O_{F_v}^×) and ψ_{v,i}(Art_{F_v}(ϖ_v)) = ε^{1−i}(Art_{F_v}(ϖ_v)) u^{(i)}_{λ,ϖ_v}/u^{(i−1)}_{λ,ϖ_v}, with ⟨u⟩_{ι,i}, u^{(i)}_{λ,ϖ_v} the Hecke eigenvalues on (ι^{-1}π_v)^ord of [Ger19, Def. 5.5].
items.note: PA.2's 'preserving the resulting filtration of the Galois representation and its characters' concerns the Hecke-algebra-valued representation; no stage names ι-ordinary automorphic representations, [Ger19]'s ordinary Hecke eigenvalues, or this single-representation corollary (PAPER-QIAN-23 likewise left its use of it missing). Proof: solvable CM base change F'/F (disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄}, containing an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits, S_p split completely, [F':Q] > 2), [Ger19, Lem. 5.7], Theorem 5.5.1 and Lemma 6.2.11 (L8's comparison of determinant-ordinary identities with flags). Suggested by a referee; not used later in ACC+. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.1: automorphy lifting in the Fontaine–Laffaille case
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, c ∈ Aut(F) complex conjugation, p a prime, and ρ : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) continuous with: (1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline for every v | p, and p unramified in F; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic (Definition 4.3.1), and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous (Definition 6.2.29); (4) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, and p > n²; (5) there is a cuspidal automorphic π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with (a) π regular algebraic of weight λ satisfying λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} < p − 2n for all τ; (b) an isomorphism ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ with ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π) and HT_τ(ρ) = {λ_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, λ_{ιτ,2} + n − 2, …, λ_{ιτ,n}} for every τ : F ↪ ℚ̄_p; (c) π_v unramified for every v | p. Then ρ is automorphic: ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for a cuspidal automorphic Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ; moreover Π_v is unramified at every finite v with v | p or with ρ and π both unramified at v. (Remark 6.1.4, folded here: the image of Pρ̄ equals that of ad ρ̄, so the first half of (4) is equivalent to ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad ρ̄}; when p is unramified in F it follows from the non-existence of a surjection (ad ρ̄)(G_F) ↠ (ℤ/pℤ)^×.)
items.note: No stage plans ACC+'s own unpolarized CM-field lifting endpoint. PA's source-to-owner matrix starts at §6.2 ('§6.2 | LocalGaloisDeformationRings; GlobalGaloisDeformations'); PA.5 leaves 'the lifting theorem with its dedicated owner', and ML.2 only 'Appl[ies] PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure' for the final potential-automorphy assembly. The pending lifting Part IIs (PolarizedAutomorphyLifting, AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles, WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting proposed by BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25) each say they are not 'this unconditional, unpolarized CM-field theorem'. Proved in §§6.4–6.5 (outside this range) from the §6.2–6.3 inputs below; decomposed generic is Definition 4.3.1 (TeX 3792, p. 972, outside this range; AG2.7 plans it). Theorem 2.4.10 (Matsushima) is cited in the §6.1 overview. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.2: ordinary automorphy lifting
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, c complex conjugation, p a prime, and ρ : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) continuous with: (1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) for every v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is potentially semistable and ordinary with regular Hodge–Tate weights: there is λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,ℚ̄_p)} such that for each v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ an upper-triangular representation with diagonal characters ψ_{v,1}, …, ψ_{v,n} : G_{F_v} → ℚ̄_p^×, where ψ_{v,i} agrees on an open subgroup of I_{F_v} with σ ↦ ∏_{τ ∈ Hom(F_v, ℚ̄_p)} τ(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1)}; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous; (4) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, and p > n; (5) there are a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic π of GL_n(𝔸_F) and ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ with π ι-ordinary and r̄_ι(π) ≅ ρ̄. Then ρ is ordinarily automorphic of weight ιλ: ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for an ι-ordinary cuspidal automorphic Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight ιλ; for finite v ∤ p with ρ and π unramified at v, Π_v is unramified. (Remark 6.1.3, folded here: the existence of Π forces λ to be conjugate self-dual up to twist, λ_{τ,i} + λ_{τc,n+1−i} = w for some w ∈ ℤ, by Clozel's purity lemma [Clo90, Lem. 4.9]; this is not assumed. The proof shows ρ contributes to the ordinary part of completed cohomology and gets Π by 'independence of weight'.)
items.note: Same position as Theorem 6.1.1. PAPER-QIAN-23 records this theorem as its item 072, status missing, routed to PA.3; this item follows that routing. With HT(ε_p) = {−1} and Art_{F_v} geometric, ψ_{v,i}|_I is ε^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1)} for F_v = ℚ_p, so the ψ_{v,i} have Hodge–Tate weights λ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1, consistent with (5)(b) of Theorem 6.1.1. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Coefficient categories CNL_Λ and the standing set-up of §6.2
items.statement: E ⊂ ℚ̄_p is a finite extension of ℚ_p with ring of integers 𝒪, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k. For Λ a complete Noetherian local 𝒪-algebra with residue field k, CNL_Λ is the category of complete Noetherian local Λ-algebras with residue field k (its objects are CNL_Λ-algebras). F is a number field, S_p its set of places above p, E contains the images of all embeddings F ↪ ℚ̄_p, ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) is continuous and absolutely irreducible, and p ∤ 2n throughout. In §6.2.1: S is a finite set of finite places containing S_p and all places where ρ̄ ramifies, F_S the maximal extension of F unramified outside S, Λ_v ∈ CNL_𝒪 for v ∈ S, Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S} Λ_v (completed tensor product over 𝒪), with forgetful functors CNL_Λ → CNL_{Λ_v}.
items.note: R03.1: 'Construct the coefficient categories and prove presentation as inverse limits of Artinian quotients. Develop ... completed tensor products over O ... State exactly when completed tensor products remain Noetherian and local.'

items.name: Local lifts of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}}, the functor D_v^□ and the framed local lifting ring R_v^□
items.statement: For v ∈ S, a lift (lifting) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is a continuous homomorphism ρ : G_{F_v} → GL_n(A), A ∈ CNL_{Λ_v}, with ρ mod 𝔪_A = ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}}. D_v^□ : CNL_{Λ_v} → Sets sends A to the set of all lifts of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} to A. Claim: D_v^□ is representable; its representing object is R_v^□ ∈ CNL_{Λ_v}.
items.note: R08.1: 'Prove framed local representability and the tangent/obstruction description.' R03.2: 'the corresponding framed representability construction.'

items.name: Local deformation problem
items.statement: A local deformation problem for ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is a subfunctor D_v ⊂ D_v^□ such that (i) D_v is represented by a quotient R_v of R_v^□, and (ii) for all A ∈ CNL_{Λ_v}, ρ ∈ D_v(A) and a ∈ ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(k)), aρa^{-1} ∈ D_v(A).
items.note: G8: 'its local subfunctors are quotient-representable and invariant under strict conjugation.' G7 (Global): 'Treat local deformation conditions as representable subfunctors or quotient rings with a proved point criterion.' PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 routed its instances of this notion to L7.

items.name: Definition 6.2.2: global deformation problem
items.statement: A global deformation problem is a tuple 𝒮 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, {D_v}_{v∈S}) with ρ̄, S, {Λ_v} as above and D_v a local deformation problem for ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} for each v ∈ S. The determinant is not fixed (this differs from [CG18, §8.5.2] and [KT17, Def. 4.2]).
items.note: G8: 'For ACC+ Definition 6.2.2 use Λ=completed tensor product of the local Λ_v, absolutely irreducible residual representation and p∤2n ... The determinant is not fixed in that definition.' Consistent with PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 (G8).

items.name: Global lifts, deformations of type 𝒮 and T-framed deformations; the functors D_𝒮 and D_𝒮^T
items.statement: A lift of ρ̄ is a continuous ρ : G_F → GL_n(A), A ∈ CNL_Λ, with ρ mod 𝔪_A = ρ̄; lifts ρ_1, ρ_2 are strictly equivalent if ρ_2 = aρ_1a^{-1} for some a ∈ ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(k)); a deformation is a strict equivalence class. ρ is of type 𝒮 if ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∈ D_v(A) for all v ∈ S (a property stable under strict equivalence); D_𝒮 : CNL_Λ → Sets sends A to the deformations of type 𝒮. For T ⊆ S, a T-framed lift of type 𝒮 is (ρ, {α_v}_{v∈T}) with ρ of type 𝒮 and α_v ∈ ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(k)); (ρ_1, {α_v}) and (ρ_2, {β_v}) are strictly equivalent if ρ_2 = aρ_1a^{-1} and β_v = aα_v for one a ∈ ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(k)); T-framed deformations of type 𝒮 are the classes, and D_𝒮^T is the corresponding functor on CNL_Λ.
items.note: R04.1: 'Define framed and strict-equivalence unframed deformations ... Prove that the local equivalence relation is the intended conjugacy relation and that restriction is well-defined.' G8 constructs 'the arbitrary-rank unpolarized problem with variable determinant'.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.3: representability of D_𝒮 and D_𝒮^T
items.statement: Let 𝒮 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}, {D_v}) be a global deformation problem and T ⊆ S. Then D_𝒮 and D_𝒮^T are representable, by R_𝒮 and R_𝒮^T respectively (and R_𝒮 = R_𝒮^T when T = ∅).
items.note: G8: 'Prove representability as in Theorem 6.2.3.' R04.2: 'prove existence of universal framed rings, and unframed rings under absolute residual irreducibility.' Proof in the paper is a citation of [Gou01, App. 1].

items.name: Lemma 6.2.4: framed versus unframed global deformation rings
items.statement: Let T ⊆ S be nonempty, fix v_0 ∈ T and put 𝒯 = 𝒪⟦X_{v,i,j} : v ∈ T, 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n⟧/(X_{v_0,1,1}). A choice of representative ρ_𝒮 : G_F → GL_n(R_𝒮) of the universal type-𝒮 deformation determines a canonical isomorphism R_𝒮^T ≅ R_𝒮 ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒯; a representative of the universal T-framed deformation over R_𝒮 ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒯 is (ρ_𝒮, {1 + (X_{v,i,j})}_{v∈T}).
items.note: G8: 'the T-framing comparison of Lemma 6.2.4 with n²|T|−1 variables for nonempty T.' R04.2: 'Compare framed and unframed rings by formally smooth power-series maps with the correct number of variables.' Proof uses Schur's lemma (ρ̄ absolutely irreducible).

items.name: The weight ring Λ_v and the universal inertial characters χ_i^univ (ordinary case)
items.statement: Let v | p and suppose ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} stabilizes a complete flag 0 = F̄il^0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F̄il^n = k^n with one-dimensional graded pieces. Let 𝒪_{F_v}^×(p) be the pro-p completion of 𝒪_{F_v}^×, so Art_{F_v} : 𝒪_{F_v}^×(p) ≅ I_{F_v^{ab}/F_v}(p). Fix a nonempty set of minimal primes of 𝒪⟦𝒪_{F_v}^×(p)^n⟧ with intersection 𝔞 and set Λ_v = 𝒪⟦𝒪_{F_v}^×(p)^n⟧/𝔞 (𝔞 corresponds to a fixed collection of ordered n-tuples of characters of the torsion subgroup of I_{F_v^{ab}/F_v}(p)). Let χ̃̄_i : G_{F_v} → k^× be the character on F̄il^i/F̄il^{i−1} and χ̄_i = χ̃̄_i|_{I_{F_v}}. χ_i^univ : I_{F_v} → Λ_v^× is the product of the Teichmüller lift of χ̄_i with the map I_{F_v} → (i-th copy of) 𝒪_{F_v}^×(p) given by Art_{F_v}^{-1}.
items.note: L8: 'Construct the universal character coefficient rings including their chosen torsion components.'

items.name: The ordinary flag scheme 𝒢_v and the ordinary deformation ring R_v^△
items.statement: Let 𝓕 be the flag variety over 𝒪 of complete flags 0 = Fil^0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Fil^n = 𝒪^n. 𝒢_v ⊂ 𝓕 ×_{Spec 𝒪} Spec R_v^□ is the closed subscheme whose A-points (A an R_v^□-algebra) are the flags Fil ∈ 𝓕(A) such that each Fil^i is preserved by the specialization to A of the universal lift and I_{F_v} acts on Fil^i/Fil^{i−1} through the pushforward of χ_i^univ. R_v^△ is the image of R_v^□ → H^0(𝒢_v, 𝒪_{𝒢_v}) (after [Ger19, §3.1]).
items.note: L8: 'the ordinary flag scheme over the framed deformation ring and the image ring of its proper pushforward are one construction.' L7: 'Construct ordinary deformation functors with a full invariant flag and specified graded characters; separate the flag-bearing functor from its image after forgetting the flag.'

items.name: The determinant-ordinary rings R̃_v^{det,ord} and R_v^{det,ord}
items.statement: Let Λ̃_v = 𝒪⟦F_v^×(p)^n⟧ ⊗_{𝒪⟦𝒪_{F_v}^×(p)^n⟧} Λ_v and R̃_v^□ = R_v^□ ⊗_{Λ_v} Λ̃_v; the χ_i^univ extend to χ̃_i^univ : G_{F_v} → Λ̃_v^× lifting χ̃̄_i. R̃_v^{det,ord} is the maximal quotient of R̃_v^□ over which, for all g, g_1, …, g_n ∈ G_{F_v}, (6.2.7) det(X − ρ^□(g)) = ∏_{i=1}^n (X − χ̃_i^univ(g)) and (6.2.8) (ρ^□(g_1) − χ̃_1^univ(g_1))(ρ^□(g_2) − χ̃_2^univ(g_2))⋯(ρ^□(g_n) − χ̃_n^univ(g_n)) = 0. R_v^{det,ord} is the image of R_v^□ → R̃_v^{det,ord}; D_v^{det,ord} is the local deformation problem it represents. (A similar ring appears in Calegari–Specter.)
items.note: L8: 'the determinant-ordinary quotient defined by the full characteristic-polynomial identities and ordered products (ρ(g₁)−χ₁(g₁))⋯(ρ(g_n)−χ_n(g_n))=0 is another.' R̃_v^□ is written with an uncompleted tensor product in the paper; the construction is meant in CNL.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.9: R̃_v^{det,ord} is finite over R_v^{det,ord}
items.statement: R̃_v^{det,ord} is a finite R_v^{det,ord}-algebra. (Proof: it suffices that R̃_v^{det,ord}/𝔪_{R_v^□} is Artinian, which follows from (6.2.7) at g = Art_{F_v}(ϖ_v).)
items.note: Step of L8's comparison: 'Prove the precise comparison only under the published hypotheses and at the indicated integral/reduced/characteristic-zero level.' The printed statement is garbled ('Let R̃ be a finite R-algebra');

items.name: Point criteria for R_v^△ and R_v^{det,ord}; Spec R_v^△ ⊂ Spec R_v^{det,ord}
items.statement: (a) For a domain R ∈ CNL_{Λ_v} with K an algebraic closure of Frac R, an R-point of Spec R_v^□ factors through Spec R_v^△ iff ρ ⊗_R K (ρ the pushforward of the universal lift) has a G_{F_v}-stable complete flag on which I_{F_v} acts on Fil^i/Fil^{i−1} by the pushforward of χ_i^univ. (b) If R → S is an injective map of R_v^□-algebras and there are characters ψ_1, …, ψ_n : G_{F_v} → S^× with ψ_i|_{I_{F_v}} equal to the pushforward of χ_i^univ and with the analogues of (6.2.7) and (6.2.8) for the ψ_i and the universal lift holding in S, then R_v^□ → R factors through R_v^{det,ord}. (c) Consequently Spec R_v^△ ⊂ Spec R_v^{det,ord} as topological spaces, and there is a surjection of R_v^□-algebras R_v^{det,ord} ↠ (R_v^△)_red.
items.note: L8: 'Prove the precise comparison only under the published hypotheses and at the indicated integral/reduced/characteristic-zero level. Equality of characteristic polynomials alone does not provide a full invariant flag over every nonreduced coefficient ring.' (c) is proved by applying (b) to R = R_v^△/𝔭 and S its integral closure in a finite extension of its fraction field.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.10: properties of R_v^△ (trivial residual representation)
items.statement: If [F_v : ℚ_p] > n(n−1)/2 + 1 and ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial, then R_v^△ is 𝒪-flat, reduced and equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² + (n(n+1)/2)[F_v : ℚ_p], and Spec R_v^△ → Spec Λ_v is bijective on generic points, hence on irreducible components.
items.note: L7: 'Prove representability, dimension and component maps under the source genericity/distinguishedness assumptions.' Quoted from [Tho15, Prop. 3.14] (proved there for Λ_v = 𝒪⟦𝒪_{F_v}^×(p)^n⟧, which also shows minimal primes of Λ_v generate minimal primes of R_v^△); external input.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.11: characteristic-polynomial and ordered-product identities give a flag
items.statement: Let K be a field, G a group, ρ : G → GL_n(K) a representation, and χ_1, …, χ_n : G → K^× pairwise distinct characters with (1) det(X − ρ(g)) = ∏_i (X − χ_i(g)) for all g ∈ G and (2) (ρ(g_1) − χ_1(g_1))(ρ(g_2) − χ_2(g_2))⋯(ρ(g_n) − χ_n(g_n)) = 0 for all g_1, …, g_n ∈ G. Then there is a G-stable complete flag 0 = Fil^0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Fil^n = K^n with Fil^i/Fil^{i−1} ≅ K(χ_i) for each i.
items.note: The field-level case of L8's comparison between the flag construction and 'the determinant-ordinary quotient defined by the full characteristic-polynomial identities and ordered products'.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.12: irreducible components of Spec R_v^{det,ord}
items.statement: Let U ⊂ Spec Λ_v be the open subscheme where χ_1^univ, …, χ_n^univ are pairwise distinct and Z its complement; let f : Spec R_v^△ → Spec Λ_v and g : Spec R_v^{det,ord} → Spec Λ_v be the structure maps. Suppose ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial and [F_v : ℚ_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1. (1) f^{-1}(U) = g^{-1}(U) inside Spec R_v^□; hence for each irreducible component C of Spec Λ_v there is a unique irreducible component C′ of Spec R_v^{det,ord} dominating C, and dim C′ = n² + 1 + (n(n+1)/2)[F_v : ℚ_p]. (2) Every irreducible component C′ of Spec R_v^{det,ord} not dominating a component of Spec Λ_v satisfies C′ ⊂ g^{-1}(Z) and dim C′ ≤ n² − 1 + (n(n+1)/2)[F_v : ℚ_p]. (The proof introduces, for σ ∈ S_n, the ring R_v^{△,σ} defined like R_v^△ with χ^univ_{σ(i)} on the i-th graded piece, and the bound dim 𝒢_v^σ ×_{Spec Λ_v} Z ≤ 1 + n² + n(n+1)/2 + n(n+1)[F_v:ℚ_p]/2 − [F_v:ℚ_p] from a tangent-space computation as in [Ger19, Lem. 3.7].)
items.note: L8: 'Prove the precise comparison only under the published hypotheses.' L7: 'Export the precise local comparisons and component support input used in ACC+ §6.2 to GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9.' The final inequality holds exactly when [F_v:ℚ_p] ≥ n(n+1)/2 + 2, i.e. under the stated hypothesis.

items.name: Fontaine–Laffaille of type (λ_τ)
items.statement: Let v | p with F_v/ℚ_p unramified and Λ_v = 𝒪. For each τ : F_v ↪ E let λ_τ = (λ_{τ,1}, …, λ_{τ,n}) be integers with λ_{τ,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_{τ,n} and λ_{τ,1} − λ_{τ,n} < p − n. A representation of G_{F_v} on a finite 𝒪-module W is Fontaine–Laffaille of type (λ_τ)_{τ∈Hom(F_v,E)} if W ≅ 𝐆(M) for some M ∈ 𝓜𝓕_𝒪 (§4.1) with FL_τ(M ⊗_𝒪 k) = {λ_{τ,1} + n − 1, λ_{τ,2} + n − 2, …, λ_{τ,n}} for every τ.
items.note: L7: 'Construct Fontaine–Laffaille deformation conditions in the proven unramified small-weight range.' R07.3 supplies 𝓜𝓕_𝒪 and 𝐆 ('Construct the integral filtered modules and the Galois functor'). Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (L7, R07.3, PA.1).

items.name: Proposition 6.2.14: the Fontaine–Laffaille deformation ring R_v^FL
items.statement: If ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is Fontaine–Laffaille of type (λ_τ), there is a quotient R_v^FL of R_v^□ such that (1) R_v^FL represents a local deformation problem D_v^FL; (2) for A ∈ CNL_𝒪 finite over 𝒪, a lift ρ ∈ D_v^□(A) lies in D_v^FL(A) iff ρ is Fontaine–Laffaille of type (λ_τ); (3) R_v^FL is formally smooth over 𝒪 of dimension 1 + n² + (n(n−1)/2)[F_v : ℚ_p].
items.note: L7: 'calculate their tangent spaces and formal smoothness where valid.' From [CHT08, §2.4.1] plus a twisting argument (§4.1). PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 already cites this as the variable-determinant version at L7.

items.name: Level-raising local deformation problems D_v^χ and rings R_v^χ
items.statement: Assume q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial and p > n; take Λ_v = 𝒪. For χ = (χ_1, …, χ_n) continuous characters χ_i : 𝒪_{F_v}^× → 𝒪^× trivial modulo ϖ, D_v^χ is the functor of lifts ρ : G_{F_v} → GL_n(A) with char_{ρ(σ)}(X) = ∏_{i=1}^n (X − χ_i(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))) for all σ ∈ I_{F_v}. It is a local deformation problem, represented by R_v^χ.
items.note: R08.2: 'Construct unramified, fixed inertial-type, Steinberg and minimally ramified deformation conditions ... calculate dimensions, smoothness and irreducible components with each residual hypothesis visible.' Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (R08.2, L7).

items.name: Proposition 6.2.16: the unipotent level-raising ring R_v^1
items.statement: If χ_i = 1 for all i, then (1) Spec R_v^1 is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² and every generic point has characteristic 0; (2) every generic point of Spec R_v^1/ϖ is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R_v^1.
items.note: R08.2: 'calculate dimensions, smoothness and irreducible components.' Contained in [Tay08, Prop. 3.1] (external input); PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 routes that proposition to L7 and R08.2.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.17: the level-raising ring R_v^χ for distinct χ_i
items.statement: If χ_1, …, χ_n are pairwise distinct, then Spec R_v^χ is irreducible of dimension 1 + n² and its generic point has characteristic 0.
items.note: As for Proposition 6.2.16 ([Tay08, Prop. 3.1]).

items.name: Lemma 6.2.19: lifts at a Taylor–Wiles place split as sums of characters
items.statement: Assume q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} unramified, Λ_v = 𝒪, and ρ̄(Frob_v) has n distinct eigenvalues α_1, …, α_n ∈ k; let γ̄_i : G_{F_v} → k^× be unramified with γ̄_i(Frob_v) = α_i. For any lift ρ : G_{F_v} → GL_n(A) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} there are unique continuous characters γ_i : G_{F_v} → A^× with γ_i mod 𝔪_A = γ̄_i such that ρ is GL_n(A)-conjugate to γ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ γ_n.
items.note: G7 (Global): 'Prove the arbitrary-n auxiliary-prime lemma with prescribed distinct Frobenius eigenvalues and chosen eigenspaces.' R04.5: 'choose primes with prescribed Frobenius eigenvalues'. PA.4: 'Track ... selected eigenvalues and framed local deformation data.' Proof in the paper: 'similar to [DDT97, Lem. 2.44]; details left to the reader'. Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (TW local problem at R04.5, G7).

items.name: The diamond group Δ_v and the map 𝒪[Δ_v] → R_v^□ at a Taylor–Wiles place
items.statement: Let Δ_v = k(v)^×(p)^n, k(v)^×(p) the maximal p-power quotient of k(v)^×. Writing the universal lift over R_v^□ as conjugate to γ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ γ_n (Lemma 6.2.19), each γ_i ∘ Art_{F_v}|_{𝒪_{F_v}^×} factors through k(v)^×(p), giving a canonical local 𝒪-algebra map 𝒪[Δ_v] → R_v^□ (depending on the ordering α_1, …, α_n). Claim: this map is formally smooth of relative dimension n².
items.note: G7 (Global): 'Export the auxiliary diamond group and its exact rank/bounds to complex patching.' PA.4: 'framed local deformation data'. The formal smoothness claim is stated as 'straightforward to check' without proof.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.21: formally smooth local lifting rings away from p
items.statement: Let v ∤ p. If H²(F_v, ad ρ̄) = 0, then R_v^□ is isomorphic to a power series ring over 𝒪 in n² variables.
items.note: R08.1: 'Prove framed local representability and the tangent/obstruction description.' R08.2: 'calculate dimensions, smoothness'. Proof left to the reader ('standard argument in obstruction theory').

items.name: The local ring R_𝒮^{T,loc} and the map R_𝒮^{T,loc} → R_𝒮^T
items.statement: Fix 𝒮 and let R_v represent D_v. Let T ⊆ S (possibly empty) with Λ_v = 𝒪 for v ∈ S ∖ T, and R_𝒮^{T,loc} = ⊗̂_{v∈T} R_v (over 𝒪), a Λ-algebra via ⊗̂_{v∈T} Λ_v ≅ ⊗̂_{v∈S} Λ_v. For v ∈ T the morphism D_𝒮^T → D_v, (ρ, {α_v}) ↦ α_v^{-1} ρ|_{G_{F_v}} α_v, induces local Λ_v-algebra maps R_v → R_𝒮^T and hence a local Λ-algebra map R_𝒮^{T,loc} → R_𝒮^T.
items.note: R04.3: 'Construct the global ring as the appropriate completed fibre product/quotient with prescribed local rings.' G7 (Global): 'Construct global-to-local morphisms and presentations over completed tensor products.' Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (R03.1, R04.3, L7).

items.name: Tangent conditions L_v^1 ⊂ Z^1(F_v, ad ρ̄) and L_v ⊂ H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄)
items.statement: ad ρ̄ is M_{n×n}(k) with the adjoint G_F-action via ρ̄. For v ∈ S, c ↦ (1 + εc)ρ̄ gives Z^1(F_v, ad ρ̄) ≅ Hom_{CNL_{Λ_v}}(R_v^□, k[ε]/(ε²)); L_v^1 is the preimage of Hom_{CNL_{Λ_v}}(R_v, k[ε]/(ε²)); it contains the coboundaries, and L_v is its image in H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄).
items.note: R02.5: 'Relate tangent conditions of finite-flat, ordinary and fixed-type deformation problems to the corresponding local H¹ subspaces.' R08.1: 'the tangent/obstruction description'.

items.name: The relative tangent complex C^•_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄), its long exact sequence (6.2.23) and Euler characteristic (6.2.24)
items.statement: C^0_{𝒮,T} = C^0(F_S/F, ad ρ̄); C^1_{𝒮,T} = C^1(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈T} C^0(F_v, ad ρ̄); C^2_{𝒮,T} = C^2(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈T} C^1(F_v, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈S∖T} C^1(F_v, ad ρ̄)/L_v^1; C^i_{𝒮,T} = C^i(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈S} C^{i−1}(F_v, ad ρ̄) for i ≥ 3; differential (φ, (ψ_v)) ↦ (∂φ, (φ|_{G_{F_v}} − ∂ψ_v)). H^i_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄), h^i_{𝒮,T} its cohomology and dimensions. (6.2.23): 0 → H^0_{𝒮,T} → H^0(F_S/F) → ⊕_{v∈T} H^0(F_v) → H^1_{𝒮,T} → H^1(F_S/F) → ⊕_{v∈T} H^1(F_v) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈S∖T} H^1(F_v)/L_v → H^2_{𝒮,T} → H^2(F_S/F) → ⊕_{v∈S} H^2(F_v) → ⋯ (coefficients ad ρ̄). Since p > 2, H^i(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) = H^i(F_v, ad ρ̄) = 0 for i ≥ 3, so H^i_{𝒮,T} = 0 for i > 3 and (6.2.24) χ_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄) = χ(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) − Σ_{v∈S} χ(F_v, ad ρ̄) − Σ_{v∈S∖T} (dim_k L_v − h^0(F_v, ad ρ̄)).
items.note: D8: 'Construct determinant/deformation tangent complexes from the actual restriction maps.' R04.3: 'Prove tangent and obstruction descriptions by the actual adjoint cohomology and the local conditions.' R02.3: 'bounds on cohomological dimension ... and the global Euler-characteristic formula.' I re-derived (6.2.24) from the cone description; it is correct.

items.name: Dual Selmer group H^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1))
items.statement: The trace pairing (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) on ad ρ̄ is perfect and G_F-equivariant, so ad ρ̄(1) is the Tate dual of ad ρ̄. For v ∈ S, L_v^⊥ ⊂ H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄(1)) is the exact annihilator of L_v under local Tate duality, and H^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) = ker(H^1(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) → ∏_{v∈S∖T} H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄(1))/L_v^⊥).
items.note: R02.5: 'identify its first cohomology with the explicit global H¹ restriction kernel used in deformation theory, and compare changes of one local condition or addition of a prime.' D8: 'Prove the dual Selmer dimension calculation in all ranks, including trace-kernel exceptions when p divides n.'

items.name: Proposition 6.2.25: presentation of R_𝒮^T over R_𝒮^{T,loc}
items.statement: With the notation of §6.2.22 and T ≠ ∅, there is a local Λ-algebra surjection R_𝒮^{T,loc}⟦X_1, …, X_g⟧ ↠ R_𝒮^T with g = h^1_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄) = h^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) − h^0(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) − Σ_{v|∞} h^0(F_v, ad ρ̄) + Σ_{v∈S∖T} (dim_k L_v − h^0(F_v, ad ρ̄)). (Proof: H^1_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄) ≅ Hom_{CNL_Λ}(R_𝒮^T/(𝔪_{R_𝒮^{T,loc}}), k[ε]/(ε²)) is the relative tangent space; h^0_{𝒮,T} = 0 as T ≠ ∅; h^2_{𝒮,T} = h^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) and h^3_{𝒮,T} = h^0(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) by comparison with Poitou–Tate.)
items.note: The reviewed node R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound cites 'ACC+ Prop. 6.2.25 computes only this number of variables, g = h¹_{S,T}(ad ρ̄)'. R04.3: 'Prove tangent and obstruction descriptions ...'. G7 (Global): 'presentations over completed tensor products'. The proof has two compensating sign slips; Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (Kisin's presentation: R03.2, R04.3, G7).

items.name: Lemma 6.2.26(1): the local ring in the Fontaine–Laffaille case, unipotent types
items.statement: Suppose T = S_p ⊔ R ⊔ S_a with: for v ∈ S_p, F_v/ℚ_p unramified, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} as in Proposition 6.2.14, D_v = D_v^FL; for v ∈ R, q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial, D_v = D_v^{χ_v} for a tuple χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n}) of characters 𝒪_{F_v}^× → 𝒪^× trivial mod ϖ; for v ∈ S_a, H²(F_v, ad ρ̄) = 0 and D_v = D_v^□. If χ_{v,i} = 1 for all v ∈ R and all i, then Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc} is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n²|T| + (n(n−1)/2)[F : ℚ], every generic point has characteristic 0, and every generic point of Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc}/ϖ is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc}.
items.note: L7: 'Export the precise local comparisons and component support input used in ACC+ §6.2 to GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9.' Deduced from Props 6.2.14, 6.2.16, 6.2.17, 6.2.21 and [BLGHT11, Lem. 3.3]; PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 records BLGHT11 Lemma 3.3 as missing. That extraction calls this 'ACC+ Lemma 6.2.25(1)' (arXiv numbering); the published number is 6.2.26.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.26(2): the local ring in the Fontaine–Laffaille case, distinct types
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 6.2.26, if χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} are pairwise distinct for each v ∈ R, then Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc} is irreducible of dimension 1 + n²|T| + (n(n−1)/2)[F : ℚ] and its generic point has characteristic 0.
items.note: As for Lemma 6.2.26(1).

items.name: Lemma 6.2.27(1): the local ring in the ordinary case, unipotent types
items.statement: Suppose T = S_p ⊔ R ⊔ S_a with: for v ∈ S_p, [F_v : ℚ_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial, Λ_v = 𝒪⟦𝒪_{F_v}^×(p)^n⟧/℘_v for a minimal prime ℘_v, D_v = D_v^{det,ord}; R and S_a as in Lemma 6.2.26. If χ_{v,i} = 1 for all v ∈ R and all i, then Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc} has dimension 1 + n²|T| + (n(n+1)/2)[F : ℚ]; every irreducible component of maximal dimension has a characteristic-0 generic point; every other component has dimension ≤ n²|T| − 1 + (n(n+1)/2)[F : ℚ]; and every irreducible component of maximal dimension of Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc}/(ϖ) (printed '(λ)') is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc}.
items.note: L7: 'Export the precise local comparisons and component support input used in ACC+ §6.2 ...'; L8 supplies the det-ord comparison (Prop 6.2.12) it rests on. The printed '(λ)' should be '(ϖ)', and the proof's claim that minimal primes pull back to minimal primes needs a small repair;

items.name: Lemma 6.2.27(2): the local ring in the ordinary case, distinct types
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 6.2.27, if χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} are pairwise distinct for each v ∈ R, then Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc} has dimension 1 + n²|T| + (n(n+1)/2)[F : ℚ], has a unique irreducible component of maximal dimension, whose generic point has characteristic 0, and every other component has dimension ≤ n²|T| − 1 + (n(n+1)/2)[F : ℚ].
items.note: As for Lemma 6.2.27(1).

items.name: Lemma 6.2.27(3): small components of the ordinary local ring lie over the diagonal locus
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 6.2.27, if x ∈ Spec R_𝒮^{T,loc} lies on an irreducible component of non-maximal dimension, then for some v ∈ S_p the image of x in Spec Λ_v lies in the closed locus χ_i^univ = χ_j^univ for some i ≠ j.
items.note: L7 exports the 'component support input used in ACC+ §6.2'; this is the input that lets §6.5 ignore the small components.

items.name: Definition 6.2.29: enormous subgroups of GL_n(k)
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic extension of 𝔽_p and ad⁰ the trace-zero matrices in M_{n×n}(k) with the adjoint GL_n(k)-action. An absolutely irreducible subgroup H ⊆ GL_n(k) is enormous over k if (1) H has no nontrivial quotient of p-power order; (2) H^0(H, ad⁰) = H^1(H, ad⁰) = 0; (3) for every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad⁰ there is a regular semisimple h ∈ H with W^h ≠ 0. The condition depends only on the image of H in PGL_n(k); if p | n no subgroup is enormous (ad⁰ contains the scalars). (Remark 6.2.31: if k contains all eigenvalues of elements of H, this is equivalent to [KT17, Def. 4.10].)
items.note: AGR G7: 'In particular ACC+ Definition 6.2.29 calls an absolutely irreducible subgroup H enormous when it has no nontrivial p-power quotient, H⁰(H,ad⁰)=H¹(H,ad⁰)=0, and for every simple H-submodule W of ad⁰ some regular semisimple h has W^h nonzero ... the displayed enormous condition cannot hold because ad⁰ contains scalars.' Reviewed node G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance. Consistent with QIAN-23, CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/-20. §6.2.28 cites '[CG18, §9.2]' for this notion;

items.name: Lemma 6.2.30: enormity is insensitive to extending k
items.statement: Let k′/k be an algebraic extension and H ⊂ GL_n(k) a subgroup. Then H is enormous over k iff it is enormous over k′.
items.note: AGR G7: 'Prove coefficient-extension invariance as in Lemma 6.2.30.' The proof reduces to condition (3) and uses Galois descent for Gal(k′/k)-stable k′[H]-submodules.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles data, the augmented problem 𝒮_Q and the Λ[Δ_Q]-structure
items.statement: Assume k contains all eigenvalues of elements of ρ̄(G_F). A Taylor–Wiles datum is (Q, (α_{v,1}, …, α_{v,n})_{v∈Q}) with Q a finite set of finite places disjoint from S, q_v ≡ 1 mod p for v ∈ Q, and for each v ∈ Q an ordering α_{v,1}, …, α_{v,n} of the eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_v), which are k-rational and distinct. The augmented problem is 𝒮_Q = (ρ̄, S ∪ Q, {Λ_v}_{v∈S} ∪ {𝒪}_{v∈Q}, {D_v}_{v∈S} ∪ {D_v^□}_{v∈Q}); Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q} k(v)^×(p)^n; by §6.2.18 the orderings make R^T_{𝒮_Q} a Λ[Δ_Q]-algebra for every T ⊆ S; 𝔞_Q = ker(Λ[Δ_Q] → Λ) is the augmentation ideal.
items.note: R04.5: 'choose primes with prescribed Frobenius eigenvalues and q≡1 mod p^n.' G7 (Global): 'Export the auxiliary diamond group and its exact rank/bounds to complex patching.' PA.4: 'Construct Taylor–Wiles auxiliary sets ... Track the size of the sets, congruences on residue cardinalities, selected eigenvalues and framed local deformation data.'

items.name: Control at Taylor–Wiles level: R^T_{𝒮_Q}/𝔞_Q ≅ R^T_𝒮
items.statement: For a Taylor–Wiles datum and T ⊆ S, the natural map R^T_{𝒮_Q} → R^T_𝒮 is surjective with kernel 𝔞_Q R^T_{𝒮_Q}.
items.note: R04.4: 'Prove the ring maps associated to ... enlarging the ramification set'. G7 (Global) exports 'the auxiliary diamond group' to patching. Stated without proof in the paper (a lift of type 𝒮_Q is of type 𝒮 iff each γ_i of Lemma 6.2.19 is unramified at v ∈ Q).

items.name: Enormous image and Chebotarev elements for dual Selmer classes (key step in the proof of Lemma 6.2.32)
items.statement: Assume ζ_p ∉ F, k contains all eigenvalues of ρ̄(G_F), and H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is enormous; let L/F be the extension cut out by ρ̄ and N ≥ 1. Then H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}); the restriction H^1(F_S/F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) → H^1(F_S/L(ζ_{p^N}), ad⁰ρ̄(1))^{G_F} is injective; and for every cocycle κ representing a nonzero class in H^1(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) there is σ ∈ G_{F(ζ_{p^N})} such that ρ̄(σ) has distinct k-rational eigenvalues and p_σκ(σ) ≠ 0, where p_σ : ad ρ̄ → (ad ρ̄)^σ is the σ-equivariant projection. (For κ in the k(1) summand this uses that the Kummer extension of κ is not abelian over F, and that it is linearly disjoint from the field cut out by ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} since H has no p-power quotient.)
items.note: AGR G7: 'Prove dimension-general residual-image criteria needed for Taylor–Wiles primes: adequacy and the particular strengthened image conditions are explicit cohomological/invariant-subspace statements with separate verification lemmas ... the ACC+ auxiliary-prime construction consumes enormous image after cyclotomic restriction.' R04.5: 'Combine Chebotarev, residual-image lemmas and dual Selmer calculations.' The proof misprints y ∉ F(ζ_{p^N}) as 'y^p ∉ F(ζ_{p^N})';

items.name: Lemma 6.2.32: existence of Taylor–Wiles data killing the dual Selmer group
items.statement: Let T ⊆ S. Assume F is CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+, ζ_p ∉ F, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is enormous; let q ≥ h^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)). Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (α_{v,1}, …, α_{v,n})_{v∈Q_N}) with (1) #Q_N = q; (2) q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N and v of degree one over ℚ for every v ∈ Q_N; (3) h^1_{𝒮_{Q_N}^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) = 0.
items.note: G7 (Global): 'Prove the arbitrary-n auxiliary-prime lemma with prescribed distinct Frobenius eigenvalues and chosen eigenspaces, q_v≡1 mod p^N, disjointness from S and control of dual Selmer.' R04.5: 'Prove the required dual-Selmer dimension reduction and uniform bound on the number of primes.' PA.4 / PA acceptance: 'PA.4 verifies enormous-image auxiliary primes'. Uses Chebotarev density (Library pointers (for parts only): a Chebotarev density theorem for finite Galois extensions of number fields; Tau Ceti has only NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime per PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18).

items.name: Proposition 6.2.33: Taylor–Wiles data with a presentation of R^T_{𝒮_{Q_N}}
items.statement: Take T = S and q ≥ h^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)). Assume F = F^+F_0 with F^+ totally real and F_0 imaginary quadratic, ζ_p ∉ F, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous.
