Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (α_{v,1}, …, α_{v,n})_{v∈Q_N}) with (1) #Q_N = q; (2) q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N and the rational prime below v splits in F_0, for every v ∈ Q_N; (3) a local Λ-algebra surjection R_𝒮^{T,loc}⟦X_1, …, X_g⟧ ↠ R^T_{𝒮_{Q_N}} with g = qn − n²[F^+ : ℚ]. (Proof: H^0(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) = 0 by enormity and ζ_p ∉ F, and dim L_v − h^0(F_v, ad ρ̄) = h^0(F_v, ad ρ̄(1)) = n for v ∈ Q_N.)
items.note: G7 (Global): 'For ACC+ Proposition 6.2.33 require F=F⁺F₀ ... With T=S and q at least the indicated dual-Selmer dimension, construct exactly q primes, with the underlying rational primes split in F₀, and the local-to-global presentation with g=qn−n²[F⁺:Q] variables.' R04.6: 'Package the global-to-local presentation with its explicit numerical terms'. I rechecked g from Prop 6.2.25: the Σ_{v|∞} term is n²[F^+:ℚ] since F is totally imaginary.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.2: length identity for multiplication by f on a one-dimensional local ring
items.statement: Let T be an excellent local ring with Spec T irreducible, f ∈ 𝔪_T, and T/(f) of Krull dimension 0. If dim T = 0, then lg_T(M/fM) − lg_T(M[f]) = 0 for every finitely generated T-module M (both lengths finite). Otherwise dim T = 1, T has a unique prime 𝔭 ≠ 𝔪_T, and there is a ∈ ℤ_{>0} (namely a = lg_T(T̃/fT̃), T̃ the normalization of T/𝔭) with lg_T(M/fM) − lg_T(M[f]) = a·lg_{T_𝔭}(M_𝔭) for every finitely generated T-module M (all lengths finite).
items.note: P9: 'Make the derived length identity of ACC+ §6.3.4 a reusable intermediate theorem ... prove the dimension-zero vanishing and dimension-one generic-length formula'. Reviewed node P9/derived-length-identity ('(Modules) Let T be an excellent local ring ...'). Proof input: structure theorem over a PID (Mathlib has the torsion/free decomposition) and finiteness of normalization for excellent rings (not in Mathlib).

items.name: Derived length lg_T(C) and its additivity
items.statement: Let S be a ring, T a Noetherian S-algebra and C ∈ D^b(S) with a map T → End_{D^b(S)}(C) over S such that H^*(C) has finite length over T. Then lg_T(C) = Σ_i (−1)^i lg_T(H^i(C)). If C_1 → C_2 → C_3 → is an exact triangle in D^b(S) with compatible T-actions and two of the C_i have finite-length cohomology, so does the third and lg_T(C_2) = lg_T(C_1) + lg_T(C_3). If f ∈ S and H^*(C) is finitely generated over T, so is H^*(C ⊗^L_S S/(f)).
items.note: P9: 'Establish localization, additivity and the needed finite-length assertions before using this identity to transport component support.' Included in the reviewed node P9/derived-length-identity.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3: splitting off a maximal ideal that is a minimal prime
items.statement: If A is a Noetherian ring and 𝔪 is a maximal ideal of A that is also a minimal prime ideal, then A ≅ A_𝔪 × B for some ring B (A_𝔪 = eA is Artinian local for an idempotent e lifting (1, 0) ∈ A/𝔪 × A/I, I the intersection of the other minimal primes).
items.note: Reviewed node P9/derived-length-identity: '(Idempotent localization) If A is Noetherian and m is a maximal ideal that is a minimal prime, then A ≅ A_m × B.' Library pointers (for parts only): Mathlib's lifting of idempotents along nilpotent kernels (e.g. the CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents / IsIdempotentElem lifting lemmas) plus Chinese remainder; the lemma itself was not seen in Mathlib.

items.name: Idempotent localization C_𝔭 = e_𝔭(C ⊗_S S_𝔮)
items.statement: Let S be Noetherian, T a finite S-algebra, 𝔭 a minimal prime of T, C ∈ D^b(S) with T → End_{D^b(S)}(C) over S, and 𝔮 = 𝔭 ∩ S. Then 𝔭 is also maximal in T_𝔮, so T_𝔮 ≅ T_𝔭 × B by Lemma 6.3.3; with e_𝔭 the idempotent of (1, 0), put C_𝔭 = e_𝔭(C ⊗_S S_𝔮) ∈ D^b(S_𝔮), with its action of T_𝔭. It is not literally a localization over T, but if C is a complex of T-modules C^i then C_𝔭 is represented by (C^i_𝔭). If H^*(C) is finitely generated over S, H^*(C_𝔭) has finite length over T_𝔭.
items.note: P9: 'localize this derived action by idempotents; do not assume an unprovided strict T-module chain model.'

items.name: Lemma 6.3.4: derived length identity modulo a nonzerodivisor
items.statement: Let S be an excellent local ring, f ∈ 𝔪_S a nonzerodivisor, T a finite S-algebra and 𝔪 a maximal ideal of T with Spec T_𝔪 irreducible and T_𝔪/(f) of Krull dimension 0 (so dim T_𝔪 ≤ 1). If dim T_𝔪 = 0, then lg_{T_𝔪}((C ⊗^L_S S/(f))_𝔪) = 0 for every C ∈ D^b(S) with finitely generated cohomology and T → End_{D^b(S)}(C) over S. Otherwise T_𝔪 has a unique prime 𝔭 ≠ 𝔪, and there is a ∈ ℤ_{>0} with lg_{T_𝔪}((C ⊗^L_S S/(f))_𝔪) = a·lg_{T_𝔭}(C_𝔭) for every such C. (Remark after the lemma: for perfect C the finiteness is automatic, and an S-subalgebra T ⊆ End_{D^b(S)}(C) is finite over S.)
items.note: P9: 'For an excellent local base S, a nonzerodivisor f in its maximal ideal, and a finite S-algebra T acting through End in the bounded derived category on a perfect S-complex ... prove the dimension-zero vanishing and dimension-one generic-length formula for the Euler characteristic after derived reduction modulo f.' (C ⊗^L S/(f))_𝔪 uses the idempotent construction for the minimal prime 𝔪 of T/fT.

items.name: The abstract Ihara-avoidance set-up (§6.3.5)
items.statement: Λ is a power series ring over 𝒪, and one is given: (1) S_∞ = Λ⟦X_1, …, X_r⟧ with augmentation ideal 𝔞_∞ = (X_1, …, X_r); (2) perfect complexes C_∞, C′_∞ of S_∞-modules and a fixed isomorphism C_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/ϖ ≅ C′_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/ϖ in D(S_∞/ϖ); (3) S_∞-subalgebras T_∞ ⊂ End_{D(S_∞)}(C_∞) and T′_∞ ⊂ End_{D(S_∞)}(C′_∞) with the same image T̄_∞ in End_{D(S_∞/ϖ)}(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ) = End_{D(S_∞/ϖ)}(C′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ) (T_∞, T′_∞ are then finite over S_∞); (4) Noetherian complete local S_∞-algebras R_∞, R′_∞ with surjections R_∞ ↠ T_∞/I_∞, R′_∞ ↠ T′_∞/I′_∞, I_∞, I′_∞ nilpotent, with images Ī_∞, Ī′_∞ in T̄_∞ (so supports of H^*(C_∞), H^*(C′_∞) over R_∞, R′_∞ make sense and lie in Spec T_∞, Spec T′_∞, finite over Spec S_∞); (5) an isomorphism R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ compatible with the S_∞-algebra structures and with the actions on H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞) = H^*(C′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞); (6) integers q_0 ∈ ℤ, l_0 ∈ ℤ_{≥0}.
items.note: Reviewed node P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara states exactly this set-up. PA.3: 'compare patched complexes for two systems of local conditions which agree modulo a chosen coefficient ideal. Prove compatibility of Hecke and deformation-ring actions'.

items.name: Assumption 6.3.6: dimension, component and generic-concentration hypotheses
items.statement: (1) dim R_∞ = dim R′_∞ = dim S_∞ − l_0 and dim R_∞/ϖ = dim R′_∞/ϖ = dim S_∞ − l_0 − 1. (2) Each generic point of Spec R_∞/ϖ of maximal dimension (dim R_∞ − 1) is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R_∞ of dimension dim R_∞; Spec R′_∞ has a unique generic point x′ of dimension dim R_∞; generic points of Spec R_∞, Spec R′_∞, Spec R_∞/ϖ not of maximal dimension have dimension < dim S_∞ − l_0 − 1 (so the maximal-dimensional generic points of Spec R_∞, Spec R′_∞ have characteristic 0). (3) There is a one-dimensional characteristic-0 prime 𝔭 ⊃ 𝔞_∞ of S_∞ with H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/𝔭)[1/p] ≠ 0 and nonzero only in degrees [q_0, q_0 + l_0]. Also noted: Supp_{R_∞}(H^*(C_∞)) = Spec T_∞ and Supp_{R′_∞}(H^*(C′_∞)) = Spec T′_∞, since the kernel of T_∞ → End_{S_∞}(H^*(C_∞)) is nilpotent.
items.note: Reviewed node P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara: 'The dimension, component and generic-concentration assumptions of ACC+ Assumption 6.3.6 are numerical hypotheses to be verified by the arithmetic consumer (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.3).' PA.3: 'Establish the generic support implication used for derived Ihara avoidance, with the exact hypotheses on local rings and residual images.'

items.name: Lemma 6.3.7: transfer of nonzero derived length between a generic point and its reduction
items.statement: Let x̄ be a minimal prime of R_∞/(ϖ) of dimension dim S_∞ − l_0 − 1 containing a minimal prime x of R_∞ of dimension dim S_∞ − l_0. Then R_{∞,x̄} has x as its unique minimal prime and R_{∞,x̄}/(ϖ) has dimension 0, and: (1) if x̄ ∈ Spec T_∞ and lg_{T_{∞,x̄}}((C_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/(ϖ))_{x̄}) ≠ 0, then x ∈ Spec T_∞ and lg_{T_{∞,x}}(C_{∞,x}) ≠ 0; (2) if x ∈ Spec T_∞ then x̄ ∈ Spec T_∞, and if moreover lg_{T_{∞,x}}(C_{∞,x}) ≠ 0 then lg_{T_{∞,x̄}}((C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/(ϖ))_{x̄}) ≠ 0. The same holds for R′_∞, T′_∞, C′_∞.
items.note: Covered by the reviewed node P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara (source 'Lemma 6.3.7'). An immediate corollary of Lemma 6.3.4 after localizing S_∞ at x̄ ∩ S_∞.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.8: full support on maximal-dimensional components (derived Ihara avoidance)
items.statement: In the set-up of §6.3.5 under Assumption 6.3.6, Supp_{R_∞}(H^*(C_∞)) = Spec T_∞ ⊂ Spec R_∞ contains every irreducible component of Spec R_∞ of maximal dimension.
items.note: P9: 'Provide algebraic derived Ihara-avoidance lemmas comparing support when auxiliary local types change'; reviewed node P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara quotes this conclusion. PA.3 is the arithmetic verification. Proof uses [KT17, Lem. 2.3] and [CG18, Lem. 6.2] (P9/codimension-amplitude-lemma).

items.name: Corollary 6.3.9: support after specialization at a characteristic-0 point
items.statement: Let x be a prime of R_∞ on an irreducible component of Spec R_∞ of maximal dimension and y = x ∩ S_∞. Then x lies in the support over Spec R_∞ of H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/y)_y; if y is one-dimensional of characteristic 0, x lies in the support of H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/y)[1/p].
items.note: Reviewed node P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara includes this ('for x on such a component with contraction y in S_∞ the support of H*(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/y)_y contains x'). PA.3: 'characteristic-zero localization and the specialization of cohomological amplitude'. Proof uses the Tor spectral sequence (P7).

items.name: Ultrapatching set-up: the patching datum (fixed ultrafilter, S_∞, R_∞ and the finite-level systems)
items.statement: Fix a non-principal ultrafilter 𝔉 on ℕ = {N ≥ 1} and a ring Λ isomorphic to a power series ring over 𝒪. Let δ, g, q be positive integers, Δ_∞ = ℤ_p^{nq}, 𝒯 a formal power series ring over Λ (framing variables) and S_∞ = 𝒯⟦Δ_∞⟧, an augmented Λ-algebra with augmentation ideal 𝔞_∞. Let R^loc, R′^loc ∈ CNL_Λ with a fixed isomorphism R^loc/ϖ ≅ R′^loc/ϖ, and let R_∞, R′_∞ be the power series rings in g variables over R^loc, R′^loc. Input, for each N ∈ ℕ ∪ {0}: (1) a quotient Δ_N of Δ_∞ with ker(Δ_∞ → Δ_N) ⊂ (p^N ℤ_p)^{nq} (Δ_0 = 1), and S_N = 𝒯[Δ_N]; (2) perfect complexes 𝒞_N, 𝒞′_N ∈ D(Λ[Δ_N]) with an isomorphism 𝒞_N ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ/ϖ[Δ_N] ≅ 𝒞′_N ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ/ϖ[Δ_N] in D(Λ/ϖ[Δ_N]) (written 𝒞_N/ϖ ≅ 𝒞′_N/ϖ), and commutative Λ[Δ_N]-subalgebras T_N ⊂ End_{D(Λ[Δ_N])}(𝒞_N), T′_N ⊂ End_{D(Λ[Δ_N])}(𝒞′_N) with the same image T̄_N in End_{D(Λ/ϖ[Δ_N])}(𝒞_N/ϖ) = End_{D(Λ/ϖ[Δ_N])}(𝒞′_N/ϖ); (3) rings R_N, R′_N ∈ CNL_{Λ[Δ_N]} with R_N/ϖ ≅ R′_N/ϖ, and R^loc-, R′^loc-algebra structures on 𝒯 ⊗̂_Λ R_N, 𝒯 ⊗̂_Λ R′_N compatible mod ϖ with R_N/ϖ ≅ R′_N/ϖ and R^loc/ϖ ≅ R′^loc/ϖ; (4) surjective R^loc- and R′^loc-algebra maps R_∞ → 𝒯 ⊗̂_Λ R_N and R′_∞ → 𝒯 ⊗̂_Λ R′_N, compatible mod ϖ; (5) nilpotent ideals I_N ⊂ T_N, I′_N ⊂ T′_N of nilpotence degree ≤ δ and continuous surjections R_N → T_N/I_N, R′_N → T′_N/I′_N such that, with Ī_N, Ī′_N the images in T̄_N, the induced maps R_N/ϖ → T̄_N/(Ī_N + Ī′_N) and R′_N/ϖ → T̄_N/(Ī_N + Ī′_N) agree under R_N/ϖ ≅ R′_N/ϖ. Level-0 compatibility (N ≥ 1): isomorphisms π_N: 𝒞_N ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ 𝒞_0 and π′_N: 𝒞′_N ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ 𝒞′_0 in D(Λ), compatible mod ϖ, such that the induced maps T_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ → End_{D(Λ)}(𝒞_0) (resp. primed) factor through maps T_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ → T_0 (resp. T′_N ⊗ Λ → T′_0) that become surjective after composing with T_0 → T_0/I_0 (resp. T′_0 → T′_0/I′_0); and isomorphisms R_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ R_0, R′_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ R′_0, compatible mod ϖ and with the maps from R_∞, R′_∞ in (4), under which, writing I_{N,0}, I′_{N,0} for the images of I_N, I′_N in T_0/I_0, T′_0/I′_0, the surjections R_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ → (T_0/I_0)/I_{N,0} and R′_N ⊗ Λ → (T′_0/I′_0)/I′_{N,0} coincide with the maps R_0 → (T_0/I_0)/I_{N,0} and R′_0 → (T′_0/I′_0)/I′_{N,0}.
items.note: P8: 'Construct patching from systems (R_N,S_N,C_N) where S_N is a finite quotient of O[Δ_N] ... State the compatibility of derived augmentation, residual rings, chosen framings and transition maps. Fix the ultrafilter in the ultrapatching construction.' The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) states exactly this input list. PA.4: 'Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter as in ACC+ §6.4.1.' As printed, (4) reads 'R′∞ → T ⊗̂Λ RN' and (5) reads 'R′N → TN/I′N'; the statement above uses the evident corrections R′_N and T′_N. Library pointers (for parts only): Mathlib's Filter.hyperfilter / Ultrafilter supplies a non-principal ultrafilter on ℕ.

items.name: Finite-level patched objects 𝒞(J,N), T(J,N), I(J,N), R(d,J,N)
items.statement: For an open ideal J ⊂ S_∞, let I_J be the (cofinite) set of N ∈ ℕ with ker(S_∞ → S_N) ⊂ J. For N ∈ I_J: 𝒞(J,N) = S_∞/J ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} 𝒞_N ∈ D(S_∞/J); T(J,N) = the image of S_∞/J ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} T_N in End_{D(S_∞/J)}(𝒞(J,N)); I(J,N) = the ideal of T(J,N) generated by the image of I_N, so I(J,N)^δ = 0; and for d ≥ 1, R(d,J,N) = R_N/𝔪_{R_N}^d ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} S_∞/J. For all d, J, N there is a surjective R^loc-algebra map R_∞ → R(d,J,N), factoring through R_∞/𝔪_{R_∞}^{e(d,J)} for some e(d,J) independent of N. (Convention of §6.4.2: except for Remark 6.4.14 and Proposition 6.4.17, everything is stated for 𝒞_N and holds equally for 𝒞′_N.)
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) proof step: 'Definition 6.4.3: C(J, N) = S_∞/J ⊗^L C_N, T(J, N) its Hecke image, I(J, N)^δ = 0, R(d, J, N) = R_N/m^d ⊗ S_∞/J, factoring through R_∞/m^{e(d,J)} independent of N'.

items.name: Minimal complexes ℱ(J,N) and their ranks
items.statement: For each pair (J,N) with N ∈ I_J fix a minimal complex ℱ(J,N) of finite free S_∞/J-modules quasi-isomorphic to 𝒞(J,N) ([KT17, Lem. 2.3]). Then rk_{S_∞/J} ℱ(J,N)^i = dim_k H^i(𝒞_0 ⊗^L_Λ k) for every i ∈ ℤ; in particular the ranks and degree range are independent of J and N.
items.note: P7: 'construct minimal representatives over local rings, uniqueness up to homotopy, Tor-amplitude'; the P7 node 'perfect-complexes-tor-amplitude-and-minimal-models' has acceptance test 'ACC+ 6.4.3: minimal complexes F(J, N) have ranks dim_k H^i(C₀ ⊗^L k), giving uniformly bounded presentations.' The P8 node lists the rank formula as a proved consequence.

items.name: Remark 6.4.4: the Galois surjection factors through R(d,J,N) uniformly in N
items.statement: The surjection R_N → T_N/I_N induces a surjection R_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} S_∞/J → T(J,N)/I(J,N). There is an integer d_0(J), depending on J but not on N, such that for every d ≥ d_0(J) and every x ∈ 𝔪_{T_N} the image of x^d in End_{D(S_∞/J)}(𝒞(J,N)) (hence in T(J,N)) is 0; so for d ≥ d_0(J) the surjection factors through a surjection R(d,J,N) → T(J,N)/I(J,N). (Proof: H^*(𝒞(J,N) ⊗^L_{S_∞/J} k) ≅ H^*(𝒞_0 ⊗^L_Λ k) has dimension independent of J, N, so x^{d_1} kills it; the spectral sequence of a filtered complex (S_∞/J of finite length) gives x^{d_2}H^*(𝒞(J,N)) = 0; perfectness with amplitude bounded in terms of 𝒞_0 and [KT17, Lem. 2.5] give d_0(J).)
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) proof step: 'Remark 6.4.4 shows R(d, J, N) → T(J, N)/I(J, N) for d sufficiently large depending on J but not on N (using KT17 Lem. 2.5 and the spectral sequence of a filtered complex)'. IHG.2 plans the input: 'Establish the nilpotence bound for the ideal of degree-zero derived endomorphisms acting trivially on all cohomology of a bounded-amplitude object ... Preserve the dependence on amplitude.'

items.name: Remark 6.4.5: the level-0 identifications s(J) and π_{J,N}
items.statement: If 𝔞_∞ ⊂ J, then S_∞/J = Λ/s(J) for an open ideal s(J) ⊂ Λ, and for N ∈ I_J the isomorphism π_N: 𝒞_N ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ 𝒞_0 induces an isomorphism π_{J,N}: 𝒞(J,N) ≅ 𝒞_0 ⊗^L_Λ Λ/s(J).
items.note: P8: 'the augmentation isomorphism C_∞⊗ᴸ_{S_∞}O ≅ C_original'; the finite-level identification is the input to Proposition 6.4.10(3) in the P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4).

items.name: Remark 6.4.6: change of the open ideal J at finite level
items.statement: For open ideals J_1 ⊂ J_2 of S_∞ and N ∈ I_{J_1}, the natural map 𝒞(J_1,N) → 𝒞(J_2,N) induces a quasi-isomorphism S_∞/J_2 ⊗^L_{S_∞/J_1} 𝒞(J_1,N) ≅ 𝒞(J_2,N); consequently there is a surjection T(J_1,N) → T(J_2,N) carrying I(J_1,N) onto I(J_2,N), hence a surjection T(J_1,N)/I(J_1,N) → T(J_2,N)/I(J_2,N).
items.note: P7: 'derived tensor products' and 'derived coefficient change'; P8: 'Prove ... the comparison of finite-level Hecke actions'. Used in the P8 node for base change in J.

items.name: The ultrafilter point x_𝔉 and ultraproducts by localization
items.statement: For J open, 𝔉 restricts to a non-principal ultrafilter on the cofinite set I_J (still written 𝔉). It corresponds to a point x_𝔉 ∈ Spec(∏_{N∈I_J} S_∞/J) ([GN22, Lem. 2.2.2]), and the localization (∏_{N∈I_J} S_∞/J)_{x_𝔉} is canonically isomorphic to S_∞/J.
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'Ultraproducts localized at the point x_F of Spec ∏ S_∞/J (GN22 Lem. 2.2.2) define C(J, ∞), R(d, J, ∞), T(J, ∞), I(J, ∞)'. The node imports GN22 Lemma 2.2.2 without proof (a recorded gap; IKM-24's extraction notes the same). Library pointers (for parts only): Mathlib Filter.Germ / Filter.Product give ultrapowers but not (∏A)_{x_𝔉} ≅ A for a finite local ring A.

items.name: Definition 6.4.7: the ultrapatched finite objects 𝒞(J,∞), R(d,J,∞), T(J,∞), I(J,∞)
items.statement: Write U(M_•) = (∏_{N∈I_J} S_∞/J)_{x_𝔉} ⊗_{∏_{N∈I_J} S_∞/J} ∏_{N∈I_J} M_N. Define 𝒞(J,∞) = U(𝒞(J,·)) ∈ D(S_∞/J); R(d,J,∞) = U(R(d,J,·)); T(J,∞) = the image of U(T(J,·)) in End_{D(S_∞/J)}(𝒞(J,∞)); and I(J,∞) ⊂ T(J,∞) = the image of U(I(J,·)) in T(J,∞).
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) statement: 'C(J, ∞) = (∏_{N} S_∞/J)_{x_F} ⊗ ∏ C(J, N) is perfect over S_∞/J'.

items.name: Remark 6.4.8: R(d,J,∞) is a quotient of R_∞/𝔪^{e(d,J)}
items.statement: Since every R(d,J,N) is a quotient of the finite ring R_∞/𝔪_{R_∞}^{e(d,J)} (so the R(d,J,N) have bounded cardinality), the ultraproduct R(d,J,∞) is itself a quotient of R_∞/𝔪_{R_∞}^{e(d,J)}.
items.note: P8: 'Uniform bounds, compactness of finite presentation data and cofinality are proved before taking a limit.' Covered by the P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) (R(d, J, ∞)).

items.name: Lemma 6.4.9: nilpotence and the Galois surjection at level (J,∞)
items.statement: (1) I(J,∞) is a nilpotent ideal of T(J,∞) with I(J,∞)^δ = 0. (2) For d sufficiently large depending on J, the maps R(d,J,N) → T(J,N)/I(J,N) of Remark 6.4.4 induce a surjective S_∞/J-algebra map R(d,J,∞) → T(J,∞)/I(J,∞).
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) proof step: 'Lemma 6.4.9 gives nilpotence and the surjection.'

items.name: Proposition 6.4.10(1): perfectness of the ultraproduct complex
items.statement: For every open ideal J ⊂ S_∞, 𝒞(J,∞) is a perfect complex of S_∞/J-modules. (By [GN22, Cor. 2.2.7], since by minimal resolutions every 𝒞(J,N) is quasi-isomorphic to a complex of finite free S_∞/J-modules of rank ≤ D concentrated in degrees [a,b], with D, a, b independent of N.)
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'Proposition 6.4.10: perfectness from uniform rank and degree bounds (GN22 Cor. 2.2.7)'. P7 owns perfectness and minimal models. GN22 Cor. 2.2.7 is imported without proof by the node.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.10(2),(5): stabilization of Hecke data on an ultrafilter set; surjections at level (J,∞)
items.statement: (2) The minimal complexes ℱ(J,N), N ∈ I_J, fall into finitely many isomorphism classes, so there is Σ_0 ∈ 𝔉 with all ℱ(J,N) (N ∈ Σ_0) isomorphic to a single complex ℱ(J,∞) (the minimal complex of 𝒞(J,∞)), and Σ_1 ⊂ Σ_0 with Σ_1 ∈ 𝔉 such that, under the induced identifications of the finite algebras End_{D(S_∞/J)}(𝒞(J,N)), T(J,∞) ≅ T(J,N) and I(J,∞) ↔ I(J,N) for all N ∈ Σ_1; hence the surjections R_∞ → T(J,N)/I(J,N) induce a surjection R_∞ → T(J,∞)/I(J,∞). (5) For open J_1 ⊂ J_2, the map 𝒞(J_1,∞) → 𝒞(J_2,∞) induces a surjection T(J_1,∞) → T(J_2,∞) carrying I(J_1,∞) onto I(J_2,∞).
items.locator: §6.4.2, Proposition 6.4.10(2),(5) and the paragraph defining ℱ(J,∞), pp. 1056–1057
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'a set in F on which all F(J, N) and Hecke data are isomorphic identifies T(J, ∞) with T(J, N)'.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.10(3),(4): level-0 identification and base change in J for ultraproduct complexes
items.statement: (3) If 𝔞_∞ ⊂ J, the isomorphisms π_{J,N} induce π_{J,∞}: 𝒞(J,∞) ≅ 𝒞_0 ⊗^L_Λ Λ/s(J). (4) For open ideals J_1 ⊂ J_2, the maps 𝒞(J_1,N) → 𝒞(J_2,N) in D(S_∞/J_1), N ∈ I_{J_1}, induce S_∞/J_2 ⊗^L_{S_∞/J_1} 𝒞(J_1,∞) ≅ 𝒞(J_2,∞). (Proof of (4): ∏ S_∞/J_2 is finitely presented over ∏ S_∞/J_1, so tensoring with it commutes with products [Stacks, Tag 059K]; localize at x_𝔉, using that I_{J_1} is cofinite in I_{J_2}.)
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'base change in J uses exactness of products and Stacks tag 059K'. P7: 'derived tensor products'.

items.name: Definition 6.4.11: the patched complex 𝒞_∞ and patched Hecke algebra T_∞
items.statement: 𝒞_∞ = lim_r ℱ(𝔪_{S_∞}^r, ∞), a complex of S_∞-modules, where for each r ≥ 1 the transition map is a chosen map of complexes lifting the natural map 𝒞(𝔪^{r+1},∞) → 𝒞(𝔪^r,∞) in D(S_∞/𝔪^{r+1}) (it exists because ℱ(𝔪^{r+1},∞) is a bounded complex of free S_∞/𝔪^{r+1}-modules, so Hom_{K(S_∞/𝔪^{r+1})}(ℱ(𝔪^{r+1},∞), ℱ(𝔪^r,∞)) = Hom_{D(S_∞/𝔪^{r+1})}(𝒞(𝔪^{r+1},∞), 𝒞(𝔪^r,∞))). T_∞ = lim_J T(J,∞) along the surjections of Proposition 6.4.10(5), and I_∞ ⊂ T_∞ is the ideal defined by the system I(J,∞); I_∞^δ = 0.
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'C_∞ = lim_r F(m^r, ∞) (minimal complexes with chosen lifts of transition maps)'. P7: 'Work with finite coefficient quotients before inverse limits ... Morphisms, homotopies and Hecke actions must survive the inverse system'.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.12(1),(2): structure and endomorphisms of 𝒞_∞
items.statement: (1) 𝒞_∞ is a bounded complex of finite free S_∞-modules (with rk ℱ(𝔪^r,∞)^i = dim_k H^i(𝒞_0 ⊗^L_Λ k) for all r and S_∞/𝔪^r ⊗ ℱ(𝔪^{r+1},∞) ≅ ℱ(𝔪^r,∞), since quasi-isomorphisms of minimal complexes are isomorphisms), and for every open ideal J there is an isomorphism 𝒞_∞ ⊗_{S_∞} S_∞/J ≅ 𝒞(J,∞) in D(S_∞/J). (2) The natural map End_{D(S_∞)}(𝒞_∞) → lim_J End_{D(S_∞/J)}(𝒞(J,∞)) is an isomorphism (by (1) and the proof of [KT17, Lem. 2.13(3)]); hence T_∞ ↪ End_{D(S_∞)}(𝒞_∞).
items.note: P8: 'its continuous action on C_∞ in the derived category ... Prove finite generation, perfectness'. The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'End_{D(S_∞)}(C_∞) = lim End(C(J, ∞)), so T_∞ = lim T(J, ∞) acts faithfully in the derived category'. KT17 Lemma 2.13 is imported without proof (recorded gap of P7/P8).

items.name: Proposition 6.4.12(3): the patched Galois surjection R_∞ → T_∞/I_∞
items.statement: The surjective Λ-algebra maps R_∞ → T(J,∞)/I(J,∞) induce a surjection R_∞ → T_∞/I_∞ (Mittag-Leffler for the finite rings T(J,∞) gives T_∞/I_∞ ≅ lim_J T(J,∞)/I(J,∞)), which factors as R_∞ → lim_{d,J} R(d,J,∞) followed by the S_∞-algebra map lim_{d,J} R(d,J,∞) → T_∞/I_∞ obtained as the inverse limit of the maps of Lemma 6.4.9(2).
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'Mittag-Leffler for finite rings gives R_∞ ↠ T_∞/I_∞'.

items.name: Remark 6.4.13: independence of the transition-map choices
items.statement: H^*(𝒞_∞) ≅ lim_J H^*(𝒞_∞/J) = lim_J H^*(𝒞(J,∞)), so the cohomology of 𝒞_∞ does not depend on the chosen transition maps; if 𝒟_∞ is built with other choices, Hom_{D(S_∞)}(𝒞_∞, 𝒟_∞) = lim_J Hom_{D(S_∞/J)}(𝒞(J,∞), 𝒞(J,∞)) (argument of Prop. 6.4.12(2)), so 𝒞_∞ and 𝒟_∞ are canonically isomorphic in D(S_∞) (for the fixed ultrafilter 𝔉).
items.note: PA.4: 'The patching owner proves the abstract construction, support statements and independence from the permitted transition-map choices for that fixed ultrafilter, as in Remark 6.4.13. Do not claim independence from the ultrafilter itself'. The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'The cohomology of C_∞, and C_∞ up to canonical isomorphism in D(S_∞), are independent of the choices of transition maps'.

items.name: Remark 6.4.14: the S_∞-algebra structure on R_∞ and R′_∞, chosen compatibly mod ϖ
items.statement: The map α: R_∞ → lim_{d,J} R(d,J,∞) is surjective and its target is an S_∞-algebra. Since S_∞ is formally smooth over Λ, the map S_∞ → α(R_∞) lifts to S_∞ → R_∞; the lifts for R_∞ and R′_∞ can be chosen compatibly mod ϖ, because (lim R(d,J,∞))/ϖ = lim(R(d,J,∞)/ϖ) ≅ lim(R′(d,J,∞)/ϖ) and R_∞ → R_∞/ϖ × lim_{d,J} R(d,J,∞) → (lim_{d,J} R(d,J,∞))/ϖ, x ↦ (x mod ϖ, α(x)), (y,z) ↦ α(y) − z mod ϖ, is exact (and likewise for R′_∞). With this structure R_∞ is an S_∞-algebra and R_∞ → T_∞/I_∞ is an S_∞-algebra map.
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'R_∞ → T_∞/I_∞ is a surjective S_∞-algebra map after choosing S_∞ → R_∞ by formal smoothness' and 'choice of S_∞ → R_∞ compatibly mod ϖ via an exact sequence of limits'. The printed target of the second map is 'R(d, J, ∞)/ϖ'; it should be (lim_{d,J} R(d,J,∞))/ϖ.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.15: the surjection R_∞/𝔞_∞ → R_0
items.statement: The isomorphisms R(d,J,N) ⊗_{S_∞/J} S_∞/(J + 𝔞_∞) ≅ R_0/(𝔪_{R_0}^d, s(J + 𝔞_∞)) induce isomorphisms R(d,J,∞) ⊗_{S_∞/J} S_∞/(J + 𝔞_∞) ≅ R_0/(𝔪_{R_0}^d, s(J + 𝔞_∞)), hence surjections R_∞/𝔞_∞ → R_0/(𝔪_{R_0}^d, s(J+𝔞_∞)) factoring through R_∞/(𝔪_{R_∞}^{e(d,J)} + 𝔞_∞), and in the limit a surjection R_∞/𝔞_∞ → R_0.
items.note: Covered by the P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) proof step 'Remarks 6.4.13–6.4.14, Lemma 6.4.15 and Propositions 6.4.16–6.4.17'.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.16: specialization of the patched complex at the augmentation ideal
items.statement: There is an isomorphism 𝒞_∞/𝔞_∞ → 𝒞_0 in D(Λ) inducing a map T_∞ → T_0 whose composite with T_0 → T_0/I_0 is surjective. Writing I_{∞,0} for the image of I_∞ under this surjection, the resulting surjection R_∞/𝔞_∞ → (T_0/I_0)/I_{∞,0} is the composite of R_∞/𝔞_∞ → R_0 (Lemma 6.4.15) with the set-up map R_0 → (T_0/I_0)/I_{∞,0}.
items.note: P8: 'the augmentation isomorphism C_∞⊗ᴸ_{S_∞}O ≅ C_original'; the P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'C_∞/a_∞ ≅ C₀ compatibly with R₀, T₀ ... (Proposition 6.4.16, again via KT17 Lem. 2.13)'.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.17: comparison of the primed and unprimed patched complexes modulo ϖ
items.statement: (1) The quasi-isomorphisms 𝒞_N/ϖ ≅ 𝒞′_N/ϖ induce a quasi-isomorphism 𝒞_∞/ϖ ≅ 𝒞′_∞/ϖ. (2) Via this identification T_∞ and T′_∞ have the same image T̄_∞ in the endomorphism algebras of 𝒞_∞/ϖ and 𝒞′_∞/ϖ (in D(S_∞/ϖ); printed D(S_∞)). (3) With Ī_∞, Ī′_∞ the images of I_∞, I′_∞ in T̄_∞, the actions of R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ (through T_∞ and T′_∞) on H^*(𝒞_∞/ϖ)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞) and H^*(𝒞′_∞/ϖ)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞) are identified via 𝒞_∞/ϖ ≅ 𝒞′_∞/ϖ.
items.note: The P8 decomposition node 'P8/ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4): 'C_∞/ϖ ≅ C′_∞/ϖ with common Hecke image and compatible actions of R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ'. PA.3: 'Use the general patching owner to compare patched complexes for two systems of local conditions which agree modulo a chosen coefficient ideal. Prove compatibility of Hecke and deformation-ring actions'. Printed End_{D(S∞)} for the mod-ϖ endomorphisms (I5).

items.name: §6.5.1: standing data and hypotheses (1)–(17) for the Fontaine–Laffaille patching argument; the level K
items.statement: F is an imaginary CM field and we fix: (1) an integer n ≥ 2 and a prime p > n²; (2) a finite set S of finite places of F containing S_p; (3) a possibly empty subset R ⊂ S of places prime to p; (4) a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight λ; (5) an isomorphism ι: Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. Assume: (6) every prime l lying below a place of S, or ramified in F, splits in some imaginary quadratic subfield of F (so each place of S is split over F⁺ and F/F⁺ is everywhere unramified); (7) p is unramified in F; (8) λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} < p − 2n for every τ: F ↪ ℂ; (9) for each v ∈ S_p, with v̄ = v|_{F⁺}, there is a place v̄′ ≠ v̄ of F⁺ above p with Σ_{v̄″ ≠ v̄, v̄′} [F⁺_{v̄″}:ℚ_p] > ½[F⁺:ℚ]; (10) r̄_ι(π) is absolutely irreducible; (11) π_v is unramified for v | p; (12) π_v^{Iw_v} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R; (13) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p): π_v is unramified, v ∉ R^c and H²(F_v, ad r̄_ι(π)) = 0; (14) S − (R ∪ S_p) contains two places of distinct residue characteristics; (15) π_v is unramified at every finite v ∉ S; (16) for v ∈ R: q_v ≡ 1 mod p and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial; (17) r̄_ι(π) is decomposed generic (Definition 4.3.1) and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has enormous image (Definition 6.2.29). The level K = ∏_v K_v ⊂ GL_n(Ô_F): K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) for v ∉ S or v ∈ S_p; K_v = Iw_v for v ∈ R; K_v = Iw_{v,1} (pro-v Iwahori) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p).
items.locator: §6.5.1 (Application of the patching argument, Fontaine–Laffaille case), pp. 1061–1062
items.note: These are the hypotheses of Theorem 6.5.4. PA.3: 'Establish the generic support implication used for derived Ihara avoidance, with the exact hypotheses on local rings and residual images.' The residual-image inputs are separately planned (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 for 'enormous', AG2.7 for decomposed generic).

items.name: Lemma 6.5.2: two pro-v Iwahori factors of distinct residue characteristics force neatness
items.statement: Let K = ∏_v K_v ⊂ GL_n(Ô_F) be an open compact subgroup, and suppose there are places v, v′ of F with distinct residue characteristics q ≠ q′ such that K_v = Iw_{v,1} and K_{v′} = Iw_{v′,1}. Then K is neat (every g ∈ K is neat: the intersection over places w of the torsion subgroups Γ_w ⊂ Q̄^× of the groups generated by the eigenvalues of g_w is trivial). Proof: every eigenvalue α of an element of Iw_{v,1} has α − 1 in the maximal ideal of 𝒪_{F̄_v}, so a root of unity of prime order q″ in Γ_v ∩ Γ_{v′} has q″ = q and likewise q″ = q′.
items.note: No stage states a neatness criterion. ALS.0 only uses neat level ('Prove proper discontinuity and, at neat level, freeness'); PA.0 says 'Keep a non-neat groupoid model available until the source selects a sufficiently small level', which is what this lemma does. Also used for the ordinary level in §6.6.1. Route: a source of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.0 levels, ALS.3 Hecke correspondences, ALS.5 comparison).

items.name: The maximal ideal 𝔪, the deformation problems 𝒮_χ and the twisted coefficients 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1}) (FL case)
items.statement: By Theorem 2.4.10 there are a coefficient field E ⊂ Q̄_p and a maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, 𝒱_λ) with ρ̄_𝔪 ≅ r̄_ι(π); after enlarging E, the residue field of 𝔪 is k. For each tuple χ = (χ_{v,i})_{v∈R, 1≤i≤n} of characters χ_{v,i}: k(v)^× → 𝒪^× trivial mod ϖ, 𝒮_χ = (ρ̄_𝔪, S, {𝒪}_{v∈S}, {𝒟_v^{FL}}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {𝒟_v^χ}_{v∈R} ∪ {𝒟_v^□}_{v∈S−(R∪S_p)}); representatives ρ_{𝒮_χ} of the universal deformations are fixed so as to be identified mod ϖ via R_{𝒮_χ}/ϖ ≅ R_{𝒮_1}/ϖ; the local problems are formally smooth away from R. 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1}) = 𝒱_λ ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(χ^{-1}) as 𝒪[K_S]-module, K_S acting on 𝒱_λ through K_p and on 𝒪(χ^{-1}) through K_S → K_R = ∏_{v∈R} Iw_v → ∏_{v∈R} (k(v)^×)^n.
items.note: G8: 'For ACC+ Definition 6.2.2 use Λ=completed tensor product of the local Λ_v, absolutely irreducible residual representation and p∤2n'. L7: 'Construct Fontaine–Laffaille deformation conditions in the proven unramified small-weight range' and 'Export the precise local comparisons and component support input used in ACC+ §6.2'. The existence of 𝔪 is Theorem 2.4.10 (another reader's range).

items.name: Proposition 6.5.3: Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations of type 𝒮_χ at level K
items.statement: Under §6.5.1, for each χ as above there are an integer δ ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F:ℚ], an ideal J ⊂ T^S(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1})))_𝔪 with J^δ = 0, and a continuous surjection f_{𝒮_χ}: R_{𝒮_χ} → T^S(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1})))_𝔪/J such that for every finite place v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of f_{𝒮_χ} ∘ ρ_{𝒮_χ}(Frob_v) is the image of P_v(X). (Proof: the representation ρ_𝔪: G_{F,S∪S^c} → GL_n(T^S(…)_𝔪/J) of Theorem 2.3.7, conjugated so that ρ_𝔪 mod 𝔪 = ρ̄_𝔪; Theorem 4.5.1 gives the Fontaine–Laffaille condition at v | p; Theorem 3.1.1, applied with its S equal to S ∪ S^c and its R equal to S − S_p, gives the inertial characteristic-polynomial condition at v ∈ R and unramifiedness with the right Frobenius polynomial at v ∈ S^c − S.)
items.note: This is the N = 0 instance of set-up item (5) of §6.4.1 (surjections R_N → T_N/I_N with nilpotent I_N). PA.4: 'Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'. PA.1 (matrix row '§§4.4–4.5 | PA.1 | Degree shifting and Fontaine–Laffaille comparison') supplies Theorem 4.5.1: 'transfer the local p-adic Hodge condition'. Theorem 2.3.7 is routed elsewhere (TC.4/IHG.5 in BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25). No stage names the combined deformation-to-Hecke map for CM GL_n explicitly; PA.4 is the closest planner.

items.name: Theorem 6.5.4: full support of H^*(X_K, 𝒱_λ(1))_𝔪 over R_{𝒮_1} (Fontaine–Laffaille case)
items.statement: Under assumptions (1)–(17) of §6.5.1, H^*(X_K, 𝒱_λ(1))_𝔪 has full support over R_{𝒮_1}, i.e. its support in Spec R_{𝒮_1}, defined through f_{𝒮_1}: R_{𝒮_1} → T^S(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ(1)))_𝔪/J (Prop. 6.5.3) as in §6.3.5, is all of Spec R_{𝒮_1} (although H^* is not literally an R_{𝒮_1}-module).
items.note: PA.3: 'Establish the generic support implication used for derived Ihara avoidance, with the exact hypotheses on local rings and residual images ... Do not demand or infer integral R=T from a support comparison alone.' The abstract step is Prop. 6.3.8 = P9 node 'support-transport-avoiding-ihara' ('Supp_{R_∞}(H*(C_∞)) = Spec T_∞ contains every irreducible component of Spec R_∞ of maximal dimension'). The arithmetic patching verification is items 266–267 (PA.4).

items.name: Corollary 6.5.5: automorphy lifting under the §6.5.1 hypotheses
items.statement: Under (1)–(17) of §6.5.1, let ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) be continuous with: (1) ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π); (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline for every v | p, with HT_τ(ρ) = {λ_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, …, λ_{ιτ,n}} (the j-th entry λ_{ιτ,j} + n − j) for every τ: F ↪ Q̄_p; (3) ρ unramified at every finite v ∉ S; (4) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} unipotently ramified for v ∈ R. Then ρ is automorphic: there is a cuspidal regular algebraic automorphic representation Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ with ρ ≅ r_ι(Π), and Π_v is unramified at every finite v with v | p or v ∉ S. (Proof: conjugate ρ into GL_n(𝒪) with ρ mod ϖ = ρ̄_𝔪; it is of type 𝒮_1, giving f: R_{𝒮_1} → E; by Theorem 6.5.4, ker f ∈ Supp H^*(X_K, 𝒱_λ(1))_𝔪[1/p]; Theorem 2.4.10 gives Π with (Π^∞)^K ≠ 0.)
items.note: No stage states an automorphy lifting theorem for GL_n over CM fields (ag.py finds none for 'automorphy lifting'). PA.3 plans 'characteristic-zero localization' of the support statement (Theorem 6.5.4); the passage from a characteristic-zero point of the support to Π is Theorem 2.4.10. BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 also recorded its analogue (Theorem 3.2.1) as missing. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Auxiliary Taylor–Wiles levels K_1(Q) ⊂ K_0(Q) ⊂ K and the Hecke algebra maps (6.5.6), (6.5.7)
items.statement: Let (Q, (α_{v,1},…,α_{v,n})_{v∈Q}) be a Taylor–Wiles datum for 𝒮_1 (§6.2.28) such that for each v ∈ Q the residue characteristic l_v splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F. It is a Taylor–Wiles datum for every 𝒮_χ, and R_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} is an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra, Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q} Δ_v = ∏_{v∈Q} k(v)^×(p)^n. Good subgroups K_1(Q) ⊂ K_0(Q) ⊂ K: K_1(Q)_v = K_0(Q)_v = K_v for v ∉ Q (printed: v ∉ S ∪ Q); for v ∈ Q, K_0(Q)_v = Iw_v and K_1(Q)_v is the maximal pro-prime-to-p subgroup of Iw_v. Then K_0(Q)/K_1(Q) ≅ Δ_Q, and (6.5.6) there are surjective T^{S∪Q}-algebra maps _{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}T^{S∪Q}(K_0(Q)/K_1(Q), 𝒱) → T^{S∪Q}(K_0(Q), 𝒱) → T^{S∪Q}(K, 𝒱) (𝒱 = 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1})): the first from K_0(Q)-invariants (𝒪[Δ_Q] acting trivially on invariants), the second t ↦ [K:K_0(Q)]^{-1} π_{Q,*} ∘ t ∘ π_Q^* for the projection π_Q: X_{K_0(Q)} → X_K, where [K:K_0(Q)] ≡ (n!)^{|Q|} mod p is a unit since p > n. T^{S∪Q}_Q(K_0(Q), 𝒱) ⊂ End_{D(𝒪)}(RΓ(X_{K_0(Q)}, 𝒱)) is the commutative T^{S∪Q}(K_0(Q),𝒱)-subalgebra generated by the U_{v,i} (v ∈ Q, 1 ≤ i ≤ n), equivalently the image of T^{S∪Q}_Q (§3.1); T^{S∪Q}_Q(K_0(Q)/K_1(Q), 𝒱) ⊂ End_{D(𝒪[Δ_Q])}(RΓ_{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}(X_{K_1(Q)}, 𝒱)) likewise (an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra). (6.5.7): the first map of (6.5.6) extends to a surjection T^{S∪Q}_Q(K_0(Q)/K_1(Q), 𝒱) → T^{S∪Q}_Q(K_0(Q), 𝒱) sending U_{v,i} to U_{v,i}.
items.note: PA.4: 'Construct Taylor–Wiles auxiliary sets ... Track the size of the sets, congruences on residue cardinalities, selected eigenvalues and framed local deformation data ... Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'. ALS.3: 'Prove change-of-level and groupoid versions with stabilizer factors' (pullback/trace maps π_Q^*, π_{Q,*}). The printed condition 'If v ∉ S ∪ Q' leaves K_0(Q)_v unspecified at v ∈ S (I10).

items.name: The maximal ideals 𝔪^Q, 𝔪_0^Q, 𝔪_1^Q and the Taylor–Wiles ideals 𝔫_0^Q, 𝔫_1^Q
items.statement: With 𝒱 = 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1}): 𝔪^Q ⊂ T^{S∪Q}(K, 𝒱) is the pullback of 𝔪 under T^{S∪Q}(K,𝒱) ⊂ T^S(K,𝒱); 𝔪_0^Q ⊂ T^{S∪Q}(K_0(Q),𝒱) is the pullback of 𝔪^Q and 𝔪_1^Q ⊂ _{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}T^{S∪Q}(K_0(Q)/K_1(Q),𝒱) the pullback of 𝔪_0^Q under the maps (6.5.6); 𝔫_0^Q ⊂ T^{S∪Q}_Q(K_0(Q),𝒱) is the ideal generated by 𝔪_0^Q and the elements U_{v,i} − q_v^{i(1−i)/2} α_{v,1}⋯α_{v,i} (v ∈ Q, 1 ≤ i ≤ n); 𝔫_1^Q ⊂ T^{S∪Q}_Q(K_0(Q)/K_1(Q),𝒱) is the preimage of 𝔫_0^Q under (6.5.7).
items.note: PA.4: 'selected eigenvalues and framed local deformation data'. (Normalization check: with t_{v,i}(ϖ_v) = q_v^{i−1}[I_v diag(1,…,ϖ_v,…,1) I_v] (§2.2.5), U_{v,i} = q_v^{i(1−i)/2} t_{v,1}⋯t_{v,i}(ϖ_v), so on 𝔫_0^Q-eigenvectors t_{v,i}(ϖ_v) ↦ α_{v,i}, consistent with the proof of Prop. 6.5.11.)

items.name: Lemma 6.5.8: the auxiliary ideals are proper maximal ideals
items.statement: Each of 𝔪^Q, 𝔪_0^Q, 𝔪_1^Q, 𝔫_0^Q, 𝔫_1^Q is a (proper) maximal ideal. The content is that 𝔫_0^Q is proper, i.e. H^*(X_{K_0(Q)}, 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1})/ϖ)[𝔪_0^Q] contains a nonzero vector on which every U_{v,i} (v ∈ Q) acts by α_{v,1}⋯α_{v,i}; this follows from (the proof of) [KT17, Lem. 5.3] once H^*(X_K, 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1}))[𝔪^Q] is killed by a power of 𝔪, which follows from the existence of ρ̄_𝔪 and its local–global compatibility at v ∈ Q.
items.note: Part of verifying that the auxiliary-level system is a patching system: PA.4 'Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'. KT17 Lemma 5.3 is an unread external input.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.9: the auxiliary-level localized complexes recover the level-K complex
items.statement: The natural morphisms RΓ(X_K, 𝒱)_{𝔪^Q} → RΓ(X_K, 𝒱)_𝔪, RΓ(X_{K_0(Q)}, 𝒱)_{𝔫_0^Q} → RΓ(X_K, 𝒱)_{𝔪^Q} (trace), and RΓ(Δ_Q, RΓ_{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}(X_{K_1(Q)}, 𝒱)_{𝔫_1^Q}) → RΓ(X_{K_0(Q)}, 𝒱)_{𝔫_0^Q} are isomorphisms in D(𝒪) (𝒱 = 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1})). (Proof: the first because 𝔪 is the unique maximal ideal of T^S(K, 𝒱) above 𝔪^Q (printed: of T^{S∪Q}(K_0(Q), 𝒱)), shown in the proof of Lemma 6.5.8; the second reduces after ⊗^L_𝒪 k to tr_{K/K_0(Q)}: H^*(X_{K_0(Q)}, 𝒱/ϖ)_{𝔫_0^Q} ≅ H^*(X_K, 𝒱/ϖ)_{𝔪^Q}, which is [KT17, Lem. 5.4]; the third is clear from the definitions.)
items.note: PA.4: 'identify its specialization with the original complex'. This lemma gives 𝒞_N ⊗^L_{𝒪[Δ_N]} 𝒪 ≅ 𝒞_0 in the proof of Theorem 6.5.4. The printed proof names the wrong Hecke algebra (I2).

items.name: (6.5.10): the Taylor–Wiles Hecke algebra is local; nearly faithful modules
items.statement: There is a surjection _{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}T^{S∪Q}(RΓ_{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}(X_{K_1(Q)}, 𝒱)_{𝔫_1^Q}) → T^{S∪Q}(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱)_{𝔪^Q}) = T^{S∪Q}(K, 𝒱)_{𝔪^Q}; its source is a local 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra whose maximal ideal is the preimage of 𝔪^Q, because it acts nearly faithfully on H^*(X_{K_1(Q)}, 𝒱)_{𝔫_1^Q}. Definition ([Tay08, Def. 2.1]): a finitely generated module over a Noetherian local ring is nearly faithful if its annihilator is a nilpotent ideal.
items.note: R03.6: 'Derive when a patched module is faithful, nearly faithful, or supported on a specified union of components'. PA.3 also insists on keeping 'near faithfulness' distinct. The locality is part of PA.4's verification of the patching input.

items.name: Proposition 6.5.11: 𝒪[Δ_Q]-linear Galois representations over the Taylor–Wiles Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let 𝕋 = _{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}T^{S∪Q}(RΓ_{K_0(Q)/K_1(Q)}(X_{K_1(Q)}, 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1}))_{𝔫_1^Q}). There are δ ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F:ℚ], an ideal J ⊂ 𝕋 with J^δ = 0, and a continuous surjective 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra homomorphism f_{𝒮_{χ,Q}}: R_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} → 𝕋/J such that for every finite v ∉ S ∪ Q the characteristic polynomial of f_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} ∘ ρ_{𝒮_{χ,Q}}(Frob_v) is the image of P_v(X). (Proof: with T′ = T^{S∪Q}_Q(K_0(Q)/K_1(Q), 𝒱)_{𝔫_1^Q} ⊃ 𝕋 (a local inclusion of finite 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebras), Theorem 2.3.7 gives ρ_{𝔫_1^Q}: G_{F,S∪Q} → GL_n(T′/J′) lifting ρ̄_𝔪; the conditions at S are as in Prop. 6.5.3 and there is none at Q. For v ∈ Q define ψ_{v,i}: W_{F_v} → (T′)^× by ψ_{v,i}(Art_{F_v}(α)) = t_{v,i}(α); Theorem 3.1.1 gives det(X − ρ_{𝔫_1^Q}(σ)) = ∏_i (X − ψ_{v,i}(σ)) for σ ∈ W_{F_v} (after enlarging J′); the ψ_{v,i} mod 𝔫_1^Q send Frobenius to the pairwise distinct α_{v,i}, so [BC09, Prop. 1.5.1] gives ρ_{𝔫_1^Q}|_{W_{F_v}} ≅ ⊕_i ψ_{v,i}, whence 𝒪[Δ_v]-linearity (§6.2.18); take J = ker(𝕋 → T′/J′).)
items.note: This is set-up item (5) of §6.4.1 for N ≥ 1, with the Λ[Δ_N]-linearity the patching needs. PA.4: 'selected eigenvalues and framed local deformation data ... Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'. Inputs: Theorem 2.3.7 (TC.4/IHG.5), Theorem 3.1.1 (ACC+ §3, routed to AG2/IHG by PA's matrix).

items.name: The Taylor–Wiles patching data for Theorem 6.5.4 (FL case)
items.statement: Set q = h¹(F_S/F, ad ρ̄_𝔪(1)), g = qn − n²[F⁺:ℚ], Δ_∞ = ℤ_p^{nq}, 𝒯 = a power series ring over 𝒪 in n²|S| − 1 variables, S_∞ = 𝒯⟦Δ_∞⟧ with augmentation ideal 𝔞_∞ (Λ = 𝒪). Enlarge E to contain ζ_p and choose, for each v ∈ R, pairwise distinct χ_{v,1},…,χ_{v,n}: 𝒪_{F_v}^× → 𝒪^× trivial mod ϖ (possible as p > n, q_v ≡ 1 mod p); χ = ∏_{v∈R} χ_v on ∏_{v∈R} I_v. For N ≥ 1 choose Taylor–Wiles data (Q_N, (α_{v,i})_{v∈Q_N}) as in Proposition 6.2.33 (possible as r̄_ι(π)(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is enormous; any imaginary quadratic subfield of F), Q_0 = ∅, Δ_N = Δ_{Q_N} with a surjection Δ_∞ ↠ Δ_N whose kernel lies in (p^N ℤ_p)^{nq} (as q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N for v ∈ Q_N). R_N = R_{𝒮_{1,Q_N}}, R′_N = R_{𝒮_{χ,Q_N}} (R_0 = R_{𝒮_1}, R′_0 = R_{𝒮_χ}); R^loc = R^{S,loc}_{𝒮_1}, R′^loc = R^{S,loc}_{𝒮_χ} (§6.2.22), also the local rings of 𝒮_{·,Q_N}; canonical isomorphisms R^loc/ϖ ≅ R′^loc/ϖ, R_N/ϖ ≅ R′_N/ϖ, R_N ⊗_{𝒪[Δ_N]} 𝒪 ≅ R_0, R′_N ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ R′_0, compatible mod ϖ; R^loc-algebra structures on R_N ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒯 (Lemma 6.2.4); R_∞, R′_∞ = power series rings in g variables over R^loc, R′^loc with surjections onto the framed rings R_N ⊗̂ 𝒯, R′_N ⊗̂ 𝒯 (Prop. 6.2.25 for N = 0, using H⁰(F_S/F, ad ρ̄_𝔪(1)) = 0 because r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is irreducible and ζ_p ∉ F; Prop. 6.2.33(3) for N ≥ 1 — printed 'Proposition 6.2.32' and 'R_∞ → R_N'), compatible mod ϖ and with R_N ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ R_0. Complexes: 𝒞_0 = RHom_𝒪(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ(1))_𝔪, 𝒪)[−d], T_0 = T^S(K, 𝒱_λ(1))_𝔪, with H^i(𝒞_0)[1/p] ≅ Hom_E(H^{d−i}(X_K, 𝒱_λ(1))_𝔪[1/p], E) as T_0-modules; 𝒞′_0, T′_0 likewise with 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1}); for N ≥ 1, 𝒞_N = RHom_{𝒪[Δ_N]}(RΓ_{K_0(Q_N)/K_1(Q_N)}(X_{K_1(Q_N)}, 𝒱_λ(1))_{𝔫_1^{Q_N}}, 𝒪[Δ_N])[−d], T_N = _{K_0/K_1}T^{S∪Q_N}(RΓ_{K_0(Q_N)/K_1(Q_N)}(X_{K_1(Q_N)}, 𝒱_λ(1))_{𝔫_1^{Q_N}}), and 𝒞′_N, T′_N with 𝒱_λ(χ^{-1}). Claim: with I_N, I′_N from Props. 6.5.3/6.5.11 these data satisfy the set-up of §6.4.1: canonical 𝒞_N ⊗^L k[Δ_N] ≅ 𝒞′_N ⊗^L k[Δ_N] with T_N, T′_N having the same image T̄_N; 𝒞_N ⊗^L_{𝒪[Δ_N]} 𝒪 ≅ 𝒞_0 (Lemma 6.5.9), compatible mod ϖ; local 𝒪[Δ_N]-algebra surjections R_N → T_N/I_N, R′_N → T′_N/I′_N compatible mod ϖ and agreeing into T̄_N/(Ī_N + Ī′_N); T_N ⊗_{𝒪[Δ_N]} 𝒪 → T_0 surjective onto T_0/I_0 (Chebotarev and the Galois representation over T_0/I_0), and likewise primed.

Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching; identify its specialization with the original complex.'
