With T=S and q at least the indicated dual-Selmer dimension, construct exactly q primes ... and the local-to-global presentation with g=qn−n²[F⁺:Q] variables. Export the auxiliary diamond group and its exact rank/bounds to complex patching.' Cross-reference 'Proposition 6.2.32' is wrong in print (I3).

items.name: The dimension count and generic concentration for the FL patched system; conclusion of Theorem 6.5.4
items.statement: Applying §6.4.2 to the data of the previous item gives: bounded complexes 𝒞_∞, 𝒞′_∞ of free S_∞-modules, T_∞ ⊂ End_{D(S_∞)}(𝒞_∞), T′_∞ ⊂ End_{D(S_∞)}(𝒞′_∞), ideals with I_∞^δ = I′_∞^δ = 0, S_∞-algebra structures on R_∞, R′_∞ and S_∞-algebra surjections R_∞ → T_∞/I_∞, R′_∞ → T′_∞/I′_∞; surjections R_∞/𝔞_∞ ↠ R_0, R′_∞/𝔞_∞ ↠ R′_0; 𝒞_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/𝔞_∞ ≅ 𝒞_0 and 𝒞′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/𝔞_∞ ≅ 𝒞′_0 with T_∞ → T_0 surjective onto T_0/I_0 and R_∞/𝔞_∞ → (T_0/I_0)/I_{∞,0} factoring through R_0; 𝒞_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ ≅ 𝒞′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ with a common image T̄_∞ of T_∞ and T′_∞ and identified actions of R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ on H^*(𝒞_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞). By Lemma 6.2.26: every generic point of Spec R_∞/ϖ specializes from a unique generic point of Spec R_∞, all generic points of Spec R_∞ have characteristic 0, Spec R′_∞ is irreducible with characteristic-0 generic point, R_∞ is equidimensional, and dim R_∞ = dim R′_∞ = 1 + g + n²|S| + ½n(n−1)[F:ℚ]. For X_K with F CM, ℓ_0 = n[F⁺:ℚ] − 1; since dim S_∞ = n²|S| + qn and g = qn − n²[F⁺:ℚ] (printed twice as qn − n[F⁺:ℚ]), dim R_∞ = dim R′_∞ = dim S_∞ − ℓ_0. H^*(𝒞_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/𝔞_∞)[1/p] ≅ Hom_E(H^{d−*}(X_K, 𝒱_λ(1))_𝔪[1/p], E) is nonzero and concentrated in [q_0, q_0 + ℓ_0] by Theorem 2.4.10. Hence Assumption 6.3.6 holds, Proposition 6.3.8 gives full support of H^*(𝒞_∞) over R_∞, hence of H^*(𝒞_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/𝔞_∞) = H^*(𝒞_0) over R_∞/𝔞_∞ and so over R_{𝒮_1}.
items.note: PA.3: 'Prove compatibility of Hecke and deformation-ring actions, component support, characteristic-zero localization and the specialization of cohomological amplitude. Establish the generic support implication'. P9: 'the balanced-dimension conclusions used in Calegari–Geraghty' and its node 'support-transport-avoiding-ihara' (Assumption 6.3.6 'are numerical hypotheses to be verified by the arithmetic consumer (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.3)'). The printed g = qn − n[F⁺:ℚ] makes the displayed equality false (I4).

items.name: Proposition 6.5.13(1): soluble base change for regular algebraic cuspidal representations
items.statement: Fix n ≥ 2, a prime p and ι: Q̄_p → ℂ. Let F be imaginary CM or totally real and E/F a finite Galois extension with Gal(E/F) soluble and E imaginary CM or totally real. Let π be a cuspidal regular algebraic automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ = (λ_τ)_{τ∈Hom(F,ℂ)} with r_ι(π)|_{G_E} irreducible. Then there is a cuspidal regular algebraic π_E of GL_n(𝔸_E) of weight λ_{E,τ} = λ_{τ|_F} (τ ∈ Hom(E,ℂ); printed λ_{τ|E}) with r_ι(π_E) ≅ r_ι(π)|_{G_E}, and rec_{E_w}(π_E) = rec_{F_v}(π)|_{W_{E_w}} for every finite place w | v. (Proof: induct to E/F cyclic of prime order with generator σ and nontrivial η: Gal(E/F) → ℂ^×; π ⊗ (η ∘ Art_F^{-1}) ≇ π since otherwise r_ι(π)|_{G_E} would be reducible; [AC89, Ch. 3, Thms 4.2, 5.1] give Π cuspidal of weight λ_E with Π_w a lift of π_{w|F} at almost all w, and Chebotarev gives r_ι(Π) ≅ r_ι(π)|_{G_E}.)
items.note: ML.5: 'Register cyclic base change, automorphic induction and selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers with exact hypotheses'. The soluble iteration and the Galois-side compatibility are not spelled out there. The local identity rec_{E_w}(π_E) = rec_{F_v}(π)|_{W_{E_w}} at every w is asserted but the proof only treats almost all w (I13). The weight subscript is misprinted (I12).

items.name: Proposition 6.5.13(2): soluble descent of automorphy
items.statement: Same F, E, n, p, ι. Let ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) be continuous with ρ|_{G_E} irreducible, and suppose ρ|_{G_E} ≅ r_ι(π) for a cuspidal regular algebraic π of GL_n(𝔸_E) of weight λ. Define λ_F by λ_{F,τ} = λ_{τ′} for any extension τ′: E ↪ ℂ of τ: F ↪ ℂ; λ_F is independent of choices, and there is a cuspidal regular algebraic π_F of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ_F with ρ ≅ r_ι(π_F), and rec_{E_w}(π) = rec_{F_v}(π_F)|_{W_{E_w}} for every finite w | v (printed without the restriction). (Proof: for E/F cyclic of prime order, strong multiplicity one gives π^σ ≅ π; [AC89, Ch. 3, Thms 4.2, 5.1] give Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ_F with π_w a lift of Π_{w|F} at almost all w; Chebotarev gives r_ι(Π)|_{G_E} ≅ ρ|_{G_E}, and irreducibility of ρ|_{G_E} gives π_F = Π ⊗ (η ∘ Art_F^{-1})^i with r_ι(π_F) ≅ ρ.)
items.note: ML.5: 'Register cyclic base change ... with exact hypotheses'; ML.2: 'track compatible systems and descent' and 'descent to the original field requires its own theorem and hypotheses'. The printed local identity compares a W_{E_w}- with a W_{F_v}-representation (I12).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1.1: reduction to Corollary 6.5.5 by soluble base change
items.statement: Let F, ρ, π, λ, ι satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 6.1.1 ((1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline for v | p, p unramified in F; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous; (4) some σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, p > n²; (5) π cuspidal regular algebraic of weight λ with λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} < p − 2n, ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π), HT_τ(ρ) = {λ_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, …, λ_{ιτ,n}}, π_v unramified for v | p). The totally real case reduces to the imaginary CM case by base change (no details given). For imaginary F: choose V_0, V_1, V_2 and a soluble CM E/F as in the next two items and auxiliary places v_0, v′_0 so that §6.5.1 (1)–(17) hold for E, π_E and S = S′ ∪ {v_0, v′_0}; Corollary 6.5.5 for ρ|_{G_E} and Proposition 6.5.13(2) give a cuspidal regular algebraic Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ with ρ ≅ r_ι(Π), with Π_{E,w} unramified for w ∉ S; unramifiedness of Π_v at finite v ∤ p where ρ and π are unramified follows from the Varma argument (item 274). (The claim Π_v unramified for v | p in Theorem 6.1.1 is not addressed explicitly; it follows from Π_{E,w} unramified for w | p and p unramified in E.)
items.note: No stage owns the automorphy lifting theorem itself; PA.5 explicitly leaves 'the lifting theorem with its dedicated owner', which is not named. ML.2 ('Apply PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure with full regularity, polarization, residual-image, local and field-extension hypotheses; track compatible systems and descent') is its first consumer. The statement of Theorem 6.1.1 itself is itemized by the §6.1 reader. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: V_0∪V_1∪V_2-split extensions preserve the residual hypotheses
items.statement: Let F be imaginary CM, ρ̄ absolutely irreducible with ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous and some σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, and K/F(ζ_p) the extension cut out by ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}}. Choose finite sets of finite places: V_0, all split in F(ζ_p), such that for each subfield F(ζ_p) ⊊ K′ ⊆ K some v ∈ V_0 splits in F(ζ_p) but not in K′; V_1 such that for each subfield F ⊊ K′ ⊆ K some v ∈ V_1 does not split in K′ (printed 'proper subfield K/K′/…'); V_2 = the p_0-adic places for a rational prime p_0 ≠ p that is decomposed generic for ρ̄; and v ∤ 2p with ρ, π unramified at every v ∈ V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2. Then for every finite Galois E/F in which all places of V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2 split: ρ̄(G_E) = ρ̄(G_F) and ρ̄(G_{E(ζ_p)}) = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}); hence ρ̄|_{G_{E(ζ_p)}} has enormous image, some σ ∈ G_E − G_{E(ζ_p)} has ρ̄(σ) scalar, and ρ̄|_{G_E} is decomposed generic (p_0 splits in E). (Used verbatim in §6.6.10.)
items.note: PA.5: 'Supply a reusable checklist theorem which records that the input package for a chosen lifting argument survives a specified base change'. Chebotarev for the choice of V_0, V_1 is a library pointer (Chebotarev density).

items.name: The soluble CM extension E = E_0·E_a·E_b·E_c (Fontaine–Laffaille case)
items.statement: Let E_0/F be a soluble CM extension such that: all places of V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2 split and p is unramified in E_0; π_{E_0,w}^{Iw_w} ≠ 0 for every finite w; at every finite prime-to-p w, either π_{E_0,w} and ρ|_{G_{E_0,w}} are both unramified, or ρ|_{G_{E_0,w}} is unipotently ramified, q_w ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄|_{G_{E_0,w}} is trivial; every w̄ | p of E_0⁺ splits in E_0 and admits w̄′ ≠ w̄, w̄′ | p, with Σ_{w̄″≠w̄,w̄′} [E⁺_{0,w̄″}:ℚ_p] > ½[E_0⁺:ℚ]. Choose imaginary quadratic E_a, E_b, E_c with: every rational prime below V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2 splits in E_aE_bE_c and p is unramified in E_aE_bE_c; 2 and p split in E_a; every l ∉ {2,p} below a place of E_0 where π_{E_0} or ρ ramifies, or ramified in E_0E_aE_c, splits in E_b; every l ∉ {2,p} ramified in E_b splits in E_c (e.g. E_b = ℚ(√−p_b) with p_b ≡ 1 mod 4 and p_b ≡ −1 mod each such l, E_c = ℚ(√−p_c) with p_c ≡ 1 mod 4p_b, p_c ≠ p; quadratic reciprocity shows p_c splits in E_b). Then E = E_0E_aE_bE_c is a soluble CM extension of F, split at V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2, with: p unramified in E; for R = {prime-to-p w: π_{E,w} or ρ|_{G_{E_w}} ramified}, S_p the p-adic places and S′ = S_p ∪ R, every prime below S′ or ramified in E splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of E; ρ̄|_{G_{E_w}} trivial and q_w ≡ 1 mod p for w ∈ R; ρ̄|_{G_{E(ζ_p)}} enormous, ρ̄|_{G_E} decomposed generic, some σ ∈ G_E − G_{E(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar; and the E⁺-analogue of the p-adic degree condition.
items.note: Only the preservation of the residual hypotheses under a V-split extension is planned (PA.5's base-change checklist). The existence of E_0 is asserted without argument, and the sample choice of E_b, E_c does not enforce the first bullet (I14, I15). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Auxiliary places v_0, v′_0 with H²(E_{v_0}, ad ρ̄) = 0
items.statement: By the Chebotarev density theorem there are infinitely many places v_0 of E of degree 1 over ℚ with odd residue characteristic, ρ̄(Frob_{v_0}) scalar, q_{v_0} ≢ 1 mod p and v_0 ∉ S′ ∪ R^c; for them H²(E_{v_0}, ad ρ̄) = H⁰(E_{v_0}, ad ρ̄(1))^∨ = 0. Choosing two such places v_0, v′_0 with distinct residue characteristics l_0 ≠ l′_0 and S = S′ ∪ {v_0, v′_0}, l_0 and l′_0 split in every imaginary quadratic subfield of E, and hypotheses (1)–(17) of §6.5.1 hold for E, π_E and S (resp. (1)–(15) of §6.6.1 in the ordinary case, §6.6.10).
items.note: No stage mentions these auxiliary places. They make K neat (Lemma 6.5.2) and satisfy §6.5.1(13)–(14). Library pointers (for parts only): Chebotarev density. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Unramifiedness of Π_v at good places via Varma's local–global compatibility
items.statement: Let v ∤ p be a finite place of F at which ρ and π are unramified. Varying the auxiliary places v_0, v′_0 shows Π_{E,w} is unramified for every w | v of E, so rec_{F_v}(Π_v) is finitely ramified (unramified on W_{E_w}); by the main theorem of [Var14] and ρ unramified at v, rec_{F_v}(Π_v) is unramified, hence Π_v is unramified. (Used verbatim in §6.6.10.)
items.locator: §6.5.12, end of proof of Theorem 6.1.1, p. 1074 (and §6.6.10, p. 1084)
items.note: AG2.5: 'For the nonselfdual branch implement Varma's interpolation of local Hecke actions and nilpotent-orbit bounds; its semisimplified comparison plus monodromy bound'. The deduction here is two lines on top of Varma's theorem.

items.name: §6.6.1: standing data and hypotheses (1)–(15) for the ordinary patching argument; the level K
items.statement: F is an imaginary CM field and we fix: (1) an integer n ≥ 2 and a prime p > n; (2) a finite set S of finite places containing S_p; (3) a possibly empty R ⊂ S of places prime to p; (4) a cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight μ; (5) ι: Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. Assume: (6) every prime below a place of S, or ramified in F, splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F; (7) r̄_ι(π) absolutely irreducible; (8) for v ∈ S_p, π_v^{Iw_v(1,1)} ≠ 0 and π is ι-ordinary at v ([Ger19, Def. 5.3]); (9) π_v^{Iw_v} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R; (10) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p): π_v unramified, v ∉ R^c, H²(F_v, ad r̄_ι(π)) = 0; (11) S − (R ∪ S_p) contains two places of distinct residue characteristics; (12) π_v unramified for finite v ∉ S; (13) for v ∈ R: q_v ≡ 1 mod p and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} trivial; (14) r̄_ι(π) decomposed generic and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} of enormous image; (15) for v ∈ S_p: [F_v:ℚ_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1 and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} trivial. The level K = ∏ K_v: K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) (v ∉ S), Iw_v(1,1) (v ∈ S_p), Iw_v (v ∈ R), Iw_{v,1} (v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p)); K is neat (Lemma 6.5.2), hence good.
items.locator: §6.6.1 (Application of the patching argument, ordinary case), pp. 1074–1076
items.note: Hypotheses of Theorem 6.6.2 and of Lemma 6.2.27. PA.3: 'the generic support implication used for derived Ihara avoidance, with the exact hypotheses on local rings and residual images'. (ζ_p ∉ F, needed by Lemma 6.2.32/Prop. 6.2.33, is implied by (10)–(11): if ζ_p ∈ F then H²(F_v, ad r̄) ⊇ k.)

items.name: Theorem 6.6.2: ordinary automorphy lifting under the §6.6.1 hypotheses
items.statement: Under (1)–(15) of §6.6.1, let ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) be continuous and λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,Q̄_p)} such that: (1) ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π); (2) for each v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is conjugate to an upper-triangular representation with diagonal characters ψ_{v,1}, …, ψ_{v,n}, where ψ_{v,i} agrees on the whole inertia group I_{F_v} with σ ↦ ∏_{τ∈Hom(F_v,Q̄_p)} τ(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1)}; (3) for each v | p, each i and each p-power root of unity x ∈ 𝒪_{F_v}: ∏_{τ∈Hom(F_v,Q̄_p)} τ(x)^{λ_{τ,n+1−i} − μ_{ιτ,n+1−i}} = 1; (4) ρ unramified at finite v ∉ S; (5) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} unipotently ramified for v ∈ R. Then ρ is ordinarily automorphic of weight ιλ: there is an ι-ordinary cuspidal automorphic Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight ιλ with ρ ≅ r_ι(Π), and Π_v is unramified for every finite v ∉ S. (No analogue of Theorem 6.5.4 is proved, because the irreducible components of the 𝒟^{det,ord} lifting rings are not understood well enough.)
items.note: As for Corollary 6.5.5, no stage states the lifting theorem. Its support core (item 288) is planned by PA.3/P9; the final passage to Π uses Corollary 6.6.6 and Theorem 2.4.10. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Weight algebras Λ_1, Λ, the weight points p_μ, p_λ and the component ℘_{0,v}
items.statement: By Theorem 2.4.10 choose E and a maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, μ)^{ord} with residue field k and ρ̄_𝔪 ≅ r̄_ι(π). For v ∈ S_p let Λ_{1,v} = 𝒪⟦𝒪_{F_v}^×(p)^n⟧ and Λ_1 = ⊗̂_{v∈S_p} Λ_{1,v} (over 𝒪). The characters χ_{μ,v,i}: 𝒪_{F_v}^×(p) → 𝒪^×, x ↦ ∏_{τ∈Hom_{ℚ_p}(F_v,E)} τ(x)^{−(μ_{ιτ,n−i+1} + i − 1)} (1 ≤ i ≤ n) define p_{μ,v}: Λ_{1,v} → 𝒪; ℘_{μ,v} = ker p_{μ,v}; ℘_{0,v} is the unique minimal prime of Λ_{1,v} contained in ℘_{μ,v}; Λ_v = Λ_{1,v}/℘_{0,v}, Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S_p} Λ_v, p_μ: Λ → 𝒪 the induced map and ℘_μ = ker p_μ; p_λ, ℘_{λ,v} similarly. Claim: condition (3) of Theorem 6.6.2 implies that ℘_{0,v} is also the unique minimal prime contained in ℘_{λ,v} for every v ∈ S_p.
items.note: L8: 'Construct the universal character coefficient rings including their chosen torsion components.' G8: 'For ACC+ Definition 6.2.2 use Λ=completed tensor product of the local Λ_v'.

items.name: Ordinary deformation problems 𝒮_χ and the lift ρ of type 𝒮_1
items.statement: For each character χ: K_R → 𝒪^× trivial mod ϖ, 𝒮_χ = (ρ̄_𝔪, S, {𝒪}_{v∈S−S_p} ∪ {Λ_v}_{v∈S_p}, {𝒟_v^{det,ord}}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {𝒟_v^χ}_{v∈R} ∪ {𝒟_v^□}_{v∈S−(R∪S_p)}), with representatives ρ_{𝒮_χ} of the universal deformations identified mod ϖ via R_{𝒮_χ}/ϖ ≅ R_{𝒮_1}/ϖ; 𝒱_μ(χ^{-1}) = 𝒱_μ ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(χ^{-1}), K_S acting through K_p and K_R. After enlarging E, ρ takes values in GL_n(𝒪) with ρ mod ϖ = ρ̄_𝔪 and is a lifting of type 𝒮_1, classified by f: R_{𝒮_1} → 𝒪.
items.note: G8: 'Construct the arbitrary-rank unpolarized problem with variable determinant ... For ACC+ Definition 6.2.2 ...'; L8: 'the determinant-ordinary quotient defined by the full characteristic-polynomial identities and ordered products (ρ(g₁)−χ₁(g₁))⋯(ρ(g_n)−χ_n(g_n))=0'.

items.name: The ordinary Hida complexes A_1(μ,χ,c), A_1(μ,χ), A(μ,χ) and (6.6.3), (6.6.4)
items.statement: For c ≥ 1, Λ_{1,c} = 𝒪[∏_{v∈S_p} ker(T_n(𝒪_{F_v}/ϖ_v^c) → T_n(𝒪_{F_v}/ϖ_v))], a quotient of Λ_1, and A_1(μ,χ,c) = RHom_{Λ_{1,c}}(RΓ(X_{K(c,c)}, 𝒱_μ(χ^{-1}))^{ord}, Λ_{1,c})[−d], a perfect complex in D(Λ_{1,c}) on which T^{S,ord} acts by transpose. (6.6.3): for c′ ≥ c there are T^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphisms A_1(μ,χ,c′) ⊗^L_{Λ_{1,c′}} Λ_{1,c} ≅ A_1(μ,χ,c) in D(Λ_{1,c}) (Corollary 5.2.16). (6.6.4): canonical T^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphisms A_1(μ,χ,c) ⊗^L_{Λ_{1,c}} Λ_{1,c}/ϖ ≅ A_1(μ,1,c) ⊗^L_{Λ_{1,c}} Λ_{1,c}/ϖ. By [KT17, Lem. 2.13] there is a perfect A_1(μ,χ) ∈ D(Λ_1) with T^{S,ord}-action and equivariant isomorphisms A_1(μ,χ) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ_{1,c} ≅ A_1(μ,χ,c) (all c ≥ 1) and A_1(μ,χ) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ_1/ϖ ≅ A_1(μ,1) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ_1/ϖ, compatible with (6.6.3) and with (6.6.4) for varying χ; A(μ,χ) = A_1(μ,χ) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ ∈ D(Λ).
items.note: PA.2: 'construct the parabolic level tower, its commuting positive-monoid operators and the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes, and prove the stabilization hypotheses'. P7: 'Work with finite coefficient quotients before inverse limits ... Morphisms, homotopies and Hecke actions must survive the inverse system' (the KT17 Lemma 2.13 limit).

items.name: The twist ν and the weight-independent complexes B_1(μ,χ), B(μ,χ)
items.statement: ν ∈ X^*((Res_{F/ℚ} T)_E) = (ℤ^n)^{Hom(F,E)} is ν_τ = (0, 1, …, n−1) for all τ. B_1(μ,χ) = A_1(μ,χ) ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1}, where 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1} is the 𝒪[T_n(F_p)]-module of §5.2.1 (the action of T_n(𝒪_{F,p}) extending uniquely to 𝒪⟦T_n(𝒪_{F,p})⟧); it is a perfect complex in D(Λ_1) with T^{S,ord}-action. B(μ,χ) = B_1(μ,χ) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ.
items.note: PA.2: 'Track positive monoids, normalization, central characters, derived limits'. The twist is the normalization that makes the Hida complex weight-independent (Lemma 6.6.5).

items.name: Lemma 6.6.5: B_1(μ,χ) is independent of the weight
items.statement: For every μ′ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} there is a T^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphism B_1(μ,χ) ≅ B_1(μ′,χ) in D(Λ_1). (Proof: Proposition 5.2.17 and [KT17, Lem. 2.13].)
items.note: PA.2: 'Construct the local ordinary-parts functor ... its maps on parabolic induction and the required adjunction/control statements'; independence of weight (Prop. 5.2.17) is the §5.2 control statement PA.2 owns (matrix row '§§5.2–5.3 | PA.2').

items.name: Corollary 6.6.6: weight specialization of the Hida complex
items.statement: For μ′ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} there is a T^{S,ord}-equivariant isomorphism in D(𝒪): B_1(μ,χ) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ′)^{-1} ≅ A_1(μ′,χ,1) ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ′)^{-1}. (By Lemma 6.6.5 reduce to μ′ = μ, where the left side is A_1(μ,χ) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} 𝒪 ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1}.)
items.note: PA.2: 'the required adjunction/control statements' (control theorem at a classical weight).

items.name: Proposition 6.6.7: Galois representations over the ordinary Hecke algebra of A(μ,χ)
items.statement: Let T^{S,Λ_1} = T^S ⊗_𝒪 Λ_1 ⊂ T^{S,ord}. There are δ ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F:ℚ], an ideal J ⊂ T^{S,Λ_1}(A(μ,χ)_𝔪 ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1}) with J^δ = 0, and a continuous surjective Λ-algebra homomorphism f_{𝒮_χ}: R_{𝒮_χ} → T^{S,Λ_1}(A(μ,χ)_𝔪 ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1})/J such that for every finite v ∉ S the characteristic polynomial of f_{𝒮_χ} ∘ ρ_{𝒮_χ}(Frob_v) is the image of P_v(X). (Proof: build compatible maps R_{𝒮_χ} → T^{S,ord}(RΓ(X_{K(c,c)}, 𝒱_μ(χ^{-1}))^{ord})_𝔪/J_c as in Prop. 6.5.3 with Theorem 5.5.1 in place of Theorem 4.5.1 (using the description of 𝒟^{det,ord} in §6.2.6); Carayol's lemma [CHT08, Lem. 2.1.10] puts the image in a nilpotent quotient of T^{S,Λ_1}(…); the Hecke algebras agree by transpose and twist; pass to the limit in c as in the proof of Theorem 4.5.1.)
items.note: Set-up item (5) of §6.4.1 at N = 0 in the ordinary case: PA.4 'Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'. PA.2 supplies Theorem 5.5.1 (matrix row '§§5.4–5.5 | PA.2 | Ordinary degree shifting/local compatibility').

items.name: Ordinary auxiliary levels K(c,c)_1(Q) ⊂ K(c,c)_0(Q) and the complexes A_1(μ,χ,Q,c), A_1(μ,χ,Q); the ideals 𝔪^Q, 𝔫^Q
items.statement: For a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q, (α_{v,i})) for 𝒮_1 whose places have residue characteristic split in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F (a TW datum for all 𝒮_χ; R_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra, Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q} k(v)^×(p)^n) and c ≥ 1: good subgroups K(c,c)_1(Q) ⊂ K(c,c)_0(Q) ⊂ K(c,c), equal to K(c,c)_v away from Q (printed: for v ∉ S ∪ Q), with K(c,c)_0(Q)_v = Iw_v and K(c,c)_1(Q)_v the maximal pro-prime-to-p subgroup of Iw_v for v ∈ Q, so K(c,c)_0(Q)/K(c,c)_1(Q) ≅ Δ_Q. A_1(μ,χ,Q,c) = RHom_{Λ_{1,c}[Δ_Q]}(RΓ_{K(c,c)_0(Q)/K(c,c)_1(Q)}(X_{K(c,c)_1(Q)}, 𝒱_μ(χ^{-1}))^{ord}, Λ_{1,c}[Δ_Q])[−d] ∈ D(Λ_{1,c}[Δ_Q]), with transpose action of T^{S∪Q,ord}_Q = T^{S∪Q,ord} ⊗_{T^{S∪Q}} T^{S∪Q}_Q. Passing to the limit in c gives A_1(μ,χ,Q) ∈ D(Λ_1[Δ_Q]) with T^{S∪Q,ord}_Q-action and equivariant isomorphisms A_1(μ,χ,Q) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ_{1,c} ≅ A_1(μ,χ,Q,c) and A_1(μ,χ,Q) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ_1/ϖ ≅ A_1(μ,1,Q) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ_1/ϖ, compatible with the level-c data. 𝔪^Q = the contraction of 𝔪 to T^{S∪Q,ord}; 𝔫^Q = the ideal of T^{S∪Q,ord}_Q generated by 𝔪^Q and U_{v,i} − α_{v,1}⋯α_{v,i} (v ∈ Q, 1 ≤ i ≤ n).
items.note: PA.4: 'Construct Taylor–Wiles auxiliary sets ... Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'; PA.2: 'the ordinary summand of the arithmetic complexes'. (𝔫^Q omits the factor q_v^{i(1−i)/2} used in §6.5; the ideals coincide because ϖ ∈ 𝔪^Q and q_v ≡ 1 mod p.) Same 'v ∉ S ∪ Q' slip as in §6.5 (I10).

items.name: Lemma 6.6.8: the ordinary auxiliary complexes specialize to A_1(μ,χ)_𝔪
items.statement: 𝔫^Q lies in the support of H^*(A_1(μ,χ,Q)), and there are T^{S∪Q,ord}-equivariant isomorphisms A_1(μ,χ,Q)_{𝔫^Q} ⊗^L_{Λ_1[Δ_Q]} Λ_1 ≅ A_1(μ,χ)_{𝔪^Q} ≅ A_1(μ,χ)_𝔪. (Proof 'as in the Fontaine–Laffaille case', details omitted.)
items.note: PA.4: 'identify its specialization with the original complex'. The paper omits the proof, referring to Lemmas 6.5.8–6.5.9.

items.name: Proposition 6.6.9: Λ[Δ_Q]-linear Galois representations over the ordinary Taylor–Wiles Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let A(μ,χ,Q) = A_1(μ,χ,Q) ⊗^L_{Λ_1} Λ and _{Δ_Q}T^{S∪Q,Λ_1} = T^{S∪Q,Λ_1} ⊗_𝒪 𝒪[Δ_Q], acting on A(μ,χ,Q)_{𝔫^Q} via K(c,c)_0(Q)/K(c,c)_1(Q) ≅ Δ_Q and passage to the limit; _{Δ_Q}T^{S∪Q,Λ_1}(A(μ,χ,Q)_{𝔫^Q}) is a local Λ[Δ_Q]-algebra (printed with A(Λ,χ,Q)). Then there are δ ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F:ℚ], an ideal J ⊂ 𝕋 := _{Δ_Q}T^{S∪Q,Λ_1}(A(μ,χ,Q)_{𝔫^Q} ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1}) with J^δ = 0, and a continuous surjective Λ[Δ_Q]-algebra homomorphism f_{𝒮_{χ,Q}}: R_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} → 𝕋/J such that for every finite v ∉ S ∪ Q the characteristic polynomial of f_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} ∘ ρ_{𝒮_{χ,Q}}(Frob_v) is the image of P_v(X) (printed: v ∉ S and f_{𝒮_χ} ∘ ρ_{𝒮_χ}). (Proof: the Λ-algebra map as in Prop. 6.6.7; Λ[Δ_Q]-linearity as in Prop. 6.5.11 via T^{S∪Q,ord}_Q(A(μ,χ,Q) ⊗ 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1})_{𝔫^Q}.)
items.locator: §6.6.1, Proposition 6.6.9 and the preceding paragraph, pp. 1079–1080
items.note: Set-up item (5) of §6.4.1 for N ≥ 1 (ordinary): PA.4 'selected eigenvalues and framed local deformation data ... compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'. Misprints I6, I7.

items.name: The Taylor–Wiles patching data for Theorem 6.6.2 (ordinary case)
items.statement: Let f: R_{𝒮_1} → 𝒪 classify ρ. Set q = h¹(F_S/F, ad ρ̄_𝔪(1)), g = qn − n²[F⁺:ℚ], Δ_∞ = ℤ_p^{nq}, 𝒯 = a power series ring over Λ (the weight algebra) in n²|S| − 1 variables, S_∞ = 𝒯⟦Δ_∞⟧, augmented over Λ with ideal 𝔞_∞. Choose χ = ∏_{v∈R} χ_v: ∏_{v∈R} Iw_v → 𝒪^× with χ_{v,1},…,χ_{v,n}: k(v)^× → 𝒪^× trivial mod ϖ and pairwise distinct. R^loc = R^{S,loc}_{𝒮_1}, R′^loc = R^{S,loc}_{𝒮_χ} (§6.2.22; printed with 𝒮_1^{ord}, 𝒮_χ^{ord}); R_∞, R′_∞ = power series rings in g variables over them. Applying §6.4.2 to the complexes A(μ,χ,Q_N)_{𝔫^{Q_N}} ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1} (and χ = 1), for Taylor–Wiles data from Proposition 6.2.33, gives: bounded complexes 𝒞_∞, 𝒞′_∞ of free S_∞-modules, T_∞, T′_∞ with nilpotent I_∞, I′_∞ (I^δ = 0), S_∞-algebra structures on R_∞, R′_∞ and surjections R_∞ → T_∞/I_∞, R′_∞ → T′_∞/I′_∞; surjections of local Λ-algebras R_∞/𝔞_∞ ↠ R_{𝒮_1}, R′_∞/𝔞_∞ ↠ R_{𝒮_χ}; and isomorphisms 𝒞_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/𝔞_∞ ≅ A(μ,1)_𝔪 ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1} = B(μ,1)_𝔪 and 𝒞′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/𝔞_∞ ≅ B(μ,χ)_𝔪 in D(Λ).
items.note: PA.4 (as for item 266): 'Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching; identify its specialization with the original complex.' GlobalGaloisDeformations G7: 'construct exactly q primes ... and the local-to-global presentation with g=qn−n²[F⁺:Q] variables'.

items.name: Support of B(μ,1)_𝔪 at the point ker f (key step of Theorem 6.6.2)
items.statement: In the situation of the previous item: Lemma 6.2.27(1),(2) give Assumption 6.3.6(1),(2) for R_∞, R′_∞ (the dimension equality dim R_∞ = dim S_∞ − ℓ_0 needs g = qn − n²[F⁺:ℚ]; printed g = qn − n[F⁺:ℚ]). For 𝔭 = the preimage in S_∞ of Ann_Λ(𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1}), Corollary 6.6.6 gives (𝒞_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/𝔭)[1/p] ≅ (B(μ,1)_𝔪 ⊗^L_Λ 𝒪(ν + w_0^G μ)^{-1})[1/p], whose cohomology is a quotient of Hom_E(H^{d−*}(X_{K(1,1)}, 𝒱_μ)_𝔪[1/p], E); π contributes, so by Theorem 2.4.10 it is nonzero and concentrated in [q_0, q_0 + ℓ_0] (Assumption 6.3.6(3)). Let x ∈ Spec R_∞ be the preimage of ker f and y its contraction to S_∞ (the preimage of Ann_Λ(𝒪(ν + w_0^G λ)^{-1})). The inertial characters on the diagonal of ρ|_{G_{F_v}} are pairwise distinct for v ∈ S_p, so x lies on a maximal-dimensional component of Spec R_∞ (Lemma 6.2.27(3)), and Corollary 6.3.9 gives ker f ∈ Supp H^*(B(μ,1)_𝔪 ⊗^L_Λ 𝒪(ν + w_0^G λ)^{-1})[1/p]; by Corollary 6.6.6, ker f ∈ Supp H^*(A_1(λ,1,1)_𝔪 ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(ν + w_0^G λ)^{-1})[1/p] (printed A(λ,1,1)), a quotient of Hom_E(H^{d−*}(X_{K(1,1)}, 𝒱_λ)_𝔪, 𝒪(ν + w_0^G λ)^{-1}[1/p]).
items.note: PA.3: 'Prove compatibility of Hecke and deformation-ring actions, component support, characteristic-zero localization and the specialization of cohomological amplitude. Establish the generic support implication used for derived Ihara avoidance'. P9 node 'support-transport-avoiding-ihara' includes Corollary 6.3.9: 'for x on such a component with contraction y in S_∞ the support of H*(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/y)_y contains x'. Misprints I4, I8.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1.2: reduction to Theorem 6.6.2 by soluble base change
items.statement: Let F, ρ, λ, π, ι satisfy Theorem 6.1.2 ((1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) for v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} potentially semistable and ordinary of regular weight λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,Q̄_p)}: upper triangular with diagonal ψ_{v,i} agreeing with σ ↦ ∏_τ τ(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1)} on an open subgroup of I_{F_v}; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous, some σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, p > n; (4) π regular algebraic cuspidal and ι-ordinary with r̄_ι(π) ≅ ρ̄). The totally real case reduces to the imaginary CM case by base change (no details given). For imaginary F choose V_0, V_1, V_2, the ordinary-variant extension E (next item) and auxiliary places v_0, v′_0 so that (1)–(15) of §6.6.1 hold for E, π_E, S; Theorem 6.6.2 applied to ρ|_{G_E} gives an ι-ordinary cuspidal Π_E of weight λ_E with r_ι(Π_E) ≅ ρ|_{G_E}; Proposition 6.5.13(2) and [Ger19, Lem. 5.7] descend it to an ι-ordinary cuspidal regular algebraic Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ with r_ι(Π) ≅ ρ; Π_{E,w} is unramified for w ∉ S, and Π_v is unramified at finite v ∤ p where ρ and π are unramified (Varma argument, item 274).
items.note: As for the proof of Theorem 6.1.1 (item 270): PA.5 leaves 'the lifting theorem with its dedicated owner', and no stage names one. The recalled hypotheses contain three misprints (I9). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: The soluble CM extension E = E_0·E_a·E_b·E_c (ordinary case)
items.statement: Let E_0/F be a soluble CM extension such that: all places of V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2 split in E_0; π_{E_0,w}^{Iw_w} ≠ 0 for every finite w; at each finite prime-to-p w, either π_{E_0,w} and ρ|_{G_{E_0,w}} are unramified, or ρ|_{G_{E_0,w}} is unipotently ramified, q_w ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄|_{G_{E_0,w}} trivial; for w | p, ρ̄|_{G_{E_0,w}} is trivial and [E_{0,w}:ℚ_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1; for v | p, w | v and each i, ψ_{v,i} agrees with σ ↦ ∏_{τ∈Hom(F_v,Q̄_p)} τ(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1)} on all of I_{E_0,w}; and, with μ the weight of π_{E_0}, ψ_{v,i}(Art_{E_0,w}(x)) · ∏_{τ∈Hom(E_{0,w},Q̄_p)} τ(x)^{μ_{ιτ,n−i+1}+i−1} = 1 for every w | p and every p-power root of unity x ∈ E_{0,w}. Choose imaginary quadratic E_a, E_b, E_c as in the FL case but without requiring p unramified (p_c any prime ≡ 1 mod 4p_b). Then E = E_0E_aE_bE_c is soluble CM, V-split, and: every prime below S′ = S_p ∪ R or ramified in E splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of E; ρ̄|_{G_{E_w}} trivial and q_w ≡ 1 mod p for w ∈ R; ρ̄|_{G_{E(ζ_p)}} enormous, ρ̄|_{G_E} decomposed generic, some σ ∈ G_E − G_{E(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar; ρ̄|_{G_{E_w}} trivial and [E_w:ℚ_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1 for w | p; and the base change π_E (Prop. 6.5.13) is ι-ordinary by [Ger19, Lem. 5.7].
items.note: As for item 272. The last bullet on E_0 makes condition (3) of Theorem 6.6.2 hold over E (it combines the preceding bullet with (3) through norms of roots of unity); the existence of such E_0 is asserted without argument (I15). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Very weakly and extremely weakly compatible systems of l-adic representations
items.statement: Let F be a number field. A rank n very weakly compatible system R of l-adic representations of G_F defined over M is a 5-tuple (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}) with: (1) M a number field; (2) S a finite set of primes of F; (3) for each prime v ∉ S of F, Q_v(X) ∈ M[X] monic of degree n; (4) for each τ : F ↪ M̄, H_τ a multiset of n integers; (5) for each prime λ of M, of residue characteristic l, a continuous semisimple r_λ : G_F → GL_n(M̄_λ) such that (a) if v ∉ S and v ∤ l then r_λ is unramified at v and r_λ(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial Q_v(X); (b) for l outside a set of rational primes of Dirichlet density 0, r_λ|_{G_{F_v}} is crystalline for all v | l and HT_τ(r_λ) = H_τ for every M̄ ↪ M̄_λ over M; (c) for all λ, HT_τ(det r_λ) = Σ_{h∈H_τ} h. Dropping (5b) gives an extremely weakly compatible system (it depends on the H_τ only through (5c)). Conventions: Frob_v is a geometric Frobenius and HT_τ(ε_l) = {−1}. (Used implicitly: every compatible family of characters is de Rham, by Henniart.)
items.note: R24.5:operations plans 'Build compatible systems as actual representations at coefficient places with common Frobenius polynomials, not only a table of traces; support weak, almost strict and strict local predicates separately. Extend the elementary operations to rank n'; PA.5 plans 'comparison lemmas for restriction to field extensions, tensor products, duals, characters and symmetric powers using the compatible-system owner'. Same routing as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/88, whose Definition 6.1.1 is this definition, and as PA's source-to-owner matrix ('§7.1 | PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems | Compatible-system operations and change of field'). Henniart's theorem (abelian l-adic families are de Rham) is not planned anywhere in the atlas (searches 'Henniart', 'locally algebraic').

items.name: The residual representation r̄_λ is defined over O_M/λ
items.statement: For a very or extremely weakly compatible system R and a prime λ of M, r̄_λ denotes the semisimplified reduction of r_λ. It is a priori defined over the algebraic closure of O_M/λ, but since its characteristic polynomials (printed: 'its trace') have coefficients in O_M/λ and the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial, it is realised as a representation r̄_λ : G_F → GL_n(O_M/λ).
items.note: R01.1 plans 'Define reduction followed by semisimplification and prove independence of lattice by characteristic polynomials and the characteristic-p Brauer–Nesbitt theorem'; R01.5 plans 'coefficient descent where a trace-and-determinant system is defined over a subfield and the descent obstruction vanishes'. The obstruction vanishes because finite fields have trivial Brauer group: Library pointers (for parts only): Mathlib `littleWedderburn` (a finite division ring is a field). For n ≥ l the traces alone do not determine r̄_λ; the paper's 'trace' should be read as the characteristic polynomials Q_v(X) mod λ.

items.name: Regular, irreducible and strongly irreducible compatible systems
items.statement: A very or extremely weakly compatible system R (as in BLGGT §5.1, mutatis mutandis) is regular if every H_τ consists of n distinct integers; irreducible if there is a set 𝓛 of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that r_λ is irreducible for all λ | l ∈ 𝓛; strongly irreducible if R|_{G_{F'}} is irreducible for every finite extension F'/F.
items.note: R24.5:operations plans the operations 'with the precise conditions for retaining irreducibility, regularity, polarization and purity; these properties are not all preserved automatically'; PA.5: 'State regularity, purity and polarization only where proved'.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.1: rank-2 systems are irreducible at every λ or split as a sum of compatible characters
items.statement: If R is an extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2, then either r_λ is irreducible for every λ, or there are weakly compatible systems (in the sense of BLGGT) 𝒳_1, 𝒳_2 of rank 1 with r_λ ≅ χ_{1,λ} ⊕ χ_{2,λ} for every λ.
items.note: Proof: if r_{λ_0} = χ_1 ⊕ χ_2, Henniart's theorem makes r_{λ_0}, hence each χ_i, de Rham, so each χ_i sits in a weakly compatible system of characters (Serre); then r_λ ≅ χ_{1,λ} ⊕ χ_{2,λ} for all λ by Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt. Neither Henniart's theorem nor Serre's classification of rank-one compatible systems by algebraic Hecke characters is planned (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 plans only 'locally algebraic Hecke characters, their algebraic and p-adic avatars'). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Reducible and Artin-up-to-twist rank-2 systems
items.statement: An extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2 is reducible if it is not irreducible; by Lemma 7.1.1 every r_λ is then reducible. A very (or extremely) weakly compatible system of rank 2 is Artin up to twist if, after possibly enlarging M, there are an irreducible Artin representation ρ : G_F → GL_2(M̄) with traces in M and a weakly compatible system of characters χ_λ with r_λ ≅ ρ ⊗ χ_λ for all λ.
items.note: No stage defines 'Artin up to twist' or 'induced' compatible systems; R24.5:operations plans 'induced systems' only as an operation. Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.2: trichotomy for irreducible rank-2 systems (strongly irreducible, Artin up to twist, or induced)
items.statement: Let R be an irreducible extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2. Then either (1) R is strongly irreducible; or (2) R is Artin up to twist; or (3) there are a quadratic extension F'/F and a weakly compatible system 𝒳 of characters of G_{F'} with R ≅ Ind_{G_{F'}}^{G_F} 𝒳 (R is then called induced).
items.note: Proof: take E/F Galois with R|_{G_E} reducible and λ of odd residue characteristic. If r_λ|_{G_E} = χ ⊕ χ, extract a square root ψ of the pro-l part ⟨det r_λ⟩ (l odd), note ψ|_{G_E} = χ after enlarging E, so ψ is de Rham and extends to a compatible system; twisting makes r_λ|_{G_E} trivial, so R is Artin up to twist. If χ_1 ≠ χ_2, Gal(E/F) permutes them transitively and r_λ = Ind χ_1 from the stabiliser field F'; then R ≅ Ind 𝒳. BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 uses the remark that distinct Hodge–Tate weights exclude case (2). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.3: residual irreducibility and large residual image for irreducible rank-2 systems
items.statement: Let R be an irreducible extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2. Then for all rational primes l in a set of Dirichlet density 1 and all λ | l, r̄_λ is absolutely irreducible. If moreover R is neither induced nor Artin up to twist, and F̃ is the normal closure of F/Q, then l can in addition be taken so that r̄_λ(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL_2(F_l) for all λ | l.
items.note: Proof: Artin-up-to-twist case immediate; induced case via a split prime v ∉ S with Q_v(X) having distinct roots. Strongly irreducible case: enlarge M so all r_λ are M_λ-valued (two auxiliary Frobenius elements); s_l = ⊕_{λ|l} r_λ : G_F → GL_{2[M:Q]}(Q_l); the Zariski closure 𝐆_l has unramified identity component for density-one l [LP92, Prop. 8.9]; the facts of the next item give 𝐆_l^ad ≅ ∏_i Res^{N_{l,i}}_{Q_l} PGL_2; Larsen's maximality [Lar95, Th. 3.17] puts a conjugate of ∏_i SL_2(O_{N_i})/{±1} in the image; perfectness of SL_2(F_l) (l > 3) lifts SL_2(F_l) into the image of r̄_λ; finally discard the l with PSL_2(F_l) a subquotient of Gal(F̃/F). Larsen–Pink and Larsen maximality are not planned anywhere (atlas search 'Larsen' returns nothing). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Unramified connected subgroups of products of Res PGL_2 (facts (1)–(8) in the proof of Lemma 7.1.3)
items.statement: Over Q̄_l: (1) every morphism PGL_2 → PGL_2 is trivial or conjugation by an element of PGL_2(Q̄_l); (2) every morphism PGL_2^r → PGL_2 is trivial or a projection followed by a conjugation; (3) up to PGL_2(Q̄_l)^J-conjugacy, morphisms PGL_2^I → PGL_2^J are induced by pairs (J_0 ⊂ J, φ : J_0 → I); (4) Aut(PGL_2^I) = PGL_2^I ⋊ S_I; (5) a connected algebraic subgroup G ⊂ PGL_2^J surjecting onto PGL_2 under every projection is ≅ PGL_2^I, embedded (up to conjugacy) through a surjection φ : J ↠ I (induction on #J and Goursat); (6) for M/Q_l finite, (Res^M_{Q_l} PGL_2)_{Q̄_l} ≅ PGL_2^{Hom_{Q_l}(M,Q̄_l)} with G_{Q_l} acting through its left action on Hom_{Q_l}(M, Q̄_l); (7) forms of PGL_2^r are classified by the middle term of H^1(Q_l, PGL_2^r) → H^1(Q_l, Aut PGL_2^r) → H^1(Q_l, S_r), and the unramified ones (quasi-split and split over an unramified extension) are exactly ∏_i Res^{N_i}_{Q_l} PGL_2 with N_i/Q_l unramified; (8) hence, if G ⊂ ∏_{j∈J} Res^{M_j}_{Q_l} PGL_2 is an unramified connected subgroup whose base change to Q̄_l surjects onto every factor of PGL_2^{⊔_j Hom(M_j,Q̄_l)}, then G ≅ ∏_{i∈I} Res^{N_i}_{Q_l} PGL_2 with N_i/Q_l unramified, and each (j, τ)-projection of G_{Q̄_l} is PGL_2(Q̄_l)-conjugate to the projection onto one factor of ∏_i (Res^{N_i}_{Q_l} PGL_2)_{Q̄_l}.
items.note: RG2.0a plans Weil restriction ('for a finite separable field extension prove the splitting-field product description'), but no stage plans the Goursat-type classification of subgroups of PGL_2^J or the classification of unramified forms of PGL_2^r. Fact (5) prints the conjugating element in PGL_2(Q̄_l)^I; it should be PGL_2(Q̄_l)^J (see issues). Route: a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, the roadmap built from this paper.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.4: symmetric powers of a subgroup containing SL_2(F_l) are enormous
items.statement: If n ≥ 2, l > 2n + 1, and H ⊂ GL_2(F̄_l) is a finite subgroup containing SL_2(F_l), then Sym^{n−1}H ⊂ GL_n(F̄_l) is enormous (Definition 6.2.29). (Printed: '⊂ GL_2(F̄_l)'.)
items.note: Proof: by Dickson [DDT97, Th. 2.47(b)] (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4) the projective image of H is PSL_2(k) or PGL_2(k), so F̄_l^× Sym^{n−1}GL_2(k) ⊃ Sym^{n−1}H ⊃ Sym^{n−1}SL_2(k), and [GN22, Lem. 3.2.5] applies. See issues for the GL_2/GL_n misprint. Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.5: a criterion for decomposed genericity
items.statement: Let L be a number field, k a finite field of characteristic l, r̄ : G_L → GL_n(k) continuous, and M the normal closure over Q of L̄^{ker ad r̄} (printed F̄^{ker ad r̄}). If M does not contain a primitive l-th root of unity, then r̄ is decomposed generic (Definition 4.3.1).
items.note: Proof: a rational prime p ≠ l that splits completely in M but not in M(ζ_l) (and is unramified in L̄^{ker r̄}) has r̄(Frob_v) scalar and p ≢ 1 mod l, so it is decomposed generic; Chebotarev supplies such p. The printed proof omits p ≠ l and the unramifiedness of r̄ itself (see issues). Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.6(1): a scalar Frobenius outside the cyclotomic extension
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Lemma 7.1.6: F/Q finite with normal closure F̃, m ∈ Z_{>0}, l > 2m + 3 prime, r̄ : G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) continuous with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL_2(F_l), and F'/F finite and linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F. (1) If l is unramified in F'/Q, then ζ_l ∉ F̄^{ker ad Sym^m r̄}·F' (so some σ ∈ G_{F'} − G_{F'(ζ_l)} has Sym^m r̄(σ) scalar).
items.note: Proof: reduce to m = 1; Gal(F'(ζ_l)/F') ≅ (Z/l)^× (l unramified in F'), while ad r̄(G_{F'}) = ad r̄(G_F) is PSL_2(k) or PGL_2(k) and has no cyclic quotient of order l − 1 > 2. Used in the proof of Theorem 7.1.11 to supply hypothesis (4) of Theorem 6.1.1. Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.6(2): enormous image after restriction to F'(ζ_l)
items.statement: Under the standing hypotheses of Lemma 7.1.6: (Sym^m r̄)(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) is enormous.
items.note: Proof: r̄(G_{F'}) = r̄(G_F) ⊇ SL_2(F_l) by linear disjointness; SL_2(F_l) is perfect, so r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) ⊇ SL_2(F_l); apply Lemma 7.1.4 with n = m + 1. Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.6(3)–(5): decomposed genericity of Sym^m r̄
items.statement: Under the standing hypotheses of Lemma 7.1.6: (3) if ad r̄(G_{F̃'}) ⊇ PSL_2(F_l), where F̃' is the normal closure of F'/Q, then Sym^m r̄|_{G_{F'}} is decomposed generic; (4) if F'/Q is unramified at l and no nontrivial quotient of im ad r̄ is unramified at all primes above l, then Sym^m r̄|_{G_{F'}} is decomposed generic; (5) if l > [F̃ : F], then Sym^m r̄ is decomposed generic.
items.note: Proof of (3): pass to F̃'(ζ_l) and a further Galois extension with ad r̄(G_{F'}) = PSL_2(k); the Galois closure H' of the PSL_2(k)-extension has Gal(H'/F') = PSL_2(k)^n (Goursat), with Gal(H'/Q) acting through Aut(PSL_2(k)^n) = (PGL_2(k) ⋊ Gal(k/F_l))^n ⋊ S_n [Die51]; Chebotarev gives p with Frob_p = (A, …, A), A ∈ PSL_2(F_l) of eigenvalue ratio α with α^{±i} ≠ 1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ m; then p splits in F', p ≡ 1 mod l, and all eigenvalue ratios α^{±i} of Sym^m r̄(Frob_w) differ from p. (4) follows from (3); (5) follows from (3). Under the standing hypothesis r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL_2(F_l), (5) is (3) with F' = F and the bound l > [F̃ : F] is not needed; the printed proof of (5) has an index misprint (see issues). Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.7: decomposed genericity and irreducibility survive disjoint base change
items.statement: Let r̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_l) be decomposed generic and absolutely irreducible, and let E/Q be a Galois extension linearly disjoint from the Galois closure H over Q of F̄^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). Then r̄|_{G_{FE}} is decomposed generic and absolutely irreducible.
items.note: Proof: as in Lemma 4.3.2 (the published cross-reference is correct) there is a conjugacy class σ ⊂ Gal(H/Q) all of whose unramified primes are decomposed generic for r̄; since Gal(HE/Q) = Gal(H/Q) × Gal(E/Q), primes with Frobenius (σ, 1) are decomposed generic for r̄|_{G_{FE}}. Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.8(1): inertial types of crystalline Z_l-lattices with Hodge–Tate numbers {0,1}
items.statement: Let K/Q_l be unramified and r : G_K → GL_2(Z_l) crystalline with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, 1} for every embedding K ↪ Q̄_l. Then either (r̄|_{I_K})^{ss} ≅ 1 ⊕ ε̄_l^{−1} or r̄|_{I_K} ≅ ω_{l,2}^{−1} ⊕ ω_{l,2}^{−l}. (This fails if Z_l is replaced by the integers of a larger extension of Q_l.)
items.note: Proof: r^∨ is the Tate module of a height-2 l-divisible group G over O_K [Bre00], [Kis06] with G ≠ G^0 ≠ 0; Raynaud's classification [Ray74, Prop. 3.2.1, Th. 3.4.3] of the l-torsion leaves four inertial types, and det r|_{I} = ε_l^{−1} excludes 1 ⊕ 1 and ε̄^{−1} ⊕ ε̄^{−1} for l > 2. The ingredients are planned: R07.4 ('classification of finite-flat groups and p-divisible groups') and R07.1 ('the (p,…,p)-type classification and its tame inertia characters … Theorems 3.4.1/3.4.3'). The proof of Theorem 7.1.11 also uses an unstated refinement of the ordinary case (r̄ is an extension of an unramified-times-ε̄^{−1} quotient by an unramified sub, with peu ramifié class), which the paper reads off from the connected–étale sequence. Route: a source of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.5 (local residual types and peu ramifié classes).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.8(2): no subextension of K̄^{ker r̄} unramified above l
items.statement: Let l > 2 and let K be a number field in which l is unramified and r : G_K → GL_2(Z_l) continuous and crystalline at the places above l with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, 1} for every embedding K ↪ Q̄_l. If r̄(G_K) ⊇ SL_2(F_l), then the only subextension of K̄^{ker r̄}/K unramified at all primes above l is K itself. (Printed without l > 2; the statement is false for l = 2.)
items.note: Proof: by part (1) det r̄ maps every inertia group above l onto F_l^×, so im r̄ = GL_2(F_l); the subgroup Δ generated by the inertia images is normal with surjective determinant, hence Δ = GL_2(F_l). Used in Corollary 7.2.4 and (with Lemma 7.1.6(4)) in the proof of Theorem 7.1.11, always with l ≥ 7. Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4 finite subgroups of GL_2/PGL_2, G7 the dimension-general residual-image API).

items.name: Pure compatible systems
items.statement: A very or extremely weakly compatible system R is pure of weight w if (i) for each v ∉ S, each root α ∈ M̄ of Q_v(X) and each ı : M̄ ↪ C, |ıα|² = q_v^w; and (ii) for each τ : F ↪ M̄ and each complex conjugation c ∈ Gal(M̄/Q), H_{cτ} = {w − h : h ∈ H_τ}.
items.note: R24.5:operations: 'the precise conditions for retaining irreducibility, regularity, polarization and purity'; PA.5: 'State regularity, purity and polarization only where proved'.

items.name: Purity of rank-one, induced and Artin-up-to-twist systems
items.statement: A rank-one very or extremely weakly compatible system is automatically pure [Ser98]; so is a system induced from an extremely weakly compatible system of characters of a finite extension of F, and a rank-2 system that is Artin up to twist.
items.note: Used in Corollary 7.1.13 (non-strongly-irreducible case) and in Theorem A of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 plans locally algebraic Hecke characters but not the purity of the attached compatible systems. Route: a source of PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5:operations.

items.name: Partial L-function and archimedean Euler factors of a pure compatible system
items.statement: If R is pure of weight w and ı : M ↪ C, the partial L-function L^S(ıR, s) = ∏_{v∉S} ı(det(1 − q_v^{−s} r_λ(Frob_v)))^{−1} (determined by the Q_v(X)) converges to an analytic function on Re s > 1 + w/2. If R is pure and regular, the Euler factor L_v(ıR, s) at each infinite place v of F is defined from the Hodge–Tate data as in BLGGT §5.1.
items.note: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.4 plans the automorphic-side partial Euler product ('Construct the partial Euler product and prove convergence where a supplied eigenvalue bound ensures it'), but no stage defines the L-function of a compatible system with Γ-factors built from Hodge–Tate numbers. Route: a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.0 normalization registry, ML.2 potential-automorphy assembly, ML.3 symmetric powers).

items.name: Automorphic compatible systems
items.statement: R is automorphic if there are a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_F) and an embedding ı : M ↪ C such that for v ∉ S, π_v is unramified and rec(π_v|det|_v^{(1−n)/2})(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial ı(Q_v(X)). Then L^S(ıR, s) is analytic for Re s ≫ 0 and, for n > 1, continues to all of C; by [Clo90, Th. 3.13], for every ı' : M ↪ C there is a regular algebraic cuspidal π_{ı'} with the same property for ı'.
items.note: ML.2 plans the assembly 'track compatible systems and descent … The output is automorphy after the specified extension'; the Clozel rationality input (σ-conjugates of regular algebraic cuspidal π are regular algebraic cuspidal) is AG2.0's 'Prove rationality of Hecke eigenvalues and finite fields of definition in the proven cohomological cases'.

items.name: The extremely weakly compatible system R_π of a regular algebraic cuspidal π over a CM field
items.statement: Let F be CM and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) of weight (a_{τ,i}). By [HLTT16] and [Var14] there is an extremely weakly compatible system R_π = (M_π, S_π, {Q_{π,v}(X)}, {r_{π,λ}}, {H_{π,τ}}) with M_π ⊂ C the fixed field of {σ ∈ Aut(C) : ^σπ^∞ ≅ π^∞}, S_π the set of primes v with π_v ramified, Q_{π,v}(X) the characteristic polynomial of rec(π_v|det|_v^{(1−n)/2})(Frob_v), and H_{π,τ} = {a_{τ,1} + n − 1, a_{τ,2} + n − 2, …, a_{τ,n}}.
items.note: AG2.4: 'Deliver the characteristic-zero semisimple system of HLTT Theorem 7.13/Corollary 7.14'; AG2.5: 'For the nonselfdual branch implement Varma's interpolation of local Hecke actions and nilpotent-orbit bounds'; AG2.6: 'Build a weakly compatible-system object from one coefficient number field, a common finite ramification set, characteristic polynomials at all good places and the constructed representations at each coefficient prime'. AG2.6 notes that HLTT alone gives no crystallinity, which is why R_π is only extremely weakly compatible here.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.9: under (DGI), R_π is very weakly compatible
items.statement: Let F be CM and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) of weight ξ = (a_{τ,i}). Assume (DGI): for a set of rational primes l of Dirichlet density one, r̄_{π,λ} : G_F → GL_n(O_{M_π}/λ) is decomposed generic and absolutely irreducible for all λ | l. Then R_π is a very weakly compatible system.
items.note: AG2.6 hands this upgrade to PA: 'the basic nonselfdual HLTT construction does not by itself supply de Rham/crystalline … the later Fontaine–Laffaille/ordinary arithmetic comparisons in PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure remain separate consumers'. PA.1 owns Theorem 4.5.1 (source matrix '§§4.4–4.5 | PA.1 | Degree shifting and Fontaine–Laffaille comparison'); PA.5 plans 'a reusable checklist theorem which records that the input package for a chosen lifting argument survives a specified base change'. Consistent with PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/91 (Lemma 7.1.10 planned AG2.4 + PA.5). Proof: apply Theorem 4.5.1 with p = l; its conditions (3)–(5) hold for l ≫ 0, (1), (2), (6) after a solvable base change [AC89] (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4), (8a) by the existence of π, (7) by (DGI); Lemma 7.1.7 preserves (DGI). Cross-references to Theorem 4.5.1 and its items (1)–(8a) match the published numbering. The disjointness required of the auxiliary field E is misstated (see issues).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.10: for GL_2, R_π is irreducible, satisfies (DGI) and is very weakly compatible
items.statement: Let F be CM and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_F) of weight ξ = (a_{τ,i}). Then R_π is irreducible, hypothesis (DGI) of Lemma 7.1.9 holds, and R_π is a very weakly compatible system.
items.note: Same as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/91 ('[ACC+ Lem. 7.1.10]', planned AG2.4 + PA.5): AG2.4 supplies the HLTT representations, PA.5 the compatible-system packaging. Proof: reducibility would give π_v ≅ χ_{1,v} ⊞ χ_{2,v} almost everywhere, contradicting cuspidality [JS81a] (strong multiplicity one for GL_2 is GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.4); (DGI) case by case via Lemma 7.1.2: strongly irreducible by Lemmas 7.1.3 and 7.1.6(5); induced by Lemma 7.1.5 (ζ_l is not in the normal closure of Ē^{ker χ̄/χ̄^τ} for l > 3 unramified in Ẽ); Artin up to twist by Lemma 7.1.5 for l > 2 unramified in the kernel field of ad ρ.

items.name: Comparison of L-functions of R_π and π
items.statement: If ı_0 : M_π ↪ C is the canonical embedding, then L^S(ı_0 R_π, s) = L^S(π, s). If moreover R_π is pure and (DGI) holds, then L_v(ı_0 R_π, s) = L_v(π, s) for every infinite place v of F.
items.note: Proof: definition of L_v(ı_0R_π, s) in BLGGT §5.1, the Hodge–Tate weights from Lemma 7.1.9, and, when F is totally real, [CLH16]. Needed to identify the Λ-functions of Corollary 7.1.13 with automorphic ones. Route: a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.0 normalization registry, ML.2 potential-automorphy assembly, ML.3 symmetric powers).

items.name: Theorem 7.1.11: potential automorphy of symmetric powers of rank-2 weight-{0,1} compatible systems over CM fields
items.statement: Let F/F_0 be a finite Galois extension of CM fields, F_0^avoid/F a finite Galois extension, 𝓛_0 a finite set of rational primes and 𝓘 a finite set; for i ∈ 𝓘 let m_i ∈ Z_{>0} and let R_i = (M_i, S_i, {Q_{i,v}(X)}, {r_{i,λ}}, {{0,1}}) be a strongly irreducible rank-2 very weakly compatible system of G_F, with no prime of S_i above 𝓛_0. Then there are a finite set 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_0 of rational primes, a finite CM Galois extension F^suffices/F unramified above 𝓛 and Galois over F_0, and a finite Galois extension F^avoid/F containing F_0^avoid and linearly disjoint from F^suffices over F, such that for every finite CM extension F'/F containing F^suffices, unramified above 𝓛 and linearly disjoint from F^avoid over F, every Sym^{m_i} R_i|_{G_{F'}} is automorphic and arises from an automorphic representation unramified above 𝓛_0.
items.note: PA's summary: 'The final potential-automorphy assembly has downstream owner ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2; symmetric powers and Sato–Tate have downstream owner ML.3'. ML.2: 'Apply PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure with full regularity, polarization, residual-image, local and field-extension hypotheses; track compatible systems and descent'; ML.3: 'Integrate … symmetric-power automorphy'. Same routing as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/4 (for m = 1 'this is ACC+ Corollary 7.1.12', planned ML.2, ML.3). Proof (§7.2.5): Assumption 7.2.6; twist R_i to det = ε^{−1} (item 'determinant twist'); Corollary 7.2.4 for an auxiliary non-CM E/Q; moduli X_i and Moret–Bailly give D_i with D_i[l_1] ≅ E[l_1], D_i[l_2] ≅ r̄'^∨_{i,λ_i}; F^suffices = F^{+,suffices}F_2^+F, F^avoid = F_1^avoid F_2^avoid, with a field-diagram proof of their linear disjointness over F; then Theorem 6.1.1 at l_1 (E ⇝ D_i, residual hypotheses from Lemma 7.1.6(1),(2),(4) and Lemma 7.1.8), compatibility of D_i's system, Theorem 6.1.1 at l_2 (D_i ⇝ R'_i), untwist. Gaps (see issues): Assumption 7.2.6 does not give p > n² or crystallinity at l_2; the avoidance hypotheses of Proposition 7.2.3 and Corollary 7.2.4 do not match their use; Corollary 7.2.4 is for totally real F' and must be applied to F'^+ and base-changed.

items.name: Corollary 7.1.12: potential automorphy of Sym^m of a strongly irreducible weight-{0,1} system
items.statement: Let F be CM and R = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {{0,1}}) a strongly irreducible rank-2 very weakly compatible system of G_F. For every integer m ≥ 0 there is a finite Galois CM extension F'/F such that Sym^m R|_{G_{F'}} is automorphic.
items.note: ML.2 ('The output is automorphy after the specified extension') and ML.3 (symmetric powers); PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/4 identifies its m = 1 case with this corollary (planned ML.2, ML.3). Applied to the system H^1 of a non-CM elliptic curve over a CM field this is the potential-modularity half of Theorem 1.0.1 (item 1; the CM case is classical). The conclusion says 'weakly compatible system Sym^m R'; it is very weakly compatible.

items.name: Corollary 7.1.13(1): purity of irreducible rank-2 systems with H_τ = {0,1}
items.statement: Let F be CM and R = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}) an irreducible rank-2 very weakly compatible system of G_F with H_τ = {0, 1} for all τ. Then R is pure of weight 1: |ıα|² = q_v for every root α of Q_v(X), v ∉ S, and every ı : M̄ ↪ C.
items.note: Proof (Deligne–Langlands method): the non-strongly-irreducible case is induced from a pure weight-1 system of characters (the Artin-up-to-twist case, excluded by H_τ = {0,1}, is not mentioned; see issues). Otherwise Theorem 7.1.11 gives cuspidal π_{ı,m} on GL_{m+1}(A_{F_m}) matching Sym^m R|_{G_{F_m}}; its central character is unitary, so the Jacquet–Shalika bound (next item) gives |ıβ| ≤ q^{(m+1)/2} for roots β of Q_{Sym^m R, v}, hence |ıα| ≤ q_v^{1/2 + 1/(2m)} for all m, and |α_1α_2| = q_v forces equality. Used by Corollary 7.1.15. Route: a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.0 normalization registry, ML.2 potential-automorphy assembly, ML.3 symmetric powers).

items.name: Jacquet–Shalika bound for unramified components of unitary cuspidal representations
items.statement: Key step in the proof of Corollary 7.1.13(1): if π is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_N(A_K) with unitary central character, then every local component π_w is generic (the final corollary of [Sha74]) and, at a finite place w where π_w is unramified, every eigenvalue α of rec(π_w)(Frob_w) satisfies |α| ≤ q_w^{1/2} [JS81b, Cor. 2.5].
items.note: No stage names the Jacquet–Shalika bound (atlas search 'Jacquet' returns only Godement–Jacquet and Jacquet–Langlands stages), and AnalyticNumberTheory has no automorphic stage covering it. Genericity of local components of cuspidal representations (Shalika) is likewise not planned by name. Route: a source of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.3 (Rankin–Selberg).

items.name: Corollary 7.1.13(2)–(3) and edge nonvanishing: continuation, functional equation and nonvanishing of L^S(ı Sym^m R, s)
items.statement: With R as in Corollary 7.1.13 and m ≥ 0: (2) each partial L-function L^S(ı Sym^m R, s) has meromorphic continuation to C; (3) for v ∈ S there are Euler factors L_v(ı Sym^m R, s) = P_{m,ı,v}(q_v^{−s})^{−1} with P_{m,ı,v} a polynomial of degree ≤ m + 1 such that Λ(ı Sym^m R, s) = L^S(ı Sym^m R, s) ∏_{v|∞} L_v(ı Sym^m R, s) ∏_{v∈S} L_v(ı Sym^m R, s) satisfies Λ(ı Sym^m R, s) = A·B^s·Λ(ı Sym^m R^∨, 1 − s) for constants A, B. If moreover R is strongly irreducible and m > 0, then L^S(ı Sym^m R, s) is holomorphic and non-vanishing for Re s ≥ m/2 + 1 (printed 'L^s'), in particular at s = m/2 + 1.
items.note: ML.3: 'resulting analytic/equidistribution arguments. Supply nonvanishing/analytic inputs for the Weyl criterion separately'; AN.4: 'Meromorphic continuation via induction is distinguished from Artin holomorphy'; AL.3: 'state analytic nonvanishing results only in their proved regions'. Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/hsbt-thm-4-2, which cites this corollary's 'usual Brauer's theorem argument … as in [HSBT10, Th. 4.2]' and is planned ML.3, AN.4, AL.3 and the Tau Ceti Brauer-induction layer (RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction layer 6). Nonvanishing on the edge uses [JS77].

items.name: Corollary 7.1.14: Sato–Tate for non-CM elliptic curves over CM fields
items.statement: Let F be a CM field and E/F an elliptic curve without CM. Then the numbers (1 + #k(v) − #E(k(v)))/(2√#k(v)), for v running over the primes of good reduction ordered by norm, are equidistributed in [−1, 1] with respect to (2/π)√(1 − t²) dt.
items.note: ML.3 is 'Symmetric powers and Sato-Tate' ('resulting analytic/equidistribution arguments') and AN.4 supplies the analytic interface; same routing as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 Theorem B and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/sato-tate-conjecture ('ACC+ Corollary 7.1.14 … is the case the PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure README hands to ML.3'). Proof: Corollary 7.1.13 plus Serre's criterion [Ser98, corollary to Th. 2, p. I-26]. This is the §7 statement of the Sato–Tate half of Theorem 1.0.1 (non-CM case).

items.name: Corollary 7.1.15: Ramanujan for weight-0 regular algebraic cuspidal representations of GL_2 over CM fields
items.statement: Let F be CM and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_F) of weight (0)_{τ,i}. Then π_v is tempered for every prime v of F.
items.note: This is Theorem 1.0.2 of the introduction ('see Corollary 7.1.15'). Same routing as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 Theorem A (planned ML.3; it cites this corollary's reduction to unramified π_v). ML.3 owns the symmetric-power endpoints and their consequences. Proof: immediate at Steinberg twists; otherwise HLTT, Varma and [TY07, Lem. 1.4(3)] reduce to purity of r_{π,λ}|_{G_{F_v}}, [TY07, Lem. 1.4(2)] and solvable base change reduce to π_v unramified, and Lemma 7.1.10 with Corollary 7.1.13(1) gives purity. The Taylor–Yoshida purity lemma is on AG2.5's list ('Prove the Caraiani/Taylor–Yoshida upgrades').

items.name: Corollary 7.1.16: Rankin–Selberg L-functions of symmetric powers of two systems
items.statement: Let F be CM and R = (M, S, {Q_v}, {r_λ}, {{0,1}}), R' = (M', S', {Q'_v}, {r'_λ}, {{0,1}}) strongly irreducible rank-2 very weakly compatible systems of G_F that are not twists of each other, and m, m' ≥ 0. Then L^S(ı Sym^m R ⊗ Sym^{m'} R', s) is meromorphic on C, has no zeros or poles in Re s ≥ 1 + m/2 + m'/2, and satisfies a functional equation relating it to L^S(ı Sym^m R^∨ ⊗ Sym^{m'} R'^∨, 1 − s) (printed with 1 + m + m' − s).
items.note: ML.3 ('resulting analytic … arguments') and AL.3 (Rankin–Selberg: 'Retain poles in the contragredient/twist case and state analytic nonvanishing results only in their proved regions'). Proof: Theorem 7.1.11 and the argument of [Har09, Th. 5.3], with Shahidi's nonvanishing [Sha81, Th. 5.2].

items.name: §7.2.1: the peu ramifié subspaces H^1_f(G_L, F_l(ε̄χ̄)) and H^1_f(G_L, Z_l(εχ))
items.statement: Let L/Q_l be finite and χ̄ (resp. χ) an unramified character of G_L valued in F_l^× (resp. Z_l^×). H^1_f(G_L, F_l(ε̄_l χ̄)) (resp. H^1_f(G_L, Z_l(ε_l χ))) is the kernel of H^1(G_L, F_l(ε̄χ̄)) → H^1(G_{L^nr}, F_l(ε̄)) ≅ L^{nr,×}/(L^{nr,×})^l → Z/lZ (resp. H^1(G_L, Z_l(εχ)) → H^1(G_{L^nr}, Z_l(ε)) ≅ lim_r L^{nr,×}/(L^{nr,×})^{l^r} → Z_l), the last maps induced by the valuation. If χ̄ (resp. χ) is nontrivial, H^1_f = H^1; and H^1(G_L, F_l(ε̄))/H^1_f(G_L, F_l(ε̄)) ≅ F_l.
items.note: Kummer theory is upstream (Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 9, 'Hilbert 90 and Kummer theory'). Route: a source of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.5 (local residual types and peu ramifié classes).

items.name: Lemma 7.2.2: H^1_f(G_L, Z_l(εχ)) → H^1_f(G_L, F_l(ε̄χ̄)) is surjective
items.statement: For L/Q_l finite and χ : G_L → Z_l^× unramified, the reduction map H^1_f(G_L, Z_l(ε_l χ)) → H^1_f(G_L, F_l(ε̄_l χ̄)) is surjective.
items.note: Proof by cases: χ̄ ≠ 1 (cokernel H^2(G_L, Z_l(εχ))[l] = 0 by Tate duality); χ ≠ 1 = χ̄ (cokernel F_l, image inside H^1_f of codimension 1); χ = 1 (surjectivity of lim_r O_L^×/(O_L^×)^{l^r} → O_L^×/(O_L^×)^l). Used for the ordinary local points of the moduli spaces X_i in the proof of Theorem 7.1.11. Route: a source of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.5 (local residual types and peu ramifié classes).

items.name: Proposition 7.2.3: potential ordinary automorphy of symplectic residual representations over totally real fields (variant of BLGGT Thm. 3.1.2)
items.statement: Let F/F_0 be a finite Galois extension of totally real fields, 𝓘 a finite set, and for i ∈ 𝓘 let n_i be a positive even integer, l_i an odd prime and ı_i : Q̄_{l_i} ≅ C; let F^avoid/F be finite Galois, 𝓛 a finite set of rational primes unramified in F and different from every l_i, and r̄_i : G_F → GSp_{n_i}(F̄_{l_i}) with open kernel, multiplier ε̄_{l_i}^{1−n_i}, unramified above 𝓛. Then there are finite Galois extensions F^suffices/F_0 and F_1^avoid/Q with F^suffices ⊇ F totally real, unramified above 𝓛 and linearly disjoint from F^avoid F_1^avoid over F, and F_1^avoid linearly disjoint from F^avoid over Q, such that for every finite totally real F_1/F^suffices linearly disjoint from F^avoid F_1^avoid over F and every i there is a regular algebraic cuspidal polarized (π_i, χ_i) of GL_{n_i}(A_{F_1}) with (r̄_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i), r̄_{l_i,ı_i}(χ_i)ε̄_{l_i}^{1−n_i}) ≅ (r̄_i|_{G_{F_1}}, ε̄_{l_i}^{1−n_i}) and π_i ı_i-ordinary of weight 0.
items.note: The Dwork family and its λ-adic realisations are not planned (PAPER-QIAN-23 proposes a Part II route, PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII, not in atlas.json); the rational point is Moret–Bailly (R23.1). The paper gives only the modifications of BLGGT's proof (choices of N, M_i, q, φ_i, l' avoiding 𝓛 and F^avoid; F_1^avoid = Q̄^{ker ∏ r̄'_i}(ζ_{l'})). See issues: the adequacy sentence should use r̄'_i, and the disjointness from F^avoid demanded of F_1 is stronger than the proof needs and stronger than Corollary 7.2.4 can supply. Route: a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.0 normalization registry, ML.2 potential-automorphy assembly, ML.3 symmetric powers).

items.name: Corollary 7.2.4: potential automorphy of symmetric powers of a non-CM elliptic curve over Q with avoidance
items.statement: Let 𝓜 be a finite set of positive integers, E/Q a non-CM elliptic curve, 𝓛 a finite set of rational primes at which E has good reduction, and F^avoid/Q finite. Then there are a finite Galois F_2^avoid/Q linearly disjoint from F^avoid over Q and a finite totally real Galois F^suffices/Q, unramified above 𝓛 and linearly disjoint from F^avoid F_2^avoid over Q, such that for every finite totally real F'/F^suffices linearly disjoint from F_2^avoid over Q and every m ∈ 𝓜 there is a regular algebraic cuspidal polarizable π of GL_{m+1}(A_{F'}) of weight (0)_{τ,i} with Sym^m r_{E,l}|^∨_{G_{F'}} ≅ r_{l,ı}(π) for some, hence every, l and ı : Q̄_l ≅ C; π is unramified above every prime where E has good reduction.
items.note: Proof: choose l ≥ max 2(m+2) with E ordinary at l [Ser81, Th. 20], r̄_{E,l}(G_Q) = GL_2(F_l) [Ser72], l ∉ 𝓛 unramified in F^avoid; Lemma 7.1.8(2) makes Q̄^{ker r̄_{E,l}} disjoint from F^avoid. Choose an imaginary quadratic L split at l, a prime q = v_q v'_q split in L, and for even m characters ψ_m of G_L [BLGGT14, Lem. A.2.5]; a ramification argument (fields L_1, L_2, L_3, M_1, M_0) shows F^avoid is disjoint from L_3. Set r_m = Sym^m r^∨_{E,l} (m odd, GSp_{m+1}, multiplier ε^{−m}) or Sym^m r^∨_{E,l} ⊗ Ind_{G_L}^{G_Q} ψ_m (m even, GSp_{2(m+1)}, multiplier ε^{−(2m+1)}), apply Proposition 7.2.3 with avoid field F^avoid L_3, adequacy by [BLGGT14, Prop. 2.1.2], automorphy lifting [BLGGT14, Th. 2.4.1], and for m even [BLGGT14, Lem. 2.2.4] and [CHT08, Lem. 4.2.2]. Three misprints write F for L (see issues). Route: a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.0 normalization registry, ML.2 potential-automorphy assembly, ML.3 symmetric powers).

items.name: Assumption 7.2.6: choice of the auxiliary primes l_1, l_2
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 7.1.11: choose a non-CM E/Q with good reduction above 𝓛_0, distinct primes l_1, l_2 and primes λ_i | l_2 of M_i such that (1) l_2 splits completely in each M_i; (2) the image of G_F on E[l_1] contains SL_2(F_{l_1}) and r̄_{i,λ_i}(G_F) ⊇ SL_2(F_{l_2}) for each i; (3) l_1, l_2 are unramified in F; (4) E has good reduction above l_1, l_2; (5) l_1, l_2 lie under no prime of any S_i; (6) l_1, l_2 > 2m_i + 3 for all i; and, as the proof needs, (6′) l_1, l_2 > (m_i + 1)² for all i (the bound p > n² of Theorem 6.1.1(4)) and (7) r_{i,λ_i} is crystalline with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, 1} at the places above l_2 (these are not printed). This is possible because (2)–(7) hold for a density-one set of primes (Lemma 7.1.3) and (1) holds for l_2 in a set of positive density. Then 𝓛 := 𝓛_0 ∪ {l_1, l_2}.
items.note: As stated, (6) does not give p > n² = (m_i + 1)², required by Theorem 6.1.1(4) at p = l_1 and p = l_2, and the list omits that l_2 lies outside the density-zero exceptional set of (5b), needed for r_{i,λ_i} to be crystalline with Hodge–Tate numbers {0,1} at l_2 (used with Lemma 7.1.8 and Theorem 6.1.1(2)). Both are density-one conditions, so the fix is to add them (see issues). Route: a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.0 normalization registry, ML.2 potential-automorphy assembly, ML.3 symmetric powers).

items.name: Twisting R_i to determinant ε_l^{−1} after a soluble totally real base change
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 7.1.11: the rank-one system ε_l det r_{i,λ} has Hodge–Tate numbers 0, so det r_{i,λ} = ψ_i ε_l^{−1} for a finite-order ψ_i : G_F → M_i^× unramified outside S_i. The obstruction ∂ψ_i ∈ H^2(G_F, {±1}) = Br_F[2] ↪ ⊕_v Br_{F_v}[2] to a square root is supported on S_i. There is a soluble Galois totally real F_1^+/Q, unramified above 𝓛 and linearly disjoint over Q from the normal closure F_1^avoid of F_0^avoid F̄^{ker(r̄_{E,l_1} × ∏_i r̄_{i,λ_i})}, in which each rational prime below a place v ∈ ∪_i S_i has inertia degree divisible by 2[F_v : Q_{p_v}] [CHT08, Lem. 4.1.2]. Then ψ_i|_{G_{FF_1^+}} = φ_i² with φ_i unramified above 𝓛 after a quadratic twist (Grunwald–Wang, [AT09, Ch. X, Th. 5]), and R'_i := R_i|_{G_{FF_1^+}} ⊗ φ_i^{−1} has det r'_{i,λ} = ε_l^{−1}.
items.note: PAPER-QIAN-23 routes the field-extension existence part of the same argument to R23.1 ('including the determinant-character root extension'). Grunwald–Wang is explicitly outside upstream ClassFieldTheory ('The Grunwald–Wang theorem is not used and is outside …'). Printed misprints: a stray entry l_i in the 5-tuple of characters, 'R|_{G_{FF_1^+}}' for R_i, and 'S'_i = S_i' although φ_i may ramify outside S_i (see issues). Route: a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4 (roots of characters, local–global obstructions).

items.name: The moduli spaces Y_i, X_i of elliptic curves with prescribed l_1- and l_2-torsion, and their local points
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 7.1.11: give V = V_{r̄'_{i,λ_i}} a symplectic pairing preserved up to ε̄_{l_2}^{−1}; let Y_i/FF_1^+ be the moduli space of elliptic curves D with symplectic isomorphisms α_1 : E[l_1] ≅ D[l_1] and α_2 : V^∨ ≅ D[l_2], and X_i = Res_{FF_1^+/F^+F_1^+} Y_i. Then X_i has real points at every infinite place, and for every place v of F^+F_1^+ above 𝓛_0 ∪ {l_1, l_2} a point over an unramified extension of (F^+F_1^+)_v given by an elliptic curve with good reduction: above 𝓛_0 ∪ {l_1} by E itself; above l_2, by Lemma 7.1.8(1) r̄'_{i,λ_i}|_{G_{(F_1^+F)_w}} is either Ind(ω_{l_2,2}^{−1}δ) (δ the unramified quadratic character), handled by a curve with good supersingular reduction, or an extension of χ̄^{−1}ε̄^{−1} by χ̄ (χ̄ unramified) with peu ramifié class in H^1_f, handled by the Serre–Tate lift D_e of an ordinary D̄/k(w) with e ∈ H^1_f(G_L, Z_{l_2}(εψ^{−2})) lifting minus that class (Lemma 7.2.2), so that D_e[l_1] ≅ E[l_1] and r̄_{D_e,l_2} ≅ (r̄'_{i,λ_i})^∨.
items.note: The ACC+ instance is the elliptic-curve (modular-curve) twist over a CM field, Weil-restricted to F^+F_1^+ (Weil restriction: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a), with Serre–Tate deformation (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4) and the peu ramifié lifting Lemma 7.2.2; R23.2 plans the Hilbert–Blumenthal version for KW. The supersingular case formula '(−l_2)^f' and the coefficient field k(w) are imprecise (see issues). Route: a source of HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H6 (twisted torsion moduli and their local points).

items.name: Moret–Bailly step: elliptic curves D_i over a totally real extension F_2^+
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 7.1.11: by Moret–Bailly ([BLGGT14, Prop. 3.1.1]) there is a finite totally real extension F_2^+/F_1^+F^+, Galois over F_0^+, with all primes above 𝓛 unramified in F_2^+/F^+, linearly disjoint over F_1^+F^+ from F^avoid F^{+,suffices} F_1^+, such that ∏_i X_i(F_2^+) ≠ ∅: there are elliptic curves D_i over F_2 = F_2^+F, with good reduction above 𝓛, D_i[l_1] ≅ E[l_1]|_{G_{F_2}} and D_i[l_2] ≅ r̄'_{i,λ_i}|^∨_{G_{F_2}}.
items.note: R23.1: 'Prove the rational-point existence theorem for the smooth geometrically irreducible varieties used here, with prescribed nonempty local open sets and a finite extension satisfying the required disjointness and real-place conditions'; R24.5:operations adds 'R23.1 is the general Moret–Bailly/Skolem theorem with specified local open conditions, prescribed splitting and linear disjointness … for an arbitrary smooth geometrically irreducible variety over a number field'. The inputs (geometric irreducibility of X_i and the local points) are the previous item.
