routes.title: Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation, Part II: ramified Hecke operators and local–global compatibility away from p
routes.brief:
Starts where Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) stops. IHG.3 normalizes the spherical Hecke polynomial P_v(X) at unramified places, and IHG.4–IHG.5 interpolate and specialize determinants; nothing in the atlas says how a determinant valued in a torsion Hecke algebra behaves at a ramified place. This Part II proves it for GL_n over a CM field, following §2.2.5 and §3 of Allen et al., 'Potential automorphy over CM fields', Ann. of Math. 197 (2023), 897–1113 (ACC+), published numbering.

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Setting (§3.1): F a CM field containing an imaginary quadratic field, with every p-adic place of F⁺ split in F; K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) good; λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}; S = S^c a finite set of finite places containing the p-adic ones (with the paper's condition on residue characteristics outside S); R ⊂ S a set of places prime to p whose residue characteristics split in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F, with Iw_{v,1} ⊂ K_v ⊂ Iw_v for v ∈ R (pro-ℓ-Iwahori ⊂ K_v ⊂ Iwahori) and K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v ∈ R^c − R; T = S − (R^c − R); and T^T_R(K, λ) ⊂ End_{D(O)}(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ)) the image of the algebra generated by the unramified Hecke operators away from T and the operators t_{v,i}(σ) (v ∈ R, σ ∈ W_{F_v}). For v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v}, P_{v,σ}(X) = Σ_i (−1)^i e_{v,i}(σ)X^{n−i} is the ramified Hecke polynomial (2.2.8) built from the pro-ℓ-Iwahori operators t_{v,i}(σ). Proposition 3.1.2: if 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) is non-Eisenstein, there are N ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F : Q], an ideal I_R ⊂ T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪 with I_R^N = 0, and a T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪/I_R-valued determinant D_{𝔪,R} of G_{F,T} of dimension n such that (1) for v ∉ T the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v is the image of P_v(X), and (2) for v ∈ R and σ ∈ W_{F_v} the characteristic polynomial of σ is the image of P_{v,σ}(X). Theorem 3.1.1 is the same with a continuous ρ_{𝔪,R} : G_{F,T} → GL_n(T^T_R(K, λ)_𝔪/I_R) in place of the determinant.

Layers. (1) Ramified Hecke operators at a split place v ∤ p (§2.2.5): the pro-ℓ-Iwahori operators t_{v,i}(α), e_{v,i}(α) and (2.2.8); Proposition 2.2.9, relating pro-ℓ-Iwahori invariants to the Weil–Deligne representation; the parahorics 𝔭_v ⊃ 𝔭_{v,1}, the level 𝔮̃_v of the unitary group G̃ and Lemma 2.2.10; the transferred operators (2.2.11)–(2.2.12) and Lemma 2.2.13; the resultant Res_v, Proposition 2.2.14 and Corollary 2.2.15 (Res_v^{(2n)!}(ρ(τ_v) − 1)P_{v,φ_v}(ρ(φ_v)) = 0); the ramified split case (2.2.17); the Satake transforms of these polynomials to the Siegel Levi at Iwahori-type levels, Propositions 2.2.18–2.2.19. (2) The ℓ ≠ p argument (§3.2): Lemma 3.2.1 (reduction to λ = 0, small decomposable level K̃ with K̃ ∩ G = K, separated Frobenius eigenvalues and an auxiliary twist ψ), Proposition 3.2.2 (the 2n-dimensional determinant on RΓ_c of the unitary locally symmetric space with the resultant-killed inertia relation), Corollary 3.2.3 (the same for the boundary), the boundary determinant D′ = D·(D^{c,∨} ⊗ ε^{1−2n}), the extraction of D_{𝔪,R} from D′ and the passage from determinants to representations. Tests: n = 1 against local class field theory; Steinberg and unramified principal series for n = 2.

Import, never re-plan: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0–IHG.5 (determinants, Cayley–Hamilton reconstruction, Hecke algebras on complexes and their nilpotent ideals, the spherical normalization, interpolation); SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1 (Hecke algebras over rings, with the Bushnell–Kutzko cover lemmas 2.1.12–2.1.13 routed there); ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.5 (arithmetic complexes, Hecke correspondences, boundary, duality); TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.3–TC.4 (the unramified Levi Satake identities and Scholze's determinants, Theorems 2.3.5 and 2.3.7 of ACC+); PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.0 (the boundary summand of Theorems 2.4.2 and 2.4.8); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0, AG2.2, AG2.4 and AG2.5 (characteristic-zero Galois representations of U(n, n) and GL_n, and local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p in characteristic zero); ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.* (Weil–Deligne representations and local Langlands normalizations). Prerequisite papers: Newton–Thorne (Forum Math. Sigma 2016), Scholze (Ann. of Math. 2015), Varma (Forum Math. Sigma 2024), Bushnell–Kutzko (Proc. LMS 1998), Chenevier (LMS Lecture Notes 414, 2014).
routes.reason: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants owns Hecke-valued determinants but plans them only through unramified Frobenius: IHG.3 is explicitly the spherical normalization at unramified places, and IHG.4–IHG.5 interpolate and specialize without any condition at ramified places. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure's owner matrix sends ACC+ §3 to this roadmap and to AG2, but AG2.5 is local–global compatibility in characteristic zero. The ramified Hecke operators of §2.2.5 and the ℓ ≠ p argument of §3 are new layers in IHG's direction, eighteen items with their own final theorem, so they form a Part II rather than a source of IHG.3.

PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure is built from this paper, and its layers own the steps these items fill. PA.0: the cohomology of U(O_K) behind the boundary degree shifts (Lemma 4.2.2(1)). PA.1: Kostant representatives, CTG weights (Definition 4.3.5, Lemma 4.3.6), the decomposed-generic twist in Corollary 4.4.8 and Lemma 4.5.2. PA.2: the torus A_K and Lemmas 5.4.14(2)–(4), 5.4.15 and 5.4.16, which reach every cohomological degree, and Corollary 5.5.2. PA.3: the lifting theorems themselves, Theorems 6.1.1 and 6.1.2, Corollary 6.5.5 and Theorem 6.6.2, and their deductions; no stage states an automorphy lifting theorem, and PAPER-QIAN-23 routed Theorem 6.1.2 here. PA.4: the auxiliary places v_0, v′_0. PA.5: the soluble base-change fields E = E_0E_aE_bE_c and the rank-2 compatible-system Lemmas 7.1.1–7.1.3, as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 routed them. ML.2 stays the downstream assembly.

IHG.5 plans 'specialization to residual semisimple representations' of Hecke-valued determinants. Definition 2.3.6 (maximal ideals of Galois type; non-Eisenstein when ρ̄_𝔪 is absolutely irreducible) and the behaviour of ρ̄_𝔪 under duality and twisting are predicates on that residual representation, used throughout §§2.4–6.

PA's owner matrix sends §§2.1–2.2 and 2.4 to ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces. ALS.3 owns Hecke correspondences on complexes, and twisting RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ) and its Hecke algebra by a character (§2.2.20) belongs there. ALS.5's later part compares Betti cohomology with automorphic forms; Theorems 2.4.10(2) and 2.4.11 localize that comparison at a non-Eisenstein ideal, which no stage states. ALS.0 owns neat levels, and Lemma 6.5.2 is a neatness criterion.

SR.1 owns Hecke algebras over rings. Lemmas 2.1.12–2.1.13 are Bushnell–Kutzko's G-cover formalism ([BK98, §§6–7]) for monoid Hecke algebras over arbitrary rings, which §2.2.5 uses to move operators between Levi and ambient levels.

AG2.7 owns the decomposed-generic condition, and Lemma 4.3.2 (infinitely many decomposed generic primes once one exists) belongs with it. AG2.0 owns algebraic weights and algebraic Hecke characters, and the crystalline character ψ with prescribed restriction to O^×_{F_v} ([HSBT10, Lem. 2.2]) used in Theorem 4.5.1 is such a character.

G7 plans the dimension-general residual-image API and names ACC+ Definition 6.2.29; the lemmas producing enormous image, scalar elements and decomposed genericity for symmetric powers (Lemmas 7.1.4–7.1.7) are its verification lemmas, as PAPER-QIAN-23 routed them. R01.4 plans the finite-subgroup facts of GL_2 and PGL_2 used by Lemmas 7.1.6(1) and 7.1.8(2). G7 also specifies oddness at real places, and totally odd characters are its rank-one case.

R07.5 plans the inertia characters of elliptic-curve torsion and the peu/très ramifiée distinctions. Lemma 7.1.8(1) is the same computation for crystalline Z_l-lattices with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, 1}, and §7.2.1 with Lemma 7.2.2 is the twisted, integral version of the peu ramifié classes.

R24.5:operations owns compatible systems and their operations with purity. Purity of rank-one systems (via Serre's algebraic Hecke characters) and of induced and Artin-up-to-twist systems is part of that interface.

ML.0 is the register of normalizations and local parameters: the archimedean rec_ℝ, rec_ℂ and the L-functions of compatible systems and their comparison with automorphic L-functions belong there. ML.2 assembles potential automorphy: Proposition 7.2.3 (the BLGGT-type potential automorphy of symplectic residual representations) and the choice of auxiliary primes in Assumption 7.2.6. ML.3 owns symmetric powers and their analytic consequences: Corollary 7.2.4 (the elliptic-curve seed) and purity, Corollary 7.1.13(1). This follows PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 and PAPER-QIAN-23.

The Jacquet–Shalika bound |α| < q^{1/2} for Satake parameters of unitary cuspidal representations follows from absolute convergence of L(s, π × π^∨) for Re s > 1, part of AL.3's Rankin–Selberg theory.

Twisting R_i to determinant ε_l^{−1} needs a square root of a character after a soluble totally real base change, whose obstruction is a local–global (Grunwald–Wang, Brauer-class) computation owned by R02.2/R02.4; PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 routed its analogous lemma here.

H6 plans twisted torsion moduli for two auxiliary residue characteristics with prescribed local points. The moduli spaces Y_i, X_i of elliptic curves with prescribed l_1- and l_2-torsion and their local points are its elliptic-curve case, exported to R23.1 for Moret-Bailly.

sourceIssues.printed: Note that a dominant weight μ̃ ∈ (ℤ^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F⁺,E)} is CTG if it satisfies the following condition: for all w ∈ W^P, we have (4.3.7) Σ_{i=1}^n (μ_{w,τ̃,i} − μ_{w,τ̃c,i}) ≠ Σ_{i=1}^n (μ_{w,τ̃_0,i} − μ_{w,τ̃_0c,i}).
sourceIssues.reason: Since λ^∨_{σ,i} = −λ_{σ,n+1−i} (§2.2.1), a w violating CTG (Definition 4.3.5) has λ_{w,σ,i} + λ_{w,σc,n+1−i} = i_0 for all σ and i, hence Σ_i(λ_{w,σ,i} + λ_{w,σc,i}) = n·i_0 for every σ, so the '+' inequality implies CTG. With '−', the dictionary (2.2.2) makes Σ_i(μ_{w,τ̃,i} − μ_{w,τ̃c,i}) the sum of all 2n entries of w(μ̃_τ + ρ_τ) − ρ_τ, i.e. of μ̃_τ, for every w, and the printed criterion is false: for n = 1, [F⁺ : Q] = 2, μ̃_{τ_0} = (1, 1), μ̃_τ = (0, 0) it holds for all w (2 ≠ 0), but for w = 1 one gets μ_{τ̃_0} = 1, μ_{τ̃_0c} = −1, μ_{τ̃} = μ_{τ̃c} = 0, so λ_{w,σ} − λ^∨_{w,σc} = (0) for every σ and μ̃ is not CTG. With '+', raising λ̃_{τ_0,1} by a moves the right-hand side by ±a for each of the finitely many w, so the proof's last sentence goes through and Lemma 4.3.6 stands.

sourceIssues.correction: It suffices to show that μ̃_{τ,n+j} − μ̃_{τ,j} (1 ≤ j ≤ n) is not independent of j, for μ̃ = w(λ̃_i + ρ) − ρ; equivalently, that the 2n entries of λ̃_i + ρ cannot be split into two n-element sets, one a translate of the other. The 'look modulo M' argument proves this for n ≥ 2 when applied to differences instead of sums: since 2a_i ≡ M/4 mod M, a difference between the two blocks of λ̃(a_i) + ρ is ≡ ±M/4 up to 2n − 1 modulo M, and these are pairwise distinct; a difference within a block is ≡ 0 up to 2n − 1; and a difference within the first block (of size < nM) never equals one within the second (a nonzero multiple of nM up to 2n − 1). So a translate-split would pair the 2n entries inside one block of n entries, which is impossible. (The multiset I′ should likewise be formed from the entries of λ̃(a_i), which is what I′_1, I′_2, I′_3 list.)

sourceIssues.locator: §6.5.12, proof of Proposition 6.5.13, p. 1071 (also in arXiv v2)
sourceIssues.printed: Statement (1): 'If w is a finite place of E lying above the place v of F, then we have rec_{E_w}(π_E) = rec_{F_v}(π)|_{W_{E_w}}.' Proof: '… to conclude the existence of a cuspidal, regular algebraic automorphic representation Π of GL_n(𝔸_E) of weight λ_E such that for almost all finite places w of E such that π_{w|_F} is unramified, Π_w is a lift of π_{w|_F}. The Chebotarev density theorem then implies that we must have r_ι(Π) ≅ r_ι(π)|_{G_E}, so we can take π_E = Π.'
sourceIssues.correction: add that Π_w is the Arthur–Clozel local base change of π_{w|_F} at every finite place w, and that local base change is compatible with the local Langlands correspondence (Harris–Taylor, Ch. VII); likewise for part (2)
sourceIssues.reason: The statement claims the local relation at every finite place, but the proof records it only at almost all unramified places and then passes to the Galois side. The isomorphism r_ι(Π) ≅ r_ι(π)|_{G_E} pins down rec_{E_w}(Π_w) at best up to semisimplification (this is how [Var14] is used at the end of the proofs of Theorems 6.1.1 and 6.1.2). The full local relation of part (2) is needed there, to pass from 'Π_{E,w} is unramified for any place w | v' to rec_{F_v}(Π_v) being finitely ramified. The statement is standard and true.

sourceIssues.locator: §6.5.12, proof of Theorem 6.1.1, choice of E_a, E_b, E_c, p. 1073; the same example in §6.6.10, p. 1083 (also in arXiv v2)
sourceIssues.printed: • Each rational prime lying below a place of V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2 splits in E_a · E_b · E_c. The prime p is unramified in E_a · E_b · E_c. … For example, we can choose any E_a satisfying the given condition. Then we can choose E_b = ℚ(√−p_b), where p_b is a prime satisfying p_b ≡ 1 mod 4 and p_b ≡ −1 mod l for any prime l ∉ {2, p} either lying below a place w of E_0 at which π_{E_0,w} or ρ|_{E_0,w} is ramified, or ramified in E_0 · E_a, and E_c = ℚ(√−p_c), where p_c ≡ 1 mod 4p_b is any prime not equal to p.
sourceIssues.correction: also require p_b ≡ −1 mod l and p_c ≡ −1 mod l for every rational prime l below V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2 (such l are odd and prime to p, so this is compatible with the other congruences by the Chinese remainder theorem), and, in the Fontaine–Laffaille case, p_b ≠ p
sourceIssues.reason: An odd prime l ∤ p_b splits in ℚ(√−p_b) if and only if −p_b is a square mod l. The listed congruences force this only for the primes in the third condition; nothing in the example makes the primes below V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2 split in E_b or E_c, and they must, for E to be V_0 ∪ V_1 ∪ V_2-split as the proof then asserts. Nothing excludes p_b = p either, which would ramify p in E_b, against the first condition. Fields with the listed properties do exist, so only the example is incomplete.

sourceIssues.locator: §7.1, Lemma 7.1.8(2) and its proof, pp. 1091–1092 (also in arXiv v2)
sourceIssues.printed: (2) Suppose that K is a number field in which l is unramified and that r : G_K → GL_2(Z_l) is a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, 1} for each embedding K ↪ Q̄_l. sourceIssues.correction: add the hypothesis l > 2 (the proof's claim about normal subgroups holds for l ≥ 5; for l = 3 the conclusion Δ = GL_2(F_3) still holds, since every proper normal subgroup of GL_2(F_3) lies in SL_2(F_3))
sourceIssues.reason: Part (2) fails for l = 2, which the proof of part (1) explicitly allows ('If l = 2 then 1 = ε̄_l^{−1} and we are done'). Take K = Q and r = T_2E for E = 37a1 : y² + y = x³ − x, which has good reduction at 2, so r is crystalline with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, 1}. Its 2-division polynomial 4x³ − 4x + 1 is irreducible of discriminant 16·37, so r̄(G_Q) = GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 ⊇ SL_2(F_2), and Q(E[2]) contains Q(√37), which is unramified at 2 because 37 ≡ 1 mod 4. The failing step is that A_3 ⊲ GL_2(F_2) is neither central nor contains SL_2(F_2). Every use in the paper has l ≥ 7 (Corollary 7.2.4 takes l ≥ 2(m + 2); Assumption 7.2.6 has l_1, l_2 > 2m_i + 3), so nothing downstream is affected.
